Тогда следующий слой — **Physical Infrastructure, Labs, Equipment & Manufacturing Observatory v0.1**. Здесь Innovation OS впервые начинает работать не только с информационными и организационными ресурсами, но и с физическими мощностями, очередями, пропускной способностью, логистикой и реальным производством.

> **Document: Physical Infrastructure, Labs, Equipment & Manufacturing Observatory v0.1**
> 
> # Physical Infrastructure, Labs, Equipment & Manufacturing Observatory v0.1
> 
> ## 1. Главный переход
> 
> До этого система уже умеет собирать проект из:
> 
> ```text
> Problem
> ↓
> People
> Code
> Research
> Funding
> ```
> 
> Теперь добавляется физический слой:
> 
> ```text
> Problem
> ↓
> Knowledge
> ↓
> People
> ↓
> Code
> ↓
> Funding
> ↓
> PHYSICAL INFRASTRUCTURE
> ↓
> Execution
> ```
> 
> То есть появляется ответ на вопросы:
> 
> > Где это можно изготовить?
> 
> > На каком оборудовании провести эксперимент?
> 
> > Какой лабораторный ресурс доступен?
> 
> > Какой производитель может изготовить прототип?
> 
> > Где bottleneck — не знания и не деньги, а физическая пропускная способность?
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2. Physical Resource
> 
> В IIR Core ничего нового не требуется.
> 
> Используются существующие:
> 
> ```text
> RESOURCE
> ACTION
> ARTIFACT
> CONSTRAINT
> EVENT
> CONTEXT
> ```
> 
> Подтипы Resource:
> 
> ```text
> LAB
> EQUIPMENT
> FACILITY
> MANUFACTURER
> WORKSHOP
> WAREHOUSE
> VEHICLE
> ROBOT
> TEST_SITE
> COMPUTE_INFRASTRUCTURE
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3. Laboratory
> 
> Lab — это Resource, который предоставляет набор capabilities.
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> Photonics Lab
> PROVIDES
> optical_characterization
> 
> Photonics Lab
> PROVIDES
> fiber_sensor_testing
> 
> Photonics Lab
> PROVIDES
> high_speed_measurement
> ```
> 
> Но Lab сам по себе может быть составным Resource.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 4. Lab contains Equipment
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> Lab A
> HAS
> Spectrometer 1
> 
> Lab A
> HAS
> High-speed camera 2
> 
> Lab A
> HAS
> Environmental chamber 3
> ```
> 
> Физически:
> 
> ```text
> Organization
> ↓
> Facility
> ↓
> Equipment
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 5. Equipment
> 
> Equipment становится отдельным Resource.
> 
> Пример:
> 
> ```yaml
> resource:
>   type: EQUIPMENT
>   name: High-Speed Camera
>   status: AVAILABLE
> ```
> 
> Capabilities:
> 
> ```text
> high_speed_imaging
> motion_capture
> vibration_analysis
> ```
> 
> Constraints:
> 
> ```text
> location
> booking
> operator_required
> sample_size
> temperature_range
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 6. Equipment Capability Contract
> 
> Физическое оборудование особенно хорошо описывается через contract.
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```yaml
> capability:
>   id: tensile_testing
> 
>   input:
>     sample
> 
>   output:
>     stress_strain_dataset
> 
>   constraints:
>     max_force: 50 kN
>     max_sample_width: 100 mm
> 
>   verification:
>     calibration_required: true
> ```
> 
> Это делает физическую capability вычислимой.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 7. Facility
> 
> Facility — более крупная единица:
> 
> ```text
> clean room
> wind tunnel
> robotics hall
> test track
> data center
> workshop
> pilot manufacturing line
> ```
> 
> Facility может:
> 
> ```text
> HAS Equipment
> HAS Operators
> HAS Safety Rules
> HAS Booking Capacity
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 8. Physical availability отличается от talent availability
> 
> Для человека:
> 
> ```text
> 20 h/week
> ```
> 
> Для машины:
> 
> ```text
> 4 h/day
> ```
> 
> или:
> 
> ```text
> throughput = 20 samples/hour
> ```
> 
> или:
> 
> ```text
> reserved until date X
> ```
> 
> Поэтому Resource Capacity должен быть типизирован.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 9. Capacity Model
> 
> Минимально:
> 
> ```text
> time capacity
> throughput capacity
> batch capacity
> spatial capacity
> ```
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> CNC:
> 8 machine-hours/day
> ```
> 
> или:
> 
> ```text
> 3D printer:
> 4 jobs/day
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 10. Booking
> 
> Физический Resource часто требует reservation.
> 
> Вместо:
> 
> ```text
> Resource AVAILABLE
> ```
> 
> нужно:
> 
> ```text
> AVAILABLE
> for time interval
> ```
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> Microscope:
> available 2026-10-10 09:00–13:00
> ```
> 
> Это уже temporal constraint.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 11. Reservation Object
> 
> Можно выразить через:
> 
> ```text
> Action
> ASSIGNED_TO
> Equipment
> 
> Context:
> time interval
> ```
> 
> или application-level `Reservation`.
> 
> Не нужен новый Core type.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 12. Equipment dependency
> 
> Некоторые machines требуют других resources.
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> CNC machine
> REQUIRES
> qualified operator
> ```
> 
> или:
> 
> ```text
> Electron microscope
> REQUIRES
> sample preparation lab
> ```
> 
> Поэтому equipment itself может иметь capability dependencies.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 13. Operator Requirement
> 
> Очень важный момент.
> 
> Наличие машины не означает доступность capability.
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> Equipment available
> Operator unavailable
> ```
> 
> → capability still blocked.
> 
> То есть:
> 
> ```text
> Physical Capability
> =
> Equipment
> +
> Operator
> +
> Material
> +
> Procedure
> +
> Access
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14. Composite Physical Capability
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> CNC milling
> ```
> 
> требует:
> 
> ```text
> CNC machine
> +
> tooling
> +
> operator
> +
> CAD/CAM file
> +
> raw material
> ```
> 
> Только вместе они создают operational capability.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15. Material Resource
> 
> Материалы тоже можно представить как Resource.
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> aluminum stock
> optical fiber
> PCB substrate
> resin
> sensor film
> ```
> 
> Особенность:
> 
> ```text
> consumable
> ```
> 
> то есть Resource quantity уменьшается.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16. Consumable State
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> Material X:
> stock = 12 kg
> ```
> 
> Action:
> 
> ```text
> manufacture prototype
> ```
> 
> потребляет:
> 
> ```text
> 2 kg
> ```
> 
> После Action:
> 
> ```text
> stock = 10 kg
> ```
> 
> Это уже inventory semantics.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17. Inventory Layer
> 
> На уровне MVP достаточно:
> 
> ```text
> Resource
> HAS quantity
> HAS unit
> ```
> 
> Events:
> 
> ```text
> STOCK_ADDED
> STOCK_CONSUMED
> STOCK_RESERVED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18. Manufacturing Resource
> 
> Manufacturer — Organization Resource, предоставляющая capabilities:
> 
> ```text
> PCB assembly
> CNC machining
> injection molding
> precision optics
> fiber processing
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19. Manufacturer ≠ Machine
> 
> Organization может обладать:
> 
> ```text
> multiple facilities
> multiple machines
> staff
> quality certifications
> ```
> 
> Project может обращаться:
> 
> ```text
> manufacturer as service
> ```
> 
> не зная внутренней machinery.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 20. Manufacturing as Service
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> Action:
> manufacture 100 housings
> ```
> 
> может быть assigned to:
> 
> ```text
> Contract Manufacturer
> ```
> 
> и система не обязана моделировать его внутренние станки.
> 
> Это важный уровень абстракции.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 21. Multi-resolution physical modeling
> 
> Как и simulation:
> 
> ```text
> L0:
> service capability
> 
> L1:
> facility
> 
> L2:
> equipment
> 
> L3:
> machine operation
> 
> L4:
> physics
> ```
> 
> Не нужно всегда идти до уровня machine commands.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22. Project requirements
> 
> Пример hardware project требует:
> 
> ```text
> PCB fabrication
> optical calibration
> environmental testing
> assembly
> ```
> 
> Physical Resolver ищет Resources для каждого capability.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 23. Physical Resource Resolver
> 
> Pipeline:
> 
> ```text
> Physical Gap
> ↓
> Capability Query
> ↓
> Facilities / Labs / Manufacturers
> ↓
> Constraints
> ↓
> Availability
> ↓
> Cost / Lead Time
> ↓
> Resolution Options
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24. Physical Gap
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> Project REQUIRES
> thermal cycling test
> ```
> 
> но нет provider:
> 
> ```text
> Equipment/Service PROVIDES
> thermal cycling
> ```
> 
> → Physical Gap.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25. Lead Time
> 
> Для физических ресурсов critical dimension:
> 
> ```text
> lead_time
> ```
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> CNC prototype:
> 3 days
> 
> custom sensor fabrication:
> 6 weeks
> 
> clean-room process:
> 2 weeks queue
> ```
> 
> Lead time должен быть отдельным property.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26. Queueing
> 
> Если Resource shared:
> 
> ```text
> 10 projects
> → one machine
> ```
> 
> возникает очередь.
> 
> Это уже не просто availability.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27. Queue Model
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> Machine capacity:
> 40 h/week
> 
> Demand:
> 65 h/week
> ```
> 
> Это означает:
> 
> ```text
> oversubscribed
> ```
> 
> и Scheduler должен учитывать delay.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28. Setup Time
> 
> Physical systems часто имеют:
> 
> ```text
> setup/changeover time
> ```
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> CNC:
> 30 min tool setup
> ```
> 
> или:
> 
> ```text
> lab:
> 2 h calibration
> ```
> 
> Поэтому batching может быть выгоднее.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29. Batch Optimization
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> 5 projects
> need same measurement
> ```
> 
> можно:
> 
> ```text
> batch together
> ```
> 
> чтобы уменьшить setup cost.
> 
> Это очень интересный shared-resource optimization.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 30. Shared Infrastructure Opportunity
> 
> Если много проектов регулярно требуют:
> 
> ```text
> environmental testing
> ```
> 
> и каждый отдельно покупает service, Opportunity Engine может предложить:
> 
> ```text
> shared environmental test facility
> ```
> 
> Это прямой analog Common Infrastructure Detector.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 31. Buy vs Access vs Build
> 
> Physical capability acquisition может иметь:
> 
> ```text
> BUY_EQUIPMENT
> RENT
> BOOK_LAB
> OUTSOURCE
> PARTNER
> BUILD_FACILITY
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 32. Example
> 
> Gap:
> 
> ```text
> high-speed imaging
> ```
> 
> Options:
> 
> ```text
> A. Buy camera
> B. Rent camera
> C. Use university lab
> D. Contract testing service
> E. Partner with company
> ```
> 
> Нельзя всё свести к одной цене.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 33. Physical Option Vector
> 
> Показывать:
> 
> ```text
> Cost
> Lead time
> Control
> Availability
> Location
> Repeatability
> Setup effort
> Certification
> Capacity
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 34. Geographic constraints
> 
> Physical resources намного сильнее зависят от location.
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> sample transport
> operator travel
> hazardous material
> customs
> ```
> 
> поэтому:
> 
> ```text
> location
> ```
> 
> становится hard/soft constraint.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 35. Logistics
> 
> Как только Resource физический, возникает:
> 
> ```text
> transport
> shipping
> storage
> customs
> handling
> ```
> 
> То есть появляется новый класс capabilities.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 36. Logistics Resource
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> courier
> freight
> warehouse
> specialized transport
> ```
> 
> можно представить как Resource/Service.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 37. Artifact becomes physical
> 
> До сих пор Artifact часто был:
> 
> ```text
> document
> code
> dataset
> ```
> 
> Теперь:
> 
> ```text
> prototype
> sample
> device
> component
> batch
> ```
> 
> тоже Artifact.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 38. Physical Artifact
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```yaml
> artifact:
>   type: prototype
>   serial_number: P-001
> ```
> 
> Physical Artifact может иметь:
> 
> ```text
> location
> condition
> version
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 39. Digital + Physical Artifact Pair
> 
> Очень важная идея:
> 
> ```text
> CAD model
> ↔
> Physical prototype
> ```
> 
> или:
> 
> ```text
> software firmware
> ↔
> Device
> ```
> 
> System должен связывать их lineage.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 40. Digital Thread
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> Requirement
> ↓
> CAD v3
> ↓
> Manufacturing Action
> ↓
> Prototype #17
> ↓
> Test Action
> ↓
> Dataset
> ↓
> Design Decision
> ↓
> CAD v4
> ```
> 
> Это классический digital thread, но встроенный в общий IIR.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 41. Digital Twin
> 
> Physical Resource/Artifact может иметь:
> 
> ```text
> Digital Twin
> ```
> 
> то есть software representation актуального состояния.
> 
> Например Robot:
> 
> ```text
> battery
> position
> faults
> firmware
> payload
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 42. Twin ≠ Physical Object
> 
> Нужно различать:
> 
> ```text
> Robot Resource
> ```
> 
> и:
> 
> ```text
> DigitalTwin Artifact/Resource representation
> ```
> 
> с relation:
> 
> ```text
> OBSERVES / REPRESENTS
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 43. State synchronization
> 
> Physical Device:
> 
> ```text
> sensor readings
> ```
> 
> → Event
> 
> → World State
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> temperature exceeded
> ```
> 
> создаёт:
> 
> ```text
> EQUIPMENT_STATE_CHANGED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 44. Device Adapter
> 
> Semantic Runtime не должен напрямую знать vendor API.
> 
> Используется:
> 
> ```text
> Semantic Action
> ↓
> Device Adapter
> ↓
> Hardware API / PLC / Robot Controller
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 45. Physical Action
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> MOVE robot arm
> ```
> 
> или:
> 
> ```text
> HEAT chamber to 80°C
> ```
> 
> это `ACTION`.
> 
> Но requirements по safety намного выше.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 46. Physical Safety Gate
> 
> Перед execution:
> 
> ```text
> authorized?
> machine ready?
> safety interlocks?
> operator present?
> environment safe?
> ```
> 
> Если нет:
> 
> ```text
> BLOCKED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 47. Simulation Before Execution
> 
> Для сложного physical action:
> 
> ```text
> Action
> ↓
> Digital Twin Simulation
> ↓
> Safety Verification
> ↓
> Approval
> ↓
> Physical Execution
> ```
> 
> Это прямое соединение с Counterfactual Engine.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 48. Shadow Execution
> 
> Можно запустить:
> 
> ```text
> simulated robot
> ```
> 
> до реального.
> 
> Один и тот же semantic action:
> 
> ```text
> MOVE_TO(point)
> ```
> 
> имеет:
> 
> ```text
> Simulation Backend
> Physical Backend
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 49. Это особенно важно для вашей идеи EVE-like world
> 
> В 3D мире можно видеть:
> 
> ```text
> virtual machine
> ```
> 
> как twin реальной машины.
> 
> Но interaction:
> 
> ```text
> click / move / assign
> ```
> 
> создаёт Command.
> 
> Runtime решает:
> 
> ```text
> simulation only?
> real execution?
> approval needed?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 50. Physical World Representation
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> Facility
> ├── Room
> │   ├── Machine A
> │   └── Machine B
> └── Storage
> ```
> 
> Это можно визуализировать пространственно.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 51. Facility Layout
> 
> 2D/3D слой получает реальные:
> 
> ```text
> positions
> zones
> routes
> capacity
> ```
> 
> Это уже не metaphorical city, а actual facility twin.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 52. Hybrid Map
> 
> Virtual Technopark может одновременно иметь:
> 
> ```text
> semantic space
> ```
> 
> и:
> 
> ```text
> physical space
> ```
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> Capability Map
> ```
> 
> не географическая.
> 
> А:
> 
> ```text
> Lab Layout
> ```
> 
> географическая/пространственная.
> 
> Не смешивать эти координатные системы без необходимости.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 53. Manufacturing Workflow
> 
> Пример:
> 
> ```text
> Design
> ↓
> Material Procurement
> ↓
> Machine Setup
> ↓
> Manufacture
> ↓
> Inspection
> ↓
> Rework?
> ↓
> Assembly
> ↓
> Test
> ```
> 
> Это Action DAG.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 54. Manufacturing Bill of Materials
> 
> Для physical product нужен:
> 
> ```text
> BOM
> ```
> 
> Можно хранить как Artifact.
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> Prototype X
> REQUIRES
> component A ×2
> component B ×1
> material C 300g
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 55. BOM Resolver
> 
> Для каждого component:
> 
> ```text
> existing inventory?
> supplier?
> manufacture internally?
> substitute?
> ```
> 
> Это тот же Capability/Resource Resolution pattern.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 56. Supplier
> 
> Supplier — Organization Resource.
> 
> Он предоставляет:
> 
> ```text
> component supply
> material supply
> ```
> 
> с:
> 
> ```text
> price
> lead time
> minimum order quantity
> location
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 57. Supply-chain dependency
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> Project
> DEPENDS_ON
> Component X
> ```
> 
> Component X:
> 
> ```text
> single supplier
> ```
> 
> → concentration risk.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 58. Alternate Component
> 
> Substitution graph:
> 
> ```text
> Component A
> ALTERNATIVE_TO
> Component B
> ```
> 
> Но constraints:
> 
> ```text
> size
> performance
> certification
> compatibility
> ```
> 
> решают, допустима ли замена.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 59. Physical Substitution
> 
> Это очень похоже на software substitution, но verification обычно дороже.
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> new material
> ```
> 
> может потребовать:
> 
> ```text
> retest
> recertification
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 60. Certification
> 
> Для некоторых projects physical capability недостаточно.
> 
> Нужно:
> 
> ```text
> certified process
> certified lab
> certified supplier
> ```
> 
> Certification — constraint/evidence.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 61. Calibration
> 
> Measurement Equipment может требовать:
> 
> ```text
> calibration validity
> ```
> 
> Если expired:
> 
> ```text
> equipment still physically works
> ```
> 
> но:
> 
> ```text
> measurement capability not valid for regulated use
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 62. Calibration Event
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> CALIBRATION_COMPLETED
> ```
> 
> создаёт Evidence.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 63. Quality Control
> 
> Manufacturing action:
> 
> ```text
> PRODUCES
> Batch
> ```
> 
> следующий Action:
> 
> ```text
> INSPECT
> ```
> 
> produces:
> 
> ```text
> Quality Report
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 64. Acceptance Criteria
> 
> Physical Artifact может иметь:
> 
> ```text
> dimension tolerance
> strength
> electrical performance
> surface quality
> ```
> 
> DONE_IF должен быть measurable.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 65. Failure
> 
> Manufacturing failure:
> 
> ```text
> out_of_tolerance
> machine_failure
> material_defect
> operator_error
> unknown
> ```
> 
> Events сохраняются.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 66. Rework
> 
> Failure не всегда означает scrap.
> 
> Можно:
> 
> ```text
> REWORK
> ```
> 
> как new Action.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 67. Scrap
> 
> Physical Artifact может перейти:
> 
> ```text
> SCRAPPED
> ```
> 
> и materials/cost записываются.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 68. Yield
> 
> Manufacturing Observatory может измерять:
> 
> ```text
> good units / total units
> ```
> 
> по конкретному process.
> 
> Это Evidence для manufacturing capability maturity.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 69. Manufacturing Capability Evidence
> 
> Если supplier изготовил:
> 
> ```text
> 50 successful batches
> ```
> 
> это stronger evidence, чем просто marketing claim.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 70. Production Maturity
> 
> Useful dimensions:
> 
> ```text
> prototype capability
> small-batch capability
> pilot production
> mass production
> ```
> 
> Capability depth здесь отличается от human expertise depth.
> 
> Поэтому нужно:
> 
> ```text
> capability_depth
> ```
> 
> и:
> 
> ```text
> production_maturity
> ```
> 
> раздельно.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 71. Scale-up Gap
> 
> Проект может иметь:
> 
> ```text
> working prototype
> ```
> 
> но:
> 
> ```text
> no scalable manufacturing
> ```
> 
> Это:
> 
> ```text
> Scale-up Gap
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 72. Manufacturing Translation Gap
> 
> Похож на science→engineering gap:
> 
> ```text
> prototype works
> ↓
> manufacturing process missing
> ```
> 
> Opportunity:
> 
> ```text
> process engineering project
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 73. Design for Manufacturing
> 
> System может выявить:
> 
> ```text
> design technically valid
> but expensive/impossible to manufacture
> ```
> 
> Тогда создаётся:
> 
> ```text
> DFM Action
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 74. Procurement Project
> 
> Закупка сложного оборудования сама может стать:
> 
> ```text
> Project
> ```
> 
> с:
> 
> ```text
> requirements
> vendor search
> quotes
> evaluation
> purchase
> installation
> commissioning
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 75. Equipment Acquisition
> 
> Options:
> 
> ```text
> BUY
> LEASE
> RENT
> SHARED_ACCESS
> OUTSOURCE
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 76. Capital Equipment Funding
> 
> Здесь соединяется Funding Observatory.
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> Equipment Gap
> ```
> 
> может быть закрыт:
> 
> ```text
> Grant for equipment
> +
> supplier
> ```
> 
> То есть resolver работает across domains.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 77. Lab Access Funding
> 
> Иногда funding оплачивает:
> 
> ```text
> lab access
> ```
> 
> вместо покупки машины.
> 
> Это может быть гораздо эффективнее.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 78. Shared Lab Opportunity
> 
> Если:
> 
> ```text
> 15 projects
> need same expensive equipment
> ```
> 
> Portfolio Engine может предложить:
> 
> ```text
> shared lab
> ```
> 
> и Funding Observatory ищет:
> 
> ```text
> infrastructure funding
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 79. Capacity Investment
> 
> Counterfactual question:
> 
> ```text
> What happens if we add second machine?
> ```
> 
> Simulation:
> 
> ```text
> queue ↓
> lead time ↓
> more projects become feasible
> ```
> 
> Это direct use of Strategic Simulator.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 80. Marginal Physical Capacity
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> +1 CNC machine
> ```
> 
> может unlock:
> 
> ```text
> 8 projects
> ```
> 
> Но если bottleneck actually:
> 
> ```text
> operator shortage
> ```
> 
> machine purchase почти не поможет.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 81. Physical Bottleneck Analysis
> 
> Distinguish:
> 
> ```text
> machine bottleneck
> operator bottleneck
> material bottleneck
> setup bottleneck
> logistics bottleneck
> certification bottleneck
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 82. Root Bottleneck Example
> 
> Observed:
> 
> ```text
> lab turnaround = 3 weeks
> ```
> 
> Possible assumptions:
> 
> ```text
> not enough equipment
> ```
> 
> Но root analysis may show:
> 
> ```text
> sample preparation is bottleneck
> ```
> 
> Тогда buying another measurement machine не помогает.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 83. Discrete-event simulation
> 
> Именно здесь она становится особенно полезной.
> 
> Entities:
> 
> ```text
> Jobs
> Machines
> Operators
> Buffers
> Materials
> ```
> 
> Events:
> 
> ```text
> job_arrival
> setup_start
> process_start
> process_finish
> failure
> repair
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 84. Manufacturing Simulation
> 
> Можно проверить:
> 
> ```text
> What if demand doubles?
> ```
> 
> или:
> 
> ```text
> What if machine B fails?
> ```
> 
> или:
> 
> ```text
> What if batch size increases?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 85. Digital Factory Twin
> 
> World State + simulation + physical telemetry образуют:
> 
> ```text
> Digital Factory Twin
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 86. Port / City extension
> 
> Тот же model естественно расширяется на:
> 
> ```text
> warehouse
> port
> rail terminal
> market
> hospital
> factory
> ```
> 
> Entities:
> 
> ```text
> people
> vehicles
> goods
> machines
> zones
> ```
> 
> Actions:
> 
> ```text
> move
> load
> unload
> inspect
> store
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 87. Именно здесь ваша идея «MMORPG реального базара/вокзала/порта» становится технически конкретной
> 
> Не видеопоток как основной representation, а:
> 
> ```text
> Camera / Sensor Observation
> ↓
> Entity State Update
> ↓
> Digital Twin
> ↓
> Simulation / Control
> ```
> 
> Визуальный мир отображает уже структурированные сущности и процессы, а не миллионы сырых пикселей. 
> 
> ---
> 
> # 88. Sensor Fusion
> 
> Physical twin может получать observations из:
> 
> ```text
> camera
> RFID
> GPS
> PLC
> IoT sensor
> manual update
> ```
> 
> Все становятся:
> 
> ```text
> Evidence / Events
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 89. Observation uncertainty
> 
> Например camera says:
> 
> ```text
> object at location X
> ```
> 
> confidence:
> 
> ```text
> 0.78
> ```
> 
> Это Claim, а не perfect truth.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 90. State reconciliation
> 
> Если:
> 
> ```text
> RFID says location A
> camera says location B
> ```
> 
> создаётся conflict.
> 
> Resolver может:
> 
> ```text
> request new observation
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 91. Physical World Model
> 
> Теперь World State включает:
> 
> ```text
> identity
> state
> location
> capacity
> availability
> dependencies
> ```
> 
> физических объектов.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 92. Operational World State
> 
> Можно разделить:
> 
> ```text
> Strategic World State
> ```
> 
> и:
> 
> ```text
> Operational World State
> ```
> 
> Первый меняется медленно.
> 
> Второй:
> 
> ```text
> seconds/minutes
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 93. Event frequency
> 
> HN/Research:
> 
> ```text
> days/months
> ```
> 
> Machines:
> 
> ```text
> milliseconds/seconds
> ```
> 
> Поэтому одна БД не обязательно должна обрабатывать весь telemetry raw.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 94. Telemetry layer
> 
> High-frequency sensor data лучше хранить отдельно:
> 
> ```text
> time-series database / stream storage
> ```
> 
> а IIR получает:
> 
> ```text
> meaningful summarized events
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 95. Example
> 
> Raw:
> 
> ```text
> 1000 temperature readings/sec
> ```
> 
> не идут все в Semantic Graph.
> 
> В IIR:
> 
> ```text
> TEMPERATURE_THRESHOLD_EXCEEDED
> ```
> 
> и link на raw telemetry.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 96. Edge Processing
> 
> Для robots/factories часть processing должна происходить:
> 
> ```text
> near device
> ```
> 
> чтобы не отправлять всё в cloud.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 97. Semantic Compression
> 
> Edge node может преобразовать:
> 
> ```text
> raw sensor stream
> ```
> 
> в:
> 
> ```text
> semantic event
> ```
> 
> например:
> 
> ```text
> object slipping
> ```
> 
> Это снова связано с вашей идеей M2M semantic state transfer: передавать не весь поток, а компактное смысловое состояние, когда это допустимо для задачи. 
> 
> ---
> 
> # 98. Physical Semantic Event
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```yaml
> event:
>   type: OBJECT_SLIP_DETECTED
>   target: object_17
>   confidence: 0.94
> ```
> 
> Вместо передачи full tactile waveform всем downstream agents.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 99. Raw data still retained when needed
> 
> Semantic compression не должна уничтожать provenance.
> 
> Event может ссылаться:
> 
> ```text
> DERIVED_FROM
> raw telemetry segment
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 100. Real-time Agent
> 
> Теперь AI agent может подписаться:
> 
> ```text
> OBJECT_SLIP_DETECTED
> ```
> 
> и предложить:
> 
> ```text
> adjust grip
> ```
> 
> Но safety controller может быть deterministic и локальным.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 101. AI vs control loop
> 
> Очень важно:
> 
> ```text
> millisecond motor control
> ```
> 
> не должно зависеть от LLM.
> 
> LLM/agent layer:
> 
> ```text
> planning
> diagnostics
> adaptation
> ```
> 
> Low-level control:
> 
> ```text
> real-time controller
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 102. Hierarchy
> 
> ```text
> Strategic Planner
> ↓
> Task Planner
> ↓
> Robot Skill
> ↓
> Real-time Controller
> ↓
> Actuator
> ```
> 
> Это та же многоуровневая compilation chain.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 103. Robot Skill as Capability
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> pick_object
> place_object
> inspect_surface
> ```
> 
> Robot Resource:
> 
> ```text
> PROVIDES
> pick_object
> ```
> 
> при определённых constraints.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 104. Skill Contract
> 
> ```yaml
> capability:
>   pick_object
> 
>   input:
>     object_pose
> 
>   output:
>     object_grasped
> 
>   constraints:
>     max_weight: 5 kg
> 
>   verification:
>     grip_confirmed: true
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 105. Physical Capability Composition
> 
> Task:
> 
> ```text
> assemble device
> ```
> 
> может require:
> 
> ```text
> pick
> position
> screw
> inspect
> ```
> 
> разные robots/tools/humans can provide.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 106. Human + Robot Team
> 
> Team Builder теперь может включать:
> 
> ```text
> Human
> Robot
> Machine
> AI Agent
> ```
> 
> в одной execution configuration.
> 
> Но roles и safety constraints различаются.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 107. Hybrid Work Cell
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> Robot:
> repetitive placement
> 
> Human:
> fine assembly
> 
> AI:
> visual inspection assistance
> 
> Machine:
> test
> ```
> 
> Это dynamic capability cell уже в физическом мире.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 108. Work Cell Compiler
> 
> Input:
> 
> ```text
> manufacturing task
> ```
> 
> Output:
> 
> ```text
> required capabilities
> resources
> sequence
> safety constraints
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 109. Digital Work Cell
> 
> Можно сначала собрать:
> 
> ```text
> simulation work cell
> ```
> 
> и проверить throughput.
> 
> После approval:
> 
> ```text
> physical work cell
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 110. Manufacturing Opportunity Engine
> 
> Он может обнаруживать:
> 
> ```text
> repeated outsourced operation
> ```
> 
> например:
> 
> ```text
> laser cutting
> ```
> 
> across many projects.
> 
> Hypothesis:
> 
> ```text
> internal shared laser cutting capability
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 111. Buy-vs-Outsource Counterfactual
> 
> Scenario A:
> 
> ```text
> continue outsource
> ```
> 
> Scenario B:
> 
> ```text
> buy machine
> ```
> 
> Simulator сравнивает:
> 
> ```text
> capital cost
> queue
> utilization
> maintenance
> operator demand
> lead time
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 112. Utilization
> 
> Machine utilization:
> 
> ```text
> actual busy time / available time
> ```
> 
> может быть observed.
> 
> Но:
> 
> ```text
> 100% utilization
> ```
> 
> не обязательно desirable, потому что queues explode.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 113. Queue-aware planning
> 
> Portfolio Engine should consider:
> 
> ```text
> capacity buffer
> ```
> 
> for shared infrastructure.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 114. Maintenance
> 
> Physical Resource periodically requires:
> 
> ```text
> maintenance
> inspection
> calibration
> ```
> 
> These are Actions.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 115. Preventive Maintenance
> 
> Based on:
> 
> ```text
> hours
> cycles
> calendar
> condition
> ```
> 
> Runtime can schedule Action.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 116. Predictive Maintenance
> 
> Later:
> 
> ```text
> telemetry
> → failure risk signal
> ```
> 
> But derived prediction remains:
> 
> ```text
> INFERENCE/HYPOTHESIS
> ```
> 
> unless actual failure occurs.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 117. Spare Parts
> 
> Equipment availability also depends on:
> 
> ```text
> spares
> ```
> 
> Spare part becomes inventory Resource.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 118. Maintenance capability
> 
> Requires:
> 
> ```text
> technician
> parts
> tools
> procedure
> ```
> 
> Again same Resource Composition logic.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 119. Physical Evidence
> 
> Examples:
> 
> ```text
> measurement report
> calibration certificate
> photo
> sensor log
> inspection report
> ```
> 
> All are Evidence/Artifacts.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 120. Traceability
> 
> For regulated/high-quality manufacturing:
> 
> ```text
> Material batch
> ↓
> Production action
> ↓
> Machine
> ↓
> Operator
> ↓
> Inspection
> ↓
> Finished unit
> ```
> 
> can be reconstructed.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 121. Serial-level provenance
> 
> For expensive prototypes:
> 
> ```text
> Device #17
> ```
> 
> can know exactly:
> 
> ```text
> which components
> which firmware
> which process
> which tests
> ```
> 
> This is extremely powerful for research and debugging.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 122. Experiment ↔ Manufacturing convergence
> 
> Research experiment and manufacturing test become structurally similar:
> 
> ```text
> Input
> ↓
> Action
> ↓
> Measurement
> ↓
> Evidence
> ↓
> Decision
> ```
> 
> This validates the shared IIR approach.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 123. Lab Experiment
> 
> ```text
> Question
> ↓
> Sample
> ↓
> Instrument
> ↓
> Measurement
> ↓
> Dataset
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 124. Production Test
> 
> ```text
> Product
> ↓
> Instrument
> ↓
> Measurement
> ↓
> Pass/Fail
> ```
> 
> Same primitives.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 125. Physical Infrastructure Dashboard
> 
> Minimum screens:
> 
> ```text
> Facility Explorer
> Equipment Detail
> Capacity View
> Manufacturing Resolver
> Digital Twin View
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 126. Facility Explorer
> 
> Shows:
> 
> ```text
> labs
> machines
> capabilities
> availability
> locations
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 127. Equipment Detail
> 
> Shows:
> 
> ```text
> capabilities
> constraints
> calendar
> maintenance
> calibration
> projects using it
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 128. Capacity View
> 
> Shows:
> 
> ```text
> available hours
> reserved hours
> queues
> bottlenecks
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 129. Manufacturing Resolver
> 
> For a Project:
> 
> ```text
> required physical operations
> candidate providers
> cost
> lead time
> constraints
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 130. Digital Twin View
> 
> Shows:
> 
> ```text
> current state
> recent events
> telemetry summary
> active tasks
> maintenance state
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 131. Physical API
> 
> Minimum:
> 
> ```text
> GET /facilities
> GET /equipment
> GET /equipment/{id}/availability
> POST /physical/resolve
> POST /reservations
> GET /capacity
> POST /simulation/run
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 132. Reservation approval
> 
> Booking expensive/shared resource may require:
> 
> ```text
> Decision
> ```
> 
> before reservation becomes active.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 133. Physical Resource Lock
> 
> Analog of project.lock:
> 
> ```yaml
> bindings:
>   environmental_test:
>     provider: lab_4
>     equipment: chamber_2
>     slot: ...
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 134. Physical Execution Lock
> 
> Before starting test:
> 
> ```text
> sample
> procedure
> equipment
> operator
> time slot
> ```
> 
> must all be pinned.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 135. Experiment reproducibility
> 
> A physical experiment should be reproducible from:
> 
> ```text
> procedure version
> equipment
> calibration
> sample
> software
> environment
> ```
> 
> This can all be represented in World State.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 136. Research + Physical integration
> 
> Now Research Observatory can move from:
> 
> ```text
> Paper
> ```
> 
> to:
> 
> ```text
> real experiment
> ```
> 
> without leaving the same architecture.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 137. Funding + Physical integration
> 
> Funding call can fund:
> 
> ```text
> equipment
> facility
> pilot line
> ```
> 
> World State already knows:
> 
> ```text
> which physical bottleneck blocks which projects
> ```
> 
> So funding search becomes strategic.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 138. GitHub + Physical integration
> 
> Software repo may control:
> 
> ```text
> robot
> sensor
> machine
> ```
> 
> Now repository capability and physical capability connect.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 139. HN + Physical integration
> 
> Talent demand can include:
> 
> ```text
> robotics
> manufacturing
> lab operations
> ```
> 
> and Candidate capabilities can match Physical Projects.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 140. Full Capability Supply Graph
> 
> Now providers include:
> 
> ```text
> Human
> Team
> AI Agent
> Software
> Repository
> Service
> Research Method
> Lab
> Equipment
> Manufacturer
> Funding Resource
> ```
> 
> This is essentially the complete resource model originally envisioned for the virtual technopark.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 141. Full Gap Taxonomy
> 
> Now gap can be:
> 
> ```text
> Talent Gap
> Technology Gap
> Knowledge Gap
> Data Gap
> Funding Gap
> Lab Gap
> Equipment Gap
> Material Gap
> Manufacturing Gap
> Logistics Gap
> Governance Gap
> ```
> 
> But semantically they are all:
> 
> ```text
> Requirement not yet satisfied
> ```
> 
> That is one of the strongest architectural simplifications in the whole design.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 142. Universal Resolution Loop
> 
> ```text
> Requirement
> ↓
> Is it satisfied?
>    │
>    ├── YES → continue
>    │
>    ├── UNKNOWN → gather evidence
>    │
>    └── NO → create Gap
>                  ↓
>             search providers
>                  ↓
>             resolution options
>                  ↓
>             validate
>                  ↓
>             decision
>                  ↓
>              binding
> ```
> 
> This same loop works for almost every resource class.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 143. Physical World + MMORPG Interface
> 
> Now the 3D layer can finally become genuinely useful.
> 
> Not merely:
> 
> ```text
> a decorative virtual city
> ```
> 
> but:
> 
> ```text
> live representation of:
> facilities
> machines
> robots
> projects
> goods
> queues
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 144. Strategic level
> 
> Zoomed out:
> 
> ```text
> city / technopark
> ```
> 
> shows:
> 
> ```text
> labs
> organizations
> programs
> resource flows
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 145. Operational level
> 
> Zoom in:
> 
> ```text
> factory
> ```
> 
> shows:
> 
> ```text
> machines
> work cells
> queues
> robots
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 146. Equipment level
> 
> Zoom further:
> 
> ```text
> machine state
> current job
> maintenance
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 147. Same entity IDs at all levels
> 
> Crucially:
> 
> ```text
> Machine #42
> ```
> 
> in 3D is the same entity as:
> 
> ```text
> resource_42
> ```
> 
> in PostgreSQL.
> 
> No duplicate game-world database.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 148. Game mechanics become operations
> 
> For example:
> 
> ```text
> drag Job to Machine
> ```
>

> ASSIGN Action
> ```
> 
> Runtime checks:
> 
> ```text
> capability
> capacity
> safety
> booking
> ```
> 
> Then executes or rejects.
>

> 
> # 149. Missions become Projects
> 
> A "mission":
>

> is actual Project IR.

> validated capability
> ```

> # 151. Resources become actual resources
>

> machine time
> lab access
> compute
> materials
> funding
> people

> 
> The game-like world therefore becomes a **serious operational interface** rather than only gamification.

> # 152. Next architectural transition

> After this module, all major resource classes are represented:

> People

> Physical infrastructure

> 
> The next logical layer is no longer another Observatory.
> 
> It is:

> # **Universal Capability Market & Resource Exchange v0.1**
> 
> Not necessarily a monetary marketplace.
> 
> Rather a unified system where:

> 
> and the system continuously resolves:

> 
> across:

> humans
> AI
> software
> labs
> equipment
> organizations
> funding

>

> # 153. Universal Capability Market
> 
> Core abstraction:
> 
> ```text
> DEMAND SIDE
> 
> Project / Task / Program
> REQUIRES
> Capability
> ```
> 
> versus:

> SUPPLY SIDE
> 
> Resource
> PROVIDES
> Capability

> It first reasons in capability space.

> integration

> deadline

> Thus one universal marketplace can have specialized resolvers.

# chatgpt response

> **Document: Universal Capability Market & Resource Exchange v0.1**
> 
> # Universal Capability Market & Resource Exchange v0.1
> 
> ## 1. Главный переход
> 
> До этого система уже умеет:
> 
> ```text
> наблюдать мир
> ↓
> извлекать capabilities
> ↓
> видеть gaps
> ↓
> находить resources
> ↓
> собирать project configurations
> ```
> 
> Теперь нужен слой, который делает это **не эпизодически по запросу**, а постоянно.
> 
> То есть:
> 
> ```text
> Projects continuously publish Demand
> Resources continuously publish Supply
> ↓
> Capability Market
> ↓
> matching / allocation / reallocation
> ```
> 
> Это уже не обычный marketplace.
> 
> Это **рынок возможностей и дефицитов**.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2. Capability Market ≠ рынок вакансий
> 
> Обычный job market:
> 
> ```text
> Employer
> ↔
> Person
> ```
> 
> Здесь:
> 
> ```text
> Project / Task / Program
> ↔
> Capability
> ↔
> Resource
> ```
> 
> А Resource может быть:
> 
> ```text
> Person
> Team
> AI Agent
> Software
> Repository
> Service
> Research Method
> Dataset
> Lab
> Equipment
> Organization
> Funding
> ```
> 
> Поэтому рынок становится универсальным.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3. Fundamental abstraction
> 
> Спрос:
> 
> ```text
> DEMAND:
> Entity REQUIRES Capability
> ```
> 
> Предложение:
> 
> ```text
> SUPPLY:
> Resource PROVIDES Capability
> ```
> 
> Matching:
> 
> ```text
> REQUIREMENT
> ↔
> PROVIDER
> ```
> 
> Это центральная формула всей системы.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 4. Demand Order
> 
> Можно ввести application-level объект:
> 
> ```yaml
> demand_order:
>   id: demand_001
>   requester: project_17
>   capability: secure_agent_execution
> 
>   target_depth: production
> 
>   quantity: 1
> 
>   constraints:
>     - remote_allowed
>     - self_hosted_required
> 
>   needed_by: 2026-11-01
> 
>   status: OPEN
> ```
> 
> Это не новый IIR Core type.
> 
> Он компилируется в:
> 
> ```text
> Project REQUIRES Capability
> +
> Constraints
> +
> Temporal Context
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 5. Supply Offer
> 
> Аналогично:
> 
> ```yaml
> supply_offer:
>   id: supply_001
> 
>   provider: resource_44
>   capability: secure_agent_execution
> 
>   depth: production
> 
>   availability:
>     from: ...
>     capacity: ...
> 
>   conditions:
>     ...
> ```
> 
> В IIR:
> 
> ```text
> Resource PROVIDES Capability
> +
> Availability Claims
> +
> Constraints
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 6. Почему нужны Orders/Offers как application objects
> 
> Хотя semantic truth уже хранится в Claims, exchange layer должен видеть:
> 
> ```text
> кто сейчас ищет
> кто сейчас предлагает
> в каком объёме
> на какой срок
> ```
> 
> То есть:
> 
> ```text
> Capability Registry
> ```
> 
> говорит:
> 
> > Кто вообще умеет?
> 
> А:
> 
> ```text
> Capability Market
> ```
> 
> говорит:
> 
> > Кто сейчас доступен и кому это сейчас нужно?
> 
> ---
> 
> # 7. Market State
> 
> Минимально:
> 
> ```text
> Open Demand
> Open Supply
> Potential Matches
> Committed Bindings
> Waitlists
> Expired Offers
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 8. Demand status
> 
> Freeze application enum:
> 
> ```text
> DRAFT
> OPEN
> MATCHING
> NEGOTIATING
> BOUND
> PARTIALLY_FILLED
> FULFILLED
> CANCELLED
> EXPIRED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 9. Supply status
> 
> ```text
> AVAILABLE
> PARTIALLY_ALLOCATED
> ALLOCATED
> UNAVAILABLE
> EXPIRED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 10. Capacity matters
> 
> Один Resource может предоставить capability нескольким projects.
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> Person A:
> 20 h/week
> ```
> 
> или:
> 
> ```text
> GPU cluster:
> 500 GPU-hours/week
> ```
> 
> или:
> 
> ```text
> Lab:
> 2 experiment slots/day
> ```
> 
> Поэтому supply:
> 
> ```text
> capability
> +
> capacity
> +
> time
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 11. Time-dependent Market
> 
> Вместо статического:
> 
> ```text
> Resource available = YES
> ```
> 
> нужно:
> 
> ```text
> Resource available
> from t1 to t2
> with capacity C
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 12. Capacity Reservation
> 
> После tentative match:
> 
> ```text
> reserve
> ```
> 
> часть capacity.
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> Person A:
> 20 h/week
> 
> Project X:
> reserve 8
> 
> remaining:
> 12
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 13. Reservation ≠ final assignment
> 
> Полезно иметь:
> 
> ```text
> PROPOSED
> HELD
> CONFIRMED
> RELEASED
> ```
> 
> Это уменьшает race conditions.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14. Market Event
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> DEMAND_OPENED
> SUPPLY_OPENED
> MATCH_PROPOSED
> CAPACITY_RESERVED
> BINDING_CONFIRMED
> BINDING_RELEASED
> DEMAND_FULFILLED
> ```
> 
> Все остаются Events.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15. Capability Unit
> 
> Не вся capability измеряется одинаково.
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> security review
> ```
> 
> может быть:
> 
> ```text
> 1 review
> ```
> 
> Но:
> 
> ```text
> software engineering
> ```
> 
> может быть:
> 
> ```text
> hours/week
> ```
> 
> А:
> 
> ```text
> GPU inference
> ```
> 
> может быть:
> 
> ```text
> GPU-hours
> ```
> 
> Поэтому capability offer должен поддерживать:
> 
> ```text
> unit
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16. Fungible vs Non-Fungible Capability
> 
> Некоторые resources почти взаимозаменяемы:
> 
> ```text
> 100 GPU-hours
> ```
> 
> Другие нет:
> 
> ```text
> specific expert
> specific microscope
> specific proprietary dataset
> ```
> 
> Это важное различие.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17. Fungibility
> 
> Можно хранить:
> 
> ```text
> HIGH
> MEDIUM
> LOW
> ```
> 
> на уровне market semantics.
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> cloud compute = high
> senior domain expert = low
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18. Matching stages
> 
> Universal Market лучше разделить на пять этапов:
> 
> ```text
> 1. Retrieval
> 2. Feasibility
> 3. Compatibility
> 4. Composition
> 5. Commitment
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19. Retrieval
> 
> Найти:
> 
> ```text
> all plausible providers
> ```
> 
> по capability:
> 
> ```text
> exact
> alias
> taxonomy
> semantic similarity
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 20. Feasibility
> 
> Проверить HARD constraints:
> 
> ```text
> availability
> location
> license
> capacity
> eligibility
> deadline
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 21. Compatibility
> 
> Проверить:
> 
> ```text
> depth
> context
> integration effort
> quality evidence
> work style
> technology fit
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22. Composition
> 
> Если один provider недостаточен:
> 
> ```text
> compose multiple resources
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 23. Commitment
> 
> После:
> 
> ```text
> human / organization / policy approval
> ```
> 
> создаётся Binding.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24. Binding
> 
> ```yaml
> binding:
>   demand_id: demand_001
>   provider_id: resource_44
> 
>   quantity: 8
>   unit: hour/week
> 
>   valid_from: ...
>   valid_to: ...
> 
>   state: CONFIRMED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25. Binding as project.lock component
> 
> То есть:
> 
> ```text
> project.lock
> ```
> 
> может быть набором confirmed capability bindings.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26. Market Resolver
> 
> Pipeline:
> 
> ```text
> Demand
> ↓
> Candidate Providers
> ↓
> Hard Filters
> ↓
> Evidence
> ↓
> Capacity Check
> ↓
> Composite Alternatives
> ↓
> Binding Proposal
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27. Supply fragmentation
> 
> Например Project требует:
> 
> ```text
> 40 h/week backend engineering
> ```
> 
> Но market has:
> 
> ```text
> Person A: 20
> Person B: 10
> AI Agent C: equivalent bounded contribution
> ```
> 
> System may build composite supply.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28. But capacity is not always additive
> 
> Two junior engineers:
> 
> ```text
> 10h + 10h
> ```
> 
> не всегда equivalent to:
> 
> ```text
> 20h senior expertise
> ```
> 
> Поэтому composition must respect:
> 
> ```text
> capability depth
> coordination cost
> role structure
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29. Complementarity
> 
> Некоторые resources усиливают друг друга.
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> AI coding agent
> +
> senior reviewer
> ```
> 
> может outperform each alone for certain tasks.
> 
> То есть market should support:
> 
> ```text
> COMPLEMENTARY resources
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 30. Substitutability vs Complementarity
> 
> Graph relations:
> 
> ```text
> ALTERNATIVE_TO
> COMPLEMENTS
> REQUIRES_TOGETHER
> ```
> 
> можно держать в library ontology.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 31. Bundle Offer
> 
> Можно создать:
> 
> ```text
> bundle:
>   person_A
>   repo_B
>   AI_agent_C
> ```
> 
> provides:
> 
> ```text
> secure_browser_runtime
> ```
> 
> Это derived composite Resource.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 32. Team as Composite Resource
> 
> `TEAM` уже есть как Resource.
> 
> Он может иметь:
> 
> ```text
> member resources
> aggregate capabilities
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 33. Dynamic Team
> 
> Market может создать:
> 
> ```text
> temporary Team Hypothesis
> ```
> 
> для одного project.
> 
> После approval:
> 
> ```text
> Team Resource
> ```
> 
> становится committed.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 34. Market does not need money
> 
> Очень важно.
> 
> Exchange can optimize:
> 
> ```text
> capability allocation
> ```
> 
> без financial price.
> 
> Например внутри university or technopark:
> 
> ```text
> machine time
> expert hours
> lab slots
> ```
> 
> can be allocated by priority, quota or policy.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 35. Allocation Modes
> 
> Useful application enum:
> 
> ```text
> MARKET_PRICE
> FIXED_PRICE
> INTERNAL_QUOTA
> PRIORITY_ALLOCATION
> GRANT_FUNDED
> BARTER
> VOLUNTEER
> SHARED_POOL
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 36. Internal Technopark Market
> 
> Пример:
> 
> ```text
> 10 projects
> 3 security experts
> 2 labs
> limited compute
> ```
> 
> Market resolves:
> 
> ```text
> who gets what when
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 37. Priority constraints
> 
> Project can have:
> 
> ```text
> critical
> normal
> exploratory
> ```
> 
> But system should not use priority as universal human-worth score.
> 
> Это только resource allocation priority.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 38. Scarcity
> 
> Capability scarcity can be derived from:
> 
> ```text
> demand
> supply
> availability
> substitutability
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 39. Scarcity ≠ value
> 
> Редкая capability:
> 
> ```text
> not necessarily important
> ```
> 
> and important capability:
> 
> ```text
> not necessarily rare
> ```
> 
> Need separate dimensions.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 40. Scarcity Vector
> 
> ```text
> Demand volume
> Available supply
> Time-to-capability
> Substitution options
> Geographic constraints
> Depth requirements
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 41. Market Signal
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> agent security
> ```
> 
> may show:
> 
> ```text
> high demand
> low supply
> few substitutes
> ```
> 
> This becomes:
> 
> ```text
> Capability Shortage Signal
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 42. Shortage can trigger interventions
> 
> Not only:
> 
> ```text
> raise price
> ```
> 
> but:
> 
> ```text
> TRAIN
> AUTOMATE
> BUILD TOOL
> STANDARDIZE
> CREATE SHARED TEAM
> ```
> 
> This is a major difference from ordinary markets.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 43. Market as intervention engine
> 
> Traditional market:
> 
> ```text
> scarcity → price
> ```
> 
> Innovation OS:
> 
> ```text
> scarcity
> → diagnose cause
> → create new capability supply
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 44. Training Opportunity
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> 20 projects need capability X
> 2 experts available
> ```
> 
> Opportunity Engine may create:
> 
> ```text
> Training Program
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 45. Tooling Opportunity
> 
> If shortage is because work is repetitive:
> 
> ```text
> automation project
> ```
> 
> may create new supply.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 46. Shared Service Opportunity
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> security reviews repeated
> ```
> 
> Create:
> 
> ```text
> Shared Security Office
> ```
> 
> as Resource.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 47. Standardization Opportunity
> 
> If every project needs custom adapters:
> 
> ```text
> common interface
> ```
> 
> may increase supply efficiency.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 48. Market creates its own supply
> 
> This is important.
> 
> The system is not only allocating fixed resources.
> 
> It can generate projects that increase future supply.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 49. Supply Creation Loop
> 
> ```text
> Scarcity
> ↓
> Opportunity
> ↓
> Project
> ↓
> New Resource / Capability
> ↓
> Supply increases
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 50. Demand Creation Loop
> 
> New capability may also create new demand:
> 
> ```text
> New technology
> ↓
> new feasible projects
> ↓
> new capability demand
> ```
> 
> So market is dynamic.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 51. Capability Price
> 
> If financial market enabled, one can track:
> 
> ```text
> hourly rate
> license cost
> service cost
> machine-hour
> ```
> 
> But avoid universal normalization.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 52. Capability Cost
> 
> Better concept:
> 
> ```text
> Cost to obtain capability
> ```
> 
> rather than:
> 
> ```text
> price of capability
> ```
> 
> because acquisition may include:
> 
> ```text
> integration
> training
> maintenance
> review
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 53. TCC inside Market
> 
> For each option:
> 
> ```text
> TCC
> TTC
> risk
> control
> ```
> 
> already developed earlier.
> 
> Market uses them continuously.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 54. Opportunity Cost
> 
> Allocating Resource A to Project X means it may be unavailable to Y.
> 
> This introduces:
> 
> ```text
> opportunity cost
> ```
> 
> at portfolio level.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 55. Example
> 
> One security expert can support:
> 
> ```text
> Project A
> or
> Projects B+C
> ```
> 
> Portfolio optimizer can expose alternatives.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 56. Do not auto-optimize everything
> 
> Human strategy remains above market.
> 
> Market can show:
> 
> ```text
> allocation scenarios
> ```
> 
> not silently choose strategic priorities.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 57. Market + Portfolio Intelligence
> 
> Architecture:
> 
> ```text
> Portfolio priorities
> ↓
> Allocation policies
> ↓
> Capability Market
> ↓
> Bindings
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 58. Market + Runtime
> 
> Runtime consumes confirmed bindings:
> 
> ```text
> Task READY
> ↓
> binding available
> ↓
> execute
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 59. Market + Event Bus
> 
> When:
> 
> ```text
> RESOURCE_UNAVAILABLE
> ```
> 
> market receives event.
> 
> Affected bindings:
> 
> ```text
> DEGRADED
> ```
> 
> Demand reopens.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 60. Continuous Reallocation
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> Person A unavailable
> ↓
> 3 tasks lose provider
> ↓
> market finds substitutes
> ↓
> proposes rebinding
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 61. Hot Standby
> 
> Critical capability may have:
> 
> ```text
> primary provider
> backup provider
> ```
> 
> Binding model should support both.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 62. Redundant Supply
> 
> For critical project:
> 
> ```text
> security approval
> ```
> 
> can require:
> 
> ```text
> 2 independent reviewers
> ```
> 
> This is deliberate redundancy.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 63. Reliability-Aware Market
> 
> Provider has capability-specific operational metrics:
> 
> ```text
> availability
> completion rate
> latency
> verification pass rate
> ```
> 
> for AI/tools/services.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 64. Human performance caution
> 
> For people, avoid reductive global rankings.
> 
> Use task-specific evidence:
> 
> ```text
> public work
> documented experience
> explicit availability
> ```
> 
> rather than hidden universal worker scores.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 65. Resource Reputation should be contextual
> 
> For Software:
> 
> ```text
> maintenance history
> ```
> 
> For Lab:
> 
> ```text
> calibration / turnaround
> ```
> 
> For AI Agent:
> 
> ```text
> verification pass rate
> ```
> 
> Different resource classes need different evidence.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 66. Market Explainability
> 
> Every match should answer:
> 
> ```text
> Why was this provider retrieved?
> Why is it feasible?
> What is unknown?
> What blocks it?
> Why is composition needed?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 67. No black-box 92%
> 
> The UI should show:
> 
> ```text
> coverage
> constraints
> evidence
> capacity
> cost
> time
> unknowns
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 68. Market Query
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> Find operational providers for:
> secure_browser_execution
> 
> needed:
> within 4 weeks
> 
> constraints:
> self-hosted
> EU-compatible
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 69. Query result
> 
> ```text
> Option A:
> Repo + internal engineer
> 
> Option B:
> Commercial service
> 
> Option C:
> External specialist + OSS
> 
> Option D:
> Build internally
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 70. Bidirectional Market
> 
> Not only:
> 
> ```text
> Demand → Supply
> ```
> 
> also:
> 
> ```text
> Supply → Demand
> ```
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> new GPU cluster available
> ```
> 
> System asks:
> 
> ```text
> which blocked projects can now use it?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 71. New Talent Event
> 
> ```text
> new specialist discovered
> ```
> 
> → scan relevant gaps.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 72. New Repo Event
> 
> ```text
> new repo discovered
> ```
> 
> → scan technology gaps.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 73. New Grant Event
> 
> ```text
> new funding resource
> ```
> 
> → scan funding gaps.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 74. New Lab Event
> 
> ```text
> new facility capacity
> ```
> 
> → scan physical gaps.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 75. Universal Reverse Index
> 
> Need:
> 
> ```text
> Capability → Open Demand
> Capability → Available Supply
> ```
> 
> This is central index.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 76. Demand Graph
> 
> ```text
> Capability
> ↓
> Projects requiring it
> ↓
> Tasks requiring it
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 77. Supply Graph
> 
> ```text
> Capability
> ↓
> Resources providing it
> ↓
> capacity / evidence / constraints
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 78. Market Snapshot
> 
> At any time:
> 
> ```text
> Capability X
> 
> Demand:
> 14 projects
> 
> Supply:
> 5 resources
> 
> Committed:
> 3
> 
> Available:
> 2
> 
> Unknown:
> 4 possible resources
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 79. Market Forecast
> 
> Using planned projects:
> 
> ```text
> future demand
> ```
> 
> can be estimated.
> 
> But label as:
> 
> ```text
> planned/forecast demand
> ```
> 
> not current demand.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 80. Forward Capacity Planning
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> next quarter:
> 3 projects will require photonics testing
> ```
> 
> System can warn:
> 
> ```text
> lab capacity insufficient
> ```
> 
> before projects block.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 81. Pre-booking
> 
> Physical resources can be reserved ahead.
> 
> But reservation policy must avoid:
> 
> ```text
> capacity hoarding
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 82. Reservation Policy
> 
> Could use:
> 
> ```text
> expiry
> deposit
> priority
> maximum hold time
> ```
> 
> depending on domain.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 83. Market Deadlock
> 
> Possible situation:
> 
> ```text
> Project A waits Resource B
> Project B waits Resource A
> ```
> 
> or resource dependency cycle.
> 
> Need:
> 
> ```text
> deadlock detector
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 84. Capability Dependency Deadlock
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> Lab requires certified operator
> Operator training requires lab access
> ```
> 
> Potential cycle.
> 
> System should detect and suggest bridge.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 85. Bridge Resource
> 
> Temporary:
> 
> ```text
> external service
> ```
> 
> can break deadlock.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 86. Market Liquidity
> 
> Interesting concept.
> 
> A capability is liquid if:
> 
> ```text
> many interchangeable providers
> quick acquisition
> low switching cost
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 87. Illiquid Capability
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> rare scientific instrument
> specific legal authority
> unique domain expert
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 88. Liquidity matters for risk
> 
> Projects depending on illiquid capabilities need:
> 
> ```text
> earlier planning
> redundancy
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 89. Capability Liquidity Vector
> 
> ```text
> provider count
> substitutability
> time-to-acquire
> switching cost
> geographic restrictions
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 90. Bottleneck Market
> 
> Capabilities with:
> 
> ```text
> high demand
> low liquidity
> high strategic importance
> ```
> 
> become candidates for strategic investment.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 91. Capability Development Market
> 
> Could publish:
> 
> ```text
> Demand:
> need capability X
> ```
> 
> and allow providers to respond:
> 
> ```text
> we can develop it
> ```
> 
> So supply need not already exist.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 92. Build Offer
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> Organization A:
> can build custom sensor in 8 weeks
> ```
> 
> This is:
> 
> ```text
> future supply
> ```
> 
> conditional on project.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 93. Conditional Supply
> 
> Supply can be:
> 
> ```text
> AVAILABLE_NOW
> BUILD_TO_ORDER
> TRAINABLE
> RESEARCH_REQUIRED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 94. Market therefore spans current and potential supply
> 
> ```text
> Current Supply
> Potential Supply
> Frontier Supply
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 95. Capability Maturity Dimension
> 
> Potential provider may offer:
> 
> ```text
> PROTOTYPE
> ```
> 
> while project requires:
> 
> ```text
> PRODUCTION
> ```
> 
> This creates:
> 
> ```text
> maturity gap
> ```
> 
> not total absence.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 96. Upgrade Path
> 
> System can propose:
> 
> ```text
> prototype provider
> +
> hardening project
> ```
> 
> instead of rejecting completely.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 97. Capability Upgrade Contract
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> Current:
> WORKING
> 
> Target:
> PRODUCTION
> 
> Needed:
> tests
> security
> documentation
> operations
> ```
> 
> This itself becomes Project.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 98. Market + Project Generator
> 
> Gap can resolve in two ways:
> 
> ```text
> find existing supply
> ```
> 
> or:
> 
> ```text
> create project to produce supply
> ```
> 
> This is extremely important.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 99. Make-or-Match decision
> 
> ```text
> MATCH:
> existing provider
> 
> MAKE:
> create new provider/capability
> ```
> 
> The system compares both.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 100. Example
> 
> Need:
> 
> ```text
> robot tactile dataset
> ```
> 
> No dataset exists.
> 
> Options:
> 
> ```text
> buy dataset
> partner
> generate dataset
> simulate dataset
> ```
> 
> If no provider:
> 
> ```text
> Dataset Creation Project
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 101. Resource Exchange Interface
> 
> For human user:
> 
> ```text
> Open Demands
> Available Supply
> Suggested Matches
> Composite Solutions
> Unresolved Gaps
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 102. Demand Detail
> 
> Shows:
> 
> ```text
> requester
> capability
> depth
> deadline
> constraints
> current coverage
> candidate providers
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 103. Supply Detail
> 
> Shows:
> 
> ```text
> resource
> capabilities
> capacity
> availability
> conditions
> open demand matches
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 104. Market Map
> 
> 2D graph:
> 
> ```text
> Demand nodes
> ↔
> Capability nodes
> ↔
> Supply nodes
> ```
> 
> Coloring can indicate state, but UI detail is later.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 105. 3D market metaphor
> 
> In MMORPG-like interface:
> 
> ```text
> Projects = demand hubs
> Resources = active units
> Capabilities = routes/ports
> ```
> 
> But actual matching still happens in semantic graph.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 106. Capability Exchange as internal operating system
> 
> This layer begins to resemble:
> 
> ```text
> scheduler + market + ERP + matching engine
> ```
> 
> for heterogeneous resources.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 107. Market Clearing
> 
> In simple case:
> 
> ```text
> many demands
> many supplies
> limited capacity
> ```
> 
> we need allocation algorithm.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 108. Allocation Problem
> 
> Inputs:
> 
> ```text
> Demand_i
> Supply_j
> Compatibility_ij
> Capacity_j
> Constraints
> Priorities
> ```
> 
> Output:
> 
> ```text
> Bindings
> Unfilled Demand
> Unused Capacity
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 109. MVP algorithm
> 
> Do not start with complex auction theory.
> 
> First:
> 
> ```text
> hard filter
> ↓
> weighted bipartite matching
> ↓
> capacity constraints
> ```
> 
> or greedy allocation.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 110. Later optimization
> 
> Could use:
> 
> ```text
> linear programming
> mixed integer programming
> min-cost flow
> constraint programming
> ```
> 
> depending on case.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 111. Market Clearing Objective
> 
> Do not define one universal objective.
> 
> Possible scenarios:
> 
> ```text
> maximize critical capability coverage
> minimize unmet MUST requirements
> minimize cost
> minimize delay
> maximize resilience
> ```
> 
> Human/policy selects scenario.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 112. Multi-objective allocation
> 
> Results can be Pareto configurations.
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> Scenario A:
> fastest
> 
> Scenario B:
> lowest cost
> 
> Scenario C:
> highest resilience
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 113. Auctions optional, not foundational
> 
> For external open marketplace, auction mechanisms may later be useful.
> 
> But internal technopark does not need auctions initially.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 114. Negotiation
> 
> Some supply requires:
> 
> ```text
> rate negotiation
> scope negotiation
> availability negotiation
> ```
> 
> This is separate from matching.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 115. Negotiation State
> 
> ```text
> MATCHED
> CONTACT_PENDING
> NEGOTIATING
> AGREED
> DECLINED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 116. No automatic outreach by default
> 
> System can identify match.
> 
> External communication remains separate approved Action.
> 
> This continues the same boundary used for HN.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 117. Contract Generation
> 
> After agreement:
> 
> ```text
> binding
> ```
> 
> may require legal/administrative Artifact:
> 
> ```text
> employment contract
> service agreement
> lab booking
> grant agreement
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 118. Contract as operational binding evidence
> 
> Project lock can reference:
> 
> ```text
> Decision
> +
> Contract Artifact
> ```
> 
> for confirmed provider.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 119. Resource Exchange and ERP
> 
> Once binding exists:
> 
> ```text
> resource
> budget
> time
> tasks
> ```
> 
> flow into execution.
> 
> This is why Capability Market can become the central planning layer of an ERP-like system.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 120. Traditional ERP vs Capability ERP
> 
> Traditional ERP often asks:
> 
> ```text
> what inventory / employee / order exists?
> ```
> 
> Capability ERP asks:
> 
> ```text
> what can this organization actually do right now?
> what is missing?
> what can be assembled?
> ```
> 
> This is more semantic.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 121. Organization Capability Balance Sheet
> 
> Interesting output:
> 
> ```text
> Internal Capabilities
> External Capabilities
> Available Capacity
> Committed Capacity
> Strategic Gaps
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 122. Capability Balance Sheet example
> 
> ```text
> Agent evaluation:
> internal 40 h/week
> external 20 h/week
> demand 70 h/week
> gap 10
> 
> Security:
> internal 5
> external 30
> demand 15
> surplus external options
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 123. Capability Liability
> 
> A project dependency on one fragile provider can be treated as:
> 
> ```text
> capability liability
> ```
> 
> not financial liability, but operational exposure.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 124. Capability Asset
> 
> A reusable:
> 
> ```text
> tool
> dataset
> trained team
> shared lab
> ```
> 
> that serves many projects is a strategic capability asset.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 125. Investment logic
> 
> Portfolio Intelligence can ask:
> 
> ```text
> Which capability asset would resolve the largest recurring gaps?
> ```
> 
> This connects Market directly to Strategic Bottleneck Engine.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 126. Resource Exchange → Program creation
> 
> Repeated demand:
> 
> ```text
> many projects request X
> ```
> 
> and no adequate supply:
> 
> ```text
> Program:
> Develop Capability X
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 127. Resource Exchange → Organization design
> 
> Repeated demand for:
> 
> ```text
> security
> grant management
> AI evaluation
> ```
> 
> can justify permanent teams.
> 
> So org structure becomes data-driven.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 128. Dynamic Organization Compiler
> 
> Potential future module:
> 
> ```text
> Demand Graph
> ↓
> stable repeated clusters
> ↓
> suggest organizational units
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 129. Example
> 
> If:
> 
> ```text
> 20 projects repeatedly need:
> security review
> threat modeling
> compliance
> ```
> 
> system may propose:
> 
> ```text
> Security Office
> ```
> 
> instead of project-by-project hiring.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 130. Capability Market → Training Market
> 
> People can declare:
> 
> ```text
> WANTS_TO_LEARN
> capability X
> ```
> 
> Projects declare:
> 
> ```text
> need capability X
> ```
> 
> Training programs bridge.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 131. Apprenticeship Model
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> Expert A
> +
> Learner B
> +
> Project X
> ```
> 
> can create capability growth while delivering work.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 132. Human Development Layer
> 
> Market should not only allocate existing human capabilities.
> 
> It can support:
> 
> ```text
> learning
> mentorship
> skill formation
> ```
> 
> This is more sustainable than pure competition for scarce specialists.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 133. AI as Capability Multiplier
> 
> AI may increase effective capacity of people.
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> one analyst
> +
> AI research agent
> ```
> 
> may cover more research tasks.
> 
> But multiplier must be empirical, task-specific.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 134. Augmented Resource
> 
> Could represent:
> 
> ```text
> Human A + AI Tool B
> ```
> 
> as composite Resource.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 135. Human-AI Bundle
> 
> Capability claims should be attached to:
> 
> ```text
> bundle configuration
> ```
> 
> not automatically to Human A alone.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 136. Example
> 
> Human alone:
> 
> ```text
> 10 reports/week
> ```
> 
> Human + AI:
> 
> ```text
> 25 reports/week
> ```
> 
> if verified.
> 
> This creates operational evidence.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 137. Market Experimentation
> 
> Low-risk tasks can test alternative resource configurations.
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> Human only
> vs
> Human + AI
> ```
> 
> Measure:
> 
> ```text
> quality
> time
> cost
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 138. Capability productivity
> 
> Again, avoid universal worker productivity score.
> 
> Measure:
> 
> ```text
> specific task type
> specific configuration
> specific context
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 139. Resource Exchange API
> 
> Minimum:
> 
> ```text
> POST /market/demand
> POST /market/supply
> 
> GET /market/demand
> GET /market/supply
> 
> POST /market/match
> POST /market/reserve
> POST /market/bind
> POST /market/release
> 
> GET /market/capabilities/{id}
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 140. Matching endpoint
> 
> Input:
> 
> ```yaml
> demand:
>   capability: cap_x
>   depth: production
>   needed_by: ...
>   constraints: ...
> ```
> 
> Output:
> 
> ```text
> individual providers
> composite configurations
> unknowns
> blockers
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 141. Reverse endpoint
> 
> ```text
> GET /resources/{id}/market-opportunities
> ```
> 
> shows open demand relevant to Resource.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 142. Event subscriptions
> 
> A Resource can subscribe:
> 
> ```text
> notify when matching demand appears
> ```
> 
> A Project:
> 
> ```text
> notify when new supply appears
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 143. Automation
> 
> This creates powerful condition watches:
> 
> ```text
> When capability X becomes available
> → reconsider project Y
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 144. Market Time Series
> 
> Over months:
> 
> ```text
> demand
> supply
> capacity
> fill rate
> TTC
> ```
> 
> per capability.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 145. Capability Fill Rate
> 
> ```text
> fulfilled demand / total compatible demand
> ```
> 
> in defined population.
> 
> This helps identify persistent bottlenecks.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 146. Time-to-Fill
> 
> For each demand:
> 
> ```text
> opened_at
> → fulfilled_at
> ```
> 
> Again domain-specific.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 147. Market Learning
> 
> Store:
> 
> ```text
> which matches accepted
> which rejected
> why
> which bindings succeeded
> which failed
> ```
> 
> This is Gold Dataset for universal resolver.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 148. Reason Codes
> 
> Examples:
> 
> ```text
> CAPABILITY_GAP
> CAPACITY_INSUFFICIENT
> LICENSE_BLOCK
> LOCATION_BLOCK
> COST_TOO_HIGH
> TIMELINE_MISMATCH
> WEAK_EVIDENCE
> INTEGRATION_TOO_COMPLEX
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 149. Binding outcome
> 
> After execution:
> 
> ```text
> SUCCESS
> PARTIAL
> FAILED
> CANCELLED
> ```
> 
> with reason.
> 
> This closes learning loop.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 150. Market self-improvement
> 
> ```text
> Match
> ↓
> Binding
> ↓
> Outcome
> ↓
> Error analysis
> ↓
> Matcher improvement proposal
> ↓
> Benchmark
> ↓
> Approval
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 151. Universal Capability Market in overall architecture
> 
> ```text
> OBSERVATORIES
>    │
>    ├── HN
>    ├── GitHub
>    ├── Research
>    ├── Funding
>    └── Physical
>         ↓
>      WORLD STATE
>         ↓
> CAPABILITY SUPPLY / DEMAND
>         ↓
> UNIVERSAL CAPABILITY MARKET
>         ↓
> RESOURCE BINDINGS
>         ↓
> PROJECT / PROGRAM EXECUTION
>         ↓
> OUTCOMES
>         ↓
> WORLD STATE
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 152. Why this is a major architectural milestone
> 
> Previously we had:
> 
> ```text
> many specialized resolvers
> ```
> 
> Now they become adapters around a universal abstraction:
> 
> ```text
> Requirement ↔ Provider
> ```
> 
> This dramatically simplifies the whole Innovation OS.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 153. Core equivalence
> 
> Employment:
> 
> ```text
> Project Gap ↔ Person
> ```
> 
> Software acquisition:
> 
> ```text
> Project Gap ↔ Repository
> ```
> 
> Research:
> 
> ```text
> Knowledge Gap ↔ Method/Researcher
> ```
> 
> Funding:
> 
> ```text
> Funding Gap ↔ Grant
> ```
> 
> Equipment:
> 
> ```text
> Physical Gap ↔ Lab
> ```
> 
> All are instances of the same market relation.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 154. But providers remain heterogeneous
> 
> Universal abstraction does **not** mean pretending:
> 
> ```text
> person = machine = grant
> ```
> 
> It only means they all can satisfy requirements.
> 
> Each retains:
> 
> ```text
> its own state
> constraints
> ethics
> permissions
> cost model
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 155. Full loop
> 
> At this point the virtual technopark can operate as:
> 
> ```text
> Observe
> ↓
> Model
> ↓
> Publish Demand
> ↓
> Discover Supply
> ↓
> Compose
> ↓
> Bind
> ↓
> Execute
> ↓
> Verify
> ↓
> Learn
> ```
> 
> ---

> ## 157. Главный переход
> 
> До этого Universal Capability Market решал:

> найти Resource
> ↓

> ```
> 
> Но со временем World State начинает видеть повторяющиеся структуры:

> ```text
> одни и те же capabilities
> +
> одни и те же люди

> +

> +

> Возникает новый вопрос:
