# chatgpt response

Продолжаю полностью на русском. Следующий слой — **Federated Innovation Network & Semantic M2M Protocol v0.1**: он нужен, чтобы отдельные экземпляры Innovation OS, университеты, технопарки, компании, лаборатории и агентные системы могли обмениваться не сырыми чатами и документами, а структурированным смысловым состоянием, сохраняя provenance, права доступа и автономию сторон.

> **Document: Federated Innovation Network & Semantic M2M Protocol v0.1**
> 
> # Federated Innovation Network & Semantic M2M Protocol v0.1
> 
> ## 502. Главный переход
> 
> До этого мы рассматривали один большой World State.
> 
> Но реальный мир состоит из независимых организаций:
> 
> ```text
> University A
> Company B
> Lab C
> Technopark D
> Public Agency E
> Open-source Community F
> ```
> 
> У каждой есть:
> 
> ```text
> свои данные
> свои проекты
> свои люди
> свои права
> свои политики
> свои AI-агенты
> ```
> 
> Поэтому глобальная система не должна требовать:
> 
> ```text
> "отдать все данные в одну центральную БД"
> ```
> 
> Вместо этого:
> 
> ```text
> Independent World States
>         ↕
> Semantic Federation Protocol
>         ↕
> Shared Innovation Network
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 503. Federation ≠ одна глобальная база
> 
> Главный принцип:
> 
> > Каждая организация сохраняет собственный источник истины.
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> Org A World State
> Org B World State
> Org C World State
> ```
> 
> А между ними передаются:
> 
> ```text
> разрешённые Claims
> Capability Offers
> Capability Demands
> Events
> Evidence references
> Semantic diffs
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 504. Федеративная модель
> 
> ```text
> ┌──────────────┐
> │ InnovationOS │
> │      A       │
> └──────┬───────┘
>        │
>        │ Semantic M2M
>        │
> ┌──────▼───────┐
> │ InnovationOS │
> │      B       │
> └──────────────┘
> ```
> 
> При этом A не получает автоматически всю внутреннюю БД B.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 505. Что должно передаваться
> 
> Не:
> 
> ```text
> полный PostgreSQL dump
> ```
> 
> а только конкретный semantic package.
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> "У нас открыт спрос на Capability X,
> уровень production,
> 20 часов в неделю,
> начало через месяц,
> EU only."
> ```
> 
> Это становится машинно-читаемым объектом.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 506. Semantic Message Envelope
> 
> Минимальный message envelope:
> 
> ```yaml
> message:
>   protocol_version: "0.1"
>   message_id: uuid
> 
>   sender: org_A
>   recipient: org_B
> 
>   message_type: CAPABILITY_DEMAND
> 
>   created_at: ...
> 
>   context:
>     project_id: public_project_reference
> 
>   payload:
>     ...
> 
>   provenance:
>     source_system: innovation_os_A
> 
>   signature:
>     ...
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 507. Message Types v0.1
> 
> Минимально:
> 
> ```text
> CAPABILITY_DEMAND
> CAPABILITY_OFFER
> CLAIM
> EVIDENCE_REFERENCE
> EVENT
> STATE_DIFF
> QUERY
> QUERY_RESULT
> PROPOSAL
> ACK
> ERROR
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 508. Capability Demand
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```yaml
> type: CAPABILITY_DEMAND
> 
> capability:
>   id: cap_secure_browser_execution
> 
> requirement:
>   depth: PRODUCTION
> 
> quantity:
>   value: 20
>   unit: hour/week
> 
> constraints:
>   geography: EU
>   self_hosted: true
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 509. Capability Offer
> 
> Ответ:
> 
> ```yaml
> type: CAPABILITY_OFFER
> 
> provider:
>   type: ORGANIZATION
>   public_id: org_B_security_team
> 
> capability:
>   id: cap_secure_browser_execution
> 
> availability:
>   from: 2026-11-01
> 
> conditions:
>   review_required: true
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 510. Offer ≠ binding
> 
> Offer означает:
> 
> ```text
> "мы потенциально можем предоставить"
> ```
> 
> Не:
> 
> ```text
> "мы уже обязаны это сделать"
> ```
> 
> Для commitment нужен отдельный договор/Decision/Binding.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 511. Query
> 
> Одна система может спросить:
> 
> ```text
> Find resources providing
> distributed tactile sensing
> ```
> 
> Но получатель сам решает:
> 
> ```text
> какие данные раскрывать
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 512. Privacy boundary
> 
> Очень важный принцип:
> 
> ```text
> Query
> does not imply
> right to underlying private data.
> ```
> 
> Ответ может быть:
> 
> ```text
> 1 suitable provider exists
> ```
> 
> без раскрытия имени.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 513. Progressive Disclosure
> 
> Можно использовать несколько уровней раскрытия.
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> Level 0:
> capability exists
> 
> Level 1:
> organization type
> 
> Level 2:
> anonymized resource profile
> 
> Level 3:
> identified provider
> 
> Level 4:
> detailed evidence
> ```
> 
> Переход между уровнями требует policy/consent.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 514. Public / Shared / Private / Confidential
> 
> Каждый объект может иметь:
> 
> ```text
> PUBLIC
> SHARED
> PRIVATE
> CONFIDENTIAL
> ```
> 
> Но это только базовые labels.
> 
> Реальная политика должна учитывать:
> 
> ```text
> кто спрашивает
> для какой цели
> какой объект
> какое действие
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 515. Attribute-Based Access Control
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> ALLOW organization_type=university
> TO READ dataset_metadata
> IF project=consortium_X
> ```
> 
> Это гибче, чем только role-based permissions.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 516. Semantic Permission
> 
> Можно формализовать:
> 
> ```text
> MAY_READ
> MAY_QUERY
> MAY_EXECUTE
> MAY_PROPOSE
> MAY_APPROVE
> MAY_PUBLISH
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 517. Authority remains local
> 
> Если Org B получает:
> 
> ```text
> PROPOSAL:
> allocate Lab 4
> ```
> 
> только Org B может авторизовать реальное действие со своим Lab 4.
> 
> Федерация не отменяет локальный control plane.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 518. Local Sovereignty Rule
> 
> ```text
> Remote semantic request
> → Local policy engine
> → Local decision
> → Local execution
> ```
> 
> Никогда:
> 
> ```text
> Remote agent
> → direct privileged physical action
> ```
> 
> без местного policy/authorization layer.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 519. Semantic State Diff
> 
> Ключевая часть протокола.
> 
> Вместо отправки всего World State:
> 
> ```text
> State t0
> ↓
> changes
> ↓
> State t1
> ```
> 
> передаётся:
> 
> ```text
> DIFF
> ```
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```yaml
> state_diff:
>   added:
>     - resource_42 PROVIDES cap_X
> 
>   removed:
>     - resource_17 AVAILABLE
> 
>   changed:
>     - project_8.status:
>         from: VALIDATION
>         to: EXECUTION
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 520. Почему diff важен
> 
> Если World State огромный:
> 
> ```text
> миллионы entities
> ```
> 
> нет смысла пересылать всё при каждом изменении.
> 
> Передаётся только:
> 
> ```text
> new / changed / removed semantic facts
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 521. Semantic Diff ≠ text diff
> 
> Text diff:
> 
> ```text
> line 42 changed
> ```
> 
> Semantic diff:
> 
> ```text
> Capability requirement removed
> Provider replaced
> Constraint hardened
> Evidence invalidated
> ```
> 
> Это гораздо полезнее для machine-to-machine interaction.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 522. Semantic Hash
> 
> Можно вычислять normalized semantic fingerprint:
> 
> ```text
> HASH(
>   normalized entity
>   + claims
>   + qualifiers
>   + context
> )
> ```
> 
> Это помогает:
> 
> ```text
> detect duplicate
> detect change
> verify synchronization
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 523. Canonicalization
> 
> Перед hashing нужно:
> 
> ```text
> normalize ordering
> normalize units
> normalize IDs where possible
> ```
> 
> Иначе одинаковый смысл даст разные hashes.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 524. Semantic Version
> 
> Каждый package должен иметь:
> 
> ```text
> schema_version
> ontology_version
> protocol_version
> ```
> 
> Это три разные вещи.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 525. Example
> 
> ```yaml
> protocol_version: "0.1"
> schema_version: "IIR-0.1"
> ontology_version: "capability-registry-2026-09"
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 526. Compatibility negotiation
> 
> При соединении:
> 
> ```text
> A supports IIR 0.1
> B supports IIR 0.1 + 0.2
> ```
> 
> Они договариваются:
> 
> ```text
> common version = 0.1
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 527. Protocol Handshake
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> HELLO
> ↓
> SUPPORTED_VERSIONS
> ↓
> SUPPORTED_CAPABILITIES
> ↓
> AUTHENTICATION
> ↓
> SESSION
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 528. Node Capability Manifest
> 
> Каждый Innovation OS node может публиковать:
> 
> ```yaml
> node_manifest:
>   supports:
>     - capability_query
>     - funding_query
>     - research_query
>     - project_exchange
> 
>   accepts:
>     - IIR_0_1
> 
>   policies:
>     external_execution: false
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 529. То есть сам узел тоже имеет capabilities
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> Node A
> PROVIDES
> semantic_resource_search
> ```
> 
> Таким образом протокол рекурсивно использует собственную модель.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 530. M2M Capability Discovery
> 
> Один узел может спросить:
> 
> ```text
> "Кто в federation умеет искать research methods?"
> ```
> 
> и получить:
> 
> ```text
> Node R
> PROVIDES
> research_resolution
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 531. Network Service Registry
> 
> В federation можно иметь:
> 
> ```text
> node
> capabilities
> public endpoints
> trust status
> ```
> 
> Но registry не обязательно должен быть централизованным.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 532. Federation topology
> 
> Возможны:
> 
> ```text
> Hub-and-spoke
> Peer-to-peer
> Hierarchical
> Hybrid
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 533. Hub-and-Spoke
> 
> Например региональный технопарк:
> 
> ```text
> Central Discovery Hub
>        ↓
> Companies
> Universities
> Labs
> ```
> 
> Hub хранит только shared metadata.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 534. Peer-to-Peer
> 
> Организации общаются напрямую:
> 
> ```text
> A ↔ B
> A ↔ C
> B ↔ C
> ```
> 
> Полезно для небольших доверенных сетей.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 535. Hierarchical Federation
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> Local Technopark
> ↓
> Regional Network
> ↓
> European Network
> ```
> 
> Каждый уровень может агрегировать только разрешённую summary information.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 536. Hybrid
> 
> Вероятно наиболее реалистично:
> 
> ```text
> public discovery hub
> +
> direct private exchanges
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 537. Discovery ≠ Data Transfer
> 
> Public registry может сказать:
> 
> ```text
> Org B provides photonics testing
> ```
> 
> Но подробные:
> 
> ```text
> equipment
> calendar
> prices
> staff
> ```
> 
> получаются только после direct authorized query.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 538. Data Minimization
> 
> Протокол должен поддерживать:
> 
> ```text
> send minimum semantic information
> needed for current task
> ```
> 
> Это полезно и для privacy, и для bandwidth.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 539. Semantic Compression
> 
> Например вместо отправки:
> 
> ```text
> 200-page technical report
> ```
> 
> одна система может отправить:
> 
> ```text
> Claim Set
> +
> Evidence references
> +
> Artifact hash
> ```
> 
> А полный документ скачивается только при необходимости.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 540. Layered Payload
> 
> Можно разделить:
> 
> ```text
> Level 1:
> semantic summary
> 
> Level 2:
> structured evidence metadata
> 
> Level 3:
> artifact
> 
> Level 4:
> raw telemetry/data
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 541. Lazy Retrieval
> 
> Получатель сначала видит:
> 
> ```text
> Claim:
> method X achieved Y
> ```
> 
> Если claim важен:
> 
> ```text
> REQUEST_EVIDENCE
> ```
> 
> и только тогда получает detailed source.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 542. Это уменьшает network traffic
> 
> Особенно для:
> 
> ```text
> datasets
> videos
> sensor logs
> large repositories
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 543. Semantic Reference
> 
> Можно передавать:
> 
> ```text
> artifact_hash
> artifact_uri
> access_policy
> ```
> 
> вместо artifact bytes.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 544. Content Addressing
> 
> Hash полезен для:
> 
> ```text
> deduplication
> integrity
> cache
> version identity
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 545. Global ID problem
> 
> Independent systems may assign:
> 
> ```text
> different UUIDs
> ```
> 
> одному и тому же entity.
> 
> Нужен entity reconciliation.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 546. Federated Identity
> 
> Можно иметь:
> 
> ```text
> local_id
> issuer
> external identities
> semantic fingerprint
> ```
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> did-like identifier
> ```
> 
> или обычный URI namespace.
> 
> Не обязательно сразу создавать blockchain identity.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 547. Canonical URI
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> iir://org-a/resource/123
> ```
> 
> или:
> 
> ```text
> https://org-a.example/iir/resource/123
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 548. Identity mapping
> 
> Org B может хранить:
> 
> ```text
> remote entity
> ↔
> local shadow entity
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 549. Shadow Entity
> 
> Если remote Resource не импортируется полностью:
> 
> ```text
> Shadow Resource
> ```
> 
> содержит:
> 
> ```text
> public ID
> minimal claims
> source node
> last synced
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 550. Remote Object ≠ Local Truth
> 
> Remote Claim должен хранить:
> 
> ```text
> issuer
> signature
> observed_at
> ```
> 
> И локальная система сама решает:
> 
> ```text
> trust / validation status
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 551. Trust Model
> 
> Не нужен один global reputation score.
> 
> Можно иметь:
> 
> ```text
> trust by claim class
> ```
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> Org A authoritative for its own lab availability
> ```
> 
> но не обязательно:
> 
> ```text
> authoritative for market forecasts
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 552. Authority Scopes
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> Organization A
> AUTHORITATIVE_FOR
> Resource ownership
> 
> Lab B
> AUTHORITATIVE_FOR
> Calibration status
> 
> Funding Agency C
> AUTHORITATIVE_FOR
> Grant eligibility rules
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 553. Trust != truth
> 
> Даже authoritative source может ошибиться.
> 
> Но authority определяет:
> 
> ```text
> which source is entitled to set certain operational state
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 554. Signed Claims
> 
> Можно подписывать:
> 
> ```text
> Claim payload
> hash
> issuer
> timestamp
> signature
> ```
> 
> чтобы проверить:
> 
> ```text
> who issued it
> whether it changed
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 555. Signed Evidence Reference
> 
> Например calibration certificate:
> 
> ```text
> Evidence
> signed_by
> Lab
> ```
> 
> может использоваться другой organization.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 556. Verifiable Credentials
> 
> В будущем можно использовать стандартные credential approaches для:
> 
> ```text
> certifications
> licenses
> qualifications
> access rights
> ```
> 
> Но IIR должен оставаться независимым от конкретной credential technology.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 557. Claims Exchange
> 
> Node A отправляет:
> 
> ```text
> CLAIM:
> Resource X PROVIDES Capability Y
> ```
> 
> Node B может:
> 
> ```text
> ACCEPT
> STORE_AS_REMOTE
> REQUEST_EVIDENCE
> REJECT
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 558. Claim Acceptance State
> 
> Application-level:
> 
> ```text
> UNSEEN
> ACCEPTED
> NEEDS_EVIDENCE
> CONTESTED
> REJECTED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 559. Contradictory Remote Claims
> 
> A:
> 
> ```text
> Repo X ACTIVE
> ```
> 
> B:
> 
> ```text
> Repo X STALE
> ```
> 
> Не перезаписывать.
> 
> Хранить:
> 
> ```text
> Claim A
> Claim B
> contexts
> timestamps
> evidence
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 560. Reconciliation Engine
> 
> Он пытается выяснить:
> 
> ```text
> different observation time?
> different definition?
> different context?
> actual contradiction?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 561. Semantic Conflict Package
> 
> Если конфликт нельзя разрешить:
> 
> ```yaml
> conflict:
>   subject: repo_x
>   predicate: status
> 
>   claims:
>     - active
>     - stale
> 
>   status: unresolved
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 562. Request for Clarification
> 
> Node может отправить:
> 
> ```text
> QUERY:
> Please provide evidence for status ACTIVE
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 563. Event Propagation
> 
> Некоторые Events можно публиковать federation-wide.
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> NEW_GRANT_CALL
> NEW_PUBLIC_DATASET
> NEW_OPEN_SOURCE_RELEASE
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 564. Private Events stay local
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> employee unavailable
> internal incident
> confidential project failure
> ```
> 
> не публикуются без policy.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 565. Subscription Model
> 
> Node может подписаться:
> 
> ```text
> capability = photonics
> event_type = NEW_RESOURCE
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 566. Federated Event Bus
> 
> Не обязательно один Kafka cluster.
> 
> Можно иметь protocol-level subscription:
> 
> ```text
> SUBSCRIBE
> FILTER
> DELIVER_EVENT
> ACK
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 567. Event Filter
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```yaml
> subscription:
>   event_types:
>     - RESOURCE_DISCOVERED
> 
>   capability:
>     - tactile_sensing
> 
>   visibility:
>     - PUBLIC
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 568. Federated Capability Market
> 
> Теперь Universal Capability Market может выйти за пределы одной организации.
> 
> ```text
> Local Demand
> ↓
> Local Market
> ↓ unresolved
> Federated Market
> ↓
> External Supply
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 569. Local-first rule
> 
> Сначала:
> 
> ```text
> search local/internal resources
> ```
> 
> затем, если policy разрешает:
> 
> ```text
> search federation
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 570. External Demand Publication
> 
> Project может публиковать:
> 
> ```text
> anonymized demand
> ```
> 
> например:
> 
> ```text
> Need EU-based robotics testing
> within 6 weeks
> ```
> 
> без раскрытия confidential project details.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 571. Demand Disclosure Levels
> 
> ```text
> PUBLIC_SUMMARY
> ANONYMIZED
> IDENTIFIED
> CONFIDENTIAL_PARTNER_ONLY
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 572. Reverse Discovery
> 
> External provider can publish:
> 
> ```text
> new photonics lab capacity available
> ```
> 
> Local systems автоматически проверяют:
> 
> ```text
> which blocked projects could use it?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 573. Federated Consortium Formation
> 
> Очень важный use case.
> 
> Grant requires:
> 
> ```text
> 3 organizations
> 3 countries
> research + SME + end-user
> ```
> 
> Federation может искать:
> 
> ```text
> compatible organizations
> ```
> 
> across independent World States.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 574. Consortium Discovery Flow
> 
> ```text
> Grant Requirements
> ↓
> Local Missing Roles
> ↓
> Federated Capability Query
> ↓
> Candidate Organizations
> ↓
> Interest Request
> ↓
> Consortium Hypothesis
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 575. Interest Request
> 
> Не сразу:
> 
> ```text
> "вы включены в consortium"
> ```
> 
> а:
> 
> ```text
> PROPOSAL:
> Would you be interested in role X?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 576. Consent
> 
> Organization отвечает:
> 
> ```text
> INTERESTED
> DECLINED
> REQUEST_MORE_INFO
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 577. Shared Project Context
> 
> После согласия создаётся:
> 
> ```text
> Federated Project Context
> ```
> 
> в котором участники публикуют только agreed data.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 578. Federated Project State
> 
> Не обязательно хранить всю project state у всех.
> 
> Можно иметь:
> 
> ```text
> shared state
> +
> local private state
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 579. Example
> 
> Shared:
> 
> ```text
> milestones
> public deliverables
> work package status
> ```
> 
> Private:
> 
> ```text
> internal staffing
> internal cost structure
> private notes
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 580. Split-Brain Problem
> 
> Если два nodes имеют разные versions shared state:
> 
> ```text
> A says milestone done
> B says pending
> ```
> 
> нужна reconciliation.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 581. Version Vector
> 
> Можно хранить:
> 
> ```text
> revision
> issuer
> timestamp
> ```
> 
> или более сложные vector clocks later.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 582. For v0.1
> 
> Достаточно:
> 
> ```text
> monotonic revision per shared object
> ```
> 
> и:
> 
> ```text
> optimistic concurrency check
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 583. Shared Object Update
> 
> ```text
> GET version 12
> ↓
> modify
> ↓
> PUT expected_version=12
> ```
> 
> Если current=13:
> 
> ```text
> CONFLICT
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 584. Semantic Merge
> 
> При conflict:
> 
> ```text
> field-level merge
> ```
> 
> не всегда достаточно.
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> constraint changed
> ```
> 
> может иметь semantic consequence.
> 
> Нужен:
> 
> ```text
> semantic diff
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 585. Merge Categories
> 
> ```text
> NON_CONFLICTING
> STRUCTURAL_CONFLICT
> POLICY_CONFLICT
> SEMANTIC_CONFLICT
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 586. Example semantic conflict
> 
> A:
> 
> ```text
> Capability requirement changed from SHOULD to MUST
> ```
> 
> B meanwhile:
> 
> ```text
> removed provider for same capability
> ```
> 
> Text merge может пройти, но project semantics изменились критически.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 587. Semantic Merge Validator
> 
> После merge:
> 
> ```text
> re-run:
> constraints
> gaps
> dependencies
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 588. Federated Task Execution
> 
> Project A may ask Org B:
> 
> ```text
> perform test X
> ```
> 
> Protocol:
> 
> ```text
> TASK_PROPOSAL
> ↓
> local authorization
> ↓
> TASK_ACCEPTED
> ↓
> execution
> ↓
> ARTIFACT/EVIDENCE returned
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 589. Task Proposal ≠ Remote Command
> 
> Crucial:
> 
> ```text
> proposal
> ```
> 
> becomes local Task only after approval.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 590. Federated Handoff
> 
> Agent/organization A can send:
> 
> ```text
> Handoff Package
> ```
> 
> containing:
> 
> ```text
> objective
> current state
> artifacts
> claims
> unknowns
> requested capability
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 591. No shared giant chat history
> 
> Federation особенно выигрывает от:
> 
> ```text
> structured handoff
> ```
> 
> вместо пересылки многомесячных разговоров.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 592. Context Package
> 
> Receiver получает:
> 
> ```text
> minimum required context
> ```
> 
> not:
> 
> ```text
> entire sender World State
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 593. Semantic Context Compiler
> 
> Before transfer:
> 
> ```text
> Task
> ↓
> Context Compiler
> ↓
> minimal claims
> artifacts
> constraints
> decisions
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 594. Redaction
> 
> Context Compiler может:
> 
> ```text
> remove personal/private information
> ```
> 
> и оставить:
> 
> ```text
> generalized technical knowledge
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 595. Public Knowledge Extraction
> 
> Например internal discussion:
> 
> ```text
> private project-specific context
> ```
> 
> может быть transformed into:
> 
> ```text
> anonymized reusable method
> ```
> 
> after review.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 596. Private → Shared → Public pipeline
> 
> ```text
> PRIVATE
> ↓ sanitize
> SHARED
> ↓ review
> PUBLIC
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 597. This directly supports Open Knowledge architecture
> 
> General technical knowledge can escape siloed chats/projects while private information remains protected.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 598. Semantic Publication Package
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```yaml
> publication:
>   concept: browser_agent_security
> 
>   claims:
>     - ...
> 
>   evidence:
>     - public references
> 
>   removed:
>     - client identity
>     - private logs
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 599. Machine-readable License
> 
> Published knowledge can include:
> 
> ```text
> license
> reuse rights
> attribution requirements
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 600. Federated Technopedia
> 
> Каждый node может публиковать pages/resources.
> 
> Federation creates:
> 
> ```text
> distributed Technopedia
> ```
> 
> without requiring one organization to own all data.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 601. Search Across Federation
> 
> Query:
> 
> ```text
> find public knowledge
> about distributed tactile sensing
> ```
> 
> can federate to:
> 
> ```text
> research node
> lab node
> GitHub node
> company node
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 602. Query Planner
> 
> Determines:
> 
> ```text
> which nodes likely know what
> ```
> 
> based on Node Capability Manifests.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 603. Cost-aware Query
> 
> Do not broadcast every query to everyone.
> 
> Use:
> 
> ```text
> routing
> capability index
> cache
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 604. Semantic Router
> 
> Like network routing, but by meaning:
> 
> ```text
> query about funding
> → funding nodes
> 
> query about photonics
> → photonics research/lab nodes
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 605. Semantic Routing Table
> 
> Node can maintain:
> 
> ```text
> Capability Domain → Nodes
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 606. Route Learning
> 
> If Node B repeatedly answers:
> 
> ```text
> robotics sensing
> ```
> 
> well, router learns:
> 
> ```text
> B relevant to robotics sensing
> ```
> 
> This is routing evidence, not general reputation.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 607. Hierarchical Semantic Routing
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> Germany
> ↓
> Saxony
> ↓
> Dresden
> ↓
> Photonics Lab Network
> ```
> 
> for location-bound resources.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 608. Global Resources vs Local Resources
> 
> Software:
> 
> ```text
> global
> ```
> 
> Lab:
> 
> ```text
> location-bound
> ```
> 
> Human:
> 
> ```text
> partly mobile
> ```
> 
> Funding:
> 
> ```text
> jurisdiction-bound
> ```
> 
> Routing should understand geography.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 609. Data Residency
> 
> Some data:
> 
> ```text
> must stay within organization/country
> ```
> 
> Federation can send:
> 
> ```text
> query to data
> ```
> 
> instead of:
> 
> ```text
> data to query
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 610. Federated Computation
> 
> Например Org B has private dataset.
> 
> Org A wants:
> 
> ```text
> Does dataset contain enough samples
> for requirement X?
> ```
> 
> Instead of transferring dataset:
> 
> ```text
> remote computation
> ```
> 
> returns:
> 
> ```text
> aggregate result
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 611. Privacy-preserving query
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> count resources
> matching capability X
> ```
> 
> returns:
> 
> ```text
> 7
> ```
> 
> without identities.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 612. Secure Compute later
> 
> More advanced versions could use:
> 
> ```text
> secure enclaves
> privacy-preserving computation
> federated learning
> ```
> 
> but v0.1 does not need this complexity.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 613. Federated Learning of Matchers
> 
> Organizations can optionally share:
> 
> ```text
> aggregated matcher outcomes
> ```
> 
> without raw private profiles.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 614. Example
> 
> Share:
> 
> ```text
> constraint reason frequencies
> ```
> 
> not:
> 
> ```text
> personal candidate data
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 615. Federation Governance
> 
> Network needs rules:
> 
> ```text
> who may join?
> what schemas required?
> what public claims allowed?
> how abuse handled?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 616. Federation Policy Artifact
> 
> Can contain:
> 
> ```text
> protocol rules
> required security
> identity rules
> data-sharing rules
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 617. Node Membership States
> 
> ```text
> DISCOVERED
> PENDING
> TRUSTED
> LIMITED
> SUSPENDED
> REVOKED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 618. Trust domains
> 
> Different federation segments may have different policies:
> 
> ```text
> public open network
> research consortium
> company supplier network
> government network
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 619. Public Federation
> 
> Any node may:
> 
> ```text
> publish public capabilities
> query public resources
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 620. Trusted Consortium Federation
> 
> Members may additionally share:
> 
> ```text
> private project state
> availability
> internal evidence
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 621. High-security Federation
> 
> Might permit only:
> 
> ```text
> signed structured messages
> no raw artifact transfer
> local execution only
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 622. Federation Bridge
> 
> One node may participate in multiple networks.
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> University Lab
> ```
> 
> belongs to:
> 
> ```text
> Open Research Network
> EU Consortium Network
> Regional Technopark
> ```
> 
> with different disclosure policies.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 623. Context Isolation
> 
> Claim shared in Network A:
> 
> ```text
> must not automatically propagate
> to Network B
> ```
> 
> unless policy permits.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 624. Propagation Policy
> 
> ```text
> LOCAL_ONLY
> DIRECT_PEER
> FEDERATION
> PUBLIC
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 625. Event TTL
> 
> Some messages should expire.
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> resource availability
> ```
> 
> has:
> 
> ```text
> valid_until
> ```
> 
> Otherwise stale supply persists forever.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 626. Cache Expiration
> 
> Remote data should carry:
> 
> ```text
> freshness
> TTL
> last_verified
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 627. Pull vs Push
> 
> Two models:
> 
> ```text
> PULL:
> ask when needed
> 
> PUSH:
> subscribe to changes
> ```
> 
> Both needed.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 628. High-frequency state
> 
> Do not push:
> 
> ```text
> machine telemetry
> ```
> 
> across federation unless necessary.
> 
> Publish:
> 
> ```text
> semantic summaries
> availability
> alerts
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 629. Semantic Event Compression
> 
> Instead of:
> 
> ```text
> 1 million sensor samples
> ```
> 
> send:
> 
> ```text
> Machine capacity degraded by 20%
> ```
> 
> with link to raw evidence.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 630. State Synchronization Modes
> 
> Useful modes:
> 
> ```text
> SNAPSHOT
> DIFF
> EVENT_STREAM
> QUERY_ONLY
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 631. Snapshot
> 
> Useful for:
> 
> ```text
> initial synchronization
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 632. Diff
> 
> Useful for:
> 
> ```text
> regular updates
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 633. Event Stream
> 
> Useful for:
> 
> ```text
> real-time important changes
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 634. Query Only
> 
> Useful where:
> 
> ```text
> data must remain local
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 635. Failure Handling
> 
> Network messages may:
> 
> ```text
> timeout
> duplicate
> arrive out of order
> ```
> 
> Protocol must tolerate this.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 636. Idempotency
> 
> Every message:
> 
> ```text
> message_id
> ```
> 
> allows duplicate suppression.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 637. Ordering
> 
> For entity changes:
> 
> ```text
> revision_number
> ```
> 
> helps detect out-of-order updates.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 638. Retry
> 
> Transient failure:
> 
> ```text
> retry
> ```
> 
> Permanent:
> 
> ```text
> dead-letter / human review
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 639. Acknowledgement
> 
> ```text
> ACK
> ```
> 
> should mean:
> 
> ```text
> message received
> ```
> 
> not necessarily:
> 
> ```text
> semantic claim accepted
> ```
> 
> Need separate states.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 640. Transport independence
> 
> Semantic protocol should not depend on:
> 
> ```text
> HTTP only
> ```
> 
> Same payload could travel over:
> 
> ```text
> HTTP
> WebSocket
> message queue
> MCP-like transport
> file exchange
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 641. Protocol Layers
> 
> Useful separation:
> 
> ```text
> Transport Layer
> ↓
> Identity/Security Layer
> ↓
> Semantic Message Layer
> ↓
> IIR Objects
> ↓
> Domain Libraries
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 642. Relationship to MCP
> 
> MCP answers roughly:
> 
> ```text
> what tools/resources can I call?
> ```
> 
> Semantic M2M layer answers:
> 
> ```text
> what does another system know,
> need,
> offer,
> believe,
> and what changed?
> ```
> 
> То есть это не замена MCP.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 643. MCP + Semantic M2M
> 
> ```text
> Semantic M2M:
> intent / state / claims / demand / supply
> 
> MCP:
> tool access / resource access / execution
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 644. Relationship to device safety protocols
> 
> Physical device layer answers:
> 
> ```text
> how safely to execute action
> ```
> 
> Semantic M2M says:
> 
> ```text
> why action is requested
> what state/goal it belongs to
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 645. Three-level stack
> 
> Conceptually:
> 
> ```text
> SEMANTIC M2M
> meaning/state
> 
> MCP-like Tool Layer
> capability invocation
> 
> Device/Execution Layer
> actual execution
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 646. Connection to earlier text-diffusion idea
> 
> Semantic M2M can also support compact multi-agent collaboration.
> 
> Instead of agents exchanging:
> 
> ```text
> long prose generations
> ```
> 
> they can exchange:
> 
> ```text
> Claims
> State Diffs
> Partial Plans
> Artifacts
> Unknowns
> ```
> 
> This resembles semantic compression of communication.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 647. Multi-Agent Parallelism
> 
> For one large task:
> 
> ```text
> Agent A explores method family 1
> Agent B explores family 2
> Agent C validates evidence
> ```
> 
> They don't send full conversations.
> 
> They publish:
> 
> ```text
> semantic deltas
> ```
> 
> to shared Project Context.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 648. Semantic Delta
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```yaml
> delta:
>   add_claims:
>     - method_X may satisfy capability_Y
> 
>   add_evidence:
>     - paper_17
> 
>   open_questions:
>     - durability_unknown
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 649. Merge Agent Results
> 
> Coordinator merges:
> 
> ```text
> Delta A
> Delta B
> Delta C
> ```
> 
> into:
> 
> ```text
> updated project state
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 650. This can reduce context duplication
> 
> Each agent needs only:
> 
> ```text
> relevant state slice
> ```
> 
> not all other agents' verbose reasoning.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 651. Diffusion-like iterative refinement
> 
> One can build:
> 
> ```text
> Initial coarse semantic state
> ↓
> parallel refinements
> ↓
> merge
> ↓
> gap detection
> ↓
> new refinements
> ```
> 
> Rather than linear token-by-token collaboration.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 652. Important distinction
> 
> This is not literal mathematical diffusion unless implemented as such.
> 
> It is better described as:
> 
> ```text
> iterative distributed semantic refinement
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 653. Machine Communication Optimization
> 
> Protocol can prefer:
> 
> ```text
> structured IDs
> typed predicates
> deltas
> hashes
> ```
> 
> instead of human-readable prose.
> 
> Humans receive generated explanation only when needed.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 654. Human ↔ Machine Dual Representation
> 
> Same semantic object can render as:
> 
> ```text
> JSON
> YAML
> graph
> natural language
> 2D card
> 3D object
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 655. One meaning, many serializations
> 
> This is a central architectural principle:
> 
> ```text
> Semantic Object
> ≠
> Presentation Format
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 656. Semantic Packet
> 
> Could define compact binary serialization later.
> 
> For now:
> 
> ```text
> JSON
> ```
> 
> is enough.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 657. Binary protocol later
> 
> Only if measurements show:
> 
> ```text
> bandwidth/latency
> ```
> 
> actually matter.
> 
> Do not prematurely optimize.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 658. Federation Security
> 
> Critical controls:
> 
> ```text
> mutual authentication
> message signing
> TLS
> scoped permissions
> rate limits
> audit log
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 659. Prompt injection isolation
> 
> Remote text/artifacts are:
> 
> ```text
> untrusted input
> ```
> 
> even when from trusted partner.
> 
> LLM must not treat embedded instructions as system authority.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 660. Semantic Validation Firewall
> 
> Incoming payload:
> 
> ```text
> schema validation
> ↓
> signature check
> ↓
> policy check
> ↓
> semantic validation
> ↓
> quarantine if suspicious
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 661. Remote Claim cannot directly trigger privileged action
> 
> Correct:
> 
> ```text
> Remote Event
> ↓
> Local Rule
> ↓
> Action Proposal
> ↓
> Authorization
> ```
> 
> Not:
> 
> ```text
> Remote Event
> ↓
> Execute payment
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 662. Rate Limiting
> 
> Needed to prevent:
> 
> ```text
> query flood
> event flood
> expensive semantic search abuse
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 663. Cost Accounting for Federation
> 
> Remote queries may consume:
> 
> ```text
> AI compute
> database search
> human review
> ```
> 
> Could eventually have:
> 
> ```text
> quota
> credits
> billing
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 664. Capability Exchange between organizations
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> Technopark A:
> needs thermal testing
> 
> Lab Network B:
> offers thermal testing
> ```
> 
> Federated Market resolves the gap.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 665. Cross-border constraints
> 
> Need:
> 
> ```text
> jurisdiction
> export controls
> data residency
> tax/legal rules
> ```
> 
> as ordinary constraints.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 666. No special federation logic for each law
> 
> The protocol carries:
> 
> ```text
> constraint metadata
> ```
> 
> and local policy engines interpret relevant jurisdiction.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 667. Federated Project Compiler
> 
> Project can contain providers from different nodes:
> 
> ```text
> Person from A
> Repo public
> Lab from B
> Funding from C
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 668. Federated project.lock
> 
> ```yaml
> bindings:
> 
>   cap_research:
>     provider: iir://org-a/resource/12
> 
>   cap_testing:
>     provider: iir://org-b/lab/7
> 
>   funding:
>     provider: iir://agency-c/grant/4
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 669. Local mirrors
> 
> Each organization stores:
> 
> ```text
> local binding reference
> ```
> 
> to remote provider.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 670. Availability synchronization
> 
> If remote provider becomes unavailable:
> 
> ```text
> RESOURCE_UNAVAILABLE
> ```
> 
> propagates to subscribed projects.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 671. Federated Replanning
> 
> ```text
> remote resource lost
> ↓
> binding degraded
> ↓
> local/federated resolver reruns
> ↓
> alternative proposed
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 672. Federated Resilience
> 
> Critical capability may deliberately use providers from:
> 
> ```text
> different organizations
> different regions
> different vendors
> ```
> 
> to reduce correlated failure.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 673. Federation as Innovation Internet
> 
> Conceptually:
> 
> ```text
> Internet connects machines
> Web connects documents
> Semantic Innovation Network connects
> problems + capabilities + resources + projects
> ```
> 
> This is a useful high-level analogy.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 674. But not one universal ontology
> 
> Different domains will have:
> 
> ```text
> robotics ontology
> legal ontology
> biotech ontology
> funding ontology
> ```
> 
> Need:
> 
> ```text
> shared semantic core
> +
> domain extensions
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 675. Ontology Mapping
> 
> Node A:
> 
> ```text
> cap_robot_grasp
> ```
> 
> Node B:
> 
> ```text
> manipulation_gripping
> ```
> 
> may be:
> 
> ```text
> EQUIVALENT / RELATED / SPECIALIZATION
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 676. Ontology Translation Service
> 
> Can create mapping hypotheses.
> 
> But mappings require:
> 
> ```text
> versioning
> provenance
> confidence
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 677. Semantic Loss
> 
> Translation between ontologies may lose detail.
> 
> Protocol should allow:
> 
> ```text
> LOSSLESS
> PARTIAL
> APPROXIMATE
> ```
> 
> mapping status.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 678. Never silently collapse distinctions
> 
> For example:
> 
> ```text
> clinical validation
> ```
> 
> and:
> 
> ```text
> technical validation
> ```
> 
> must not become same concept merely because embeddings are close.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 679. Federation Capability Registry
> 
> Common high-level IDs are useful for frequently exchanged concepts.
> 
> But local systems may extend them.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 680. Namespace
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> iir.core:secure_execution
> orgA.robotics:tactile_slip_detection
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 681. Domain package
> 
> An organization can publish:
> 
> ```text
> ontology package
> ```
> 
> with:
> 
> ```text
> concepts
> aliases
> relations
> versions
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 682. Package Manager
> 
> This points to another future component:
> 
> ```text
> Semantic Package Registry
> ```
> 
> for:
> 
> ```text
> ontologies
> agent skills
> tool bindings
> archetypes
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 683. Federated Skill Packages
> 
> Node A could publish:
> 
> ```text
> "grant eligibility extractor"
> ```
> 
> as reusable agent skill.
> 
> Node B can:
> 
> ```text
> inspect
> test
> approve
> install
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 684. Safe Capability Import
> 
> Correct loop:
> 
> ```text
> discover package
> ↓
> inspect manifest
> ↓
> sandbox
> ↓
> benchmark
> ↓
> policy approval
> ↓
> register
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 685. This connects to technological self-awareness
> 
> System can discover:
> 
> ```text
> external capability package
> ```
> 
> that improves its own Resource Graph.
> 
> Then:
> 
> ```text
> self gap
> ↓
> external discovery
> ↓
> test
> ↓
> approval
> ↓
> capability added
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 686. Node Self-Description
> 
> Each node can publish:
> 
> ```text
> what it can do
> what protocols it supports
> what domains it knows
> ```
> 
> This is machine-level self-description.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 687. Federation Discovery
> 
> New node joins.
> 
> Others do not need manual documentation reading.
> 
> They query:
> 
> ```text
> NODE_MANIFEST
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 688. Human-readable manifest
> 
> Same data can render:
> 
> ```text
> "This node provides funding search,
> robotics lab discovery,
> and GitHub analysis."
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 689. Federation Search
> 
> User can ask one local system:
> 
> ```text
> "Найдите лабораторию для испытания сенсора."
> ```
> 
> Local node:
> 
> ```text
> local search
> ↓
> federated query
> ↓
> multiple remote nodes
> ↓
> normalize
> ↓
> compare
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 690. Result provenance
> 
> Every result shows:
> 
> ```text
> source organization
> observed_at
> evidence
> visibility
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 691. No hidden cross-system inference
> 
> If remote system sends:
> 
> ```text
> INFERENCE
> ```
> 
> local system must preserve that epistemic type.
> 
> Not upgrade to FACT.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 692. Epistemic Preservation Rule
> 
> ```text
> FACT stays FACT
> INFERENCE stays INFERENCE
> HYPOTHESIS stays HYPOTHESIS
> ```
> 
> unless local validation explicitly promotes/demotes it.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 693. Context Preservation Rule
> 
> Remote claim:
> 
> ```text
> valid in Project A
> ```
> 
> must not become:
> 
> ```text
> global truth
> ```
> 
> after import.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 694. Time Preservation Rule
> 
> Preserve:
> 
> ```text
> observed_at
> valid_from
> valid_to
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 695. Provenance Preservation Rule
> 
> Every transformation adds provenance but does not erase prior provenance.
> 
> ```text
> Source A
> ↓
> Node B normalization
> ↓
> Node C inference
> ```
> 
> All three remain visible.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 696. Provenance Chain
> 
> ```text
> Raw Source
> ↓
> Claim
> ↓
> Translation
> ↓
> Inference
> ↓
> Decision
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 697. Federation Audit
> 
> For any imported data:
> 
> ```text
> who sent it?
> when?
> under which policy?
> who accessed it?
> what decision used it?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 698. Right to Withdraw Shared Data
> 
> Some shared information may be revoked.
> 
> Need:
> 
> ```text
> REVOKE
> ```
> 
> message.
> 
> But previously derived public knowledge may have different legal/contractual status.
> 
> Policy matters.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 699. Revocation semantics
> 
> Remote object can become:
> 
> ```text
> REVOKED
> ```
> 
> rather than silently deleted.
> 
> Local system knows:
> 
> ```text
> do not use for future decisions
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 700. Historical audit remains
> 
> If lawful/policy-compliant, system can retain:
> 
> ```text
> "claim was used at time t"
> ```
> 
> without continuing to expose source data.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 701. Federated Innovation Market
> 
> Now Universal Capability Market becomes networked:
> 
> ```text
> Local Market A
> ↔
> Local Market B
> ↔
> Local Market C
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 702. Market tiers
> 
> Useful:
> 
> ```text
> Internal
> Trusted Partners
> Regional Network
> Public Network
> ```
> 
> Search can expand progressively.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 703. Search Escalation
> 
> ```text
> Internal resources
> ↓ if unresolved
> Trusted partners
> ↓
> Regional federation
> ↓
> Public federation
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 704. This reduces unnecessary exposure
> 
> Sensitive demand need not be publicly broadcast if local supply exists.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 705. Anonymous Market Query
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> "EU robotics project needs
> thermal cycling capability."
> ```
> 
> without:
> 
> ```text
> company identity
> project details
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 706. Private negotiation later
> 
> If provider responds:
> 
> ```text
> possible match
> ```
> 
> 双方 can establish private session.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 707. Federation Session
> 
> Session has:
> 
> ```text
> participants
> purpose
> permissions
> expiry
> shared context
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 708. Purpose Limitation
> 
> Data shared for:
> 
> ```text
> grant consortium evaluation
> ```
> 
> should not automatically be reusable for:
> 
> ```text
> marketing
> ```
> 
> Protocol metadata can carry:
> 
> ```text
> purpose
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 709. Data Usage Policy
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```yaml
> usage:
>   purpose:
>     - consortium_matching
> 
>   redisclosure: false
>   expires_at: ...
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 710. Policy Enforcement Limits
> 
> Protocol can carry policy, but technical enforcement across independent organizations may not always be perfect.
> 
> Therefore:
> 
> ```text
> technical controls
> +
> contracts/governance
> ```
> 
> both matter.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 711. Federation Health
> 
> Network-level observability:
> 
> ```text
> nodes online
> protocol versions
> message failures
> stale mirrors
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 712. But no centralized visibility into all private activity
> 
> Health telemetry should be minimal.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 713. Node Offline
> 
> If node unavailable:
> 
> ```text
> remote bindings
> ```
> 
> may become:
> 
> ```text
> DEGRADED / UNKNOWN
> ```
> 
> not automatically failed.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 714. Offline-first
> 
> Some nodes may operate disconnected.
> 
> Later:
> 
> ```text
> sync diffs
> ```
> 
> when connection returns.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 715. Conflict after offline work
> 
> Use semantic merge.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 716. Federated Digital Twin
> 
> For physical networks:
> 
> ```text
> Port A
> Rail B
> Warehouse C
> ```
> 
> can each keep local twin.
> 
> Federated layer shares:
> 
> ```text
> capacity
> shipments
> handoff state
> ```
> 
> not all raw sensors.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 717. Logistics example
> 
> Port sends:
> 
> ```text
> Container 17 cleared
> ready for pickup
> ```
> 
> Rail node responds:
> 
> ```text
> train capacity available 14:00
> ```
> 
> This is semantic M2M coordination.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 718. This is far more compact than sharing raw cameras
> 
> Raw visual data remains local unless specifically needed.
> 
> Federation exchanges:
> 
> ```text
> entity state
> events
> availability
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 719. Scientific federation
> 
> University A can publish:
> 
> ```text
> new method
> ```
> 
> Lab B:
> 
> ```text
> can replicate
> ```
> 
> Company C:
> 
> ```text
> has application gap
> ```
> 
> System assembles:
> 
> ```text
> cross-organization validation project
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 720. Open-source federation
> 
> GitHub-like communities can publish:
> 
> ```text
> capability packages
> issues
> open gaps
> maintainer availability
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 721. Funding federation
> 
> Funding agencies can publish machine-readable:
> 
> ```text
> calls
> eligibility
> deadlines
> ```
> 
> directly.
> 
> This reduces extraction errors.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 722. Machine-readable Calls
> 
> Instead of scraping PDFs:
> 
> ```text
> Funding Agency
> publishes IIR Funding Package
> ```
> 
> with signed claims.
> 
> This would be much stronger infrastructure.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 723. Machine-readable Procurement
> 
> Similarly:
> 
> ```text
> buyer
> problem
> budget
> constraints
> deadline
> ```
> 
> can be published as semantic demand.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 724. Machine-readable Research Outputs
> 
> Paper publishers could expose:
> 
> ```text
> claims
> methods
> datasets
> code links
> ```
> 
> in structured form.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 725. Semantic Internet of Innovation
> 
> Long-term architecture:
> 
> ```text
> Problems
> Capabilities
> Resources
> Evidence
> Projects
> ```
> 
> become addressable semantic objects across organizations.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 726. Minimal v0.1 implementation
> 
> Do not build global internet immediately.
> 
> Start with:
> 
> ```text
> 2 Innovation OS nodes
> ```
> 
> A and B.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 727. First test
> 
> Node A publishes:
> 
> ```text
> Capability Demand
> ```
> 
> Node B publishes:
> 
> ```text
> Capability Offer
> ```
> 
> A discovers B.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 728. Second test
> 
> A requests:
> 
> ```text
> evidence
> ```
> 
> B returns:
> 
> ```text
> signed Evidence Reference
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 729. Third test
> 
> A proposes:
> 
> ```text
> Task
> ```
> 
> B accepts locally.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 730. Fourth test
> 
> B completes task and returns:
> 
> ```text
> Artifact
> +
> Event
> +
> Evidence
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 731. Fifth test
> 
> B changes availability.
> 
> A receives:
> 
> ```text
> STATE_DIFF
> ```
> 
> and updates binding status.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 732. Sixth test
> 
> A and B modify same shared object.
> 
> System detects:
> 
> ```text
> semantic conflict
> ```
> 
> rather than silently overwriting.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 733. Seventh test
> 
> Private claim remains:
> 
> ```text
> PRIVATE
> ```
> 
> and is not exported by federation endpoint.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 734. Eighth test
> 
> An anonymized Demand is published without leaking project identity.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 735. Minimal API
> 
> ```text
> POST /federation/hello
> GET /federation/manifest
> 
> POST /federation/query
> POST /federation/messages
> 
> POST /federation/subscribe
> DELETE /federation/subscribe/{id}
> 
> GET /federation/objects/{id}
> GET /federation/diff
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 736. Node manifest endpoint
> 
> ```text
> GET /.well-known/iir-node
> ```
> 
> could eventually return Node Manifest.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 737. Why `.well-known`
> 
> It could make automatic node discovery easy.
> 
> But exact standardization should come later.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 738. Transport v0.1
> 
> Start simply:
> 
> ```text
> HTTPS
> JSON
> ```
> 
> with:
> 
> ```text
> TLS
> API keys / mutual authentication
> message signatures
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 739. Do not start with custom binary networking
> 
> The main uncertainty remains semantics.
> 
> Not packet encoding.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 740. Reference node
> 
> Create:
> 
> ```text
> iir-federation-node
> ```
> 
> as small service/module.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 741. Suggested package structure
> 
> ```text
> federation/
> ├── protocol/
> │   ├── messages.py
> │   ├── envelope.py
> │   └── versions.py
> │
> ├── identity/
> ├── policy/
> ├── sync/
> ├── routing/
> ├── subscriptions/
> └── transport/
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 742. Integration with existing IIR Core
> 
> Important:
> 
> Federation must not create its own duplicate object model.
> 
> Payloads contain:
> 
> ```text
> IIR Core objects
> ```
> 
> or references to them.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 743. Federation is transport/orchestration layer
> 
> Not second ontology.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 744. Protocol invariants
> 
> Freeze initial rules.
> 
> ### Rule 1
> 
> ```text
> Remote data never silently becomes local authoritative truth.
> ```
> 
> ### Rule 2
> 
> ```text
> Epistemic type must be preserved.
> ```
> 
> ### Rule 3
> 
> ```text
> Provenance must be preserved.
> ```
> 
> ### Rule 4
> 
> ```text
> Context must be preserved.
> ```
> 
> ### Rule 5
> 
> ```text
> Remote request cannot bypass local authorization.
> ```
> 
> ### Rule 6
> 
> ```text
> Private objects are not exported without explicit policy.
> ```
> 
> ### Rule 7
> 
> ```text
> All mutations are versioned/auditable.
> ```
> 
> ### Rule 8
> 
> ```text
> UNKNOWN remains UNKNOWN.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 745. Protocol evolutionary path
> 
> ```text
> v0.1
> direct node-to-node
> 
> v0.2
> subscriptions + routing
> 
> v0.3
> shared project contexts
> 
> v0.4
> semantic package registry
> 
> v0.5
> large federation / multi-hop routing
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 746. Connection to Resource Economy
> 
> Cross-organization resource usage can create:
> 
> ```text
> billing
> credits
> contracts
> ```
> 
> but these are optional higher layers.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 747. Federation does not require common currency
> 
> One exchange may be:
> 
> ```text
> commercial
> ```
> 
> another:
> 
> ```text
> grant consortium
> ```
> 
> another:
> 
> ```text
> open-source contribution
> ```
> 
> another:
> 
> ```text
> reciprocal research access
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 748. Capability exchange is more fundamental than money
> 
> The protocol first asks:
> 
> ```text
> what is needed?
> what is offered?
> under what conditions?
> ```
> 
> Payment model comes later.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 749. Federation + Dynamic Organization
> 
> Temporary consortium can emerge across organizational boundaries.
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> University A
> +
> SME B
> +
> Lab C
> +
> Open-source Team D
> ```
> 
> becomes:
> 
> ```text
> Federated Project Team
> ```
> 
> without merging organizations.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 750. Federated Organization
> 
> In future:
> 
> ```text
> virtual organizations
> ```
> 
> can exist purely as coordinated resource graphs across legal entities.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 751. Virtual Technopark becomes network-native
> 
> Instead of one virtual building:
> 
> ```text
> global / regional graph of autonomous nodes
> ```
> 
> appears.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 752. 2D/3D federation view
> 
> UI can show:
> 
> ```text
> Node / Organization
> ↓
> Capabilities
> ↓
> Projects
> ↓
> Cross-node flows
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 753. Geographical layer
> 
> Physical nodes:
> 
> ```text
> labs
> factories
> ports
> universities
> ```
> 
> may appear on geographical map.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 754. Semantic layer
> 
> Capabilities and project dependencies form non-geographical graph.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 755. Two maps should coexist
> 
> ```text
> Physical Geography
> +
> Semantic Capability Space
> ```
> 
> Switching between them can be very powerful.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 756. Example
> 
> Click:
> 
> ```text
> tactile sensing capability
> ```
> 
> Semantic view shows:
> 
> ```text
> researchers
> papers
> repos
> projects
> ```
> 
> Physical view shows:
> 
> ```text
> labs
> equipment
> manufacturers
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 757. Federated simulation
> 
> A scenario can span nodes.
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> What if Lab B becomes unavailable?
> ```
> 
> Local project graph sees affected remote binding and recomputes.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 758. But remote internal simulation remains private
> 
> Node B need not expose its full internal model.
> 
> It can return:
> 
> ```text
> availability degraded until date X
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 759. Federated Counterfactual Query
> 
> A can ask:
> 
> ```text
> If demand increases to 100 samples/week,
> could you support it?
> ```
> 
> B locally simulates and returns:
> 
> ```text
> YES / NO / UNKNOWN
> +
> conditions
> ```
> 
> This is powerful and privacy-preserving.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 760. Semantic Contract Negotiation
> 
> Instead of sending long free-form documents first, organizations can negotiate structured terms:
> 
> ```text
> capability
> quantity
> deadline
> price
> quality
> IP
> visibility
> ```
> 
> Then generate human/legal contract documents.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 761. Semantic Contract ≠ Legal Contract
> 
> It is operational specification.
> 
> Legal agreement remains separate Artifact.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 762. Machine-readable commitment
> 
> Once legal/human approval exists:
> 
> ```text
> Binding
> ```
> 
> can become signed machine-readable commitment.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 763. Smart Contract without blockchain
> 
> This can work as:
> 
> ```text
> signed state machine
> ```
> 
> in ordinary databases.
> 
> Blockchain optional.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 764. Semantic Agreement
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```yaml
> agreement:
>   provider: lab_B
>   consumer: org_A
> 
>   capability:
>     thermal_testing
> 
>   quantity:
>     20 samples
> 
>   deadline:
>     ...
> 
>   verification:
>     test_report_required
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 765. Runtime enforcement
> 
> Project Runtime checks:
> 
> ```text
> is agreement active?
> ```
> 
> before remote task execution.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 766. Cross-node Artifact Lineage
> 
> Artifact produced at B:
> 
> ```text
> report_17
> ```
> 
> imported by A retains:
> 
> ```text
> created_by B
> action_id
> hash
> signature
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 767. Supply-chain traceability
> 
> For physical products:
> 
> ```text
> Supplier A
> → Component
> → Manufacturer B
> → Assembly
> → Lab C
> → Certification
> ```
> 
> all can exist across nodes.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 768. Federated Digital Thread
> 
> This enables end-to-end provenance across organizational boundaries.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 769. Scientific reproducibility
> 
> Similarly:
> 
> ```text
> University A method
> → Lab B replication
> → Company C application
> ```
> 
> all evidence remains connected.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 770. Cross-domain learning
> 
> Federation grows World State without centralizing ownership.
> 
> That may be one of the strongest long-term properties of the architecture.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 771. The network can be partially open
> 
> Public part:
> 
> ```text
> Capabilities
> public Projects
> public Knowledge
> ```
> 
> Private part:
> 
> ```text
> internal operations
> personal data
> commercial secrets
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 772. Open Knowledge Commons
> 
> Public federation can become:
> 
> ```text
> distributed technological encyclopedia
> ```
> 
> containing:
> 
> ```text
> methods
> standards
> capabilities
> public evidence
> open projects
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 773. Private Innovation Networks
> 
> Companies can run restricted federation using the same protocol.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 774. Same protocol, different governance
> 
> This is important for adoption.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 775. Reference Architecture after federation
> 
> Now the full stack becomes:
> 
> ```text
>            HUMAN / 2D / 3D UI
>                    │
>              STRATEGY LAYER
>                    │
>           PROJECT / PROGRAM OS
>                    │
>            CAPABILITY MARKET
>                    │
>             SEMANTIC RUNTIME
>                    │
>                WORLD STATE
>                    │
>                IIR CORE
>                    │
>         FEDERATION / M2M LAYER
>             ↕       ↕       ↕
>         NODE A   NODE B   NODE C
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 776. Or from the network perspective
> 
> ```text
> Organization A
>    │
>    ├── People
>    ├── AI
>    ├── Code
>    └── Projects
>    │
> Semantic M2M
>    │
> Organization B
>    │
>    ├── Labs
>    ├── Research
>    └── Equipment
>    │
> Semantic M2M
>    │
> Funding Node C
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 777. The architecture now becomes recursive
> 
> Each node internally has:
> 
> ```text
> World State
> Capability Market
> Runtime
> ```
> 
> and externally appears as:
> 
> ```text
> Resource Provider + Demand Source
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 778. Node as Resource
> 
> One entire organization can be treated by another as:
> 
> ```text
> Resource
> ```
> 
> providing high-level capabilities.
> 
> For example:
> 
> ```text
> University A
> PROVIDES
> advanced_photonics_research
> ```
> 
> without exposing internal composition.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 779. Recursive abstraction
> 
> ```text
> Person
> Team
> Department
> Organization
> Federation
> ```
> 
> can all be capability providers at different resolutions.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 780. Multi-resolution organizational semantics
> 
> This is important for scalability.
> 
> Project need not inspect:
> 
> ```text
> every employee
> ```
> 
> if Organization offers:
> 
> ```text
> certified testing capability
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 781. Expand on demand
> 
> Only when necessary:
> 
> ```text
> Organization
> ↓
> Lab
> ↓
> Equipment
> ↓
> Operator
> ```
> 
> This is semantic zoom.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 782. Semantic Zoom
> 
> Same principle can power UI.
> 
> At high level:
> 
> ```text
> Lab B
> ```
> 
> Zoom:
> 
> ```text
> equipment
> staff
> queues
> ```
> 
> Further:
> 
> ```text
> machine state
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 783. Semantic M2M + 3D
> 
> A remote organization could expose a simplified 3D/2D twin:
> 
> ```text
> available lab
> active project
> resource capacity
> ```
> 
> without exposing confidential internals.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 784. This enables a true distributed virtual technopark
> 
> Not one game server pretending to contain the world.
> 
> Rather:
> 
> ```text
> many real independent systems
> federated into one navigable semantic environment
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 785. The next architectural problem
> 
> After federation, a new question appears:
> 
> > Как стандартизировать переносимые capabilities themselves — AI-skills, tool adapters, semantic archetypes, workflows, ontologies and validated procedures?
> 
> This leads to the next module:
> 
> # **Semantic Package Registry & Capability Package Manager v0.1**
> 
> It would define:
> 
> ```text
> Capability Package
> Skill Package
> Ontology Package
> Workflow Package
> Tool Binding Package
> Agent Package
> ```
> 
> and the lifecycle:
> 
> ```text
> discover
> ↓
> inspect
> ↓
> sandbox
> ↓
> verify
> ↓
> approve
> ↓
> install
> ↓
> register capability
> ↓
> version/update/rollback
> ```
> 
> This is essentially the **package manager of the Innovation OS** — the layer through which an organization can safely import new machine capabilities from the federated network without uncontrolled self-modification.

Именно этот следующий слой особенно важен для ранее сформулированной идеи технологического самоосознания: система сможет не просто увидеть, что у неё отсутствует capability, а найти во внешней сети переносимый пакет, проверить его в песочнице, сравнить с существующей конфигурацией и после разрешения добавить новую способность в собственный Self Capability Graph.

Продолжаю полностью **на русском языке**. > # Semantic Package Registry & Capability Package Manager v0.1
> 
> ## 786. Главный переход
> 
> До этого система уже умеет:
> 
> ```text
> обнаруживать Capability Gap
> ↓
> искать внешние Resources
> ↓
> сравнивать варианты
> ↓
> собирать Project
> ↓
> выполнять Actions
> ```
> 
> Но появляется более сильный вопрос:
> 
> > А что, если внешняя сеть содержит не просто сервис или человека, а переносимую способность, которую сама Innovation OS может установить в себя?
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> новый GitHub adapter
> новый grant parser
> новый robotics skill
> новый semantic archetype
> новый ontology package
> новый agent workflow
> новый evaluator
> ```
> 
> Тогда система должна уметь пройти:
> 
> ```text
> DISCOVER
> ↓
> INSPECT
> ↓
> TEST
> ↓
> VERIFY
> ↓
> APPROVE
> ↓
> INSTALL
> ↓
> REGISTER
> ↓
> MONITOR
> ↓
> UPDATE / ROLLBACK
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 787. Capability Package
> 
> Основная новая application-level абстракция:
> 
> ```text
> CAPABILITY PACKAGE
> ```
> 
> Это переносимый пакет, который после установки добавляет или изменяет capability системы.
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> GitHubSearchSkill
> ```
> 
> после установки может дать:
> 
> ```text
> System PROVIDES repository_discovery
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 788. Package ≠ Capability
> 
> Очень важно различать:
> 
> ```text
> Capability
> ```
> 
> — способность.
> 
> ```text
> Package
> ```
> 
> — переносимый технический артефакт, который эту способность реализует.
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> Capability:
> PDF semantic extraction
> 
> Package:
> pdf-extractor-v2
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 789. Package как Artifact + Resource candidate
> 
> На уровне IIR:
> 
> ```text
> Package
> → ARTIFACT
> ```
> 
> а после установки:
> 
> ```text
> Installed Package
> → SOFTWARE / AI_AGENT / SERVICE Resource
> ```
> 
> который:
> 
> ```text
> PROVIDES Capability
> ```
> 
> ---
>

> 
> Для v0.1 достаточно:
> 
> ```text
> TOOL_PACKAGE
> AGENT_SKILL_PACKAGE

> ONTOLOGY_PACKAGE

> 
> Каждый пакет обязан иметь machine-readable manifest.

>   package_type: AGENT_SKILL_PACKAGE

>   - repository_capability_extraction

>   - web_access

>   - evaluator

> # 800. Manifest — это контракт

> ```text

> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 862. Reverse Package Search
> 
> Новый package:
> 
> ```text
> What current system gaps could this package close?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 863. Package Opportunity
> 
> Если один package может закрыть:
> 
> ```text
> 20 recurring gaps
> ```
> 
> Opportunity Engine может предложить:
> 
> ```text
> evaluate/install package
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 864. Package Composition
> 
> Capability может требовать несколько packages.
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> Research Scout
> =
> Web Connector
> +
> Paper Parser
> +
> Research Ontology
> +
> Evidence Evaluator
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 865. Composite Installation Plan
> 
> Package Manager строит:
> 
> ```text
> Dependency DAG
> ```
> 
> и install order.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 866. Dependency Lock File
> 
> Analog:
> 
> ```text
> package.lock
> ```
> 
> например:
> 
> ```yaml
> packages:
>   web_connector: 1.4.2
>   paper_parser: 0.9.1
>   research_ontology: 2.1.0
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 867. Reproducibility
> 
> Одинаковый:
> 
> ```text
> package.lock
> ```
> 
> должен позволять восстановить semantic runtime configuration.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 868. Environment Lock
> 
> Кроме package versions:
> 
> ```text
> model versions
> tool versions
> policy versions
> ontology versions
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 869. Runtime Fingerprint
> 
> System instance can have:
> 
> ```text
> configuration hash
> ```
> 
> Useful for:
> 
> ```text
> reproducibility
> audit
> benchmark comparison
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 870. Agent Package
> 
> Особый package type.
> 
> Не просто prompt.
> 
> Он может включать:
> 
> ```text
> role
> model requirements
> tools
> permissions
> context builder
> procedure graph
> verification
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 871. Example Agent Package
> 
> ```yaml
> agent:
>   role: TECHNOLOGY_SCOUT
> 
>   provides:
>     - technology_discovery
> 
>   tools:
>     - web_search
>     - github_connector
> 
>   permissions:
>     - network_read
> 
>   outputs:
>     - resource_candidates
>     - evidence
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 872. Agent ≠ Model
> 
> Package может работать с:
> 
> ```text
> Model A
> Model B
> Local model
> ```
> 
> если capability requirements satisfied.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 873. Model Requirements
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> requires:
> context_window >= X
> tool_calling = true
> structured_output = true
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 874. Model Router
> 
> Runtime resolves:
> 
> ```text
> which model provider satisfies package requirements?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 875. Model Package
> 
> Можно также представить:
> 
> ```text
> model weights
> configuration
> tokenizer
> runtime
> ```
> 
> как package ecosystem.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 876. But model weights are Artifact
> 
> А deployed model endpoint:
> 
> ```text
> Resource
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 877. Tool Binding Package
> 
> Связывает semantic Action:
> 
> ```text
> CREATE_REPOSITORY
> ```
> 
> с:
> 
> ```text
> GitHub API implementation
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 878. Multiple Bindings
> 
> Same Action:
> 
> ```text
> CREATE_REPOSITORY
> ```
> 
> could map to:
> 
> ```text
> GitHub
> GitLab
> Gitea
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 879. Semantic Portability
> 
> Project workflow does not need rewrite.
> 
> Only provider binding changes.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 880. Workflow Package
> 
> Contains:
> 
> ```text
> Action templates
> dependencies
> conditions
> verification
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 881. Example
> 
> ```text
> Grant Application Workflow
> ```
> 
> could compile into:
> 
> ```text
> extract call
> ↓
> eligibility check
> ↓
> consortium gap analysis
> ↓
> budget draft
> ↓
> proposal draft
> ↓
> review
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 882. Workflow Parameterization
> 
> Package accepts:
> 
> ```text
> project_id
> funding_call_id
> organization_id
> ```
> 
> and produces Task Graph.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 883. Archetype Package
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> Research Project Archetype
> ```
> 
> defines:
> 
> ```text
> required claims
> tasks
> artifacts
> verification
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 884. Archetype vs Workflow
> 
> Archetype says:
> 
> ```text
> what structure such project has
> ```
> 
> Workflow:
> 
> ```text
> how to execute it
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 885. Ontology Package Dependencies
> 
> Workflow may require:
> 
> ```text
> specific concepts/predicates
> ```
> 
> Therefore manifest declares ontology versions.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 886. Package Compatibility Matrix
> 
> For installed packages:
> 
> ```text
> Package A v2
> compatible with
> Ontology B v1.3–1.9
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 887. Package Conflict Detector
> 
> Find:
> 
> ```text
> permission conflicts
> dependency conflicts
> ontology conflicts
> port conflicts
> resource conflicts
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 888. Permission Conflict
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> Package A assumes network access
> Policy forbids external network
> ```
> 
> → BLOCKED.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 889. Resource Conflict
> 
> Two packages require:
> 
> ```text
> exclusive GPU
> ```
> 
> simultaneously.
> 
> Runtime handles capacity.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 890. Package Provenance
> 
> Store:
> 
> ```text
> publisher
> repository
> release
> signature
> license
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 891. License
> 
> Package Manager checks:
> 
> ```text
> license compatibility
> commercial restrictions
> redistribution
> ```
> 
> before install.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 892. SBOM-like Manifest
> 
> Software package can include:
> 
> ```text
> dependencies
> versions
> licenses
> hashes
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 893. Semantic BOM
> 
> Analogously:
> 
> ```text
> capabilities
> ontologies
> policies
> workflows
> ```
> 
> that package depends on.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 894. Capability BOM
> 
> For high-level Agent:
> 
> ```text
> Technology Scout
> ```
> 
> requires:
> 
> ```text
> web_search
> repo_inspection
> semantic_normalization
> evidence_extraction
> ```
> 
> This can be represented explicitly.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 895. Missing Dependency becomes Gap
> 
> If package needs:
> 
> ```text
> Capability X
> ```
> 
> which system lacks:
> 
> ```text
> new Capability Gap
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 896. Recursive Resolution
> 
> Package installation itself can trigger:
> 
> ```text
> Resolver
> ```
> 
> to find missing dependencies.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 897. Prevent Infinite Dependency Loops
> 
> Dependency graph must be acyclic or detect cycles.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 898. Bootstrapping Problem
> 
> Some core capabilities must exist before package system works.
> 
> Minimal trusted base:
> 
> ```text
> package parser
> signature verifier
> sandbox
> policy engine
> installer
> rollback
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 899. Trusted Computing Base
> 
> Keep it small.
> 
> The smaller core:
> 
> ```text
> the easier to audit
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 900. Package Sandbox Types
> 
> Depending risk:
> 
> ```text
> process sandbox
> container
> VM
> restricted interpreter
> simulator
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 901. Physical Skill Sandbox
> 
> Robot package should first run:
> 
> ```text
> in simulation/digital twin
> ```
> 
> before physical execution.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 902. Financial Package Sandbox
> 
> Payment connector:
> 
> ```text
> test account
> fake transaction
> ```
> 
> before production credential access.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 903. Email/Communication Package
> 
> Must not send real external messages in benchmark.
> 
> Use:
> 
> ```text
> draft/shadow mailbox
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 904. Package Permissions at Runtime
> 
> Even installed package may receive:
> 
> ```text
> temporary scoped token
> ```
> 
> per Action.
> 
> Not permanent full credential.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 905. Capability Token
> 
> Conceptually:
> 
> ```text
> allow this package
> to perform Action X
> on Resource Y
> until time T
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 906. Ephemeral Authorization
> 
> Especially useful for:
> 
> ```text
> cloud
> GitHub
> email
> robotics
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 907. Tool Firewall
> 
> Every outbound action passes:
> 
> ```text
> Tool Firewall
> ```
> 
> checking:
> 
> ```text
> permission
> target
> rate
> context
> policy
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 908. Package Behavior Monitoring
> 
> Installed package may behave unexpectedly.
> 
> Monitor:
> 
> ```text
> unexpected network calls
> unexpected file access
> excessive cost
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 909. Runtime Quarantine
> 
> If violation:
> 
> ```text
> QUARANTINED
> ```
> 
> and bindings removed.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 910. Automatic rollback can be allowed for machine packages
> 
> For example:
> 
> ```text
> new parser crashes repeatedly
> ```
> 
> Runtime may revert to previous version under policy.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 911. Human-impacting packages need stronger controls
> 
> Especially:
> 
> ```text
> hiring
> legal
> financial
> physical safety
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 912. Package Quality Evidence
> 
> Registry can store:
> 
> ```text
> benchmark results
> security audit
> usage history
> known issues
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 913. No universal package rating
> 
> Instead show dimensions:
> 
> ```text
> security evidence
> benchmark coverage
> maintenance activity
> compatibility
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 914. Package Maintenance
> 
> Package has:
> 
> ```text
> maintainer
> release activity
> support status
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 915. Abandoned Package
> 
> If:
> 
> ```text
> maintainer inactive
> critical dependency stale
> ```
> 
> health may become:
> 
> ```text
> DEGRADED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 916. Package Replacement
> 
> System can search:
> 
> ```text
> alternative package providing same capability
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 917. Migration Project
> 
> Replacing package:
> 
> ```text
> old provider
> → new provider
> ```
> 
> can itself be Project.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 918. Parallel Migration
> 
> Run both:
> 
> ```text
> old
> new
> ```
> 
> until new passes.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 919. Capability Continuity
> 
> Critical capability should not disappear during upgrade.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 920. Package Registry Federation
> 
> Each organization may have:
> 
> ```text
> internal registry
> ```
> 
> plus access to:
> 
> ```text
> trusted federation registry
> public registry
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 921. Registry Tiers
> 
> ```text
> INTERNAL
> TRUSTED
> PUBLIC
> EXPERIMENTAL
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 922. Search Escalation
> 
> Same pattern:
> 
> ```text
> Internal
> ↓
> Trusted
> ↓
> Federated
> ↓
> Public
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 923. Package Publishing
> 
> Developer/organization can publish:
> 
> ```text
> manifest
> artifact
> signature
> tests
> benchmark
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 924. Publish Review
> 
> Public registry may require:
> 
> ```text
> schema validation
> security scan
> license metadata
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 925. Package Fork
> 
> Package can be:
> 
> ```text
> DERIVED_FROM
> ```
> 
> another package.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 926. Fork Provenance
> 
> Keep lineage:
> 
> ```text
> original
> fork
> patches
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 927. Local Patch
> 
> Organization may patch external package internally.
> 
> Then:
> 
> ```text
> local package version
> DERIVED_FROM
> upstream release
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 928. Upstream Reconciliation
> 
> When upstream updates:
> 
> ```text
> semantic/code diff
> ```
> 
> can be inspected.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 929. Package Diff
> 
> Not only file diff.
> 
> For semantic packages:
> 
> ```text
> new capability
> removed permission
> changed ontology
> new required tool
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 930. Security-sensitive diff
> 
> If update adds:
> 
> ```text
> NETWORK_WRITE
> ```
> 
> approval must be reconsidered.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 931. Policy-sensitive upgrade
> 
> Package previously:
> 
> ```text
> read-only
> ```
> 
> new version:
> 
> ```text
> writes external systems
> ```
> 
> This is not routine patch.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 932. Breaking Semantic Change
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> output Claim structure changed
> ```
> 
> downstream workflows may break.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 933. Compatibility Tests
> 
> Before upgrade:
> 
> ```text
> run dependent workflows
> ```
> 
> in sandbox.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 934. Reverse Dependency Graph
> 
> Need know:
> 
> ```text
> which projects/workflows depend on Package X?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 935. Upgrade Impact Analysis
> 
> Before installing:
> 
> ```text
> affected agents
> affected workflows
> affected projects
> affected ontologies
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 936. Update Window
> 
> Critical package may update only:
> 
> ```text
> during maintenance window
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 937. Emergency Security Update
> 
> Exception:
> 
> ```text
> critical vulnerability
> ```
> 
> can trigger faster policy path.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 938. Package Vulnerability Event
> 
> ```text
> PACKAGE_SECURITY_ALERT
> ```
> 
> can mark:
> 
> ```text
> capability degraded
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 939. External advisories
> 
> Could come from:
> 
> ```text
> publisher
> security database
> federated partner
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 940. Self-Protection
> 
> If package compromised:
> 
> ```text
> disable
> revoke credentials
> quarantine
> rebind capability
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 941. Capability Failover
> 
> If Provider A disabled:
> 
> ```text
> Resolver
> ```
> 
> searches Provider B.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 942. Package Manager + Capability Market
> 
> Very tight integration:
> 
> ```text
> Capability Market detects shortage
> ↓
> Package Registry search
> ↓
> installable provider discovered
> ↓
> evaluation
> ↓
> install
> ↓
> Supply increases
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 943. Package Manager + Opportunity Engine
> 
> Repeated gap:
> 
> ```text
> no existing package
> ```
> 
> may create:
> 
> ```text
> Build Package Project
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 944. Package Development Project
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> Need:
> Funding Eligibility Extractor
> ```
> 
> No package exists.
> 
> System creates:
> 
> ```text
> Project:
> build semantic package
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 945. Package Factory
> 
> This suggests another subsystem:
> 
> ```text
> Capability Gap
> ↓
> Package Specification
> ↓
> Implementation
> ↓
> Tests
> ↓
> Publication
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 946. Auto-generated package skeleton
> 
> System can generate:
> 
> ```text
> manifest
> schemas
> tests
> workflow skeleton
> ```
> 
> from capability requirement.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 947. But implementation still requires validation
> 
> Especially for privileged tools.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 948. Package as reusable project output
> 
> A Project can produce:
> 
> ```text
> Package Artifact
> ```
> 
> then registry publishes it.
> 
> Thus:
> 
> ```text
> Project
> → Package
> → New Supply
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 949. Capability Supply Compounding
> 
> One successful project can generate package reused by hundreds of later projects.
> 
> This creates strong:
> 
> ```text
> network effect
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 950. Open Capability Commons
> 
> Public packages can form:
> 
> ```text
> open library of reusable capabilities
> ```
> 
> analogous to package ecosystems, but richer:
> 
> ```text
> code
> workflow
> semantics
> evaluation
> policy
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 951. Semantic Package Registry as Technopedia
> 
> Every package page can include:
> 
> ```text
> what it does
> what capability it provides
> how it works
> dependencies
> evidence
> examples
> alternatives
> ```
> 
> This naturally merges with Technopedia.

> # 952. Package Comparison
> 
> For Capability X:
> 
> ```text
> Package A
> Package B
> Package C
> ```
> 
> compare:
> 
> ```text
> permissions
> cost
> latency
> evidence
> compatibility
> maintenance
> ```
>

> 
> # 953. Alternatives Graph
> 
> Package A:
> 
> ```text
> ALTERNATIVE_TO
> Package B
> ```
> 
> Package C:
> 
> ```text
> COMPLEMENTS
> Package A
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 954. Capability Composition Map
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> Agent Research Capability
> ├── Search Package
> ├── Parser Package
> ├── Evidence Package
> └── Synthesis Package
> ```

> ---
> 
> # 955. Visual Programming

> This connects directly to visual 2D workflows.

> Packages become:
> 
> ```text
> nodes
> ```
> 
> Capabilities become:
> 
> ```text
> ports/interfaces
> ```
> 
> Relations:
> 
> ```text
> edges
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 956. Package Port
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> PaperParser
> INPUT: Document
> OUTPUT: StructuredClaims
> ```

> ---
> 
> # 957. Typed Connection
> 
> UI prevents:
> 
> ```text
> Image

> ```
> 
> if evaluator expects:
> 
> ```text
> FundingCallIR
> ```
> 
> unless adapter exists.
