> 
> # 958. Smart Object
> 
> Package node can be a Smart Object:
> 
> ```text
> data
> capabilities
> constraints
> execution binding
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 959. Visual Macro
> 
> Several packages can be grouped:
> 
> ```text
> Research Pipeline
> ```
> 
> as one macro node.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 960. Conlang / DSL Integration
> 
> Human-friendly command:
> 
> ```text
> исследуй технологию X
> ```
> 
> could compile to archetype:
> 
> ```text
> TechnologyScoutWorkflow
> ```
> 
> which expands into package graph.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 961. Archetype expansion
> 
> ```text
> SCOUT_TECHNOLOGY
> ↓
> Search
> Inspect
> Extract Claims
> Find Repos
> Find Papers
> Generate Gaps
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 962. Package Registry + Semantic Language
> 
> Semantic language can reference capability instead of implementation:
> 
> ```text
> USE capability:research_search
> ```
> 
> Package Manager resolves implementation.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 963. This preserves portability
> 
> Workflow does not depend on exact vendor.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 964. Package Manager + Federation
> 
> Remote node can advertise:
> 
> ```text
> Package X available
> ```
> 
> but local system chooses:
> 
> ```text
> remote execution
> or
> local install
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 965. Remote Package Execution
> 
> Sometimes better not install.
> 
> Use:
> 
> ```text
> Remote Capability Service
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 966. Local vs Remote Resolution
> 
> For Capability X:
> 
> ```text
> install Package locally
> ```
> 
> or:
> 
> ```text
> call remote provider
> ```
> 
> Comparison:
> 
> ```text
> privacy
> latency
> cost
> control
> maintenance
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 967. Package Supply Modes
> 
> ```text
> LOCAL_INSTALL
> REMOTE_SERVICE
> HOSTED_INSTANCE
> CONTAINER
> WASM
> AGENT_SERVICE
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 968. Portable execution formats
> 
> Later package may ship as:
> 
> ```text
> container
> WASM
> Python package
> binary
> workflow IR
> ```
> 
> But semantic manifest remains same.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 969. Forth possibility
> 
> Low-level deterministic capabilities could eventually compile to:
> 
> ```text
> Forth-like stack execution
> ```
> 
> especially embedded/robotic control.
> 
> But Forth remains backend implementation, not package semantics.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 970. Package Runtime Adapter
> 
> Each package format has adapter:
> 
> ```text
> PythonAdapter

# chatgpt response

Продолжаю полностью **на русском языке**, без параллельного перевода. Перевод можно будет сделать позже уже для стабилизированной версии документа. Теперь переходим к исполняемому слою: **Procedural Graph Compiler & Adaptive Workflow Engine v0.1** — механизму, который превращает цель и Project IR в конкретный граф действий для людей, AI-агентов, программ, сервисов и физических устройств.

> **Document: Procedural Graph Compiler & Adaptive Workflow Engine v0.1**
> 
> # Procedural Graph Compiler & Adaptive Workflow Engine v0.1
> 
> ## 1068. Главный переход
> 
> До этого система уже знает:
> 
> ```text
> что существует
> что требуется
> какие capability доступны
> какие ресурсы подходят
> какие пакеты установлены
> ```
> 
> Теперь возникает следующий вопрос:
> 
> > Что именно делать, в каком порядке, какими ресурсами, с какими проверками и что делать при отклонении от плана?
> 
> Это задача Procedural Graph.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1069. Общая цепочка компиляции
> 
> ```text
> Human Goal
> ↓
> Project Compiler
> ↓
> Project IR
> ↓
> Task Compiler
> ↓
> Task Graph
> ↓
> Procedure Compiler
> ↓
> Procedural Graph
> ↓
> Capability Resolver
> ↓
> Execution Backend
> ↓
> Actions / Events / Artifacts
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1070. Project Graph ≠ Procedural Graph
> 
> Project Graph отвечает:
> 
> ```text
> что должно быть достигнуто?
> ```
> 
> Procedural Graph:
> 
> ```text
> как именно это выполнить?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1071. Пример
> 
> Project:
> 
> ```text
> Создать безопасный browser-agent runtime.
> ```
> 
> Project Graph:
> 
> ```text
> Browser Automation
> Security
> Evaluation
> Backend
> Deployment
> ```
> 
> Procedural Graph уже конкретнее:
> 
> ```text
> 1. Найти существующие runtime
> 2. Сравнить sandbox approaches
> 3. Выбрать candidate
> 4. Развернуть prototype
> 5. Запустить security tests
> 6. Запустить benchmark
> 7. Human review
> 8. Approve / reject
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1072. Task Graph
> 
> Первый промежуточный слой:
> 
> ```text
> Task
> ```
> 
> описывает результат работы, но ещё не обязательно низкоуровневую процедуру.
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> TASK:
> Evaluate sandbox technologies
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1073. Procedural Graph
> 
> Task может развернуться в:
> 
> ```text
> search
> ↓
> collect candidates
> ↓
> filter licenses
> ↓
> inspect documentation
> ↓
> run benchmark
> ↓
> compare results
> ↓
> produce report
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1074. Почему нужны оба уровня
> 
> Если хранить сразу тысячи low-level steps:
> 
> ```text
> Project Graph становится нечитаемым.
> ```
> 
> Если хранить только high-level Tasks:
> 
> ```text
> Runtime не знает, что конкретно делать.
> ```
> 
> Поэтому:
> 
> ```text
> Project
> → Tasks
> → Procedures
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1075. Procedure
> 
> `Procedure` — application-level объект, описывающий способ выполнения Task.
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```yaml
> procedure:
>   task_id: task_17
>   version: 3
>   nodes: [...]
>   edges: [...]
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1076. Procedure может быть временной
> 
> Task остаётся тем же:
> 
> ```text
> Evaluate Repository X
> ```
> 
> а Procedure может измениться:
> 
> ```text
> v1 manual inspection
> v2 automated benchmark
> v3 automated + human review
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1077. Это позволяет улучшать способ выполнения без изменения Project IR
> 
> Очень важное разделение:
> 
> ```text
> WHAT
> ```
> 
> и:
> 
> ```text
> HOW
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1078. Procedure Node
> 
> Минимальный узел:
> 
> ```text
> ACTION
> DECISION
> WAIT
> CHECK
> PARALLEL
> MERGE
> LOOP
> SUBPROCEDURE
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1079. ACTION node
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> SEARCH_GITHUB
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1080. DECISION node
> 
> ```text
> License compatible?
> ```
> 
> ветки:
> 
> ```text
> YES → continue
> NO → reject candidate
> UNKNOWN → human/legal review
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1081. WAIT node
> 
> Для:
> 
> ```text
> ожидать API response
> ожидать человека
> ожидать лабораторию
> ожидать события
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1082. CHECK node
> 
> Проверяет:
> 
> ```text
> verification condition
> policy condition
> constraint condition
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1083. PARALLEL node
> 
> Запускает несколько веток:
> 
> ```text
> search papers
> search GitHub
> search experts
> ```
> 
> одновременно.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1084. MERGE node
> 
> Объединяет результаты:
> 
> ```text
> Candidate Set A
> +
> Candidate Set B
> +
> Candidate Set C
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1085. LOOP node
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> для каждого repository:
>   inspect
>   evaluate
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1086. SUBPROCEDURE
> 
> Вызывает reusable workflow:
> 
> ```text
> EvaluateRepository()
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1087. Typed Procedure
> 
> У каждого узла должны быть:
> 
> ```text
> Inputs
> Outputs
> Capabilities
> Constraints
> Verification
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1088. Example node
> 
> ```yaml
> node:
>   id: inspect_repo
> 
>   action: repository_inspection
> 
>   inputs:
>     - repository_ref
> 
>   outputs:
>     - repository_report
> 
>   requires:
>     - cap_repository_analysis
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1089. Capability-based execution
> 
> Procedure не обязательно говорит:
> 
> ```text
> use exact Tool X
> ```
> 
> Лучше:
> 
> ```text
> REQUIRES capability repository_analysis
> ```
> 
> А Runtime выбирает provider.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1090. Late Binding
> 
> Binding может происходить:
> 
> ```text
> при compile time
> ```
> 
> или:
> 
> ```text
> при runtime
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1091. Compile-time binding
> 
> Использовать, если:
> 
> ```text
> project.lock pins provider
> ```
> 
> например:
> 
> ```text
> GitHubConnector v1.4
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1092. Runtime binding
> 
> Использовать, если допустим выбор:
> 
> ```text
> Provider A
> Provider B
> Provider C
> ```
> 
> по текущей availability/cost.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1093. Procedure Compiler
> 
> Вход:
> 
> ```text
> Task
> Context
> Available capabilities
> Policies
> Packages
> ```
> 
> Выход:
> 
> ```text
> Executable Procedural Graph
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1094. Compiler stages
> 
> ```text
> 1. Task decomposition
> 2. Pattern/archetype lookup
> 3. Capability resolution
> 4. Dependency construction
> 5. Policy insertion
> 6. Verification insertion
> 7. Error paths
> 8. Optimization
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1095. Task decomposition
> 
> Task:
> 
> ```text
> Validate technology X
> ```
> 
> разворачивается:
> 
> ```text
> find evidence
> inspect implementation
> run experiment
> compare requirements
> produce conclusion
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1096. Archetype lookup
> 
> Если существует package:
> 
> ```text
> TechnologyValidationWorkflow
> ```
> 
> compiler использует его вместо генерации с нуля.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1097. Generate only missing pieces
> 
> Лучший принцип:
> 
> ```text
> reuse known procedure
> +
> synthesize only gaps
> ```
> 
> Это делает system более стабильной.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1098. Procedure Archetype
> 
> Примеры:
> 
> ```text
> Research Review
> Repository Evaluation
> Grant Eligibility Check
> Security Review
> Experiment
> Deployment
> Manufacturing Test
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1099. Compiler chooses archetype by Task semantics
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> TASK subtype = SECURITY_REVIEW
> ```
> 
> → candidate:
> 
> ```text
> SecurityReviewProcedure
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1100. Archetype parameterization
> 
> Параметры:
> 
> ```text
> artifact
> risk class
> environment
> deadline
> required evidence
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1101. Capability resolution
> 
> Для каждого node:
> 
> ```text
> What capability is required?
> ```
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> PDF extraction
> ```
> 
> providers:
> 
> ```text
> local package
> remote service
> AI agent
> human
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1102. Policy insertion
> 
> Если Action имеет side effect:
> 
> ```text
> SEND_EMAIL
> ```
> 
> Compiler вставляет:
> 
> ```text
> APPROVAL CHECK
> ```
> 
> перед Action.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1103. Example
> 
> Исходный workflow:
> 
> ```text
> Draft Email
> ↓
> Send Email
> ```
> 
> после policy compilation:
> 
> ```text
> Draft Email
> ↓
> Human Review
> ↓
> Approval
> ↓
> Send Email
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1104. Physical safety insertion
> 
> Workflow:
> 
> ```text
> Run robot task
> ```
> 
> может компилироваться:
> 
> ```text
> Simulation
> ↓
> Safety Check
> ↓
> Human Approval
> ↓
> Physical Execution
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1105. Verification insertion
> 
> Task:
> 
> ```text
> Build parser
> ```
> 
> не заканчивается:
> 
> ```text
> code generated
> ```
> 
> Compiler добавляет:
> 
> ```text
> tests
> schema validation
> human/code review
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1106. DONE_IF contract
> 
> Каждый Task должен иметь:
> 
> ```text
> DONE_IF
> ```
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> parser passes 95% golden fixtures
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1107. Task Completion
> 
> Правило:
> 
> ```text
> Action executed
> ```
> 
> не означает:
> 
> ```text
> Task completed
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1108. Completion pipeline
> 
> ```text
> execute
> ↓
> produce artifact
> ↓
> verify
> ↓
> accept
> ↓
> DONE
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1109. Failure paths
> 
> Каждый risky node должен иметь:
> 
> ```text
> on_failure
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1110. Failure categories
> 
> ```text
> TOOL_FAILURE
> INPUT_INVALID
> CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE
> POLICY_DENIED
> QUALITY_FAILURE
> TIMEOUT
> RESOURCE_UNAVAILABLE
> UNKNOWN
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1111. Different failures require different recovery
> 
> Tool failure:
> 
> ```text
> retry / switch provider
> ```
> 
> Quality failure:
> 
> ```text
> revise output
> ```
> 
> Resource unavailable:
> 
> ```text
> replan
> ```
> 
> Policy denied:
> 
> ```text
> human escalation / alternative method
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1112. Retry policy
> 
> Не:
> 
> ```text
> retry everything 5 times
> ```
> 
> Нужно учитывать failure class.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1113. Transient error
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> HTTP 503
> ```
> 
> → retry.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1114. Deterministic invalid input
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> schema invalid
> ```
> 
> → retrying same input бессмысленно.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1115. Adaptive Workflow
> 
> Procedural Graph может меняться во время выполнения.
> 
> Но не произвольно.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1116. Adaptation triggers
> 
> ```text
> new evidence
> resource unavailable
> task failed
> deadline changed
> constraint changed
> new capability discovered
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1117. Replanning boundary
> 
> Не пересобирать весь Project при каждом событии.
> 
> Определять:
> 
> ```text
> affected subgraph
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1118. Local Replanning
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> Repository A unavailable
> ```
> 
> затрагивает только:
> 
> ```text
> integration branch
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1119. Global Replanning
> 
> Если:
> 
> ```text
> core requirement changed
> ```
> 
> может потребоваться пересборка большого Task Graph.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1120. Replan event
> 
> ```text
> REPLAN_REQUESTED
> ```
> 
> должен содержать:
> 
> ```text
> trigger
> affected nodes
> reason
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1121. Procedure Versioning
> 
> При replanning:
> 
> ```text
> Procedure v3
> →
> Procedure v4
> ```
> 
> Старый graph не стирается.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1122. Running nodes
> 
> При обновлении procedure нужно определить:
> 
> ```text
> что делать уже запущенным Actions?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1123. Safe cases
> 
> Если branch independent:
> 
> ```text
> allow finish
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1124. Unsafe cases
> 
> Если result больше не нужен:
> 
> ```text
> cancel if reversible
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1125. Irreversible action
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> send contract
> manufacture batch
> move robot
> ```
> 
> не может быть просто «отменён».
> 
> Need compensation/recovery.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1126. Side-effect classes
> 
> Freeze:
> 
> ```text
> READ_ONLY
> REVERSIBLE
> COMPENSATABLE
> IRREVERSIBLE
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1127. READ_ONLY
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> search
> read file
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1128. REVERSIBLE
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> create temporary branch
> ```
> 
> can delete/revert.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1129. COMPENSATABLE
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> reserve lab slot
> ```
> 
> can later release.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1130. IRREVERSIBLE
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> physical cutting
> external legal filing
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1131. Compiler uses side-effect class
> 
> Чем выше необратимость:
> 
> ```text
> тем раньше и сильнее approval / simulation / verification
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1132. Procedural Graph node state
> 
> ```text
> PENDING
> READY
> CLAIMED
> RUNNING
> WAITING
> REVIEW
> DONE
> FAILED
> SKIPPED
> CANCELLED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1133. CLAIMED
> 
> Исполнитель резервирует node.
> 
> Это предотвращает:
> 
> ```text
> двойное выполнение
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1134. Lease
> 
> Claim может иметь:
> 
> ```text
> lease_until
> ```
> 
> Если executor исчез:
> 
> ```text
> lease expires
> ```
> 
> node возвращается в READY, если повтор безопасен.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1135. Idempotency
> 
> Каждый repeatable Action должен иметь:
> 
> ```text
> idempotency_key
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1136. Example
> 
> ```text
> Create GitHub issue
> ```
> 
> при retry не должен создать:
> 
> ```text
> 5 одинаковых issues
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1137. At-least-once execution
> 
> Практически реалистичная модель:
> 
> ```text
> event/action may be delivered more than once
> ```
> 
> поэтому actions должны быть repeat-safe.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1138. Exactly-once не нужно обещать
> 
> Лучше:
> 
> ```text
> at-least-once
> +
> idempotency
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1139. Scheduler
> 
> Runtime continuously computes:
> 
> ```text
> which nodes are READY?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1140. Readiness criteria
> 
> Node ready, если:
> 
> ```text
> dependencies satisfied
> inputs available
> provider available
> constraints pass
> required approvals exist
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1141. Scheduler priority
> 
> Можно учитывать:
> 
> ```text
> critical path
> deadline
> resource availability
> project priority
> ```
> 
> но не один opaque score.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1142. Critical Path
> 
> Task Graph позволяет определить:
> 
> ```text
> which tasks delay whole project
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1143. Slack
> 
> Некоторые Tasks могут быть delayed без project delay.
> 
> Runtime может использовать этот запас.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1144. Resource-aware scheduling
> 
> Если два Tasks требуют:
> 
> ```text
> same specialist
> ```
> 
> Scheduler serializes or allocates capacity.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1145. AI resource scheduling
> 
> AI may have:
> 
> ```text
> token budget
> concurrency limit
> rate limit
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1146. Human scheduling
> 
> Для людей учитывать:
> 
> ```text
> availability
> consent
> working hours
> existing assignments
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1147. Physical scheduling
> 
> Для machine:
> 
> ```text
> booking
> setup
> maintenance
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1148. Mixed scheduler
> 
> Таким образом один scheduler видит:
> 
> ```text
> Human
> AI
> Software
> Machine
> Lab
> ```
> 
> через общую Resource/Capability abstraction.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1149. Но execution backends различаются
> 
> Universal scheduler:
> 
> ```text
> assigns work
> ```
> 
> Backend:
> 
> ```text
> executes according to resource type
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1150. Human Backend
> 
> Создаёт:
> 
> ```text
> task card
> context package
> deadline
> required output
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1151. AI Backend
> 
> Создаёт:
> 
> ```text
> prompt/context
> tools
> policies
> output schema
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1152. Tool Backend
> 
> Выполняет:
> 
> ```text
> deterministic API/tool call
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1153. Robot Backend
> 
> Выполняет:
> 
> ```text
> device skill
> ```
> 
> через safety controller.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1154. External Organization Backend
> 
> Создаёт:
> 
> ```text
> federated task proposal
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1155. Backend Interface
> 
> Общий контракт:
> 
> ```text
> prepare()
> execute()
> observe()
> verify()
> cancel()
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1156. Command vs Event
> 
> Compiler creates:
> 
> ```text
> COMMAND
> ```
> 
> Runtime later records:
> 
> ```text
> EVENT
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1157. Example
> 
> Command:
> 
> ```text
> RUN benchmark
> ```
> 
> Event:
> 
> ```text
> BENCHMARK_COMPLETED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1158. Never store command as if it happened
> 
> Это принципиально для audit.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1159. Procedure Inputs
> 
> Node может принимать:
> 
> ```text
> Artifact
> Entity reference
> Claim set
> Scalar value
> Context
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1160. Procedure Outputs
> 
> Могут быть:
> 
> ```text
> Artifact
> Claim
> Evidence
> Event
> Decision proposal
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1161. LLM output
> 
> LLM не должен напрямую менять World State.
> 
> Он produces:
> 
> ```text
> Artifact / Candidate Claims / Proposal
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1162. Structured Output
> 
> По возможности:
> 
> ```text
> Pydantic / JSON Schema
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1163. Validation
> 
> После LLM:
> 
> ```text
> schema
> semantic rules
> constraints
> ```
> 
> перед записью.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1164. Free text remains Artifact
> 
> Если LLM пишет:
> 
> ```text
> analysis
> ```
> 
> это Artifact.
> 
> Любые extracted facts становятся отдельными Claims.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1165. Context Compiler
> 
> Перед каждым node:
> 
> ```text
> Task + state
> ↓
> Context Builder
> ```
> 
> собирает только relevant context.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1166. Не использовать огромную историю чата
> 
> Context Package:
> 
> ```text
> goal
> current task
> inputs
> relevant claims
> constraints
> previous outputs
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1167. Context Budget
> 
> У каждого AI node:
> 
> ```text
> max_context
> ```
> 
> Context Builder prioritizes:
> 
> ```text
> hard constraints
> current artifacts
> critical evidence
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1168. Memory tiers
> 
> ```text
> Scratch
> Working
> Project
> World
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1169. Scratch
> 
> Temporary reasoning/output during one action.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1170. Working
> 
> Current procedure execution.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1171. Project Memory
> 
> Validated project-level Claims/Artifacts.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1172. World Memory
> 
> Cross-project reusable knowledge.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1173. Promotion
> 
> Observation:
> 
> ```text
> scratch
> ↓
> candidate claim
> ↓
> validation
> ↓
> project/world memory
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1174. Procedure Blackboard
> 
> Agents communicate through:
> 
> ```text
> shared structured state
> ```
> 
> not direct endless conversations.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1175. Blackboard contents
> 
> ```text
> Tasks
> Claims
> Artifacts
> Events
> Decisions
> Open Questions
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1176. Agent message
> 
> A message is:
> 
> ```text
> request / proposal / report
> ```
> 
> not automatically fact.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1177. Agent message types
> 
> ```text
> TASK_REQUEST
> TASK_RESULT
> QUESTION
> EVIDENCE_FOUND
> BLOCKER
> REVIEW_REQUEST
> ESCALATION
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1178. Handoff
> 
> When executor changes:
> 
> ```text
> what is done
> what remains
> what artifacts exist
> what blocks progress
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1179. Handoff Package
> 
> ```yaml
> handoff:
>   task: ...
>   completed: [...]
>   remaining: [...]
>   artifacts: [...]
>   blockers: [...]
>   requested_capability: ...
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1180. Parallel Agents
> 
> One task may be decomposed:
> 
> ```text
> Agent A: papers
> Agent B: repos
> Agent C: patents
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1181. Merge
> 
> Their outputs are merged into:
> 
> ```text
> Evidence Set
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1182. No majority-vote truth
> 
> Если A и B disagree:
> 
> ```text
> store conflict
> ```
> 
> Не:
> 
> ```text
> 2 vs 1 → truth
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1183. Conflict Resolution
> 
> Possible nodes:
> 
> ```text
> request evidence
> run experiment
> human expert review
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1184. Adaptive branching by uncertainty
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> confidence high
> → continue
> 
> confidence low
> → additional validation
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1185. UNKNOWN as workflow trigger
> 
> Это очень важно:
> 
> ```text
> UNKNOWN
> ```
> 
> может создавать Action:
> 
> ```text
> Gather Evidence
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1186. Example
> 
> ```text
> Candidate work authorization = UNKNOWN
> ```
> 
> Procedure:
> 
> ```text
> ask candidate
> ```
> 
> rather than reject.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1187. Evidence Acquisition Node
> 
> General pattern:
> 
> ```text
> Question
> ↓
> Source Resolver
> ↓
> Observation
> ↓
> Evidence
> ↓
> Claim Update
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1188. Value of Information
> 
> Если uncertainty не влияет на decision:
> 
> ```text
> не тратить resources
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1189. Example
> 
> Есть два providers.
> 
> Provider A явно дешевле и satisfies all constraints.
> 
> Unknown minor detail about Provider B:
> 
> ```text
> можно не исследовать сейчас
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1190. Procedure Optimization
> 
> Compiler may minimize:
> 
> ```text
> unnecessary checks
> duplicate search
> sequential bottlenecks
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1191. Parallelization
> 
> Independent nodes:
> 
> ```text
> run concurrently
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1192. Dependency detection
> 
> Но не parallelize:
> 
> ```text
> test artifact
> ```
> 
> до:
> 
> ```text
> artifact created
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1193. Speculative execution
> 
> Low-risk branch can start early.
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> research alternatives
> ```
> 
> while primary implementation running.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1194. But speculative physical/external actions require stronger restrictions
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1195. Cancellation
> 
> Speculative branch can be cancelled when no longer needed.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1196. Procedure Cost Estimate
> 
> Before execution:
> 
> ```text
> AI cost
> human hours
> API cost
> lab cost
> ```
> 
> can be estimated.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1197. Runtime Cost
> 
> Actual usage is recorded.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1198. Procedure comparison
> 
> Two possible procedures:
> 
> ```text
> Procedure A:
> more AI
> less human
> 
> Procedure B:
> more human
> less compute
> ```
> 
> Can compare:
> 
> ```text
> cost
> time
> risk
> control
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1199. Procedure Planner should not select by price only
> 
> Depending context:
> 
> ```text
> privacy
> quality
> reliability
> authority
> ```
> 
> matter.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1200. Procedural Archetype Library
> 
> Useful initial set:
> 
> ```text
> RESEARCH
> COMPARE
> VALIDATE
> BUILD
> TEST
> REVIEW
> DEPLOY
> MONITOR
> MIGRATE
> PROCURE
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1201. RESEARCH
> 
> ```text
> define question
> search
> collect evidence
> synthesize
> identify unknowns
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1202. COMPARE
> 
> ```text
> define criteria
> collect alternatives
> normalize evidence
> compare dimensions
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1203. VALIDATE
> 
> ```text
> define claim
> define acceptance criteria
> run check/experiment
> collect evidence
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1204. BUILD
> 
> ```text
> specify
> implement
> test
> review
> package
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1205. DEPLOY
> 
> ```text
> prepare
> backup
> deploy
> health check
> rollback if failed
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1206. MONITOR
> 
> ```text
> observe
> detect condition
> emit event
> possibly trigger workflow
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1207. MIGRATE
> 
> ```text
> inventory
> mapping
> dry run
> migration
> verification
> rollback path
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1208. PROCURE
> 
> ```text
> requirements
> vendors
> quotes
> comparison
> decision
> purchase
> acceptance
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1209. Procedure Package Registry
> 
> Procedures themselves могут быть packages.
> 
> То есть:
> 
> ```text
> Workflow Package
> ```
> 
> из предыдущего модуля именно здесь исполняется.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1210. Procedure Reuse
> 
> Если:
> 
> ```text
> Security Review Procedure v4
> ```
> 
> успешно использовалась 100 раз,
> 
> не генерировать новую каждый раз.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1211. Procedure Evolution
> 
> При recurring failures:
> 
> ```text
> propose v5
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1212. Procedure Gold Dataset
> 
> Store:
> 
> ```text
> task type
> procedure version
> outcome
> cost
> time
> failure reasons
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1213. Procedure Benchmark
> 
> Можно сравнивать:
> 
> ```text
> Workflow A
> Workflow B
> ```
> 
> на standard fixtures.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1214. But real context matters
> 
> Benchmark result not universal.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1215. Adaptive Procedure Selection
> 
> Runtime can choose procedure based on:
> 
> ```text
> risk
> deadline
> available resources
> project stage
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1216. Example
> 
> Research stage:
> 
> ```text
> fast lightweight review
> ```
> 
> Production decision:
> 
> ```text
> deep verified review
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1217. Procedure Fidelity Levels
> 
> ```text
> FAST
> STANDARD
> HIGH_ASSURANCE
> ```
> 
> application-level archetype.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1218. FAST
> 
> For:
> 
> ```text
> exploration
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1219. HIGH_ASSURANCE
> 
> For:
> 
> ```text
> security
> legal
> physical safety
> critical deployment
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1220. Verification intensity scales with risk
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1221. Procedural Graph + n8n / Make
> 
> n8n/Make can execute deterministic portions:
> 
> ```text
> Trigger
> ↓
> API
> ↓
> Transform
> ↓
> Store
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1222. But n8n workflow is backend representation
> 
> Source of truth:
> 
> ```text
> Procedural Graph
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1223. Compiler Backend
> 
> ```text
> Procedural Graph
> ↓
> n8n compiler
> ```
> 
> can generate workflow definition.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1224. Other backends
> 
> ```text
> Make
> Python
> Temporal
> Airflow
> GitHub Actions
> Robot controller
> Human task system
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1225. One procedure, many backends
> 
> This is crucial.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1226. n8n good for
> 
> ```text
> API integrations
> deterministic automation
> business workflows
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1227. Python good for
> 
> ```text
> custom computation
> ML
> complex control
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1228. Agent Runtime good for
> 
> ```text
> semantic reasoning
> unstructured research
> adaptive planning
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1229. Human good for
> 
> ```text
> authority
> judgment
> negotiation
> physical/creative work
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1230. Robot controller good for
> 
> ```text
> real-time physical execution
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1231. Backend Router
> 
> For every Procedure Node:
> 
> ```text
> which backend can execute?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1232. Backend selection
> 
> Based on:
> 
> ```text
> capability
> permissions
> latency
> cost
> risk
> availability
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1233. Semantic syscall
> 
> Conceptually:
> 
> ```text
> REQUEST_CAPABILITY(
>     capability,
>     inputs,
>     constraints
> )
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1234. Example
> 
> ```text
> REQUEST_CAPABILITY(
>   translate_document,
>   input=document_17,
>   constraints={DE→RU, confidential}
> )
> ```
> 
> Runtime may choose:
> 
> ```text
> local model
> human translator
> approved service
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1235. This decouples Project from provider
> 
> Очень сильное свойство architecture.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1236. Procedure Graph Compiler phases
> 
> More formal:
> 
> ```text
> Semantic Expansion
> ↓
> Type Check
> ↓
> Dependency Resolution
> ↓
> Policy Compilation
> ↓
> Provider Resolution
> ↓
> Verification Compilation
> ↓
> Optimization
> ↓
> Executable Graph
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1237. Semantic Expansion
> 
> High-level:
> 
> ```text
> VALIDATE_REPOSITORY
> ```
> 
> expands into known subgraph.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1238. Type Check
> 
> Check:
> 
> ```text
> outputs fit inputs
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1239. Dependency Resolution
> 
> Find:
> 
> ```text
> required packages/resources
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1240. Policy Compilation
> 
> Insert:
> 
> ```text
> approval/security/privacy nodes
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1241. Provider Resolution
> 
> Bind capabilities.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1242. Verification Compilation
> 
> Add tests/checks.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1243. Optimization
> 
> Parallelization/batching/reuse.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1244. Executable Graph
> 
> Immutable revision used by Runtime.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1245. Compile Error
> 
> If no provider:
> 
> ```text
> CAPABILITY_UNRESOLVED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1246. Compile Error can create Gap
> 
> Then Capability Market searches provider.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1247. Package Resolution during compile
> 
> If provider installable:
> 
> ```text
> Package Manager
> ```
> 
> may propose install.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1248. Recursive compilation
> 
> Task requires package.
> 
> Package requires setup.
> 
> Setup becomes subprocedure.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1249. Guard against infinite recursion
> 
> Compiler maintains:
> 
> ```text
> resolution stack
> ```
> 
> detecting cycles.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1250. Procedure Graph as DAG?
> 
> Mostly yes.
> 
> But loops exist.
> 
> So better:
> 
> ```text
> directed graph
> ```
> 
> with controlled loop constructs.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1251. Avoid arbitrary cycles
> 
> Cycles should be represented explicitly as:
> 
> ```text
> LOOP node
> ```
> 
> rather than hidden dependency cycle.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1252. Loop termination
> 
> Every loop should have:
> 
> ```text
> exit condition
> max iterations
> timeout
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1253. Example iterative refinement
> 
> ```text
> Generate draft
> ↓
> Review
> ↓
> quality pass?
>  ├─ yes → DONE
>  └─ no → revise
> ```
> 
> with max iterations.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1254. Infinite agent loop prevention
> 
> Mandatory:
> 
> ```text
> budget
> iteration limit
> progress check
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1255. Progress invariant
> 
> Each loop should produce:
> 
> ```text
> new evidence
> new artifact version
> state change
> ```
> 
> otherwise detect stagnation.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1256. Stagnation Event
> 
> ```text
> PROCEDURE_STALLED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1257. Escalation
> 
> Then:
> 
> ```text
> switch method
> switch provider
> human intervention
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1258. Long-running procedures
> 
> Some tasks last:
> 
> ```text
> days
> weeks
> months
> ```
> 
> Runtime must support durable state.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1259. Durable Wait
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> WAIT until grant decision
> ```
> 
> No process should sit in memory for 3 months.
> 
> State persisted.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1260. Condition Watch
> 
> ```text
> WAIT UNTIL condition
> ```
> 
> Examples:
> 
> ```text
> new release appears
> funding call opens
> lab slot available
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1261. Time trigger
> 
> ```text
> WAIT UNTIL 2026-10-01
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1262. Event trigger
> 
> ```text
> WAIT UNTIL RESOURCE_AVAILABLE
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1263. Procedure resumption
> 
> After Event:
> 
> ```text
> resume affected node
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1264. Deadline
> 
> Each Task/node can have:
> 
> ```text
> deadline
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1265. Deadline Risk
> 
> Runtime predicts:
> 
> ```text
> current trajectory threatens deadline
> ```
> 
> then emits:
> 
> ```text
> DEADLINE_RISK
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1266. Corrective options
> 
> ```text
> parallelize
> add resource
> simplify scope
> switch provider
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1267. Procedure Simulation
> 
> Before execution:
> 
> ```text
> simulate resource/time graph
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1268. Simulation predicts
> 
> ```text
> critical path
> resource conflicts
> possible deadlocks
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1269. Shadow Runtime
> 
> Entire project procedure can run:
> 
> ```text
> proposal-only
> ```
> 
> without side effects.
> 
> Useful for validating Agent OS.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1270. Replay
> 
> Given:
> 
> ```text
> Event Log
> Artifacts
> Procedure Version
> ```
> 
> system can replay decision/state logic.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1271. External side effects not replayed
> 
> Instead:
> 
> ```text
> mocked/simulated
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1272. Deterministic state transitions
> 
> Where possible:
> 
> ```text
> same events
> → same state
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1273. LLM non-determinism
> 
> LLM output stored as Artifact.
> 
> Replay can:
> 
> ```text
> reuse original output
> ```
> 
> rather than regenerate.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1274. Reproducibility
> 
> This allows forensic analysis:
> 
> ```text
> why did project branch here?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1275. Procedure Trace
> 
> Every execution has:
> 
> ```text
> trace_id
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1276. Trace contains
> 
> ```text
> nodes executed
> providers used
> inputs/outputs
> events
> timing
> cost
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1277. Distributed Trace
> 
> Across federation:
> 
> ```text
> correlation_id
> ```
> 
> links remote task execution.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1278. Observability
> 
> Dashboard can show:
> 
> ```text
> READY
> RUNNING
> WAITING
> BLOCKED
> FAILED
> ```
> 
> nodes.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1279. Procedure Heatmap
> 
> Highlight:
> 
> ```text
> slow nodes
> failure-prone nodes
> high-cost nodes
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1280. Process Mining
> 
> After many executions:
> 
> ```text
> actual execution traces
> ```
> 
> can reveal:
> 
> ```text
> real workflow differs from designed workflow
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1281. Actual Path
> 
> Example intended:
> 
> ```text
> A→B→C
> ```
> 
> Observed:
> 
> ```text
> A→B→D→B→C
> ```
> 
> because rework common.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1282. Procedure Improvement Opportunity
> 
> Repeated:
> 
> ```text
> B→D→B
> ```
> 
> may mean:
> 
> ```text
> B lacks validation
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1283. Procedural Debt
> 
> Repeated workarounds can form:
> 
> ```text
> Procedural Debt
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1284. Procedure Refactoring
> 
> Possible interventions:
> 
> ```text
> automate
> merge steps
> split step
> insert verification earlier
> change provider
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1285. Workflow Evolution
> 
> ```text
> v1 manual
> v2 semi-automated
> v3 agent-assisted
> v4 mostly automated
> ```
> 
> while semantic goal stays constant.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1286. Automation Gradient
> 
> Не всё должно быть fully automated.
> 
> Possible:
> 
> ```text
> H0 Human-only
> H1 AI suggests
> H2 AI prepares
> H3 AI executes reversible
> H4 bounded automation
> H5 machine-only within policy
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1287. Autonomy belongs to Action × Context
> 
> Не просто:
> 
> ```text
> Agent has autonomy level 4
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1288. Example
>

> # 1351. Следующий фундаментальный слой
> 
> После появления Procedural Graph Compiler возникает следующий вопрос:
> 
> > Как система должна управлять целями, приоритетами и конфликтующими стратегическими намерениями, если одновременно существуют тысячи проектов и workflows?
> 
> Следующий модуль:
> 
> # **Goal, Policy & Governance Engine v0.1**
> 
> Он должен формализовать:
> 
> ```text
> кто задаёт цели;
> какие цели обязательны;
> какие цели конфликтуют;
> кто имеет право принимать решения;
> какие действия запрещены;
> где требуется согласование;
> как стратегия превращается в ограничения для Project/Procedure Compiler;
> как человек может остановить, изменить или отменить автоматическое выполнение.
> ```
> 
> Это будет слой, который окончательно отделяет **интеллект и автоматизацию** от **власти, полномочий и целей** — критически важный элемент для безопасной работы всей архитектуры.

Следующая часть логично будет посвящена **Goal, Policy & Governance Engine v0.1**: именно он определит, кто вправе ставить системе цели, какие цели могут исполняться автоматически, где требуется человек, как разрешать конфликт «быстрее / дешевле / безопаснее / открытее» и как управлять всей системой без превращения AI в самостоятельный источник целей.

# chatgpt response

Продолжаю полностью на русском языке. Теперь переходим к **Goal, Policy & Governance Engine v0.1** — слою, который определяет не «как выполнить задачу», а **кто вправе ставить цели, какие ограничения обязательны, где требуется человеческое решение и как разрешать конфликты между скоростью, стоимостью, безопасностью, открытостью и другими приоритетами**.

> **Document: Goal, Policy & Governance Engine v0.1**
> 
> # Goal, Policy & Governance Engine v0.1
> 
> ## 1352. Главный переход
> 
> До этого Innovation OS уже умеет:
> 
> ```text
> Goal
> ↓
> Project IR
> ↓
> Task Graph
> ↓
> Procedural Graph
> ↓
> Resource Resolution
> ↓
> Execution
> ```
> 
> Но остаётся принципиальный вопрос:
> 
> > Откуда сама Goal взялась и кто имеет право её утвердить?
> 
> AI может:
> 
> ```text
> обнаружить проблему
> предложить opportunity
> создать project hypothesis
> сформировать procedure
> ```
> 
> Но это ещё не означает:
> 
> ```text
> система получила право действовать
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1353. Разделение интеллекта и власти
> 
> Это один из важнейших принципов всей архитектуры.
> 
> ```text
> INTELLIGENCE
> может:
> анализировать
> предлагать
> моделировать
> объяснять
> ```
> 
> Но:
> 
> ```text
> AUTHORITY
> определяет:
> что разрешено
> что обязательно
> кто может принять решение
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1354. Основная формула
> 
> ```text
> Observation
> ↓
> Analysis
> ↓
> Proposal
> ↓
> Governance
> ↓
> Decision
> ↓
> Authorized Goal
> ↓
> Execution
> ```
> 
> То есть:
> 
> ```text
> AI proposal ≠ authorized objective
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1355. Goal
> 
> Goal — желаемое состояние мира.
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> Reduce average grant-processing time.
> ```
> 
> или:
> 
> ```text
> Develop secure agent runtime.
> ```
> 
> или:
> 
> ```text
> Increase robotics testing capacity.
> ```
> 
> В IIR Core Goal можно хранить как:
> 
> ```text
> CLAIM
> with modality = DESIRED
> ```
> 
> или как archetype поверх Claim.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1356. Goal Claim
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```yaml
> goal:
>   subject: project_x
>   desired_state:
>     secure_runtime_available: true
> 
>   success_criteria:
>     benchmark_passed: true
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1357. Goal ≠ Task
> 
> Goal:
> 
> ```text
> что хотим получить
> ```
> 
> Task:
> 
> ```text
> что нужно сделать
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1358. Goal ≠ Metric
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> Goal:
> Improve reliability.
> ```
> 
> Metric:
> 
> ```text
> failure_rate < 1%
> ```
> 
> Metric помогает проверить Goal, но не заменяет её.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1359. Goal hierarchy
> 
> Useful structure:
> 
> ```text
> Mission
> ↓
> Strategic Goals
> ↓
> Program Goals
> ↓
> Project Goals
> ↓
> Task Outcomes
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1360. Mission
> 
> Mission — самый высокий устойчивый уровень.
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> Improve accessibility of scientific infrastructure.
> ```
> 
> Она может существовать годы.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1361. Strategic Goal
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> Create shared robotics test infrastructure in 3 years.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1362. Program Goal
> 
> ```text
> Build common tactile-sensing platform.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1363. Project Goal
> 
> ```text
> Validate optical-fiber tactile prototype.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1364. Task Outcome
> 
> ```text
> Produce validated durability dataset.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1365. Goal dependency
> 
> Одна Goal может:
> 
> ```text
> ENABLE
> ```
> 
> другую.
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> Build benchmark
> ↓
> enables
> Compare methods
> ↓
> enables
> Select technology
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1366. Goal Conflict
> 
> Goals могут конфликтовать.
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> Goal A:
> minimize cost
> ```
> 
> и:
> 
> ```text
> Goal B:
> maximize redundancy
> ```
> 
> или:
> 
> ```text
> Goal A:
> publish everything openly
> ```
> 
> и:
> 
> ```text
> Goal B:
> protect confidential partner data
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1367. Не решать конфликт одной функцией score
> 
> Лучше показать:
> 
> ```text
> какие цели конфликтуют
> какие constraints затронуты
> какие варианты существуют
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1368. Goal Priority
> 
> Priority может быть:
> 
> ```text
> CRITICAL
> HIGH
> NORMAL
> EXPLORATORY
> ```
> 
> но это governance field, а не объективная ценность Goal.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1369. Goal Source
> 
> Очень важно хранить:
> 
> ```text
> who/what proposed the goal?
> ```
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> HUMAN
> ORGANIZATION
> POLICY
> PROJECT
> AI_HYPOTHESIS
> EVENT
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1370. Proposed Goal
> 
> AI может создать:
> 
> ```text
> Goal Proposal
> ```
> 
> например:
> 
> ```text
> Create shared security service.
> ```
> 
> Но state:
> 
> ```text
> PROPOSED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1371. Goal lifecycle
> 
> Freeze:
> 
> ```text
> PROPOSED
> UNDER_REVIEW
> APPROVED
> ACTIVE
> PAUSED
> ACHIEVED
> REJECTED
> CANCELLED
> SUPERSEDED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1372. Goal approval
> 
> Для перехода:
> 
> ```text
> PROPOSED → APPROVED
> ```
> 
> нужен:
> 
> ```text
> DECISION
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1373. Authority
> 
> Теперь появляется центральное понятие:
> 
> ```text
> кто имеет право принимать какой тип решения?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1374. Authority Scope
> 
> Пример:
> 
> ```text
> Project Lead
> can approve:
> project scope
> ```
> 
> ```text
> Security Officer
> can approve:
> security exception
> ```
> 
> ```text
> Finance Officer
> can approve:
> budget increase
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1375. Authority ≠ Capability
> 
> Человек может иметь capability:
> 
> ```text
> security expertise
> ```
> 
> но не иметь authority:
> 
> ```text
> approve production deployment
> ```
> 
> И наоборот.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1376. Responsibility ≠ Authority
> 
> Можно быть:
> 
> ```text
> responsible for preparing decision
> ```
> 
> но не:
> 
> ```text
> authorized to approve it
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1377. Execution ≠ Accountability
> 
> AI agent может выполнить analysis.
> 
> Human may remain accountable for:
> 
> ```text
> final decision
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1378. Governance Roles
> 
> Application-level archetypes:
> 
> ```text
> OWNER
> APPROVER
> EXECUTOR
> REVIEWER
> OBSERVER
> AUDITOR
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1379. OWNER
> 
> Отвечает за:
> 
> ```text
> goal / resource / project
> ```
> 
> на уровне управления.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1380. APPROVER
> 
> Может сделать Decision authoritative.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1381. EXECUTOR
> 
> Может выполнить Action.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1382. REVIEWER
> 
> Может проверить Artifact/Claim.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1383. OBSERVER
> 
> Имеет read access.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1384. AUDITOR
> 
> Может анализировать историю и compliance.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1385. Один Resource может иметь несколько ролей
> 
> Но для high-risk процессов желательно разделение.
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> executor ≠ approver
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1386. Separation of Duties
> 
> Критические процессы могут требовать:
> 
> ```text
> one person prepares
> another approves
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1387. Example
> 
> Payment:
> 
> ```text
> AI prepares transaction
> Human A reviews
> Human B approves
> Payment adapter executes
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1388. Multi-Approval
> 
> Для особо критических actions:
> 
> ```text
> 2 of 3 approvals
> ```
> 
> или:
> 
> ```text
> all required authorities
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1389. Approval Policy
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```yaml
> approval:
>   action_type: PHYSICAL_IRREVERSIBLE
>   required_roles:
>     - SAFETY_OFFICER
>     - OPERATOR
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1390. Policy
> 
> Policy определяет:
> 
> ```text
> что разрешено
> что запрещено
> что требует approval
> что требует review
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1391. Policy Effects
> 
> Freeze:
> 
> ```text
> ALLOW
> DENY
> REQUIRE_APPROVAL
> REQUIRE_REVIEW
> REQUIRE_EVIDENCE
> REQUIRE_SIMULATION
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1392. Policy Rule
> 
> ```yaml
> policy:
>   if:
>     action.side_effect_class: IRREVERSIBLE
> 
>   then:
>     effect: REQUIRE_APPROVAL
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1393. Deny-by-default vs allow-by-default
> 
> Для low-risk read operations можно использовать:
> 
> ```text
> allow-by-policy
> ```
> 
> Для privileged actions лучше:
> 
> ```text
> deny-by-default
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1394. Policy Scope
> 
> Policy may apply to:
> 
> ```text
> organization
> project
> resource
> action type
> capability
> context
> jurisdiction
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1395. Policy Hierarchy
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> Federation Policy
> ↓
> Organization Policy
> ↓
> Program Policy
> ↓
> Project Policy
> ↓
> Action Policy
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1396. Policy precedence
> 
> Нельзя просто сказать:
> 
> ```text
> lower level overrides higher
> ```
> 
> Для v0.1 лучше консервативно:
> 
> ```text
> DENY dominates ALLOW
> ```
> 
> если нет explicit exception authority.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1397. Exception
> 
> Exception itself must be:
> 
> ```text
> Decision
> ```
> 
> with:
> 
> ```text
> authority
> reason
> validity period
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1398. Temporary Exception
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> Allow external service
> until 2026-12-31
> for Project X only.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1399. Exception expiration
> 
> После:
> 
> ```text
> valid_to
> ```
> 
> policy returns to default automatically.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1400. Policy conflict
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> Organization:
> external cloud prohibited
> ```
> 
> Project:
> 
> ```text
> external cloud preferred
> ```
> 
> Result:
> 
> ```text
> DENY
> ```
> 
> unless authorized exception exists.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1401. Policy Compiler
> 
> Before execution:
> 
> ```text
> Action
> +
> Context
> +
> Actor
> +
> Target
> ↓
> Policy Engine
> ↓
> Decision
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1402. Policy Decision
> 
> Output:
> 
> ```text
> ALLOW
> DENY
> APPROVAL_REQUIRED
> REVIEW_REQUIRED
> ```
> 
> with explanation.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1403. Explainability
> 
> Policy engine should answer:
> 
> ```text
> Denied because:
> Policy SEC-17
> applies to external network write
> in confidential Project X.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1404. Policy as code, but readable
> 
> Policy should have machine-readable form.
> 
> Но также:
> 
> ```text
> human-readable explanation
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1405. Goal → Policy interaction
> 
> Goal cannot override policy automatically.
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> Goal:
> Finish today.
> ```
> 
> does not authorize:
> 
> ```text
> bypass security review.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1406. Constraint vs Policy
> 
> Constraint:
> 
> ```text
> Project must be under €100k.
> ```
> 
> Policy:
> 
> ```text
> Any budget > €50k requires CFO approval.
> ```
> 
> Разные функции.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1407. Policy vs Preference
> 
> Preference:
> 
> ```text
> prefer open source
> ```
> 
> Policy:
> 
> ```text
> proprietary software prohibited
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1408. Governance Decision
> 
> Decision should include:
> 
> ```text
> question
> options
> selected option
> authority
> evidence
> reason
> time
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1409. Decision record
> 
> ```yaml
> decision:
>   question:
>     Which sandbox provider should Project X use?
> 
>   selected:
>     provider_B
> 
>   authority:
>     project_lead
> 
>   evidence:
>     - benchmark_17
>     - security_review_4
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1410. Decision rationale
> 
> Not mandatory for trivial choices.
> 
> But for significant decisions useful:
> 
> ```text
> why?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1411. Decision provenance
> 
> Need know:
> 
> ```text
> what information was available at decision time?
> ```
> 
> This is crucial for audit.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1412. Decision Snapshot
> 
> Store:
> 
> ```text
> relevant claims
> evidence versions
> policy versions
> ```
> 
> used in Decision.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1413. Decision can become stale
> 
> If critical evidence changes:
> 
> ```text
> Decision may require review.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1414. Decision dependency graph
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> Decision B
> DEPENDS_ON
> Claim X
> ```
> 
> If Claim X refuted:
> 
> ```text
> Decision B
> → REVIEW_REQUIRED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1415. Decision Review Trigger
> 
> Events:
> 
> ```text
> EVIDENCE_INVALIDATED
> POLICY_CHANGED
> RESOURCE_UNAVAILABLE
> ASSUMPTION_REFUTED
> ```
> 
> can reopen Decision.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1416. Approved ≠ eternal
> 
> This is very important.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1417. Strategy lock
> 
> Earlier introduced:
> 
> ```text
> strategy.lock
> ```
> 
> can store high-level approved choices.
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> open-source-first
> EU data residency
> human approval for external outreach
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1418. Strategy lock is not every policy
> 
> It stores:
> 
> ```text
> selected strategic commitments
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1419. Strategy vs Policy
> 
> Strategy:
> 
> ```text
> prefer sovereign infrastructure
> ```
> 
> Policy:
> 
> ```text
> production data must remain in EU
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1420. Strategy Goal
> 
> Strategic Goal may drive:
> 
> ```text
> project priorities
> investment
> capability development
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1421. Goal decomposition
> 
> Strategic Goal:
> 
> ```text
> Reduce external dependency.
> ```
> 
> can produce candidate subgoals:
> 
> ```text
> deploy local model
> train internal team
> replace proprietary service
> ```
> 
> But these remain proposals until approved.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1422. Goal Compiler
> 
> Input:
> 
> ```text
> Approved Goal
> ```
> 
> Output:
> 
> ```text
> candidate Programs / Projects
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1423. Goal Compiler ≠ Procedure Compiler
> 
> Goal Compiler:
> 
> ```text
> Goal → Projects
> ```
> 
> Procedure Compiler:
> 
> ```text
> Task → Actions
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1424. Goal feasibility
> 
> Before approval, system can estimate:
> 
> ```text
> capability gaps
> resources
> budget
> time
> risks
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1425. Goal conflict detector
> 
> For all active goals:
> 
> ```text
> shared resource conflict
> policy conflict
> logical conflict
> schedule conflict
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1426. Logical conflict
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> Goal A:
> all software open source
> ```
> 
> and:
> 
> ```text
> Goal B:
> use mandatory proprietary vendor X
> ```
> 
> cannot both be fully satisfied.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1427. Resource conflict
> 
> Two high-priority goals both require:
> 
> ```text
> same scarce lab
> same month
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1428. Policy conflict
> 
> Goal requires Action prohibited by current policy.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1429. Schedule conflict
> 
> Goal A:
> 
> ```text
> deadline October
> ```
> 
> Goal B consumes critical resource until December.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1430. Conflict Resolution Package
> 
> System should present:
> 
> ```text
> conflict
> affected goals
> available options
> consequences
> ```
> 
> Not secretly resolve strategic trade-off.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1431. Example options
> 
> ```text
> delay Goal A
> increase capacity
> reduce scope
> change provider
> cancel Goal B
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1432. Human/Policy decision
> 
> Selects option.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1433. Objective dimensions
> 
> Governance may care about:
> 
> ```text
> cost
> speed
> quality
> safety
> privacy
> control
> open source
> resilience
> scientific value
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1434. No universal objective function
> 
> Different organizations/projects choose different weights or hard constraints.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1435. Objective Profile
> 
> Application object:
> 
> ```yaml
> objective_profile:
>   minimize_cost: preference
>   maximize_resilience: high
>   EU_data_residency: hard
>   open_source: preferred
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1436. Objective Profile guides optimization
> 
> Capability Market and Simulator can use it.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1437. Hard vs Soft objectives
> 
> Hard:
> 
> ```text
> must never violate
> ```
> 
> Soft:
> 
> ```text
> optimize if possible
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1438. Goal Satisfaction
> 
> Need define measurable criteria.
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> Goal:
> Improve proposal turnaround.
> ```
> 
> Success:
> 
> ```text
> median lead time < 5 days
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1439. Multi-criteria success
> 
> Goal may require:
> 
> ```text
> latency < 5 days
> quality >= threshold
> no budget increase > 20%
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1440. Success Criteria as Claims/Constraints
> 
> Reusable in verification.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1441. Partial Goal Satisfaction
> 
> Some goals can be:
> 
> ```text
> PARTIALLY_ACHIEVED
> ```
> 
> at application layer.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1442. Goal abandonment
> 
> If assumptions invalid:
> 
> ```text
> CANCELLED
> ```
> 
> or:
> 
> ```text
> SUPERSEDED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1443. Kill Criteria
> 
> Useful before project begins.
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> If benchmark < threshold
> after 3 iterations,
> stop project.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1444. Kill criteria prevent sunk-cost continuation
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1445. Escalation Policy
> 
> When runtime encounters:
> 
> ```text
> unknown
> failure
> conflict
> ```
> 
> it needs know:
> 
> ```text
> who should decide?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1446. Escalation Chain
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> AI Agent
> ↓
> Reviewer
> ↓
> Project Lead
> ↓
> Program Lead
> ↓
> Executive Authority
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1447. Escalation by domain
> 
> Security:
> 
> ```text
> Security Officer
> ```
> 
> Legal:
> 
> ```text
> Legal Reviewer
> ```
> 
> Finance:
> 
> ```text
> Finance Authority
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1448. Escalation by impact
> 
> Low impact:
> 
> ```text
> automated resolution
> ```
> 
> High impact:
> 
> ```text
> human authority
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1449. Escalation timeout
> 
> If decision not made:
> 
> ```text
> Task may remain WAITING
> ```
> 
> or:
> 
> ```text
> fallback policy
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1450. No silent timeout approval
> 
> Very important:
> 
> ```text
> No response
> ≠
> approval
> ```
> 
> unless explicit policy says otherwise.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1451. Human Override
> 
> Authorized human can:
> 
> ```text
> pause
> cancel
> rebind
> change scope
> override recommendation
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1452. Override Event
> 
> Every override recorded:
> 
> ```text
> HUMAN_OVERRIDE
> ```
> 
> with:
> 
> ```text
> authority
> reason
> scope
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1453. Emergency Stop
> 
> Critical systems need:
> 
> ```text
> STOP
> ```
> 
> that bypasses normal workflow.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1454. Kill Switch
> 
> For:
> 
> ```text
> physical devices
> external communications
> financial actions
> high-cost agent loops
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1455. Safe State
> 
> After emergency stop:
> 
> ```text
> what should system do?
> ```
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> robot → stop motion
> workflow → no new actions
> AI agents → read-only
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1456. Governance mode
> 
> Useful operating modes:
> 
> ```text
> OBSERVE_ONLY
> ADVISORY
> SUPERVISED
> BOUNDED_AUTONOMY
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1457. OBSERVE_ONLY
> 
> System only:
> 
> ```text
> collects
> analyzes
> reports
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1458. ADVISORY
> 
> Also:
> 
> ```text
> proposes actions
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1459. SUPERVISED
> 
> Executes after explicit approval.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1460. BOUNDED_AUTONOMY
> 
> Can automatically execute pre-authorized reversible actions inside limits.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1461. Governance mode can differ by capability
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> research search → bounded autonomy
> ```
> 
> ```text
> email sending → supervised
> ```
> 
> ```text
> money transfer → supervised/high assurance
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1462. Autonomy Budget
> 
> Could constrain:
> 
> ```text
> max monetary impact
> max external calls
> max compute
> max runtime
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1463. Example
> 
> AI may spend automatically:
> 
> ```text
> up to €10 compute/day
> ```
> 
> but above:
> 
> ```text
> approval required
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1464. Scope Boundary
> 
> Agent may act only within:
> 
> ```text
> Project X
> ```
> 
> not global organization.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1465. Permission as capability token
> 
> Earlier semantic capability token now gains governance context:
> 
> ```text
> Actor
> may perform Capability C
> on Resource R
> within Context X
> until T
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1466. Delegation
> 
> Authority may be delegated.
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> Project Lead delegates
> approval up to €1,000
> to Team Lead
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1467. Delegation must be explicit
> 
> Fields:
> 
> ```text
> delegator
> delegate
> scope
> limits
> validity
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1468. Delegation cannot exceed original authority
> 
> If A lacks authority:
> 
> ```text
> A cannot delegate it.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1469. Revocation
> 
> Delegation can be revoked.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1470. Governance Graph
> 
> Entities:
> 
> ```text
> People
> Roles
> Organizations
> Projects
> Policies
> Decisions
> ```
> 
> relations describe authority.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1471. Authority Query
> 
> Runtime can ask:
> 
> ```text
> Who can approve Action X
> in Project Y?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1472. Governance Resolver
> 
> Finds:
> 
> ```text
> eligible approvers
> ```
> 
> according to policy.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1473. Multiple authorities
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> legal + finance
> ```
> 
> both required.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1474. Governance availability
> 
> Approver can be:
> 
> ```text
> unavailable
> ```
> 
> Then:
> 
> ```text
> delegation / escalation
> ```
> 
> may apply.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1475. Governance bottleneck
> 
> An organization can become blocked because:
> 
> ```text
> one person approves everything
> ```
> 
> This is structural bottleneck.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1476. Governance Capacity
> 
> Even approval is a capability with capacity.
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> Security Officer:
> 10 reviews/week
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1477. Governance Market?
> 
> Not monetary, but approval demand can also be modeled as:
> 
> ```text
> Task REQUIRES approval capability
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1478. Approval delegation can resolve queues
> 
> But must respect authority rules.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1479. Policy Simulation
> 
> Before adopting a new policy:
> 
> ```text
> simulate impact
> ```
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> Require human approval
> for every external API call.
> ```
> 
> Simulation may show:
> 
> ```text
> massive queue
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1480. Governance Counterfactual
> 
> Compare:
> 
> ```text
> strict centralized approval
> ```
> 
> vs:
> 
> ```text
> bounded delegation
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1481. Policy impact dimensions
> 
> ```text
> risk reduction
> latency
> human workload
> automation level
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1482. Policy Debt
> 
> Old policy may no longer fit current technology.
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> every deployment manually signed by one person
> ```
> 
> with 1000 deployments/day.
> 
> This creates:
> 
> ```text
> Governance Debt
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1483. Governance Refactoring
> 
> Possible:
> 
> ```text
> delegate
> automate low-risk approval
> introduce threshold
> create new review unit
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1484. Policy Lifecycle
> 
> ```text
> DRAFT
> REVIEW
> ACTIVE
> SUSPENDED
> RETIRED
> SUPERSEDED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1485. Policy versioning
> 
> Every Action records:
> 
> ```text
> which policy version authorized it
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1486. Policy changes do not rewrite history
> 
> Past Actions remain evaluated under past policy version.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1487. Compliance
> 
> Compliance means:
> 
> ```text
> did execution obey applicable policies?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1488. Compliance Check
> 
> Can run:
> 
> ```text
> before action
> during action
> after action
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1489. Pre-action
> 
> ```text
> is action allowed?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1490. During action
> 
> For long-running process:
> 
> ```text
> did constraints change?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1491. Post-action
> 
> ```text
> was required evidence/audit produced?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1492. Compliance Artifact
> 
> System can generate:
> 
> ```text
> Audit Report
> ```
> 
> from events/decisions/policies.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1493. Policy-as-Constraint Compilation
> 
> Some policies can compile directly into constraints.
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> no non-EU data storage
> ```
> 
> becomes:
> 
> ```text
> data_location IN EU
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1494. But not all policies are simple constraints
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> high-risk action requires two approvals
> ```
> 
> needs workflow semantics.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1495. Governance Compiler
> 
> Pipeline:
> 
> ```text
> Goal / Action
> ↓
> Applicable Policies
> ↓
> Authority Resolution
> ↓
> Required Decisions
> ↓
> Required Reviews
> ↓
> Executable Governance Plan
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1496. Governance Plan
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> Security Review
> ↓
> Project Lead Approval
> ↓
> Finance Approval
> ↓
> Execution
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1497. Governance Nodes in Procedural Graph
> 
> Thus procedural graph may include:
> 
> ```text
> APPROVAL
> REVIEW
> POLICY_CHECK
> ESCALATION
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1498. Governance is executable
> 
> Not just PDF manuals.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1499. Machine-readable policies reduce ambiguity
> 
> But natural-language source remains important.
> 
> Policy Artifact can contain:
> 
> ```text
> original legal/organizational text
> +
> structured rule representation
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1500. Translation from policy text
> 
> LLM can extract candidate rules.
> 
> But:
> 
> ```text
> candidate policy rule
> ```
> 
> requires human/legal validation before authoritative use.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1501. Policy provenance
> 
> Every machine rule links back to:
> 
> ```text
> source document
> section
> version
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1502. Legal uncertainty
> 
> If policy interpretation uncertain:
> 
> ```text
> UNKNOWN
> ```
> 
> and escalation.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1503. Do not encode uncertain legal interpretation as definite rule
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1504. Federation Governance
> 
> Cross-organization project may have:
> 
> ```text
> local policies
> +
> shared consortium policy
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1505. Local policy sovereignty
> 
> Shared governance cannot silently override local legal obligations.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1506. Cross-node approval
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> Org A requests Lab B action.
> ```
> 
> Needed:
> 
> ```text
> A project approval
> +
> B local lab approval
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1507. Federated Governance Graph
> 
> Can model:
> 
> ```text
> who controls which resource
> who can authorize which cross-node action
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1508. Conflict of Policies
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> Org A requires open publication.
> Org B requires confidential results.
> ```
> 
> System should detect conflict before project execution.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1509. Consortium Policy Negotiation
> 
> Possible options:
> 
> ```text
> split outputs
> delay publication
> exclude confidential data
> change partner
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1510. Governance as contract layer
> 
> Shared project can have:
> 
> ```text
> semantic governance agreement
> ```
> 
> describing:
> 
> ```text
> decision rights
> publication
> IP
> resource commitments
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1511. Human-readable legal contract remains separate
> 
> Again:
> 
> ```text
> semantic agreement ≠ legal contract
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1512. Public Governance
> 
> For open-source/public projects:
> 
> ```text
> community voting
> maintainer approval
> RFC process
> ```
> 
> can be modeled as governance archetypes.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1513. RFC Governance
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> Proposal
> ↓
> Discussion
> ↓
> Review
> ↓
> Decision
> ↓
> Implementation
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1514. This is useful for IIR standard itself
> 
> Changes to core ontology can use:
> 
> ```text
> Semantic RFC
> ```
> 
> with stricter authority.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1515. Core-change policy
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> No core predicate removal
> without major version.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1516. Package governance
> 
> New high-risk package requires:
> 
> ```text
> security approval
> ```
> 
> before system.lock update.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1517. Model governance
> 
> Switching AI model for critical workflow may require:
> 
> ```text
> benchmark
> review
> approval
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1518. Data governance
> 
> Dataset may have:
> 
> ```text
> access policy
> purpose limitation
> retention policy
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1519. Artifact governance
> 
> Some documents:
> 
> ```text
> PUBLIC
> PRIVATE
> CONFIDENTIAL
> ```
> 
> with separate permissions.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1520. Knowledge publication policy
> 
> Private Claim can become public only through:
> 
> ```text
> sanitize
> review
> approve
> publish
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1521. Open Knowledge Governance
> 
> Important for Technopedia.
> 
> Need distinguish:
> 
> ```text
> public fact
> community hypothesis
> personal opinion
> validated reference
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1522. Publication states
> 
> ```text
> DRAFT
> REVIEW
> PUBLISHED
> CONTESTED
> RETRACTED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1523. Community contribution
> 
> External person/agent can propose edit.
> 
> But:
> 
> ```text
> proposal ≠ authoritative publication
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1524. Multiple versions can coexist
> 
> Unlike classical encyclopedia:
> 
> ```text
> one final article
> ```
> 
> system may preserve:
> 
> ```text
> alternative interpretations
> branches
> claims
> evidence
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1525. Governance can vary by knowledge space
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> official standard page
> ```
> 
> strict review.
> 
> ```text
> discussion area
> ```
> 
> open contribution.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1526. AI participation
> 
> AI can:
> 
> ```text
> draft
> summarize
> detect conflicts
> suggest citations
> ```
> 
> but authorship/provenance remains explicit.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1527. Agent Identity
> 
> If AI publishes Claim:
> 
> ```text
> issuer = agent_instance_X
> ```
> 
> with:
> 
> ```text
> model
> package
> version
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1528. Human Approval of AI content
> 
> Can change publication state, but should not erase AI provenance.
> 
> ---
>

> 
> Minimum views:
> 
> ```text
> Goals
> Policies
> Pending Decisions
> Authority Map
> Exceptions
> Audit
> ```
> 
> ---
>

> 
> Shows:
>

> progress

>

>

>

>

>

> what waits for approval

>

> 
> # 1534. Exception View
>

>

> temporary overrides

> 
> # 1535. Audit View
> 
> Shows:
> 
> ```text
> goal → decision → action → outcome
> ```

> 
> # 1536. Governance API
> 
> Minimum:
> 
> ```text
> POST /goals
> POST /goals/{id}/approve
> POST /goals/{id}/pause
> 
> GET /policies
> POST /policies/evaluate
> 
> POST /decisions
> POST /decisions/{id}/approve
> 
> GET /authority/resolve
> POST /exceptions
> ```
>

> 
> # 1537. Policy Evaluation endpoint
> 
> Input:
> 
> ```yaml
> actor: agent_17
> action: send_email
> target: external_party
> context: project_X
> ```
> 
> Output:
> 
> ```yaml
> result: REQUIRE_APPROVAL
> policy_ids:
>   - communication_policy_4
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1538. Goal approval endpoint
> 
> Should check:
> 
> ```text
> authority
> conflicts
> required evidence
> ```
> 
> before approval.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1539. Governance Event types
> 
> ```text
> GOAL_PROPOSED
> GOAL_APPROVED
> GOAL_REJECTED
> POLICY_ACTIVATED
> POLICY_CHANGED
> DECISION_APPROVED
> EXCEPTION_GRANTED
> EXCEPTION_EXPIRED
> OVERRIDE_USED
> EMERGENCY_STOP
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1540. Governance Gold Dataset
> 
> For improvement:
> 
> ```text
> proposal
> decision
> reason
> outcome
> ```
> 
> can be analyzed.
> 
> But system should not learn:
> 
> ```text
> "humans usually approve this, so auto-approve"
> ```
> 
> unless explicit policy authorizes such automation.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1541. Decision Pattern Detection
> 
> AI may observe:
> 
> ```text
> same low-risk approval repeated 500 times
> ```
> 
> and propose:
> 
> ```text
> policy automation
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1542. Governance Automation Proposal
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> Automatically allow read-only GitHub searches
> within approved project.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1543. Then human governance may approve the rule
> 
> This converts repeated manual decision into policy.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1544. Governance Compaction
> 
> Таким образом система может постепенно переходить:
> 
> ```text
> manual approvals
> ↓
> stable policy
> ↓
> bounded automation
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1545. Reverse direction also needed
> 
> If automated policy causes problems:
> 
> ```text
> increase human review
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1546. Policy rollback
> 
> Same as software:
> 
> ```text
> new policy
> ↓
> unexpected effects
> ↓
> rollback
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1547. Governance Simulation
> 
> Before activation:
> 
> ```text
> replay historical events
> ```
> 
> under candidate policy.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1548. Example
> 
> Candidate policy:
> 
> ```text
> AI can auto-send internal notifications.
> ```
> 
> Replay shows:
> 
> ```text
> how many actions would have been auto-approved?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1549. Policy Shadow Mode
> 
> New policy can evaluate:
> 
> ```text
> what it would decide
> ```
> 
> without actually controlling runtime.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1550. Compare
> 
> ```text
> current policy
> vs
> shadow policy
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1551. Governance metrics
> 
> Useful:
> 
> ```text
> decision latency
> approval queue
> policy-denial frequency
> override frequency
> exception frequency
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1552. But not as manager performance scores
> 
> Metrics are for process diagnostics.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1553. High exception rate
> 
> May mean:
> 
> ```text
> policy poorly fits reality
> ```
> 
> rather than:
> 
> ```text
> users are bad
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1554. High override rate
> 
> Could indicate:
> 
> ```text
> automation needs adjustment
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1555. Governance Bottleneck Engine
> 
> Detect:
> 
> ```text
> one approval role blocks many projects
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1556. Possible interventions
> 
> ```text
> delegate
> increase capacity
> automate low-risk cases
> redesign policy
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1557. Goal hierarchy visualization
> 
> 2D:
> 
> ```text
> Mission
> ├── Strategic Goal A
> │   ├── Program 1
> │   └── Program 2
> └── Strategic Goal B
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1558. Goal-to-Execution trace
> 
> Click Goal:
> 
> ```text
> Goal
> ↓
> Programs
> ↓
> Projects
> ↓
> Tasks
> ↓
> Actions
> ↓
> Artifacts
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1559. This gives strategic observability
> 
> Management sees:
> 
> ```text
> что реально делается ради какой цели
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1560. Orphan Project Detector
> 
> Project not linked to any active goal:
> 
> ```text
> ORPHAN PROJECT
> ```
> 
> might be legitimate, but requires review.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1561. Goal without execution
> 
> Goal approved but:
> 
> ```text
> no projects
> no resources
> ```
> 
> → strategic execution gap.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1562. Goal-resource mismatch
> 
> High-priority Goal receives:
> 
> ```text
> very little capacity
> ```
> 
> while low-priority activities consume much.
> 
> System can expose mismatch.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1563. Strategy-to-budget linkage
> 
> Resource Accounting can answer:
> 
> ```text
> how much capacity is allocated to each strategic goal?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1564. Strategy Drift
> 
> If actual execution gradually diverges from:
> 
> ```text
> approved strategy
> ```
> 
> system detects:
> 
> ```text
> Strategy Drift
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1565. Example
> 
> Strategy:
> 
> ```text
> open-source-first
> ```
> 
> Actual:
> 
> ```text
> 80% new dependencies proprietary
> ```
> 
> System flags discrepancy.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1566. Goal Drift
> 
> Project originally intended:
> 
> ```text
> build shared benchmark
> ```
> 
> but execution becomes:
> 
> ```text
> custom solution for one client
> ```
> 
> May require scope review.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1567. Scope Change
> 
> Significant scope change requires:
> 
> ```text
> Decision
> ```
> 
> not silent adaptation.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1568. Adaptive Runtime boundary
> 
> Runtime can adapt:
> 
> ```text
> method
> provider
> ordering
> ```
> 
> within approved Goal/scope.
> 
> It cannot silently redefine:
> 
> ```text
> why project exists
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1569. This is the central governance boundary
> 
> ```text
> HOW
> may be adaptively optimized.
> 
> WHAT/WHY
> requires governance.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1570. Bounded Goal Delegation
> 
> Human can explicitly authorize:
> 
> ```text
> AI may create subgoals needed
> to achieve Goal X
> ```
> 
> within scope.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1571. Example
> 
> Goal:
> 
> ```text
> Deploy service.
> ```
> 
> AI may generate subgoal:
> 
> ```text
> Fix failing integration test.
> ```
> 
> without executive approval.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1572. But not:
> 
> ```text
> Change product target market.
> ```
> 
> That exceeds scope.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1573. Goal Scope Contract
> 
> Can define:
> 
> ```text
> allowed subgoal types
> budget
> time
> resources
> forbidden actions
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1574. Goal Budget
> 
> Not just money.
> 
> ```text
> compute
> human time
> external actions
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1575. Goal termination condition
> 
> Every Goal should know:
> 
> ```text
> success
> failure
> expiration
> cancellation
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1576. Goal State is derived partly from evidence
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> Success criterion verified
> ```
> 
> → Goal may become ACHIEVED.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1577. But human acknowledgement may still be required
> 
> For strategic Goal:
> 
> ```text
> evidence suggests achieved
> ```
> 
> system may propose:
> 
> ```text
> CLOSE GOAL
> ```
> 
> rather than close automatically.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1578. Governance modes by Goal type
> 
> Operational low-risk:
> 
> ```text
> automatic closure
> ```
> 
> Strategic:
> 
> ```text
> human closure
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1579. Goal Review Cycle
> 
> Long-running Goal:
> 
> ```text
> review every quarter
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1580. Review asks
> 
> ```text
> still relevant?
> assumptions valid?
> resources adequate?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1581. Assumption Registry integration
> 
> Goal can depend on:
> 
> ```text
> Assumptions
> ```
> 
> If assumption refuted:
> 
> ```text
> Goal Review
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1582. Example
> 
> Goal:
> 
> ```text
> build technology X
> ```
> 
> Assumption:
> 
> ```text
> market need persists
> ```
> 
> New Evidence refutes it.
> 
> System should not continue blindly.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1583. Governance + Counterfactual Engine
> 
> Before major decision:
> 
> ```text
> simulate options
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1584. Example
> 
> Decision:
> 
> ```text
> Create internal Security Office?
> ```
> 
> Scenarios:
> 
> ```text
> internal unit
> external providers
> hybrid
> ```
> 
> Governance receives trade-offs.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1585. Governance does not become optimizer dictatorship
> 
> Simulation informs authority.
> 
> Authority decides.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1586. Goal/Policy package system
> 
> Policies and governance archetypes can be packages.
> 
> But high-trust core policies should remain protected.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1587. Governance Package
> 
> Examples:
> 
> ```text
> Research Consortium Governance
> Open Source Project Governance
> High-Risk Robotics Governance
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1588. Governance Archetype
> 
> Contains:
> 
> ```text
> roles
> approval paths
> decision classes
> policy defaults
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1589. Organization can instantiate template
> 
> Then customize.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1590. Policy library
> 
> Common policies:
> 
> ```text
> external communication
> data access
> resource spending
> package installation
> physical execution
> publication
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1591. Policy testing
> 
> Every policy package should include:
> 
> ```text
> allowed case tests
> denied case tests
> edge cases
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1592. Formal policy language later
> 
> v0.1 can use:
> 
> ```text
> structured conditions
> ```
> 
> rather than inventing full new language immediately.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1593. Example structured condition
> 
> ```yaml
> if:
>   action_type: EXTERNAL_MESSAGE
>   visibility: CONFIDENTIAL
> 
> then:
>   effect: REQUIRE_APPROVAL
> 
> authority:
>   role: PROJECT_OWNER
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1594. Complex rule
> 
> Could eventually compile to:
> 
> ```text
> OPA/Rego-like backend
> ```
> 
> or custom engine.
> 
> But semantic representation remains backend-independent.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1595. Governance microkernel
> 
> Minimal trusted governance core:
> 
> ```text
> Policy Evaluation
> Authority Resolution
> Decision Registry
> Approval Gates
> Override/Emergency Stop
> Audit
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1596. Why microkernel
> 
> Because this is security-sensitive and should remain small.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1597. LLM role in governance
> 
> LLM may:
> 
> ```text
> explain policy
> find relevant rules
> draft decision summary
> detect conflicts
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1598. LLM should not silently invent authority
> 
> Authority is deterministic registry/policy data.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1599. LLM should not silently waive rule
> 
> Exception requires authorized Decision.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1600. Governance invariants
> 
> Freeze initial set.
> 
> ### Invariant 1
> 
> ```text
> Proposal ≠ Decision.
> ```
> 
> ### Invariant 2
> 
> ```text
> Capability ≠ Authority.
> ```
> 
> ### Invariant 3
> 
> ```text
> No response ≠ Approval.
> ```
> 
> ### Invariant 4
> 
> ```text
> Runtime cannot exceed approved Goal scope.
> ```
> 
> ### Invariant 5
> 
> ```text
> High-impact actions require applicable governance checks.
> ```
> 
> ### Invariant 6
> 
> ```text
> Policy version used for execution must be auditable.
> ```
> 
> ### Invariant 7
> 
> ```text
> Human override must be explicit and logged.
> ```
> 
> ### Invariant 8
> 
> ```text
> AI may propose goals but does not become default source of organizational authority.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1601. Full control chain
> 
> Теперь вся система имеет:
> 
> ```text
> MISSION
> ↓
> GOALS
> ↓
> POLICIES / AUTHORITY
> ↓
> PROGRAMS
> ↓
> PROJECTS
> ↓
> TASKS
> ↓
> PROCEDURES
> ↓
> RESOURCE BINDINGS
> ↓
> ACTIONS
> ↓
> EVENTS
> ↓
> EVIDENCE
> ↓
> WORLD STATE
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1602. Обратная петля
> 
> ```text
> WORLD STATE
> ↓
> Observed Outcomes
> ↓
> Goal Evaluation
> ↓
> Policy Review
> ↓
> Strategy Review
> ```
>

> human review;

> достоверность Claims;

> оценку Procedure;

> 
> в одну общую архитектуру проверки.

> Именно этот слой нужен, чтобы Innovation OS была не просто системой, которая много делает, а системой, которая умеет постоянно проверять, **насколько её собственная модель мира и результаты соответствуют реальности**.

Следующая часть будет про **Verification, Benchmarking & Epistemic Quality Engine v0.1** — общий «контур истины и качества» для людей, AI-агентов, кода, научных гипотез, процедур и физических экспериментов.
