# chatgpt response

Продолжаю полностью **на русском языке**. Теперь переходим к **Verification, Benchmarking & Epistemic Quality Engine v0.1** — общему контуру проверки, который должен отвечать не только «выполнено ли действие», но и **правильно ли оно выполнено, достаточно ли доказательств, насколько вывод соответствует реальности и не деградирует ли система со временем**.

> **Document: Verification, Benchmarking & Epistemic Quality Engine v0.1**
> 
> # Verification, Benchmarking & Epistemic Quality Engine v0.1
> 
> ## 1611. Главный переход
> 
> До этого Innovation OS умеет:
> 
> ```text
> поставить Goal
> ↓
> создать Project
> ↓
> скомпилировать Procedure
> ↓
> выбрать Resources
> ↓
> выполнить Actions
> ↓
> получить Artifacts / Claims / Events
> ```
> 
> Но остаётся критический вопрос:
> 
> > Откуда система знает, что результат действительно корректен?
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1612. Execution Success ≠ Correct Result
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> API call succeeded
> ```
> 
> не означает:
> 
> ```text
> данные правильные
> ```
> 
> И:
> 
> ```text
> LLM ответил без ошибки
> ```
> 
> не означает:
> 
> ```text
> ответ соответствует фактам
> ```
> 
> И:
> 
> ```text
> эксперимент завершился
> ```
> 
> не означает:
> 
> ```text
> гипотеза подтверждена
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1613. Поэтому после Execution нужен отдельный Verification Layer
> 
> ```text
> Action
> ↓
> Output
> ↓
> Verification
> ↓
> Evidence
> ↓
> Acceptance / Rejection
> ↓
> World State Update
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1614. Центральная формула
> 
> ```text
> CLAIM
> +
> EVIDENCE
> +
> VERIFICATION PROCEDURE
> +
> CONTEXT
> =
> EPISTEMIC STATE
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1615. Что должен проверять Verification Engine
> 
> Минимум:
> 
> ```text
> структурную корректность
> семантическую корректность
> фактическую поддержку
> соответствие требованиям
> качество
> полноту
> воспроизводимость
> согласованность
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1616. Несколько классов проверки
> 
> Можно выделить:
> 
> ```text
> SCHEMA VERIFICATION
> CONSTRAINT VERIFICATION
> EVIDENCE VERIFICATION
> BEHAVIORAL VERIFICATION
> HUMAN REVIEW
> EXPERIMENTAL VERIFICATION
> CROSS-SOURCE VERIFICATION
> REGRESSION VERIFICATION
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1617. Schema Verification
> 
> Самый простой уровень.
> 
> Проверяет:
> 
> ```text
> правильные поля?
> правильные типы?
> обязательные значения?
> ```
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> FundingCallIR
> ```
> 
> без deadline может быть:
> 
> ```text
> schema-invalid
> ```
> 
> если deadline required.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1618. Schema Valid ≠ Semantically Correct
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```yaml
> temperature: 5000
> unit: Celsius
> ```
> 
> может быть schema-valid,
> 
> но физически бессмысленно для конкретного оборудования.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1619. Semantic Verification
> 
> Проверяет:
> 
> ```text
> значение допустимо?
> relation имеет правильные domain/range?
> units совместимы?
> context логичен?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1620. Constraint Verification
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> Project requires EU hosting
> ```
> 
> Provider:
> 
> ```text
> US-only
> ```
> 
> →
> 
> ```text
> NO
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1621. Three-valued verification
> 
> Результат:
> 
> ```text
> YES
> NO
> UNKNOWN
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1622. UNKNOWN не должен превращаться в PASS
> 
> Очень важный принцип.
> 
> Если:
> 
> ```text
> license unclear
> ```
> 
> то:
> 
> ```text
> verification = UNKNOWN
> ```
> 
> а не:
> 
> ```text
> assume compatible
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1623. Verification Result
> 
> Application-level объект:
> 
> ```yaml
> verification_result:
>   subject: artifact_17
>   check: schema_conformance
> 
>   state: YES
> 
>   evidence:
>     - test_run_4
> 
>   verifier:
>     validator_package_2
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1624. Verification as Claim
> 
> Формально результат проверки тоже можно представить как:
> 
> ```text
> CLAIM
> ```
> 
> например:
> 
> ```text
> Artifact 17
> SATISFIES
> Schema X
> ```
> 
> с Evidence.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1625. Verifier
> 
> Verifier может быть:
> 
> ```text
> deterministic software
> AI agent
> human reviewer
> laboratory instrument
> external authority
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1626. Verification Mode
> 
> Useful enum:
> 
> ```text
> AUTOMATED
> HUMAN
> AI_REVIEW
> CROSS_AGENT
> EXPERIMENTAL
> EXTERNAL
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1627. Automated Verification
> 
> Подходит для:
> 
> ```text
> unit tests
> schema checks
> hash validation
> constraint checks
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1628. Human Verification
> 
> Нужно для:
> 
> ```text
> judgment
> legal interpretation
> creative quality
> physical inspection
> complex strategic review
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1629. AI Review
> 
> Полезен как дополнительный слой:
> 
> ```text
> consistency check
> evidence check
> draft critique
> ```
> 
> Но:
> 
> ```text
> AI review
> ≠ independent proof
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1630. Cross-Agent Verification
> 
> Один AI создаёт результат.
> 
> Другой:
> 
> ```text
> ищет ошибки
> ```
> 
> Но оба могут:
> 
> ```text
> share same blind spot
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1631. Поэтому Cross-Agent Verification — Evidence, а не guarantee
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1632. Experimental Verification
> 
> Используется, когда истину можно проверить только действием:
> 
> ```text
> запустить код
> измерить датчик
> провести испытание
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1633. External Verification
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> сертификационная лаборатория
> финансирующая организация
> государственный орган
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1634. Verification Contract
> 
> Каждый Task/Artifact может иметь:
> 
> ```text
> verification contract
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1635. Example
> 
> ```yaml
> verification:
>   target:
>     parser
> 
>   checks:
>     - schema_valid
>     - accuracy_on_gold_set
>     - no_critical_security_findings
> 
>   acceptance:
>     all_must_pass: true
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1636. Verification Contract ≠ Test Implementation
> 
> Contract says:
> 
> ```text
> что должно быть доказано
> ```
> 
> Evaluator package says:
> 
> ```text
> как это проверить
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1637. Acceptance Criteria
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> accuracy >= 0.95
> ```
> 
> или:
> 
> ```text
> no critical security issue
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1638. But threshold needs provenance
> 
> Почему:
> 
> ```text
> 0.95
> ```
> 
> а не:
> 
> ```text
> 0.90
> ```
> 
> ?
> 
> Threshold должен происходить из:
> 
> ```text
> policy
> benchmark standard
> human decision
> domain requirement
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1639. Arbitrary threshold problem
> 
> System should not invent:
> 
> ```text
> 95%
> ```
> 
> без основания.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1640. Gold Dataset
> 
> Для repeatable semantic tasks нужен:
> 
> ```text
> Gold Dataset
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1641. Gold Dataset содержит
> 
> ```text
> input
> expected output
> human label
> reason codes
> version
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1642. Пример для HN matching
> 
> ```text
> Job 17
> Candidate 4
> Label: INVESTIGATE
> Reason:
> work_authorization_unknown
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1643. Gold Dataset должен быть versioned
> 
> Потому что:
> 
> ```text
> ontology
> rules
> labels
> ```
> 
> могут меняться.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1644. Benchmark
> 
> Benchmark:
> 
> ```text
> Dataset
> +
> Procedure
> +
> Metrics
> +
> Environment
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1645. Benchmark Result без environment неполон
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> model latency = 100 ms
> ```
> 
> без:
> 
> ```text
> hardware
> batch size
> input length
> ```
> 
> почти бесполезно.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1646. Benchmark Context
> 
> Mandatory fields:
> 
> ```text
> hardware
> software version
> dataset version
> configuration
> time
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1647. Reproducibility
> 
> Другой executor должен иметь возможность:
> 
> ```text
> повторить benchmark
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1648. Reproduction ≠ Identical Number
> 
> Иногда допустим диапазон:
> 
> ```text
> 100–110 ms
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1649. Tolerance
> 
> Verification contract может задавать:
> 
> ```text
> absolute tolerance
> relative tolerance
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1650. Deterministic vs Stochastic Systems
> 
> Для deterministic software:
> 
> ```text
> same input → same output
> ```
> 
> часто ожидаемо.
> 
> Для LLM:
> 
> ```text
> distributional behavior
> ```
> 
> важнее.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1651. LLM Benchmark
> 
> Лучше оценивать:
> 
> ```text
> success rate
> constraint compliance
> evidence preservation
> error types
> cost
> latency
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1652. Не использовать только одну average score
> 
> Потому что модель может:
> 
> ```text
> хорошо отвечать обычно
> ```
> 
> но:
> 
> ```text
> плохо выполнять критический constraint
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1653. Critical Failure Rate
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> wrongly marks ineligible grant as eligible
> ```
> 
> может быть гораздо важнее небольшой average error.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1654. Severity-weighted error categories
> 
> Можно иметь:
> 
> ```text
> MINOR
> MAJOR
> CRITICAL
> ```
> 
> но severity должна быть domain-specific.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1655. Error Taxonomy
> 
> Например для extraction:
> 
> ```text
> MISSING_FIELD
> WRONG_ENTITY
> WRONG_RELATION
> UNSUPPORTED_INFERENCE
> CONTEXT_LOSS
> PROVENANCE_LOSS
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1656. Для matching:
> 
> ```text
> FALSE_BLOCK
> MISSED_HARD_CONSTRAINT
> OVERSTATED_CAPABILITY
> UNKNOWN_COLLAPSED_TO_NO
> UNKNOWN_COLLAPSED_TO_YES
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1657. Для research:
> 
> ```text
> SOURCE_MISREAD
> CONTEXT_GENERALIZATION
> CAUSATION_OVERCLAIM
> CONTRADICTORY_EVIDENCE_IGNORED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1658. Error Registry
> 
> Все значимые ошибки должны попадать в:
> 
> ```text
> Error Registry
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1659. Error Record
> 
> ```yaml
> error:
>   component: matcher_v4
>   case: fixture_42
>   error_type: MISSED_HARD_CONSTRAINT
>   severity: CRITICAL
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1660. Error Registry нужен не для наказания
> 
> А для:
> 
> ```text
> system improvement
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1661. False Positive
> 
> System says:
> 
> ```text
> MATCH
> ```
> 
> but should not.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1662. False Negative
> 
> System rejects useful option.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1663. False Unknown
> 
> System says:
> 
> ```text
> UNKNOWN
> ```
> 
> although evidence sufficient.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1664. Overconfidence
> 
> System labels:
> 
> ```text
> FACT
> ```
> 
> when evidence only supports:
> 
> ```text
> INFERENCE
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1665. Underconfidence
> 
> Система может слишком часто:
> 
> ```text
> refuse to infer
> ```
> 
> and lose useful connections.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1666. Epistemic Calibration
> 
> Goal:
> 
> ```text
> confidence should correspond
> to observed correctness
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1667. Example
> 
> Among claims assigned:
> 
> ```text
> confidence ≈ 0.8
> ```
> 
> roughly:
> 
> ```text
> ~80%
> ```
> 
> should survive verification,
> 
> if confidence is actually calibrated.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1668. Если confidence не calibrated — лучше его не использовать как вероятность
> 
> Очень важный принцип.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1669. Confidence Types
> 
> Можно различать:
> 
> ```text
> MODEL_CONFIDENCE
> EVIDENCE_STRENGTH
> VERIFICATION_STATUS
> ```
> 
> Не смешивать.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1670. Model Confidence
> 
> Как уверена модель.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1671. Evidence Strength
> 
> Насколько сильна поддержка.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1672. Verification Status
> 
> Прошёл ли explicit check.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1673. FACT should require policy-defined verification
> 
> То есть LLM не может просто поставить:
> 
> ```text
> FACT
> ```
> 
> потому что звучит уверенно.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1674. Claim Promotion
> 
> Lifecycle:
> 
> ```text
> HYPOTHESIS
> ↓
> SUPPORTED
> ↓
> VERIFIED
> ```
> 
> можно хранить application-level.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1675. Claim Demotion
> 
> Если new evidence contradicts:
> 
> ```text
> VERIFIED
> →
> CONTESTED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1676. Claim Retraction
> 
> Если ясно опровергнуто:
> 
> ```text
> REFUTED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1677. История сохраняется
> 
> Не удалять старый Claim.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1678. Evidence Graph
> 
> Для одного Claim:
> 
> ```text
> Claim X
> ├── SUPPORTS Evidence A
> ├── SUPPORTS Evidence B
> └── REFUTES Evidence C
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1679. Evidence Independence
> 
> A и B могут быть:
> 
> ```text
> двумя статьями
> ```
> 
> но если B просто пересказывает A:
> 
> ```text
> они не независимы
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1680. Evidence Dependency Graph
> 
> Useful relation:
> 
> ```text
> Evidence B
> DERIVED_FROM
> Evidence A
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1681. Independent Evidence Count
> 
> Не просто:
> 
> ```text
> number of sources
> ```
> 
> а:
> 
> ```text
> number of independent evidence chains
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1682. Source Authority
> 
> Некоторые sources authoritative for specific claims.
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> Funding agency
> ```
> 
> authoritative for:
> 
> ```text
> its own deadline
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1683. Но authority is contextual
> 
> Funding agency не authoritative для:
> 
> ```text
> whether a scientific method works
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1684. Source Reliability Vector
> 
> Вместо universal rating:
> 
> ```text
> authority_scope
> freshness
> directness
> independence
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1685. Direct Evidence
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> measured benchmark
> ```
> 
> сильнее для performance claim, чем:
> 
> ```text
> marketing text
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1686. Self-Report
> 
> Valid evidence for:
> 
> ```text
> "candidate says they are available"
> ```
> 
> Но слабее для:
> 
> ```text
> independent technical proficiency
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1687. Observed Evidence
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> successful public implementation
> ```
> 
> может лучше support capability.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1688. Derived Evidence
> 
> Analysis itself can create secondary evidence,
> 
> но provenance chain required.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1689. Evidence Freshness
> 
> Некоторые Evidence quickly becomes stale.
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> availability
> price
> API behavior
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1690. Other evidence nearly timeless
> 
> ```text
> historical event
> mathematical proof
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1691. Freshness Policy
> 
> By evidence/claim type.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1692. Stale Evidence Event
> 
> ```text
> EVIDENCE_STALE
> ```
> 
> can trigger:
> 
> ```text
> Claim Review
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1693. Verification expiration
> 
> Certain verifications expire.
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> security audit
> calibration
> certification
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1694. Verification Validity Interval
> 
> ```text
> valid_from
> valid_to
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1695. Reverification
> 
> When expired:
> 
> ```text
> REVERIFY
> ```
> 
> becomes Task.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1696. Continuous Verification
> 
> For critical live systems:
> 
> ```text
> monitor
> ```
> 
> instead of one-time check.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1697. Runtime Health Check
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> service responds
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1698. Behavioral Verification
> 
> More important:
> 
> ```text
> service still satisfies actual contract
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1699. Example
> 
> Package endpoint is alive,
> 
> but now:
> 
> ```text
> returns malformed data
> ```
> 
> Health check passes,
> 
> behavioral verification fails.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1700. Contract Test
> 
> Check provider against capability contract.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1701. Capability Contract
> 
> ```text
> Inputs
> Outputs
> Constraints
> Side Effects
> Verification
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1702. Provider Certification
> 
> Resource may be certified as:
> 
> ```text
> PROVIDES Capability X
> ```
> 
> under context Y.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1703. Certification not global
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> Model A
> ```
> 
> may be certified for:
> 
> ```text
> summarization
> ```
> 
> but not:
> 
> ```text
> legal interpretation
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1704. Capability-specific benchmark
> 
> Essential.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1705. Human Capability Verification
> 
> Could use:
> 
> ```text
> portfolio
> public work
> certification
> trial task
> references
> ```
> 
> depending context.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1706. Do not require invasive testing by default
> 
> Verification should be proportionate to need and consent.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1707. Team Verification
> 
> Team capability may be verified by:
> 
> ```text
> past joint outcomes
> pilot project
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1708. Organizational Capability Verification
> 
> For lab/service:
> 
> ```text
> certification
> past delivery
> equipment
> staff
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1709. Physical Capability Verification
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> machine calibrated
> operator qualified
> procedure validated
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1710. Composite Capability Verification
> 
> If capability provided by:
> 
> ```text
> Human + AI + Tool
> ```
> 
> verify the configuration itself.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1711. Configuration-level Evidence
> 
> Do not attribute whole result automatically to each component.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1712. Example
> 
> Human + AI produces:
> 
> ```text
> 95% correct extraction
> ```
> 
> does not prove:
> 
> ```text
> AI alone = 95%
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1713. A/B Evaluation
> 
> Can compare configurations.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1714. Example
> 
> ```text
> Human only
> Human + AI
> AI only
> ```
> 
> measure:
> 
> ```text
> time
> quality
> cost
> error types
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1715. Controlled Experiment
> 
> Need define:
> 
> ```text
> population
> sample
> outcome
> confounders
> ```
> 
> when strong conclusions needed.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1716. Operational experiments
> 
> Not every process needs academic rigor.
> 
> But system should know difference between:
> 
> ```text
> informal trial
> ```
> 
> and:
> 
> ```text
> controlled validation
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1717. Experiment Fidelity
> 
> ```text
> EXPLORATORY
> CONTROLLED
> REPLICATED
> PRODUCTION_OBSERVED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1718. Production Observation
> 
> Real-world outcomes often more valuable than benchmark,
> 
> but less controlled.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1719. Combine both
> 
> ```text
> Benchmark
> +
> Production Evidence
> ```
> 
> gives stronger picture.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1720. Benchmark Overfitting
> 
> Danger:
> 
> ```text
> optimize only benchmark
> ```
> 
> while real performance deteriorates.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1721. Holdout Set
> 
> Important for AI/matcher evaluation.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1722. Blind Evaluation
> 
> Reviewers may not know which algorithm produced output.
> 
> Useful for reducing bias.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1723. Benchmark Leakage
> 
> If model trained on gold test cases:
> 
> ```text
> benchmark meaningless
> ```
> 
> Need dataset provenance.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1724. Evaluation Dataset Registry
> 
> Track:
> 
> ```text
> training use?
> development use?
> test use?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1725. Benchmark Versioning
> 
> Never compare:
> 
> ```text
> v1 score
> ```
> 
> and:
> 
> ```text
> v2 score
> ```
> 
> as if identical benchmark.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1726. Benchmark Lineage
> 
> Store:
> 
> ```text
> dataset version
> metric version
> evaluator version
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1727. Metric Definition
> 
> Metric itself must be versioned.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1728. Example
> 
> ```text
> match_precision_v1
> ```
> 
> may calculate differently than:
> 
> ```text
> match_precision_v2
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1729. Metric Gaming
> 
> System optimizing one metric can distort behavior.
> 
> Therefore multi-dimensional quality vector preferred.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1730. Example HN Matcher
> 
> Metrics:
> 
> ```text
> Precision@5
> Recall@20
> Hard-block false-positive rate
> Critical UNKNOWN rate
> Explainability coverage
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1731. Explainability Coverage
> 
> What percentage of match decisions have:
> 
> ```text
> evidence
> constraints
> unknowns
> reason codes
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1732. Evidence Coverage
> 
> What fraction of capability claims have:
> 
> ```text
> at least one evidence link
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1733. Unsupported Claim Rate
> 
> Useful epistemic quality metric.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1734. Provenance Completeness
> 
> What percentage of imported Claims have:
> 
> ```text
> source
> observed_at
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1735. Context Completeness
> 
> Important scientific/technical claims require:
> 
> ```text
> context
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1736. Contradiction Detection Rate
> 
> How often system detects known conflicting evidence instead of silently flattening it.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1737. Epistemic Quality Dashboard
> 
> Minimum:
> 
> ```text
> Claims
> Evidence Coverage
> Unknowns
> Conflicts
> Stale Evidence
> Verification Status
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1738. Claim Quality View
> 
> For each Claim:
> 
> ```text
> type
> source
> supporting evidence
> refuting evidence
> freshness
> verification
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1739. World State Quality
> 
> World State itself needs health metrics.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1740. World State Quality dimensions
> 
> ```text
> freshness
> coverage
> consistency
> provenance completeness
> conflict density
> unknown density
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1741. High Unknown Density is not automatically bad
> 
> It can mean:
> 
> ```text
> honest uncertainty representation
> ```
> 
> rather than fabricated certainty.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1742. But critical unknowns matter
> 
> Need distinguish:
> 
> ```text
> critical unknown
> ```
> 
> from:
> 
> ```text
> irrelevant unknown
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1743. Critical Unknown
> 
> Unknown affecting:
> 
> ```text
> decision
> hard constraint
> safety
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1744. Critical Unknown Queue
> 
> System can prioritize evidence acquisition.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1745. Value of Information
> 
> Already introduced.
> 
> Verification Engine can formalize:
> 
> ```text
> Which unknown is worth investigating next?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1746. VOI factors
> 
> ```text
> decision impact
> cost of investigation
> probability result changes decision
> deadline
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1747. Example
> 
> Unknown:
> 
> ```text
> Repo X license
> ```
> 
> If incompatible license would eliminate top option,
> 
> high VOI.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1748. Another unknown
> 
> ```text
> README formatting style
> ```
> 
> low VOI.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1749. Epistemic Budget
> 
> Project can have:
> 
> ```text
> validation budget
> ```
> 
> for:
> 
> ```text
> research
> tests
> reviews
> experiments
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1750. Verification Cost
> 
> Verification consumes resources.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1751. Over-verification
> 
> Checking everything infinitely is impossible.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1752. Under-verification
> 
> Too little validation produces unreliable World State.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1753. Verification intensity by risk
> 
> Low-risk exploratory:
> 
> ```text
> light verification
> ```
> 
> High-risk irreversible:
> 
> ```text
> deep verification
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1754. Verification Profile
> 
> Possible:
> 
> ```text
> FAST
> STANDARD
> HIGH_ASSURANCE
> REGULATED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1755. FAST
> 
> ```text
> schema
> basic evidence
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1756. STANDARD
> 
> ```text
> multiple evidence
> automated test
> review
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1757. HIGH_ASSURANCE
> 
> ```text
> independent review
> reproduction
> strong audit
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1758. REGULATED
> 
> Depends on external legal/industry requirements.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1759. Verification Compiler
> 
> Input:
> 
> ```text
> Artifact / Claim / Action
> +
> Risk
> +
> Policy
> +
> Context
> ```
> 
> Output:
> 
> ```text
> Verification Procedure
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1760. Example
> 
> ```text
> AI-generated legal summary
> ```
> 
> may compile:
> 
> ```text
> source-check
> ↓
> citation verification
> ↓
> human legal review
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1761. Another example
> 
> ```text
> Read-only web research
> ```
> 
> may need only:
> 
> ```text
> source provenance
> basic semantic validation
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1762. Verification Procedures themselves are packages
> 
> Can be versioned and benchmarked.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1763. Evaluator Dependency
> 
> One evaluator may depend on:
> 
> ```text
> test dataset
> ontology
> reference implementation
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1764. Evaluator Quality
> 
> Who verifies verifier?
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1765. Meta-Verification
> 
> Evaluator itself passes:
> 
> ```text
> benchmark
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1766. Reference cases
> 
> Known PASS/FAIL fixtures.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1767. Evaluator drift
> 
> If underlying model changes:
> 
> ```text
> revalidate evaluator
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1768. Human Reviewer Calibration
> 
> Human reviews can disagree.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1769. Inter-rater Agreement
> 
> Useful for:
> 
> ```text
> ambiguous semantic tasks
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1770. Disagreement is signal
> 
> High disagreement may mean:
> 
> ```text
> bad rubric
> ambiguous task
> insufficient evidence
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1771. Don't hide reviewer disagreement
> 
> Store it.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1772. Adjudication
> 
> Third reviewer or expert can resolve.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1773. Review Rubric
> 
> Human reviewers need explicit criteria.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1774. Rubric Package
> 
> Reusable for:
> 
> ```text
> proposal review
> research claim review
> security review
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1775. Reviewer Confidence
> 
> Can be recorded,
> 
> but not used as authority substitute.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1776. Blind Spot Detector
> 
> If same error repeatedly escapes:
> 
> ```text
> review process has blind spot
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1777. Verification Coverage Graph
> 
> Shows:
> 
> ```text
> which requirements
> have which checks
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1778. Unverified Requirement
> 
> If Requirement has no verification path:
> 
> ```text
> Verification Gap
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1779. Verification Gap
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> Project requires privacy-preserving behavior
> ```
> 
> but no test exists.
> 
> System creates:
> 
> ```text
> Build Privacy Evaluation Project
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1780. Benchmark Gap
> 
> Many providers claim same capability,
> 
> but no common benchmark.
> 
> Opportunity:
> 
> ```text
> create benchmark
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1781. This connects to Opportunity Engine
> 
> Verification infrastructure itself can be strategic asset.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1782. Benchmark as Shared Infrastructure
> 
> One benchmark may serve:
> 
> ```text
> dozens of projects
> vendors
> research teams
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1783. Standardization Opportunity
> 
> If everyone evaluates differently:
> 
> ```text
> standard benchmark
> ```
> 
> reduces friction.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1784. Epistemic Debt
> 
> Очень важное понятие.
> 
> Epistemic Debt:
> 
> ```text
> system relies on claims
> whose evidence is weak/stale/missing
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1785. Example
> 
> ```text
> "We think service X scales."
> ```
> 
> used in 8 projects,
> 
> but never benchmarked.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1786. Epistemic Debt grows with reuse
> 
> The more decisions depend on weak Claim,
> 
> the more important validation becomes.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1787. Claim Dependency Count
> 
> Can estimate:
> 
> ```text
> how many projects/decisions depend on Claim X
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1788. High-leverage verification
> 
> A single experiment validating Claim X may de-risk many projects.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1789. Verification Prioritization
> 
> ```text
> criticality
> ×
> dependency count
> ×
> uncertainty
> ```
> 
> can identify candidates,
> 
> without turning it into one unquestioned score.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1790. Epistemic Bottleneck
> 
> Knowledge uncertainty can itself block portfolio.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1791. Example
> 
> 10 projects depend on:
> 
> ```text
> "new sensor survives 1M cycles"
> ```
> 
> unknown.
> 
> One durability experiment can unlock all 10.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1792. Evidence Production Project
> 
> Thus:
> 
> ```text
> verification itself
> ```
> 
> can be Project IR.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1793. Verification Economy
> 
> Verification consumes:
> 
> ```text
> people
> compute
> lab time
> money
> ```
> 
> but reduces:
> 
> ```text
> decision risk
> rework
> failure
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1794. Verification Return
> 
> Useful dimensions:
> 
> ```text
> uncertainty reduced
> projects unlocked
> risk reduced
> reuse of evidence
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1795. Not every validation needs expensive experiment
> 
> Search existing evidence first.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1796. Verification Resolver
> 
> For Claim X:
> 
> ```text
> what is cheapest adequate way to verify?
> ```
> 
> Possible:
> 
> ```text
> existing source
> automated test
> expert review
> simulation
> physical experiment
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1797. Evidence Acquisition Hierarchy
> 
> Conceptually:
> 
> ```text
> reuse existing evidence
> ↓
> cheap automated check
> ↓
> expert review
> ↓
> simulation
> ↓
> expensive physical experiment
> ```
> 
> if sufficient.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1798. But cheapest is not always adequate
> 
> Context determines.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1799. Scientific Reproducibility Engine
> 
> For research claims:
> 
> ```text
> Paper
> ↓
> Method
> ↓
> Code
> ↓
> Dataset
> ↓
> Reproduction Procedure
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1800. Replication Package
> 
> Can include:
> 
> ```text
> environment
> dependencies
> procedure
> expected outcomes
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1801. Reproduction Result
> 
> ```text
> REPRODUCED
> PARTIAL
> FAILED
> UNKNOWN
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1802. Failed reproduction ≠ automatic refutation
> 
> Possible causes:
> 
> ```text
> implementation mismatch
> environment mismatch
> method unclear
> ```
> 
> Need diagnosis.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1803. Replication Conflict
> 
> Stores:
> 
> ```text
> original result
> replication result
> context differences
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1804. Engineering Validation Engine
> 
> For code/software:
> 
> ```text
> functional
> performance
> security
> compatibility
> operability
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1805. Functional Verification
> 
> Does it perform promised function?
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1806. Performance Verification
> 
> Under what load/context?
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1807. Security Verification
> 
> Threat model-specific.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1808. Compatibility Verification
> 
> Does it integrate with actual environment?
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1809. Operability Verification
> 
> Can organization run/maintain it?
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1810. Physical Verification Engine
> 
> For hardware:
> 
> ```text
> dimensions
> strength
> thermal
> electrical
> reliability
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1811. Calibration-aware Evidence
> 
> Measurement valid only if equipment calibration valid.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1812. Measurement Uncertainty
> 
> Physical data should carry:
> 
> ```text
> precision
> error bounds
> ```
> 
> when relevant.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1813. AI Output Verification
> 
> Potential layers:
> 
> ```text
> schema
> source support
> consistency
> cross-check
> human review
> real-world test
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1814. Retrieval-Augmented Verification
> 
> For factual output:
> 
> ```text
> Claims
> ↓
> retrieve sources
> ↓
> compare support
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1815. Citation Presence ≠ Citation Support
> 
> Need verify:
> 
> ```text
> does cited source actually support claim?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1816. Citation Entailment Check
> 
> Can be automated partly,
> 
> but critical cases may require human review.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1817. Claim-to-Source Alignment
> 
> For each sentence/Claim:
> 
> ```text
> supporting source span
> ```
> 
> where possible.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1818. Unsupported Generalization
> 
> Common error:
> 
> Source:
> 
> ```text
> worked in benchmark X
> ```
> 
> Output:
> 
> ```text
> works universally
> ```
> 
> Verification should catch context expansion.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1819. Quantitative Claim Verification
> 
> Numbers require:
> 
> ```text
> source
> unit
> population
> time
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1820. Example
> 
> ```text
> "Demand increased 40%."
> ```
> 
> requires:
> 
> ```text
> from what to what?
> which period?
> which sample?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1821. Temporal Verification
> 
> Check data freshness.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1822. Entity Verification
> 
> Is:
> 
> ```text
> Company A
> ```
> 
> same entity as:
> 
> ```text
> Company A GmbH
> ```
> 
> ?
> 
> Entity Resolution confidence matters.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1823. Identity errors propagate badly
> 
> Wrong merge can corrupt many Claims.
> 
> Therefore high-impact entity merge needs stronger verification.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1824. Merge Verification
> 
> Use:
> 
> ```text
> explicit links
> official identifiers
> domains
> ```
> 
> before merge.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1825. Ambiguous identity
> 
> Keep separate entities with:
> 
> ```text
> possible_same_as
> ```
> 
> rather than force merge.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1826. Data Integrity
> 
> Artifact hash checks:
> 
> ```text
> did file change?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1827. Semantic Integrity
> 
> More subtle:
> 
> ```text
> did meaning change?
> ```
> 
> Semantic diff helps.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1828. Regression Testing
> 
> Any change to:
> 
> ```text
> package
> ontology
> policy
> matcher
> procedure
> ```
> 
> can trigger benchmark suite.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1829. Regression Gate
> 
> Before production:
> 
> ```text
> no critical benchmark regression
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1830. Expected Change
> 
> Sometimes metric worsens intentionally.
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> slower
> but more accurate
> ```
> 
> Need decision record.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1831. Benchmark Delta
> 
> Show:
> 
> ```text
> Metric A +5%
> Metric B -8%
> Critical errors -50%
> Cost +20%
> ```
> 
> without forcing single winner.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1832. Upgrade Decision
> 
> Governance chooses based on objective profile.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1833. Shadow Evaluation
> 
> New system runs alongside old.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1834. Online Evaluation
> 
> Real workload split:
> 
> ```text
> control
> candidate
> ```
> 
> where safe.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1835. Canary for AI workflow
> 
> 5% low-risk tasks.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1836. Automatic rollback
> 
> Allowed if explicit criteria:
> 
> ```text
> critical error rate > threshold
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1837. Drift Detection
> 
> System behavior may degrade without version change due to:
> 
> ```text
> data drift
> API changes
> model provider changes
> environment changes
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1838. Input Drift
> 
> Current inputs differ from benchmark population.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1839. Capability Drift
> 
> Provider still works,
> 
> but no longer fits required context.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1840. Model Drift
> 
> Outputs shift.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1841. Ontology Drift
> 
> World concepts change:
> 
> ```text
> new terminology
> new technologies
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1842. Policy Drift
> 
> Policies no longer fit actual workflows.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1843. Drift Event
> 
> ```text
> DRIFT_DETECTED
> ```
> 
> creates review.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1844. Calibration Loop
> 
> ```text
> Prediction
> ↓
> Actual Outcome
> ↓
> Error
> ↓
> Model/Rule Review
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1845. Prediction Registry
> 
> Every forecast should ideally store:
> 
> ```text
> predicted value
> time horizon
> assumptions
> model version
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1846. Outcome arrives later
> 
> Compare.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1847. Forecast Calibration
> 
> Useful for:
> 
> ```text
> cost
> time
> resource demand
> project success criteria
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1848. Do not hide failed forecasts
> 
> They are valuable evidence.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1849. Simulation Calibration
> 
> Counterfactual Engine predictions vs actual outcomes.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1850. Example
> 
> Simulator predicted:
> 
> ```text
> new machine reduces queue 40%
> ```
> 
> Actual:
> 
> ```text
> 12%
> ```
> 
> Need root analysis.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1851. Simulation Error Registry
> 
> Store:
> 
> ```text
> scenario
> prediction
> actual
> error
> cause if known
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1852. Model Updating
> 
> Could update:
> 
> ```text
> queue model
> capacity assumptions
> ```
> 
> after review.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1853. Benchmark Governance
> 
> Who can change benchmark?
> 
> Important because changing benchmark can make metrics look better.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1854. Benchmark Definition is governed artifact
> 
> Need:
> 
> ```text
> version
> authority
> reason
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1855. Benchmark Retirement
> 
> Old benchmark may become obsolete.
> 
> State:
> 
> ```text
> ACTIVE
> DEPRECATED
> RETIRED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1856. Benchmark Compatibility
> 
> Historical results remain tied to old benchmark version.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1857. Standard Benchmark Registry
> 
> Could become part of Technopedia.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1858. Community Benchmark Contributions
> 
> Users/agents propose:
> 
> ```text
> new cases
> hard examples
> failure cases
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1859. Adversarial Cases
> 
> Important for:
> 
> ```text
> AI
> security
> entity resolution
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1860. Failure Corpus
> 
> Collect difficult cases intentionally.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1861. Regression Corpus
> 
> Every critical production failure can become:
> 
> ```text
> future test fixture
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1862. This turns mistakes into permanent system memory
> 
> Not personal memory,
> 
> but engineering memory.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1863. Postmortem
> 
> Significant failure produces:
> 
> ```text
> Failure Artifact
> ```
> 
> with:
> 
> ```text
> what happened
> why
> impact
> corrective action
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1864. Root Cause Claim
> 
> Need distinguish:
> 
> ```text
> confirmed root cause
> ```
> 
> from:
> 
> ```text
> suspected cause
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1865. Postmortem to Benchmark
> 
> Failure pattern → new fixture.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1866. Postmortem to Policy
> 
> If failure due to missing control:
> 
> ```text
> new policy proposal
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1867. Postmortem to Procedure
> 
> If failure due to workflow:
> 
> ```text
> procedure update
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1868. Postmortem to Capability Gap
> 
> If failure due to missing capability:
> 
> ```text
> new gap
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1869. Full learning loop
> 
> ```text
> Failure
> ↓
> Evidence
> ↓
> Root Cause
> ↓
> Improvement Proposal
> ↓
> Benchmark
> ↓
> Governance
> ↓
> Deploy
> ↓
> Verify
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1870. Quality Gate
> 
> Before lifecycle transitions:
> 
> ```text
> Prototype → Pilot
> Pilot → Production
> ```
> 
> Verification gates may be required.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1871. Stage Gate
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> Stage 0:
> concept evidence
> 
> Stage 1:
> prototype verification
> 
> Stage 2:
> pilot evidence
> 
> Stage 3:
> production readiness
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1872. Promotion requires evidence
> 
> Not enthusiasm.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1873. Technology Readiness Matrix
> 
> Dimensions:
> 
> ```text
> scientific
> engineering
> operational
> security
> ecosystem
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1874. No single maturity score required
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1875. Readiness Gap
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> science = strong
> engineering = medium
> operations = weak
> ```
> 
> Then next project is obvious:
> 
> ```text
> operational hardening
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1876. Verification Map of Project
> 
> For every requirement:
> 
> ```text
> Requirement
> → Evidence
> → Verification
> → Status
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1877. Example
> 
> ```text
> Requirement: secure execution
> Evidence: benchmark_1
> Verification: security_review_3
> Status: VERIFIED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1878. Unverified requirement
> 
> Visible immediately.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1879. Completion Percentage by tasks can mislead
> 
> Better complement with:
> 
> ```text
> verification coverage
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1880. Example
> 
> Project:
> 
> ```text
> 90% tasks DONE
> ```
> 
> but:
> 
> ```text
> critical safety requirement unverified
> ```
> 
> not production-ready.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1881. Verification Coverage Matrix
> 
> ```text
> Requirement      Evidence   Check   Status
> A                yes        yes     pass
> B                yes        no      unknown
> C                no         no      gap
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1882. Evidence Lineage to Goal
> 
> Can trace:
> 
> ```text
> Goal
> ↓
> Requirement
> ↓
> Claim
> ↓
> Evidence
> ↓
> Experiment
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1883. Goal Verification
> 
> Final question:
> 
> ```text
> Was Goal actually achieved?
> ```
> 
> not just:
> 
> ```text
> Were Tasks completed?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1884. Goal Outcome Evidence
> 
> Example Goal:
> 
> ```text
> Reduce processing time below 5 days.
> ```
> 
> Need actual operational data.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1885. Goal Closure Proposal
> 
> System can propose:
> 
> ```text
> ACHIEVED
> ```
> 
> with Evidence.
> 
> Governance closes strategic Goal.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1886. Goal Failure Evidence
> 
> Could show:
> 
> ```text
> target not achieved
> ```
> 
> without hiding result.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1887. Learning from negative result
> 
> Negative result can still create:
> 
> ```text
> valuable knowledge
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1888. Scientific null result
> 
> May reduce uncertainty substantially.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1889. Project Success ≠ only positive outcome
> 
> A validation project can succeed by proving:
> 
> ```text
> technology unsuitable
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1890. Success criteria must reflect information gain
> 
> For research/validation:
> 
> ```text
> resolve question
> ```
> 
> can be success.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1891. Verification and Innovation Economy
> 
> Evidence production has cost.
> 
> But verified capability becomes more reusable.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1892. Evidence Asset
> 
> High-quality benchmark/report can be reusable infrastructure.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1893. Evidence Reuse
> 
> One security audit may support:
> 
> ```text
> multiple projects
> ```
> 
> if contexts compatible.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1894. Context compatibility must be checked
> 
> Audit on version 1 does not necessarily validate version 3.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1895. Evidence Scope
> 
> Store:
> 
> ```text
> subject version
> environment
> time
> conditions
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1896. Evidence invalidation
> 
> If underlying artifact changes:
> 
> ```text
> verification may expire
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1897. Dependency-triggered invalidation
> 
> Package update:
> 
> ```text
> v1 → v2
> ```
> 
> can invalidate:
> 
> ```text
> security benchmark
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1898. Verification Dependency Graph
> 
> Need:
> 
> ```text
> Verification
> DEPENDS_ON
> Artifact Version
> Package Version
> Environment
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1899. Automatic Reverification Queue
> 
> Affected checks become:
> 
> ```text
> STALE
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1900. Verification Scheduler
> 
> Schedules:
> 
> ```text
> due checks
> expired checks
> high-criticality stale evidence
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1901. Periodic checks
> 
> Examples:
> 
> ```text
> weekly health
> monthly benchmark
> annual calibration
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1902. Event-triggered checks
> 
> Examples:
> 
> ```text
> new release
> policy change
> security advisory
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1903. Verification Capacity
> 
> Reviewers, labs, evaluators are Resources.
> 
> Thus verification itself can bottleneck.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1904. Verification Market
> 
> Project:
> 
> ```text
> REQUIRES security verification
> ```
> 
> Provider:
> 
> ```text
> Security Office
> PROVIDES security verification
> ```
> 
> Same universal market.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1905. Verification Queue
> 
> Could become strategic bottleneck.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1906. Shared Validation Center
> 
> Repeated verification demand may justify:
> 
> ```text
> central validation service
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1907. Independent Verification
> 
> For certain contexts, verifier must not be same as builder.
> 
> Policy can enforce:
> 
> ```text
> builder_id != verifier_id
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1908. Independent Evidence
> 
> Especially important for:
> 
> ```text
> security
> science
> regulated systems
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1909. Verification Authority
> 
> Some results require authorized external body.
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> certification
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1910. Internal PASS does not equal certification
> 
> Keep distinction.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1911. Verification Trust Chain
> 
> ```text
> Artifact
> ↓
> Evaluator
> ↓
> Evaluator Certification
> ↓
> Authority
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1912. Evaluator may itself need calibration
> 
> Physical measuring instrument:
> 
> ```text
> calibrated?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1913. Meta-dependency
> 
> This can recurse,
> 
> so use trusted roots.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1914. Trusted Verification Base
> 
> Keep small set of foundational:
> 
> ```text
> schema validators
> crypto hash
> policy engine
> calibration references
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1915. Verification Microkernel
> 
> Minimal trusted core:
> 
> ```text
> Verification Contract
> Evaluator Registry
> Evidence Links
> Result States
> Invalidation
> Audit
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1916. LLM role
> 
> LLM can:
> 
> ```text
> generate test ideas
> review evidence
> compare claims
> find contradictions
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1917. LLM cannot declare itself correct merely because it agrees with itself
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1918. Self-Evaluation is weak evidence
> 
> Useful as one layer only.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1919. External Grounding
> 
> Prefer:
> 
> ```text
> source
> execution
> measurement
> human review
> ```
> 
> where possible.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1920. Verification API
> 
> Minimum:
> 
> ```text
> POST /verify
> GET /verifications/{id}
> 
> POST /benchmarks/run
> GET /benchmarks/{id}/results
> 
> GET /claims/{id}/evidence
> POST /claims/{id}/reverify
> 
> GET /quality/world-state
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1921. Verification Request
> 
> ```yaml
> target:
>   type: CLAIM
>   id: claim_17
> 
> profile: STANDARD
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1922. Output
> 
> ```yaml
> result:
>   state: UNKNOWN
> 
> supporting_evidence:
>   - evidence_1
> 
> missing:
>   - independent_source
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1923. Benchmark API
> 
> ```text
> POST /benchmarks/{id}/run
> ```
> 
> with:
> 
> ```text
> provider
> environment
> version
> ```
>

> 
> Views:
> 
> ```text
> World State Quality
> Benchmark Status
> Stale Evidence
> Verification Gaps
> Critical Unknowns
> Drift
> Regression
> ```

> 
> Could show:
> 
> ```text
> 85% claims with provenance
> 62% critical claims verified
> 14 critical unknowns
> 3 unresolved conflicts
> ```
> 
> Descriptive metrics, not universal quality score.

> # 1926. Critical Unknown View
> 
> Sorted by:
> 
> ```text
> affected projects
> decision impact
> deadline
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1927. Verification Gap View
> 
> Shows:
> 
> ```text
> requirement
> missing check
> possible evaluators
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1928. Regression View
> 
> Shows:
> 
> ```text
> component
> old benchmark
> new benchmark
> changed dimensions
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1929. Epistemic Map
> 
> 2D graph:
> 
> ```text
> Claims
> ↔
> Evidence
> ↔
> Experiments
> ↔
> Sources
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1930. Confidence visualization
> 
> Should distinguish:
> 
> ```text
> verified
> supported
> contested
> unknown
> stale
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1931. 3D representation
> 
> In virtual technopark:
> 
> ```text
> knowledge buildings
> ```
> 
> could have:
> 
> ```text
> structural integrity
> ```
> 
> representing evidence quality,
> 
> but this is only UI metaphor.

> ---
> 
> # 1932. Fog of War
> 
> Очень подходящая игровая метафора для uncertainty.
> 
> Areas with insufficient evidence:
> 
> ```text
> partially hidden
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1933. But never confuse visual fog with factual uncertainty model
> 
> Canonical state remains explicit:
> 
> ```text
> UNKNOWN
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1934. Research missions
> 
> Could be generated specifically to:
> 
> ```text
> remove fog
> ```
> 
> that is:
> 
> ```text
> resolve critical unknown
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1935. This makes exploration meaningful
> 
> Not fictional exploration,
> 
> but real evidence acquisition.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1936. Verification-driven mission generation
> 
> ```text
> Critical Unknown
> ↓
> Evidence Gap
> ↓
> Research/Experiment Project
> ↓
> Mission
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1937. This closes the science loop
> 
> ```text
> Unknown
> ↓
> Hypothesis
> ↓
> Experiment
> ↓
> Evidence
> ↓
> Updated World
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1938. This also closes the engineering loop
> 
> ```text
> Requirement
> ↓
> Build
> ↓
> Test
> ↓
> Failure
> ↓
> Fix
> ↓
> Re-test
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1939. And organizational loop
> 
> ```text
> Organization hypothesis
> ↓
> pilot
> ↓
> measure
> ↓
> restructure / reject
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1940. And policy loop
> 
> ```text
> Policy proposal
> ↓
> shadow mode
> ↓
> measure effects
> ↓
> adopt / reject
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1941. Universal structure
> 
> Across science, software, organizations, policy:
> 
> ```text
> Hypothesis
> ↓
> Intervention
> ↓
> Observation
> ↓
> Evidence
> ↓
> Decision
> ```
> 
> This is one of the deepest common patterns in the architecture.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1942. Verification Engine therefore becomes universal feedback layer
> 
> It connects:
> 
> ```text
> World State
> Runtime
> Governance
> Simulation
> Package Manager
> Opportunity Engine
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1943. Full learning architecture
> 
> ```text
> WORLD STATE
> ↓
> Hypothesis / Goal
> ↓
> Action
> ↓
> Outcome
> ↓
> Verification
> ↓
> Evidence
> ↓
> World State Update
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1944. Error becomes information
> 
> Failure is not just:
> 
> ```text
> FAILED
> ```
> 
> It is:
> 
> ```text
> new evidence about model/world
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1945. Negative Evidence
> 
> System must support:
> 
> ```text
> REFUTES
> ```
> 
> as first-class relation.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1946. Avoid confirmation-only behavior
> 
> Resolvers should search for:
> 
> ```text
> disconfirming evidence
> ```
> 
> for important hypotheses.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1947. Falsification-first validation
> 
> For expensive opportunity:
> 
> ```text
> What cheapest evidence could show this idea is wrong?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1948. Kill-test
> 
> Before large investment:
> 
> ```text
> run small decisive experiment
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1949. Example
> 
> Hypothesis:
> 
> ```text
> sensor is durable enough
> ```
> 
> Instead of full product build:
> 
> ```text
> accelerated durability test
> ```
> 
> first.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1950. Evidence Efficiency
> 
> Measure:
> 
> ```text
> uncertainty reduced
> per unit resource
> ```
> 
> as descriptive analysis.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1951. Experiment Portfolio
> 
> When many unknowns exist,
> 
> choose experiments that resolve multiple unknowns.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1952. Multi-claim Evidence
> 
> One experiment can support/refute several Claims.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1953. Shared Experiment Opportunity
> 
> Several projects depend on same unknown.
> 
> Run one shared validation.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1954. Evidence Commons
> 
> Publicly reusable high-quality evidence can become shared infrastructure.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1955. Open Benchmark Commons
> 
> A public benchmark can reduce duplicated evaluation across ecosystem.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1956. Verification Standards
> 
> Eventually standardized:
> 
> ```text
> Capability X certified by Test Suite Y
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1957. Machine-readable certification
> 
> Certificate:
> 
> ```text
> subject
> capability
> version
> test suite
> issuer
> validity
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1958. Federated Verification
> 
> Remote lab can return signed:
> 
> ```text
> Verification Result
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1959. Local acceptance policy decides whether sufficient
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1960. Verification cannot be fully centralized
> 
> Different contexts need different standards.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1961. Shared base + local policy
> 
> Same architectural pattern again.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1962. Epistemic Security
> 
> Malicious actor may inject:
> 
> ```text
> false claims
> fake evidence
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 1963. Evidence Integrity
> 
> Use:
> 
> ```text
> hashes

> ## 2043. Главный переход
> 
> До этого Innovation OS уже умеет:

> ↓
> создавать Claims
> ↓
> собирать Evidence
> ↓
> выполнять Projects
> ↓
> проверять результаты
> ↓

> 
> Но возникает новая проблема:
> 
> ```text id="km2044"
> если всё сохранять одинаково,
> World State со временем превращается

> старых событий
> локальных наблюдений
> устаревших Claims

> ↓
> EPISODIC MEMORY
> ↓

> 
> Это сырые или почти сырые события:

> 
> Группирует события в осмысленные эпизоды.

> Например:

> current capabilities
> current valid claims
> current projects
> open gaps
> active policies
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2065. Historical Store
> 
> Содержит:
> 
> ```text id="km2073"

> old projects
> retired packages
> expired policies
> old resource states
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2066. Archive does not mean delete
> 
> Историческая информация остаётся для:
> 
> ```text id="km2074"
> audit
> learning
> replay
> research
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2067. Hot / Warm / Cold Memory
>

> 
> ```text id="km2075"
> HOT
> current operational state
> 
> WARM
> recent project/program history
> 
> COLD
> deep archive
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2068. Hot Memory
> 
> Fast database indexes.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2069. Warm Memory
> 
> Slower but searchable.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2070. Cold Memory
> 
> Object storage / archival database.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2071. Retrieval should be semantic
> 
> Context Builder может запросить:
> 
> ```text id="km2076"

> for Capability X
> ```
> 
> не загружая весь архив.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2072. Forgetting as engineering function
> 
> Не всё должно оставаться активным навсегда.
> 
> Но «забывание» здесь означает:
> 
> ```text id="km2077"
> deactivate from working memory
> ```
> 
> а не обязательно физически уничтожить.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2073. Forgetting Policies
> 
> Можно учитывать:
> 
> ```text id="km2078"
> age
> relevance
> supersession
> legal retention
> reuse frequency
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2074. Important exception
> 
> Evidence supporting active critical decisions:
> 
> ```text id="km2079"
> не должно быть автоматически forgotten
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2075. Dependency-aware retention
> 
> If Artifact supports:
> 
> ```text id="km2080"
> active Claim
> active Decision
> active Policy
> ```
> 
> retention policy must account for dependency.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2076. Garbage Collection
> 
> Semantic Garbage Collector can identify:
> 
> ```text id="km2081"
> orphan artifacts
> expired caches
> duplicate embeddings
> obsolete materialized views
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2077. Do not garbage-collect canonical evidence casually
> 
> Canonical history has different retention class.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2078. Materialized View Rebuild
> 
> Derived structures:
> 
> ```text id="km2082"
> matches
> gaps
> capability indices
> ```
> 
> can be deleted/recomputed.
> 
> Canonical Claims/Evidence cannot.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2079. Canonical vs Derived Storage
> 
> Freeze:
> 
> ```text id="km2083"
> CANONICAL
> DERIVED
> CACHE
> ARCHIVE
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2080. CANONICAL
> 
> ```text id="km2084"
> Claims
> Evidence
> Events
> Decisions
> Artifacts
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2081. DERIVED
> 
> ```text id="km2085"
> Open Gaps
> Matches
> Clusters
> Scores
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2082. CACHE
> 
> ```text id="km2086"
> embeddings
> query results
> temporary summaries
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2083. ARCHIVE
> 
> Historical canonical objects no longer active.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2084. Temporal World Model
> 
> World State should answer not only:
> 
> ```text id="km2087"
> что верно сейчас?
> ```
> 
> Но:
> 
> ```text id="km2088"
> что считалось верным на дату T?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2085. Valid Time vs Transaction Time
> 
> Useful distinction:
> 
> ```text id="km2089"
> VALID_TIME
> когда факт был верен в мире
> 
> TRANSACTION_TIME
> когда система его узнала
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2086. Example
> 
> Lab unavailable:
> 
> ```text id="km2090"
> valid_from = 10 Sept
> ```
> 
> но система узнала:
> 
> ```text id="km2091"
> 12 Sept
> ```
> 
> Это разные времена.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2087. Why important
> 
> Historical reconstruction:
> 
> ```text id="km2092"
> Decision made 11 Sept
> ```
> 
> не должна использовать knowledge discovered 12 Sept.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2088. Time-travel query
> 
> ```text id="km2093"
> SHOW WORLD STATE
> AS KNOWN AT 2026-09-11
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2089. Another query
> 
> ```text id="km2094"
> SHOW ACTUAL VALID STATE
> for 2026-09-11
> using all later corrections
> ```
> 
> Это две разные задачи.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2090. Bitemporal model
> 
> Long-term system may need:
> 
> ```text id="km2095"
> valid time
> +
> system knowledge time
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2091. Claim Supersession
> 
> New Claim may:
> 
> ```text id="km2096"
> SUPERSEDE
> ```
> 
> old Claim.
> 
> Old one remains historical.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2092. Correction
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text id="km2097"
> deadline = Oct 10
> ```
> 
> later corrected:
> 
> ```text id="km2098"
> deadline = Oct 17
> ```
> 
> History preserves both.
> 
> ---
>

> 
> If source retracts:
> 
> ```text id="km2099"

> ```
>

> 
> ```text id="km2100"

> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2094. Memory Consolidation Job
> 
> Periodically:
> 
> ```text id="km2101"
> collect recent events
> cluster episodes
> find repeated patterns
> identify stale knowledge
> produce consolidation proposals
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2095. Consolidation should not directly rewrite truth
> 
> It creates:
> 
> ```text id="km2102"
> Consolidation Proposal

> 
> for validation.

>

> 
> ```text id="km2103"

> 
> Proposal:
> 
> ```text id="km2104"
> Create Claim:
> API X rate limit
> is recurring operational bottleneck.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2097. Pattern Confidence
> 
> Depends on:
> 
> ```text id="km2105"
> number of episodes
> independence
> context similarity
> recency
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2098. Pattern ≠ universal law
> 
> Should preserve:
> 
> ```text id="km2106"
> scope
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2099. Scope
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text id="km2107"
> within EU-hosted deployment
> ```

> or:
> 
> ```text id="km2108"
> for Python-based agent services
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2100. Overgeneralization Detector
> 
> Consolidation Engine should ask:
> 
> ```text id="km2109"

> 
> # 2101. Example
> 
> Five failures share:
> 
> ```text id="km2110"
> same root cause

> good candidate for pattern.

> Five failures in unrelated contexts:
> 
> ```text id="km2111"

> ---
> 
> # 2102. Semantic Deduplication
> 
> World State may contain:
> 
> ```text id="km2112"
> browser automation
> web automation
> browser control
> ```
> 
> Possibly same/related concepts.
> 
> Need cautious dedup.
>

>

> 
> ```text id="km2113"
> candidate similarity
> ↓
> ontology/context comparison
> ↓
> evidence
> ↓
> merge proposal

> ---
> 
> # 2104. Embeddings only propose candidates
> 
> Never automatic entity merge.

> ---
> 
> # 2105. Merge states
> 
> ```text id="km2114"
> DISTINCT
> RELATED
> POSSIBLY_SAME
> SAME

> 
> # 2106. Merge Decision
> 
> For high-impact concepts/entities may require review.

> ---
> 
> # 2107. Entity Merge
> 
> If confirmed:
> 
> ```text id="km2115"
> Entity B
> MERGED_INTO
> Entity A

> But aliases/old IDs remain resolvable.

>

> 
> Sometimes one concept was too broad.
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text id="km2116"

> later splits into:
> 
> ```text id="km2117"
> task accuracy evaluation
> security evaluation
> tool-use evaluation
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2109. Semantic Split
> 
> Need migration of dependent Claims carefully.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2110. Concept Evolution
> 
> Concept registry itself evolves over time.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2111. Concept Versioning
> 
> Concept definition may change.
> 
> Store:
> 
> ```text id="km2118"
> definition version
> aliases
> relations
> effective dates
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2112. Avoid semantic drift without visibility
> 
> If meaning changes, old Claims need explicit historical interpretation.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2113. Ontology Evolution Engine
> 
> Functions:
> 
> ```text id="km2119"
> new concept proposal
> merge proposal
> split proposal
> relation update
> deprecation
> ```
>

> 
> # 2114. Ontology change is governed
> 
> Especially for canonical concepts.

> ---
>

>

> 
> ```text id="km2120"

> 
> ```text id="km2121"
> RepositoryEvaluation Archetype
> ```

> # 2116. Archetype extraction
> 
> Find:
> 
> ```text id="km2122"

> common Outputs

> 
> # 2117. Archetype ≠ copy of one project
>

>

> 
> For different contexts:
> 
> ```text id="km2123"
> FAST
> STANDARD
> HIGH_ASSURANCE
> ```

> 
> # 2119. Procedure Consolidation
>

> From execution traces:
>

> Example:
>

> license check
> ↓

> 
> Repeated failure modes should become structured knowledge.

> # 2123. Failure Pattern
> 
> Fields:
> 
> ```text id="km2127"
> symptoms
> conditions
> probable causes
> diagnostics
> known mitigations
> ```

> ---
> 
> # 2124. Example
> 
> ```text id="km2128"
> Symptom:
> API returns inconsistent pagination
>

> high-volume repository search
> 
> Mitigation:
> cursor validation + retry
> ```

> 
> # 2125. Troubleshooting Memory
> 
> Runtime can query:
> 
> ```text id="km2129"

> 
> ---
> 
> # 2126. Case-Based Reasoning
> 
> Current case:
> 
> ```text id="km2130"
> Problem P

> 
> retrieve:
> 
> ```text id="km2131"
> similar past episodes
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2127. Similarity by structure, not just text
> 
> Compare:
> 
> ```text id="km2132"
> capabilities
> constraints
> failure type
> resource graph
> ```

> ---
> 
> # 2128. Case Library
> 
> Useful for:
> 
> ```text id="km2133"
> debugging
> project estimation
> risk analysis
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2129. Lesson Learned
> 
> Project completion can produce:
> 
> ```text id="km2134"
> Lesson

> 
> as structured Claim.

> 
> # 2130. Good lesson format
> 
> ```text id="km2135"
> Context
> Observation
> Interpretation
> Evidence
> Applicability
> Exceptions
> ```

> 
> # 2131. Bad lesson
>

> 
> without context.
>

> 
> # 2132. Local Lesson
> 
> Could be:
> 
> ```text id="km2137"

> 
> Much stronger epistemically.

> ---
> 
> # 2133. Negative Knowledge
> 
> System must deliberately preserve:
> 
> ```text id="km2138"

> ```

> ---
> 
> # 2134. Why
> 
> Otherwise future agents repeatedly try same failed paths.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2135. Negative Knowledge types
> 
> ```text id="km2139"
> Rejected Technology
> Failed Procedure
> Invalid Hypothesis
> Incompatible Provider
> Dead-end Research Path
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2136. But negative result also contextual
> 
> ```text id="km2140"
> didn't work in context X
> ```
> 
> not:
> 
> ```text id="km2141"
> never works
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2137. Dead-End Cache
> 
> For low-level search:
> 
> ```text id="km2142"
> already checked candidate
> failed because hard blocker
> ```
> 
> can prevent repeated work.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2138. Cache expiry
> 
> If blocker can change:
> 
> ```text id="km2143"

> new version released
> availability changed
> ```
> 
> dead-end cache expires/rechecks.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2139. Stable Negative Knowledge
> 
> Some failures remain long-lived.
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text id="km2144"
> hardware physically incompatible
> ```
> 
> unless hardware version changes.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2140. Memory Retrieval
> 
> Need several modes:
> 
> ```text id="km2145"
> EXACT
> SEMANTIC
> GRAPH
> TEMPORAL
> CASE-BASED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2141. Exact retrieval
> 
> Known ID/term.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2142. Semantic retrieval
> 
> Find similar meaning.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2143. Graph retrieval
> 
> Follow dependencies/relations.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2144. Temporal retrieval
> 
> Find:
> 
> ```text id="km2146"
> what happened before/after event X
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2145. Case-based retrieval
> 
> Find similar historical episodes.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2146. Contextual Retrieval
> 
> Agent should not receive all relevant-ish memories.
> 
> Need rank by:
> 
> ```text id="km2147"
> task relevance
> authority
> freshness
> evidence
> scope match
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2147. Memory Retrieval Contract
> 
> Input:
> 
> ```text id="km2148"
> task
> context
> required knowledge types
> token/size budget
> ```
> 
> Output:
> 
> ```text id="km2149"
> minimal useful memory package
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2148. Context Builder integration
> 
> Before AI Action:
> 
> ```text id="km2150"
> current task
> +
> active state
> +
> retrieved memory
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2149. Avoid Memory Flooding
> 
> Too much historical context can:
> 
> ```text id="km2151"

> increase cost
> surface stale assumptions
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2150. Retrieval Diversity
> 
> For contested questions, retrieve:
> 
> ```text id="km2152"
> supporting
> refuting
> alternative
> ```
> 
> memory.

> 
> # 2151. Not only nearest-neighbor search
> 
> Otherwise semantic retrieval may create echo chamber.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2152. Memory Freshness
> 
> Every memory item should know:
> 
> ```text id="km2153"
> last validated
> last used
> current applicability
> ```
>

>

>

> 
> # 2154. Example
>

> ---
> 
> # 2155. Revalidation on Reactivation
> 
> Before relying on old knowledge:
> 
> ```text id="km2155"
> check stale dependencies
> versions
> context
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2156. Knowledge Half-Life
> 
> Different classes decay differently:
> 
> ```text id="km2156"

> software compatibility: medium
> physics principle: slow
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2157. Half-life is heuristic
> 
> Not delete schedule.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2158. Memory Usage Statistics
> 
> Track:
> 
> ```text id="km2157"
> which memories are retrieved
> which affect decisions
> which become stale
> ```

> ---
> 
> # 2159. Popular ≠ True
>

> 
> ---
> 
> # 2160. Memory Influence Graph
> 
> Can trace:
> 
> ```text id="km2158"
> Memory Claim
> ↓
> Decision
> ↓
> Action
> ↓
> Outcome
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2161. This permits evaluating memory quality
> 
> If one old heuristic repeatedly causes failures:
> 
> ```text id="km2159"

> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2162. Knowledge Utility
> 
> Dimensions:
> 
> ```text id="km2160"
> reuse
> decision relevance
> accuracy
> freshness
> cost saved
> ```
> 
> No universal score required.

> ---
> 
> # 2163. Semantic Summary
> 
> Long project can produce:
> 
> ```text id="km2161"

> 
> but summaries need provenance links.

> 
> # 2164. Hierarchical Summary
> 
> ```text id="km2162"
> Task Summary
> ↓
> Project Summary
> ↓
> Program Summary
> ↓
> Portfolio Summary

>

> 
> # 2166. Summary is not canonical truth

> 
> # 2167. Semantic Compression with drill-down
>

> User/agent can expand:

> ```text id="km2165"

> → Evidence

> 
> # 2168. Knowledge Graph vs Document Store
> 
> Need both.
> 
> Knowledge Graph:
> 
> ```text id="km2166"
> structured relations
> ```

> Document Store:
> 
> ```text id="km2167"

> PDFs
> code
> datasets

> # 2169. Graph should reference artifacts

> ---
> 
> # 2170. Granularity principle

> ```text id="km2168"

> # 2171. Over-structuring is costly

> System may choose:
> 
> ```text id="km2169"

> 
> based on importance.

>

> 
> ```text id="km2170"

> ---
> 
> # 2174. Low-value Artifact
> 
> Minor log:
>

> 
> # 2175. Adaptive Structuring
> 
> If low-value artifact later becomes important:
> 
> ```text id="km2172"

> 
> ---
> 
> # 2176. Memory Consolidation Policies
> 
> Could run:
> 
> ```text id="km2173"

> weekly for events

> ```

> ---
> 
> # 2177. Triggered Consolidation
> 
> Events:
> 
> ```text id="km2174"

> ONTOLOGY_CONFLICT

> ---
> 
> # 2178. Project Closeout
> 
> Should generate:

> ```text id="km2175"

> remaining unknowns

> ```

> 
> Example:
> 
> ```yaml id="km2176"

>   outcomes: [...]

> ```text id="km2177"

> # 2181. Unused Artifact

> 
> # 2182. Reusable Asset Promotion
> 
> Artifact reused across several projects can become:

> in registry.

> Procedure used repeatedly:

>

>

> # 2186. Reusable Policy Pattern
> 
> Stable repeated approvals:

> ```text id="km2182"

> ```text id="km2183"

> Pattern
> ↓
> Package
> ↓
> Reusable Capability

> # 2188. Experience-to-Package Pipeline
>

> System can learn not only model weights,

> procedures
> archetypes
> policies
> templates
> ```

> 
> # 2189. Structured Learning over model fine-tuning
>

> explicit knowledge
> workflow
> rule

> 
> rather than silently fine-tune model.

> # 2190. Why
> 
> Explicit knowledge is:
> 
> ```text id="km2186"
> auditable
> reversible
> versioned
> ```

> ---
> 
> # 2191. Model Fine-tuning remains optional
> 
> And should happen through separate governed pipeline.

> ---
> 
> # 2192. Memory Branching
> 
> Counterfactual/scenario worlds need separate memory.
> 
> Do not let:
> 
> ```text id="km2187"
> simulated event
> ```
> 
> enter base-world history as real event.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2193. Scenario Memory
> 
> Tagged:
> 
> ```text id="km2188"
> context = SCENARIO
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2194. Merge Scenario Knowledge
> 
> If simulation reveals useful insight:
> 
> ```text id="km2189"
> can create HYPOTHESIS in base world
> ```
> 
> not FACT.

> ---
> 
> # 2195. Example
> 
> Simulation shows:
> 
> ```text id="km2190"
> possible bottleneck migration
> ```
> 
> Base World gets:
>

> B may become bottleneck.
> ```

> 
> # 2196. Memory Isolation
> 
> Private project memory should not automatically become organization-wide memory.

>

>

> PROJECT
> PROGRAM
> ORGANIZATION
> FEDERATION
> PUBLIC
> ```

>

> 
> Before moving:
> 
> ```text id="km2193"
> PRIVATE PROJECT
> →
> PUBLIC KNOWLEDGE

> 
> run:
> 
> ```text id="km2194"
> redaction
> review
> license
> approval
> ```

> 
> # 2199. Confidential Knowledge
>

> 
> # 2200. Federated Memory
> 
> Each node owns memory.
> 
> Federation shares only permitted semantic objects.

>

>

>

>

>

> and inspect dependent local decisions.

> 
> # 2204. Memory Dependency Review

>

> 
> ```text id="km2199"

> 
> ```text id="km2200"

> 
> # 2207. Context-aware federation is essential

> ---
>

>

> 
> # 2209. Consensus is derived, not forced

> 
> # 2210. Memory Quality
>

> verification
> freshness
> scope
> conflicts

> 
> # 2215. Sybil-resistant consolidation
>

> 
> # 2216. Provenance clustering
> 
> Detect common root source.

> ---
>

> 
> Raw untrusted text remains Artifact.

> until validated.

> # 2356. Следующий фундаментальный слой
> 
> После этого появляется следующий вопрос:
> 
> > Если Innovation OS накопила огромную память, множество capabilities, procedures, packages и federated nodes, как ей эффективно находить **новые причинные связи и объяснять, почему одно изменение приводит к другому**, а не только обнаруживать корреляции?
> 
> Следующий модуль:
> 
> # **Causal Reasoning, Dependency Discovery & Intervention Engine v0.1**
> 
> Он должен различать:
> 
> ```text id="km2318"
> корреляцию
> причинную гипотезу
> структурную зависимость
> наблюдаемое последствие
> ```
> 
> и работать с:
> 
> ```text id="km2319"
> causal graphs
> interventions
> counterfactuals
> root-cause analysis
> causal experiments
> ```
> 
> Чтобы система могла отвечать не только:
> 
> > «Какие события часто происходят вместе?»
> 
> но и:
> 
> > «Что, вероятно, является причиной bottleneck?»  
> > «Какое минимальное изменение может его устранить?»  
> > «Что нужно измерить, чтобы отличить две конкурирующие причинные гипотезы?»  
> > «Если изменить Resource X, какие downstream effects действительно следуют из зависимости, а какие только коррелируют?»
> 
> Это будет следующий шаг от **семантической памяти** к **объясняющей модели мира**.

Следующая часть — **Causal Reasoning, Dependency Discovery & Intervention Engine v0.1**: слой причинности, root-cause анализа, интервенций и различения «вместе произошло» от «одно действительно вызвало другое».
