Теперь следующий слой — **Multi-Agent Coordination, Negotiation & Collective Intelligence Engine v0.1**: не «чат многих агентов», а формальная система разделения труда, передачи контекста, конкурирующих предложений, согласования, проверки и совместного выполнения задач людьми, AI-агентами, командами и внешними организациями.

> **Document: Multi-Agent Coordination, Negotiation & Collective Intelligence Engine v0.1**
> 
> # Multi-Agent Coordination, Negotiation & Collective Intelligence Engine v0.1
> 
> ## 2966. Главный переход
> 
> До этого Innovation OS уже умеет:
> 
> ```text
> ставить цели
> ↓
> строить стратегии
> ↓
> создавать проекты
> ↓
> компилировать процедуры
> ↓
> распределять ресурсы
> ↓
> проверять результаты
> ```
> 
> Но при масштабировании возникает новая проблема:
> 
> ```text
> одновременно существуют:
> 50 AI-агентов
> 20 людей
> 10 команд
> 15 внешних сервисов
> 5 организаций
> ```
> 
> Они не могут эффективно работать как один гигантский групповой чат.
> 
> Нужен отдельный coordination layer.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2967. Основная формула
> 
> ```text
> Work
> ↓
> Decomposition
> ↓
> Assignment
> ↓
> Parallel Execution
> ↓
> Structured Handoffs
> ↓
> Conflict Detection
> ↓
> Verification
> ↓
> Merge
> ↓
> Shared State Update
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2968. Multi-Agent System ≠ множество моделей
> 
> Важно различать:
> 
> ```text
> MODEL
> AGENT
> ROLE
> TASK
> RESOURCE
> ```
> 
> Модель:
> 
> ```text
> GPT / local LLM / other model
> ```
> 
> Agent:
> 
> ```text
> runtime entity
> with state, tools, permissions
> ```
> 
> Role:
> 
> ```text
> SCOUT
> ANALYST
> BUILDER
> REVIEWER
> ```
> 
> Task:
> 
> ```text
> конкретная работа
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2969. Agent не должен быть пожизненно привязан к одной роли
> 
> Один Agent instance может:
> 
> ```text
> Task A → SCOUT
> Task B → ANALYST
> ```
> 
> если capability и policy позволяют.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2970. Agent Identity
> 
> Каждый Agent должен иметь:
> 
> ```text
> agent_id
> instance_id
> model/provider
> package version
> permissions
> current roles
> active tasks
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2971. Agent ≠ Model Session
> 
> Одна model session может завершиться.
> 
> Agent identity может жить дольше:
> 
> ```text
> state
> tasks
> history
> bindings
> ```
> 
> сохраняются отдельно.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2972. Основная проблема коллективного интеллекта
> 
> Не:
> 
> ```text
> как заставить 100 агентов говорить одновременно?
> ```
> 
> А:
> 
> ```text
> как разбить проблему,
> кому что дать,
> как объединить результат,
> как обнаружить ошибки,
> как не дублировать работу?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2973. Blackboard Architecture
> 
> Основной coordination pattern:
> 
> ```text
> Shared Blackboard
> ```
> 
> содержит:
> 
> ```text
> Tasks
> Claims
> Artifacts
> Evidence
> Questions
> Decisions
> Events
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2974. Агенты не обязаны общаться напрямую
> 
> Agent A:
> 
> ```text
> публикует Artifact
> ```
> 
> Agent B:
> 
> ```text
> читает Artifact
> ```
> 
> Coordinator:
> 
> ```text
> видит state transition
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2975. Почему это лучше гигантского чата
> 
> Chat-based coordination создаёт:
> 
> ```text
> context duplication
> message explosion
> lost decisions
> unclear authority
> ```
> 
> Blackboard:
> 
> ```text
> shared structured state
> ```
> 
> решает значительную часть проблемы.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2976. Direct Message всё же нужен
> 
> Но только для:
> 
> ```text
> request
> clarification
> handoff
> review
> ```
> 
> а не как основной storage.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2977. Agent Message Types
> 
> Минимально:
> 
> ```text
> TASK_REQUEST
> TASK_ACCEPT
> TASK_RESULT
> QUESTION
> ANSWER
> REVIEW_REQUEST
> REVIEW_RESULT
> BLOCKER
> PROPOSAL
> COUNTERPROPOSAL
> ESCALATION
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2978. Message ≠ Claim
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> Agent A:
> "I think Repo X is suitable."
> ```
> 
> Это сообщение.
> 
> Чтобы попасть в World State:
> 
> ```text
> Candidate Claim
> +
> Evidence
> ```
> 
> нужны отдельно.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2979. Message ≠ Decision
> 
> Даже если Agent пишет:
> 
> ```text
> "Use Provider B."
> ```
> 
> это Proposal.
> 
> Decision возникает только через governance.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2980. Task Ownership
> 
> Каждый активный Task должен знать:
> 
> ```text
> OWNER
> EXECUTOR
> REVIEWER
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2981. Owner ≠ Executor
> 
> Owner отвечает за достижение Task outcome.
> 
> Executor выполняет конкретную работу.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2982. Task Claiming
> 
> Agent может:
> 
> ```text
> CLAIM task
> ```
> 
> на определённый lease period.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2983. Lease
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> lease_until = 10:30
> ```
> 
> Если Agent исчез:
> 
> ```text
> Task → READY
> ```
> 
> при условии, что повтор безопасен.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2984. Duplicate Work Prevention
> 
> До начала Agent проверяет:
> 
> ```text
> кто уже выполняет эту задачу?
> существует ли Artifact?
> существует ли active lease?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2985. Intent Reservation
> 
> Для дорогой работы полезно сначала:
> 
> ```text
> RESERVE_INTENT
> ```
> 
> например:
> 
> ```text
> Agent A plans expensive simulation.
> ```
> 
> Чтобы другой Agent не запустил ту же simulation.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2986. Work Decomposition
> 
> Coordinator получает:
> 
> ```text
> Complex Task
> ```
> 
> и разбивает на:
> 
> ```text
> Subtask A
> Subtask B
> Subtask C
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2987. Независимость subtasks
> 
> Compiler должен определить:
> 
> ```text
> можно ли выполнять параллельно?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2988. Example
> 
> Technology analysis:
> 
> ```text
> Agent A → papers
> Agent B → GitHub
> Agent C → patents
> Agent D → funding
> ```
> 
> параллельно.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2989. Merge Dependency
> 
> После:
> 
> ```text
> A
> B
> C
> D
> ```
> 
> нужен:
> 
> ```text
> SYNTHESIS TASK
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2990. Synthesis Agent
> 
> Он получает не полные chats,
> 
> а:
> 
> ```text
> structured outputs
> claims
> evidence
> unknowns
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2991. Handoff Contract
> 
> Передача работы должна иметь:
> 
> ```text
> objective
> completed
> remaining
> artifacts
> open questions
> blockers
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2992. Handoff Example
> 
> ```yaml
> handoff:
>   from: agent_A
>   to: agent_B
> 
>   task: repo_analysis
> 
>   completed:
>     - metadata
>     - license
> 
>   remaining:
>     - security review
> 
>   artifacts:
>     - report_17
> 
>   blockers:
>     - dependency_version_unknown
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2993. Context Minimization
> 
> Agent B не получает:
> 
> ```text
> 50 000 tokens истории
> ```
> 
> если достаточно:
> 
> ```text
> Task
> Artifact
> Constraints
> Open Questions
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2994. Agent Context Builder
> 
> Для каждого Task формируется:
> 
> ```text
> Task Context Package
> ```
> 
> с минимально достаточным state.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2995. Context Package Priority
> 
> Порядок примерно:
> 
> ```text
> Hard Constraints
> Current Goal
> Task Inputs
> Relevant Decisions
> Relevant Evidence
> Recent Failures
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2996. Agent Isolation
> 
> Каждый Agent работает:
> 
> ```text
> within scoped context
> ```
> 
> чтобы снизить:
> 
> ```text
> cross-task contamination
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2997. Shared Memory ≠ shared prompt
> 
> Общая память живёт:
> 
> ```text
> в World State / Project State
> ```
> 
> а не в одной общей token sequence.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2998. Coordination Roles
> 
> Начальный набор:
> 
> ```text
> COORDINATOR
> SCOUT
> ANALYST
> PLANNER
> BUILDER
> REVIEWER
> VERIFIER
> MONITOR
> NEGOTIATOR
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 2999. Coordinator
> 
> Функции:
> 
> ```text
> decompose
> assign
> track
> merge
> escalate
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3000. Scout
> 
> Ищет:
> 
> ```text
> resources
> technologies
> people
> papers
> funding
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3001. Analyst
> 
> Проверяет:
> 
> ```text
> fit
> constraints
> evidence
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3002. Planner
> 
> Создаёт:
> 
> ```text
> Task Graph
> Procedure
> Resource Plan
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3003. Builder
> 
> Создаёт:
> 
> ```text
> code
> artifact
> prototype
> configuration
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3004. Reviewer
> 
> Критикует:
> 
> ```text
> quality
> completeness
> reasoning
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3005. Verifier
> 
> Запускает:
> 
> ```text
> tests
> benchmarks
> external checks
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3006. Monitor
> 
> Следит за:
> 
> ```text
> conditions
> deadlines
> resource state
> drift
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3007. Negotiator
> 
> Работает с:
> 
> ```text
> offers
> constraints
> resource commitments
> ```
> 
> но не получает полномочия подписывать соглашения без authority.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3008. Role Composition
> 
> Один Task может требовать:
> 
> ```text
> Scout
> +
> Analyst
> +
> Reviewer
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3009. Separation of Roles
> 
> Для high-risk output полезно:
> 
> ```text
> Builder ≠ Reviewer
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3010. Independence
> 
> Но разные Agent instances на одной и той же модели:
> 
> ```text
> не полностью независимы
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3011. Independent Verification
> 
> Для критичных задач лучше сочетать:
> 
> ```text
> different models
> deterministic tools
> human review
> external evidence
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3012. Agent Capability Profile
> 
> Agent может PROVIDE:
> 
> ```text
> literature_search
> code_generation
> document_analysis
> ```
> 
> с operational evidence.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3013. Agent Capability ≠ model marketing claim
> 
> System должна измерять:
> 
> ```text
> actual verified performance
> ```
> 
> по конкретным Tasks.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3014. Agent Registry
> 
> Хранит:
> 
> ```text
> agent instance
> roles
> capabilities
> permissions
> availability
> cost model
> health
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3015. Agent Health
> 
> States:
> 
> ```text
> AVAILABLE
> BUSY
> DEGRADED
> FAILED
> UNKNOWN
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3016. Agent Capacity
> 
> Может измеряться:
> 
> ```text
> concurrent tasks
> token budget
> requests/minute
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3017. Human Agent Representation
> 
> Люди тоже могут участвовать в coordination graph.
> 
> Но:
> 
> ```text
> не как программные процессы
> ```
> 
> а как Resources с availability/authority/consent.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3018. Human Task Interface
> 
> Human получает:
> 
> ```text
> короткий brief
> inputs
> required decision/output
> deadline
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3019. External Organization as Agent-Like Node
> 
> Organization может принимать:
> 
> ```text
> Task Proposal
> ```
> 
> и возвращать:
> 
> ```text
> Artifact / Evidence
> ```
> 
> через federation.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3020. Collective Intelligence
> 
> Главная идея:
> 
> ```text
> результат группы
> не должен быть просто
> средним мнением агентов
> ```
> 
> Он должен появляться через:
> 
> ```text
> specialization
> competition
> critique
> verification
> synthesis
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3021. Ensemble ≠ Collective Intelligence
> 
> Ensemble:
> 
> ```text
> ask 10 agents same question
> take majority
> ```
> 
> Collective system:
> 
> ```text
> agents perform different functions
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3022. Когда полезен параллельный independent solve
> 
> Для:
> 
> ```text
> ambiguous reasoning
> architecture alternatives
> creative design
> ```
> 
> можно получить:
> 
> ```text
> Proposal A
> Proposal B
> Proposal C
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3023. Proposal Tournament
> 
> Не обязательно «голосование».
> 
> Pipeline:
> 
> ```text
> multiple proposals
> ↓
> constraint check
> ↓
> critique
> ↓
> evidence
> ↓
> comparison
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3024. Proposal Object
> 
> ```yaml
> proposal:
>   author: agent_A
>   target: architecture_problem
> 
>   solution: ...
> 
>   assumptions: [...]
>   required_resources: [...]
>   risks: [...]
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3025. Counterproposal
> 
> Другой Agent может:
> 
> ```text
> COUNTERPROPOSAL
> ```
> 
> с указанием:
> 
> ```text
> какое assumption изменено
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3026. Critique должна быть структурированной
> 
> Не:
> 
> ```text
> "Я не согласен."
> ```
> 
> А:
> 
> ```text
> Constraint violation
> Unsupported assumption
> Missing evidence
> Alternative explanation
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3027. Critique Categories
> 
> ```text
> FACTUAL
> LOGICAL
> CONSTRAINT
> EVIDENCE
> SECURITY
> COST
> SCOPE
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3028. Debate Graph
> 
> Можно хранить:
> 
> ```text
> Proposal
> ↔ Critique
> ↔ Rebuttal
> ↔ Evidence
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3029. Но бесконечный debate запрещён
> 
> Need:
> 
> ```text
> iteration limit
> decision rule
> progress criterion
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3030. Debate Termination
> 
> Завершить, если:
> 
> ```text
> critical objections resolved
> no new evidence
> budget exhausted
> human decision requested
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3031. No-progress Detector
> 
> Если последние iterations:
> 
> ```text
> не добавили Evidence
> не изменили Proposal
> ```
> 
> →
> 
> ```text
> DEBATE_STALLED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3032. Argument Count ≠ truth
> 
> Пять Agents могут повторять одну ошибку.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3033. Evidence-weighted Synthesis
> 
> Synthesis должен смотреть:
> 
> ```text
> evidence quality
> constraint satisfaction
> unknowns
> ```
> 
> а не число сторонников.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3034. Consensus
> 
> Useful state:
> 
> ```text
> CONSENSUS
> PARTIAL_CONSENSUS
> CONTESTED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3035. Consensus ≠ verification
> 
> Даже unanimous agents:
> 
> ```text
> могут ошибаться
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3036. Dissent Preservation
> 
> Если один reviewer имеет сильное evidence-backed objection:
> 
> ```text
> не скрывать его
> ```
> 
> ради красивого consensus.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3037. Minority Report
> 
> Можно хранить:
> 
> ```text
> minority_proposal
> ```
> 
> с conditions:
> 
> ```text
> when it would become relevant
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3038. Negotiation Engine
> 
> Отдельный слой для:
> 
> ```text
> resources
> time
> scope
> conditions
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3039. Negotiation ≠ governance decision
> 
> Negotiator может:
> 
> ```text
> обсуждать условия
> ```
> 
> но final binding требует authority.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3040. Negotiation Object
> 
> ```yaml
> negotiation:
>   demand: demand_17
>   provider: resource_B
> 
>   negotiable:
>     - quantity
>     - start_date
>     - price
> 
>   non_negotiable:
>     - data_residency
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3041. Hard vs Negotiable Terms
> 
> Очень важно.
> 
> ```text
> HARD:
> cannot change
> 
> NEGOTIABLE:
> can trade
> 
> PREFERENCE:
> nice to have
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3042. Example
> 
> Project wants:
> 
> ```text
> 20h/week
> start Oct 1
> €100/h
> ```
> 
> Provider offers:
> 
> ```text
> 15h/week
> start Oct 15
> €90/h
> ```
> 
> Negotiation explores feasible overlap.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3043. Constraint Satisfaction Negotiation
> 
> Не обязательно language-model bargaining.
> 
> Often:
> 
> ```text
> constraint solver
> ```
> 
> can identify:
> 
> ```text
> feasible agreement region
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3044. Negotiation Envelope
> 
> Human/organization can pre-authorize:
> 
> ```text
> price <= €110
> start <= Oct 15
> minimum 15h/week
> ```
> 
> Agent can negotiate inside envelope.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3045. Outside Envelope
> 
> →
> 
> ```text
> ESCALATE
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3046. This allows bounded autonomous negotiation
> 
> without giving Agent unrestricted authority.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3047. Negotiation Privacy
> 
> Agent does not need know:
> 
> ```text
> full internal budget
> ```
> 
> Only:
> 
> ```text
> allowed negotiation envelope
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3048. Reservation During Negotiation
> 
> Scarce resource may be:
> 
> ```text
> temporarily held
> ```
> 
> while terms negotiated.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3049. Negotiation Timeout
> 
> If no agreement by T:
> 
> ```text
> release reservation
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3050. Multi-Party Negotiation
> 
> Consortium may involve:
> 
> ```text
> Org A
> Org B
> Org C
> ```
> 
> with:
> 
> ```text
> roles
> budget shares
> work packages
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3051. Consortium Negotiation Graph
> 
> ```text
> Partner
> ↔ Role
> ↔ Capability
> ↔ Budget
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3052. Local Constraints remain private
> 
> Each organization may expose only:
> 
> ```text
> acceptable public terms
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3053. Agreement Proposal
> 
> Negotiation result:
> 
> ```text
> PROPOSED AGREEMENT
> ```
> 
> not active commitment.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3054. Agreement approval
> 
> Requires:
> 
> ```text
> local decisions
> ```
> 
> from relevant parties.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3055. Agent-to-Agent Contract
> 
> Для machine work можно иметь:
> 
> ```text
> Task Contract
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3056. Task Contract
> 
> Fields:
> 
> ```text
> objective
> inputs
> expected outputs
> deadline
> budget
> verification
> permissions
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3057. Example
> 
> ```yaml
> task_contract:
>   task: analyze_repositories
>   max_candidates: 20
>   max_cost: ...
>   output_schema: RepositoryCandidateSet
>   done_if: evaluator_pass
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3058. Contract prevents scope drift
> 
> Agent не должен превращать:
> 
> ```text
> analyze 20 repositories
> ```
> 
> в:
> 
> ```text
> redesign entire platform
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3059. Agent Budget
> 
> Per Task:
> 
> ```text
> token
> time
> API
> tool-call
> money
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3060. Budget Exhaustion
> 
> If exhausted:
> 
> ```text
> WAITING_FOR_BUDGET
> ```
> 
> or return partial result.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3061. Partial Result
> 
> Must explicitly state:
> 
> ```text
> what completed
> what incomplete
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3062. Progressive Results
> 
> Для long tasks agents can publish:
> 
> ```text
> intermediate artifacts
> ```
> 
> before final completion.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3063. Useful for early steering
> 
> Coordinator can stop useless branch.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3064. Speculative Agents
> 
> Можно запускать:
> 
> ```text
> alternative exploration
> ```
> 
> in parallel.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3065. Speculative Budget
> 
> Strictly bounded.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3066. Early Cancellation
> 
> If primary branch succeeds:
> 
> ```text
> cancel redundant speculation
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3067. Agent Scheduling
> 
> Scheduler chooses:
> 
> ```text
> which agent handles which Task
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3068. Assignment Factors
> 
> ```text
> capability fit
> availability
> permissions
> cost
> context locality
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3069. Context Locality
> 
> Agent already working on related project may require:
> 
> ```text
> less context rebuilding
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3070. But sticky assignment can create silos
> 
> Sometimes independent reviewer is preferable.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3071. Assignment Modes
> 
> ```text
> CONTINUITY
> INDEPENDENCE
> LOW_COST
> FASTEST_AVAILABLE
> ```
> 
> as policy lenses.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3072. No universal best Agent
> 
> Same principle as all resource matching.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3073. Agent Specialization
> 
> Over time agent packages may become specialized:
> 
> ```text
> Grant Scout
> Repo Auditor
> Causal Analyst
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3074. Specialization should come from:
> 
> ```text
> explicit package
> verified performance
> ```
> 
> not arbitrary personality labels.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3075. Dynamic Role Formation
> 
> Repeated task bundle may create:
> 
> ```text
> new Agent Role Archetype
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3076. Example
> 
> Tasks:
> 
> ```text
> find sources
> verify citations
> detect contradictions
> ```
> 
> repeat together.
> 
> Could form:
> 
> ```text
> Evidence Auditor
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3077. Role Registry
> 
> Maintains:
> 
> ```text
> required capabilities
> permissions
> typical tasks
> verification
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3078. Multi-Agent Procedure
> 
> Procedure Graph can assign:
> 
> ```text
> node → role
> ```
> 
> not exact Agent.
> 
> Runtime resolves actual instance.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3079. Example
> 
> ```text
> SEARCH → SCOUT
> ANALYZE → ANALYST
> VERIFY → REVIEWER
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3080. Role Late Binding
> 
> At runtime choose:
> 
> ```text
> Agent A
> Agent B
> Human C
> ```
> 
> for each role.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3081. Agent Pool
> 
> Maintain:
> 
> ```text
> SCOUT_POOL
> REVIEWER_POOL
> ```
> 
> with capacity.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3082. Autoscaling
> 
> Machine Agents can:
> 
> ```text
> spawn more instances
> ```
> 
> within policy/budget.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3083. Human resources cannot be autoscaled similarly
> 
> System may propose:
> 
> ```text
> additional staffing
> ```
> 
> only.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3084. Agent Spawn Policy
> 
> Conditions:
> 
> ```text
> queue length
> budget
> max instances
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3085. Agent Lifecycle
> 
> ```text
> CREATED
> AVAILABLE
> CLAIMED
> RUNNING
> IDLE
> DEGRADED
> TERMINATED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3086. Ephemeral Agents
> 
> Task-specific instances:
> 
> ```text
> spawn
> execute
> destroy
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3087. Persistent Agents
> 
> Useful where:
> 
> ```text
> long-running monitoring
> local working memory
> specialized tools
> ```
> 
> matter.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3088. Persistent Agent risk
> 
> Can accumulate:
> 
> ```text
> stale state
> drift
> permission creep
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3089. Periodic Revalidation
> 
> Persistent Agent needs:
> 
> ```text
> capability benchmark
> permission review
> memory cleanup
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3090. Agent State Reset
> 
> Sometimes safer:
> 
> ```text
> new clean instance
> ```
> 
> than endlessly continuing old session.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3091. Agent Memory Boundary
> 
> Persistent agent memory should not override:
> 
> ```text
> canonical Project/World State
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3092. Agent local memory
> 
> Can be:
> 
> ```text
> cache / scratch
> ```
> 
> not authoritative.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3093. Agent Failure
> 
> Types:
> 
> ```text
> CRASH
> TIMEOUT
> HALLUCINATED_OUTPUT
> TOOL_FAILURE
> POLICY_VIOLATION
> STAGNATION
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3094. Failure Recovery
> 
> ```text
> retry
> switch agent
> switch model
> switch method
> human escalation
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3095. Model diversity
> 
> For difficult tasks:
> 
> ```text
> Agent A using Model X
> Agent B using Model Y
> ```
> 
> can improve independence.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3096. But diversity has cost
> 
> ```text
> integration
> latency
> different output formats
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3097. Normalization Layer
> 
> All agents return:
> 
> ```text
> canonical schemas
> ```
> 
> regardless of model.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3098. Structured Output Contracts
> 
> Crucial for scalable collective work.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3099. Free-form agent prose
> 
> May be stored as Artifact,
> 
> but coordination depends on:
> 
> ```text
> structured fields
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3100. Agent Output Example
> 
> ```yaml
> result:
>   claims: [...]
>   evidence: [...]
>   unknowns: [...]
>   blockers: [...]
>   recommendations: [...]
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3101. Recommendation ≠ Decision
> 
> Again preserved.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3102. Multi-Agent Merge
> 
> Need merge by object type.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3103. Claims
> 
> Combine:
> 
> ```text
> support
> refute
> qualify
> ```
> 
> without flattening.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3104. Artifacts
> 
> Version or compose.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3105. Tasks
> 
> Deduplicate and reconcile dependencies.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3106. Proposals
> 
> Keep alternatives.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3107. Conflicting Claims
> 
> Create:
> 
> ```text
> CONTESTED
> ```
> 
> state.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3108. Merge Agent
> 
> A dedicated synthesis role can propose merge.
> 
> But deterministic rules handle simple cases.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3109. Deterministic before LLM
> 
> Examples:
> 
> ```text
> same ID → merge metadata
> exact duplicate hash → dedup
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3110. LLM for semantic ambiguity
> 
> For:
> 
> ```text
> possibly same concept
> contradictory descriptions
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3111. Conflict Types
> 
> ```text
> FACT_CONFLICT
> PLAN_CONFLICT
> RESOURCE_CONFLICT
> POLICY_CONFLICT
> OWNERSHIP_CONFLICT
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3112. Fact Conflict
> 
> Agents disagree on world state.
> 
> Resolve through Evidence.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3113. Plan Conflict
> 
> Two valid approaches.
> 
> Keep alternatives or Governance decides.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3114. Resource Conflict
> 
> Both agents need same scarce resource.
> 
> Scheduler/Market handles it.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3115. Policy Conflict
> 
> Plan violates rule.
> 
> Policy dominates.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3116. Ownership Conflict
> 
> Two agents claim same Task.
> 
> Lease system resolves.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3117. Agent Negotiation vs Conflict Resolution
> 
> Not every conflict needs conversation.
> 
> Many are:
> 
> ```text
> constraint-solver problems
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3118. Machine Negotiation should prefer structured protocol
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> OFFER
> COUNTEROFFER
> ACCEPT
> REJECT
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3119. Natural-language negotiation
> 
> Useful only when terms are not yet formalized.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3120. Negotiation Compiler
> 
> Can convert natural-language discussion into:
> 
> ```text
> structured candidate terms
> ```
> 
> for review.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3121. Coalition Formation
> 
> Some Tasks require multiple resources.
> 
> System may form:
> 
> ```text
> temporary coalition
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3122. Coalition
> 
> Could be:
> 
> ```text
> 3 AI Agents
> 1 human reviewer
> 1 repository
> ```
> 
> providing combined capability.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3123. Coalition Formation Problem
> 
> Find smallest/feasible combination satisfying:
> 
> ```text
> capability coverage
> constraints
> capacity
> verification
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3124. Similar to Team Builder
> 
> Indeed same generalized mechanism.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3125. Multi-Agent Team
> 
> Represent as:
> 
> ```text
> TEAM Resource
> ```
> 
> with temporary context.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3126. Collective Capability
> 
> Team may PROVIDE:
> 
> ```text
> capability unavailable individually
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3127. Example
> 
> ```text
> Research Agent
> +
> Code Agent
> +
> Reviewer
> ```
> 
> provides:
> 
> ```text
> research_to_reference_implementation
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3128. Coalition Lifecycle
> 
> ```text
> HYPOTHESIS
> FORMING
> ACTIVE
> DISSOLVED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3129. Temporary Agent Organization
> 
> At large scale, agents may form:
> 
> ```text
> cells
> squads
> pools
> ```
> 
> like human organizations.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3130. But machine organization can reconfigure faster
> 
> Within:
> 
> ```text
> policy
> budget
> permissions
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3131. Agent Organization Engine
> 
> Can derive structure from:
> 
> ```text
> task clusters
> handoff patterns
> resource demand
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3132. Example
> 
> Repeated pipeline:
> 
> ```text
> Scout → Analyst → Reviewer
> ```
> 
> may become permanent service cell.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3133. Agent Service Unit
> 
> Publishes high-level capability:
> 
> ```text
> Technology Intelligence
> ```
> 
> instead of exposing internal agent composition.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3134. Recursive organization
> 
> ```text
> Agent
> → Team
> → Service Unit
> → Organization
> ```
> 
> all appear as capability providers.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3135. Collective Decision Support
> 
> Agents may produce:
> 
> ```text
> different analyses
> ```
> 
> but Governance still makes authoritative decision.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3136. Collective Intelligence should increase quality of information
> 
> Not seize authority.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3137. Deliberation Protocol
> 
> For important proposal:
> 
> ```text
> 1 Draft
> 2 Independent Critique
> 3 Evidence Check
> 4 Revision
> 5 Final Review
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3138. Debate Roles
> 
> Possible:
> 
> ```text
> PROPONENT
> CRITIC
> EVIDENCE_CHECKER
> SYNTHESIZER
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3139. Avoid adversarial theater
> 
> Critic must search for:
> 
> ```text
> actual failure modes
> ```
> 
> not disagree for its own sake.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3140. Critique Budget
> 
> After useful objections exhausted:
> 
> ```text
> stop
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3141. Red Team
> 
> For high-risk systems:
> 
> ```text
> actively search for breakage
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3142. Blue Team
> 
> Defends/fixes.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3143. Purple Synthesis
> 
> Converts findings into:
> 
> ```text
> improvements
> tests
> policies
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3144. Red Team Output
> 
> Should be:
> 
> ```text
> attack path
> evidence
> impact
> reproduction
> ```
> 
> not vague warnings.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3145. Research adversarial review
> 
> Equivalent:
> 
> ```text
> find counterexamples
> contradictory papers
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3146. Architecture review
> 
> Alternative agents can challenge:
> 
> ```text
> scalability
> security
> maintainability
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3147. Negotiation Agent constraints
> 
> It must never:
> 
> ```text
> invent commitment
> fake authority
> claim consent
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3148. External Communication Gate
> 
> Any real outreach:
> 
> ```text
> send email
> submit form
> sign contract
> ```
> 
> passes Governance/Communication policy.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3149. Agent Reputation
> 
> Avoid universal reputation score.
> 
> Use:
> 
> ```text
> capability-specific operational evidence
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3150. Example
> 
> Agent A:
> 
> ```text
> high verification pass
> for repository extraction
> ```
> 
> says nothing automatically about:
> 
> ```text
> legal analysis
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3151. Agent Performance Record
> 
> Per Capability:
> 
> ```text
> task count
> verification pass
> error types
> latency
> cost
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3152. Model Change
> 
> If Agent switches underlying model:
> 
> ```text
> performance history may not fully transfer
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3153. Configuration Identity
> 
> Operational agent capability depends on:
> 
> ```text
> Agent Package
> +
> Model
> +
> Tools
> +
> Policy
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3154. Agent Configuration Fingerprint
> 
> Store hash.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3155. Benchmark by configuration
> 
> Not just agent name.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3156. Routing by Verified Capability
> 
> Scheduler uses:
> 
> ```text
> verified performance
> ```
> 
> where available.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3157. Exploration routing
> 
> New Agent may get:
> 
> ```text
> low-risk test tasks
> ```
> 
> to establish evidence.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3158. Agent Graduation
> 
> ```text
> EXPERIMENTAL
> LIMITED
> PRODUCTION
> ```
> 
> similar to packages.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3159. Agent Quarantine
> 
> Policy violation or repeated critical failure:
> 
> ```text
> QUARANTINED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3160. Agent Revocation
> 
> Credentials immediately removed.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3161. Collective Cost Accounting
> 
> Agent work consumes:
> 
> ```text
> tokens
> API costs
> compute
> human review
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3162. Multi-Agent Inflation
> 
> Danger:
> 
> ```text
> 10 agents solve task
> that one could solve
> ```
> 
> without quality benefit.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3163. Coordination Overhead
> 
> Need track:
> 
> ```text
> duplicate work
> messages
> merge time
> review time
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3164. Collective Intelligence Efficiency
> 
> Dimensions:
> 
> ```text
> quality improvement
> time
> cost
> coordination overhead
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3165. More Agents ≠ Better
> 
> Sometimes:
> 
> ```text
> 1 strong agent + verifier
> ```
> 
> better than:
> 
> ```text
> 10 debating agents
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3166. Team Size Experiment
> 
> Benchmark:
> 
> ```text
> 1 agent
> 2 agents
> 4 agents
> ```
> 
> on same Task class.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3167. Adaptive Team Size
> 
> Simple Tasks:
> 
> ```text
> 1 executor
> ```
> 
> Critical ambiguous Tasks:
> 
> ```text
> multiple roles
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3168. Coordination Profile
> 
> Possible:
> 
> ```text
> SOLO
> EXECUTOR_REVIEWER
> PARALLEL_SEARCH
> MULTI_PROPOSAL
> HIGH_ASSURANCE
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3169. SOLO
> 
> Low-risk deterministic.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3170. EXECUTOR_REVIEWER
> 
> Standard knowledge work.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3171. PARALLEL_SEARCH
> 
> Broad discovery.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3172. MULTI_PROPOSAL
> 
> Architecture/design decisions.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3173. HIGH_ASSURANCE
> 
> Independent analysis + deterministic checks + human gate.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3174. Coordination Compiler
> 
> Input:
> 
> ```text
> Task
> Risk
> Uncertainty
> Available Resources
> ```
> 
> Output:
> 
> ```text
> coordination topology
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3175. Example
> 
> Task:
> 
> ```text
> extract invoice fields
> ```
> 
> may compile:
> 
> ```text
> one extraction agent
> +
> schema validator
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3176. Another
> 
> Task:
> 
> ```text
> choose platform architecture
> ```
> 
> may compile:
> 
> ```text
> 3 independent proposals
> +
> 2 reviewers
> +
> synthesis
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3177. Another
> 
> Task:
> 
> ```text
> physical robot action
> ```
> 
> may require:
> 
> ```text
> planner
> simulator
> safety verifier
> human approval
> controller
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3178. Coordination Graph
> 
> Separate from Procedure Graph?
> 
> Conceptually:
> 
> ```text
> Procedure Graph = work structure
> Coordination Graph = executor interaction structure
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3179. Could be compiled together
> 
> Procedure node:
> 
> ```text
> ARCHITECTURE_REVIEW
> ```
> 
> expands into coordination subgraph.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3180. Coordination Archetypes
> 
> Reusable:
> 
> ```text
> SCOUT_SWARM
> BUILDER_REVIEWER
> RED_BLUE
> PROPOSAL_TOURNAMENT
> CONSENSUS_REVIEW
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3181. SCOUT_SWARM
> 
> Many agents search different source spaces.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3182. Builder-Reviewer
> 
> One produces, another verifies.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3183. Red-Blue
> 
> One tries to break, another fixes.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3184. Proposal Tournament
> 
> Multiple solutions compete on evidence/constraints.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3185. Consensus Review
> 
> Used carefully where judgment requires multiple domain experts.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3186. Hierarchical Coordination
> 
> Large project:
> 
> ```text
> Program Coordinator
> ↓
> Project Coordinators
> ↓
> Task Agents
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3187. Flat swarm does not scale indefinitely
> 
> Hierarchy reduces:
> 
> ```text
> communication complexity
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3188. But hierarchy can create bottlenecks
> 
> Coordinator overload.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3189. Federation-like agent structure
> 
> Agent groups can expose:
> 
> ```text
> high-level capability
> ```
> 
> without central coordinator seeing every low-level message.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3190. Semantic Compression between levels
> 
> Subteam reports:
> 
> ```text
> state diff
> summary claims
> blockers
> ```
> 
> not all internal traffic.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3191. Distributed Coordination
> 
> Different nodes may independently execute branches.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3192. Correlation ID
> 
> All branches share:
> 
> ```text
> project_trace_id
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3193. Cross-node Handoff
> 
> Uses Federation protocol.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3194. Local Authority
> 
> Remote coordinator cannot bypass local policies.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3195. Multi-Agent Deadlock
> 
> Possible:
> 
> ```text
> Agent A waits output B
> Agent B waits output A
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3196. Dependency Deadlock Detector
> 
> Find cycles in:
> 
> ```text
> WAIT_FOR graph
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3197. Deadlock Resolution
> 
> Possible:
> 
> ```text
> break dependency
> provide provisional artifact
> human resolution
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3198. Livelock
> 
> Agents repeatedly:
> 
> ```text
> revise
> criticize
> revise
> criticize
> ```
> 
> without progress.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3199. Livelock Detector
> 
> Uses:
> 
> ```text
> no new evidence
> same objections
> no state change
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3200. Starvation
> 
> Low-priority Task may never receive resource.
> 
> Need policy for:
> 
> ```text
> aging / fairness
> ```
> 
> where appropriate.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3201. Priority Aging
> 
> Waiting Task gradually gains scheduling attention.
> 
> But strategic priority still governed.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3202. Agent Race Condition
> 
> Two agents modify same Artifact.
> 
> Need:
> 
> ```text
> version
> optimistic locking
> branch/merge
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3203. Artifact Branching
> 
> Agent A:
> 
> ```text
> draft branch A
> ```
> 
> Agent B:
> 
> ```text
> draft branch B
> ```
> 
> Then merge.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3204. Structured Merge preferred
> 
> For semantic objects:
> 
> ```text
> field-level semantic diff
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3205. Code artifacts
> 
> Can use Git-like branching.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3206. Document artifacts
> 
> May use:
> 
> ```text
> versioned sections
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3207. Claim merge
> 
> Never overwrite contested Claim.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3208. Shared Blackboard Consistency
> 
> Use transactional database for canonical objects.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3209. Eventual consistency
> 
> Possible for:
> 
> ```text
> derived views
> federated mirrors
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3210. Strong consistency
> 
> Needed for:
> 
> ```text
> critical locks
> resource reservation
> authority decisions
> ```
> 
> ---

> 
> ```text
> TASK_CLAIMED
> TASK_RELEASED
> HANDOFF_CREATED
> PROPOSAL_CREATED

> Reviewer
> ↓
> Verifier
> ↓
> Acceptance

>

> 
> ```text
> semantic/judgment critique
> ```
> 
> Verifier:
> 
> ```text
> formal/empirical test
> ```

> # 3214. Collective Hallucination Risk
> 
> Agents can reinforce shared incorrect assumption.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3215. Independence Injection
> 
> Coordinator can intentionally assign:
> 
> ```text
> one agent without seeing prior conclusion
> ```
> 
> for independent check.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3216. Blind Review
> 
> Useful when:
> 
> ```text
> confirmation bias
> ```
> 
> risk high.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3217. Evidence-First Agent
> 
> One agent sees:
> 
> ```text
> sources only
> ```
> 
> and independently extracts claims.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3218. Claim-First Reviewer
> 
> Another sees:
> 
> ```text
> claim
> ```
> 
> and asks whether evidence supports it.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3219. Role separation reduces correlated error
> 
> Not eliminate it.
> 
> ---
>

> 
> ```text
> model
> prompt/package
> tools
> information source
> method
> ```

> # 3221. Same model + same prompt ×10
> 
> Provides little real diversity.

>

> 
> ```text

> Agent B → code benchmark
> Agent C → expert review
> ```
> 
> stronger than repeated text generation.

> ```text
> agreed claims
> contested claims
> unknowns
> evidence gaps
> ```

> # 3224. Not:
> 
> ```text

> 2 vote NO
> ```
> 
> unless the Task truly is preference aggregation.

> 
> Two Agents attempt same Task.
> 
> Lease system prevents duplicate execution.

> 
> Agent dies mid-task.

> Lease expires, Task reassigns.

> 
> Two agents disagree.
> 
> System stores conflict and creates verification Task.

> Task stops/escalates.

# chatgpt response

Продолжаю на русском языке. Теперь следующий слой — **Distributed Runtime, Event Fabric & System Resilience Engine v0.1**: инфраструктурный фундамент, который должен обеспечить работу Innovation OS при тысячах параллельных процессов, сбоях агентов, недоступности внешних сервисов, сетевых разрывах и восстановлении после аварий.

> **Document: Distributed Runtime, Event Fabric & System Resilience Engine v0.1**
> 
> # Distributed Runtime, Event Fabric & System Resilience Engine v0.1
> 
> ## 3356. Главный переход
> 
> До этого мы построили логическую архитектуру:
> 
> ```text
> Goals
> ↓
> Strategies
> ↓
> Projects
> ↓
> Procedures
> ↓
> Tasks
> ↓
> Agents / Humans / Services
> ↓
> Artifacts / Events / Evidence
> ```
> 
> Но реальная система должна переживать:
> 
> ```text
> agent crash
> network timeout
> database restart
> API outage
> duplicate message
> delayed event
> machine failure
> partial execution
> ```
> 
> и не терять состояние проекта.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3357. Главный принцип
> 
> Innovation OS должна исходить не из предположения:
> 
> ```text
> всё работает всегда
> ```
> 
> а из:
> 
> ```text
> любая отдельная часть
> может временно отказать
> ```
> 
> Поэтому устойчивость должна быть архитектурным свойством.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3358. Failure is normal state
> 
> В распределённой системе:
> 
> ```text
> timeout
> retry
> temporary unavailability
> partial completion
> ```
> 
> — нормальные эксплуатационные события.
> 
> Не исключения из архитектуры.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3359. Основной инфраструктурный цикл
> 
> ```text
> Command
> ↓
> Queue
> ↓
> Executor
> ↓
> Action
> ↓
> Event
> ↓
> State Update
> ↓
> Next Commands
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3360. Command ≠ Event
> 
> Это фундаментально.
> 
> Command:
> 
> ```text
> что система хочет сделать
> ```
> 
> Event:
> 
> ```text
> что реально произошло
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3361. Пример
> 
> Command:
> 
> ```text
> RUN_SECURITY_TEST
> ```
> 
> Event:
> 
> ```text
> SECURITY_TEST_COMPLETED
> ```
> 
> или:
> 
> ```text
> SECURITY_TEST_FAILED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3362. Никогда не считать Command доказательством выполнения
> 
> Плохая модель:
> 
> ```text
> send_email command
> → email_sent=true
> ```
> 
> Правильная:
> 
> ```text
> SEND_EMAIL
> ↓
> mail backend
> ↓
> delivery result
> ↓
> EMAIL_SENT event
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3363. Command Bus
> 
> Передаёт:
> 
> ```text
> намерения выполнить действия
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3364. Event Bus
> 
> Передаёт:
> 
> ```text
> факты о произошедшем
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3365. Эти каналы могут технически использовать одну инфраструктуру
> 
> Но семантически должны оставаться раздельными.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3366. Event Envelope
> 
> Минимально:
> 
> ```yaml
> event:
>   id: uuid
>   type: TASK_COMPLETED
>   aggregate_id: task_17
>   occurred_at: ...
>   recorded_at: ...
>   actor: agent_4
>   correlation_id: project_trace_7
>   causation_id: command_21
>   payload: ...
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3367. correlation_id
> 
> Связывает:
> 
> ```text
> все события одного бизнес-процесса
> ```
> 
> например одного Project execution.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3368. causation_id
> 
> Показывает:
> 
> ```text
> какое предыдущее событие или command
> стало непосредственной причиной
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3369. Distributed Trace
> 
> Цепочка:
> 
> ```text
> Goal
> ↓
> Project
> ↓
> Task
> ↓
> Command
> ↓
> Agent
> ↓
> Tool Call
> ↓
> Event
> ```
> 
> должна быть восстанавливаема.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3370. Durable Queue
> 
> Command нельзя хранить только:
> 
> ```text
> в памяти процесса
> ```
> 
> Нужна:
> 
> ```text
> durable queue
> ```
> 
> чтобы после restart работа не исчезла.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3371. Queue Item
> 
> Содержит:
> 
> ```text
> command
> priority
> available_after
> attempt_count
> lease
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3372. Worker
> 
> Worker:
> 
> ```text
> получает command
> ```
> 
> но не удаляет его окончательно до подтверждения результата.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3373. Delivery semantics
> 
> Для большинства Innovation OS разумная база:
> 
> ```text
> AT_LEAST_ONCE
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3374. Почему не обещать exactly-once
> 
> В реальной распределённой системе exactly-once:
> 
> ```text
> дорого
> сложно
> часто иллюзорно
> ```
> 
> Лучше:
> 
> ```text
> at-least-once delivery
> +
> idempotent execution
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3375. Idempotency
> 
> Повторный Command не должен создавать:
> 
> ```text
> дублирующий side effect
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3376. Example
> 
> ```text
> CREATE_GITHUB_ISSUE
> ```
> 
> с idempotency key:
> 
> ```text
> project17-task8-issue1
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3377. Backend checks
> 
> Если операция уже выполнена:
> 
> ```text
> return existing result
> ```
> 
> вместо повторного создания.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3378. Но не все physical Actions идемпотентны
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> CUT_MATERIAL
> ```
> 
> нельзя бездумно retry.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3379. Side-effect awareness
> 
> Каждый Command должен знать:
> 
> ```text
> READ_ONLY
> REPEATABLE
> REVERSIBLE
> COMPENSATABLE
> IRREVERSIBLE
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3380. Retry Policy зависит от класса Action
> 
> READ_ONLY:
> 
> ```text
> retry freely within limits
> ```
> 
> IRREVERSIBLE:
> 
> ```text
> requires observation/reconciliation
> before retry
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3381. Unknown execution outcome
> 
> Критический случай:
> 
> ```text
> Command sent
> ↓
> network timeout
> ↓
> did action happen?
> UNKNOWN
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3382. Never blindly retry
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> payment
> email
> physical movement
> ```
> 
> Нужно сначала:
> 
> ```text
> RECONCILE
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3383. Reconciliation Procedure
> 
> Проверить external system:
> 
> ```text
> did transaction exist?
> did message deliver?
> did machine complete operation?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3384. Reconciliation Result
> 
> ```text
> COMPLETED
> NOT_COMPLETED
> UNKNOWN
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3385. UNKNOWN remains dangerous
> 
> Если невозможно определить:
> 
> ```text
> human/operator escalation
> ```
> 
> может быть правильнее автоматического retry.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3386. Inbox Pattern
> 
> Каждый consumer хранит:
> 
> ```text
> processed_message_ids
> ```
> 
> чтобы duplicate Event не обрабатывался дважды.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3387. Outbox Pattern
> 
> Когда local transaction:
> 
> ```text
> changes database state
> ```
> 
> и должна отправить Event,
> 
> нельзя делать:
> 
> ```text
> DB commit
> then network publish
> ```
> 
> без защиты.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3388. Проблема
> 
> DB committed,
> 
> но process crashed before Event publish.
> 
> Получается:
> 
> ```text
> state changed
> event lost
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3389. Transactional Outbox
> 
> В одной DB transaction:
> 
> ```text
> state update
> +
> outbox record
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3390. Publisher
> 
> Отдельный worker отправляет:
> 
> ```text
> outbox → Event Bus
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3391. После успешной доставки
> 
> outbox record помечается:
> 
> ```text
> published
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3392. Это один из ключевых reliability patterns для MVP
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3393. Event Log
> 
> Append-only Event Log должен быть:
> 
> ```text
> immutable
> ```
> 
> с логическими corrections через новые Events.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3394. Materialized State
> 
> Текущее состояние:
> 
> ```text
> Task.status
> Project.status
> Resource.availability
> ```
> 
> может храниться отдельно для быстрых queries.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3395. Event Log ≠ full event sourcing requirement
> 
> Innovation OS не обязана сразу строить абсолютно всё только из Events.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3396. Pragmatic architecture
> 
> Лучше:
> 
> ```text
> canonical relational state
> +
> append-only event journal
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3397. Replay
> 
> Event Journal должен позволять:
> 
> ```text
> reconstruct significant state transitions
> ```
> 
> и анализировать:
> 
> ```text
> что произошло?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3398. Snapshot
> 
> При длинной истории нет смысла replay миллионов Events каждый раз.
> 
> Нужны:
> 
> ```text
> snapshots
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3399. Snapshot
> 
> Сохраняет:
> 
> ```text
> state at revision N
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3400. Recovery
> 
> ```text
> load latest snapshot
> ↓
> replay events after snapshot
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3401. Snapshot frequency
> 
> Не фиксировать универсально.
> 
> Зависит от:
> 
> ```text
> event volume
> recovery requirements
> storage cost
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3402. Checkpoint
> 
> Для long-running Procedure:
> 
> ```text
> checkpoint
> ```
> 
> сохраняет:
> 
> ```text
> completed nodes
> active nodes
> artifacts
> leases
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3403. Agent crash
> 
> После crash:
> 
> ```text
> load checkpoint
> ```
> 
> и продолжить с безопасной точки.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3404. Never rely on LLM conversation state alone
> 
> Conversation memory может исчезнуть.
> 
> Canonical execution state живёт:
> 
> ```text
> в Runtime DB
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3405. Durable Workflow
> 
> Workflow продолжает существовать:
> 
> ```text
> дни
> недели
> месяцы
> ```
> 
> даже если worker processes постоянно restart.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3406. WAIT state
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> WAITING_FOR_HUMAN_APPROVAL
> ```
> 
> не потребляет активный worker.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3407. WAIT stored as durable state
> 
> И пробуждается:
> 
> ```text
> Event
> или
> Timer
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3408. Timer Service
> 
> Нужен отдельный механизм для:
> 
> ```text
> deadlines
> scheduled retries
> timeouts
> condition rechecks
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3409. Durable Timer
> 
> Timer должен переживать restart.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3410. Example
> 
> ```text
> wake Task 17
> at 2026-10-01 09:00
> ```
> 
> сохраняется в DB/queue.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3411. Lease System
> 
> Исполнитель получает Task:
> 
> ```text
> на время
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3412. Lease fields
> 
> ```text
> holder
> acquired_at
> expires_at
> heartbeat
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3413. Heartbeat
> 
> Worker периодически сообщает:
> 
> ```text
> I am alive
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3414. Lost Worker
> 
> Если heartbeat исчез:
> 
> ```text
> lease expires
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3415. Но Task нельзя сразу переисполнять, если Action potentially irreversible
> 
> Сначала:
> 
> ```text
> reconciliation
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3416. Fencing Token
> 
> Для shared Resources useful:
> 
> ```text
> monotonic fencing token
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3417. Why
> 
> Old worker может «проснуться» после lease expiration.
> 
> Без fencing он может:
> 
> ```text
> продолжить писать
> ```
> 
> и конфликтовать с new worker.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3418. Token rule
> 
> Каждый new lease получает:
> 
> ```text
> higher token
> ```
> 
> Resource rejects commands with old token.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3419. Особенно важно для:
> 
> ```text
> resource reservation
> physical controller
> shared document mutation
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3420. Distributed Lock
> 
> Использовать только там, где действительно нужно.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3421. Не превращать всю систему в giant global lock
> 
> Это уничтожит scalability.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3422. Prefer optimistic concurrency
> 
> Для большинства semantic objects:
> 
> ```text
> read version
> ↓
> modify
> ↓
> write expected_version=N
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3423. Version conflict
> 
> If current version changed:
> 
> ```text
> CONFLICT
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3424. Semantic merge
> 
> Then:
> 
> ```text
> retry
> merge
> or human review
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3425. Strong Locks
> 
> Нужны для некоторых operations:
> 
> ```text
> equipment slot reservation
> single-writer financial action
> critical deployment
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3426. Resource Reservation Service
> 
> Хранит:
> 
> ```text
> resource
> time interval
> quantity
> owner
> status
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3427. Reservation lifecycle
> 
> ```text
> PROPOSED
> HELD
> CONFIRMED
> RELEASED
> EXPIRED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3428. Temporary Hold
> 
> Negotiation может удерживать Resource:
> 
> ```text
> короткое время
> ```
> 
> чтобы избежать double-booking.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3429. Hold expiration
> 
> Если confirmation не произошло:
> 
> ```text
> auto release
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3430. Saga Pattern
> 
> Distributed business process часто затрагивает:
> 
> ```text
> несколько независимых services
> ```
> 
> без общей DB transaction.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3431. Example
> 
> ```text
> reserve lab
> ↓
> reserve operator
> ↓
> order material
> ```
> 
> Третья операция failed.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3432. Global rollback невозможен
> 
> Поэтому:
> 
> ```text
> compensating actions
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3433. Saga
> 
> ```text
> Action A
> ↓
> Action B
> ↓
> Action C fails
> ↓
> Compensate B
> ↓
> Compensate A
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3434. Compensation ≠ undo
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> email sent
> ```
> 
> нельзя unsend.
> 
> Compensation может быть:
> 
> ```text
> send correction
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3435. Compensation Contract
> 
> Для Action:
> 
> ```text
> if failed downstream,
> what corrective action exists?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3436. Saga State
> 
> ```text
> RUNNING
> COMPENSATING
> COMPLETED
> FAILED
> MANUAL_INTERVENTION
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3437. Human-in-the-loop Saga
> 
> Некоторые compensation paths требуют:
> 
> ```text
> human decision
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3438. Circuit Breaker
> 
> Если external service repeatedly fails:
> 
> ```text
> stop calling temporarily
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3439. States
> 
> ```text
> CLOSED
> OPEN
> HALF_OPEN
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3440. CLOSED
> 
> Normal operation.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3441. OPEN
> 
> Calls blocked fast.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3442. HALF_OPEN
> 
> Limited test requests check recovery.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3443. Why important
> 
> Without breaker:
> 
> ```text
> failing API
> ```
> 
> может создать:
> 
> ```text
> thousands retries
> queue explosion
> cost explosion
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3444. Retry Storm
> 
> Очень опасный failure pattern.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3445. Exponential Backoff
> 
> Retry interval:
> 
> ```text
> grows after failures
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3446. Jitter
> 
> Добавляет небольшую случайность,
> 
> чтобы тысячи workers не retry одновременно.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3447. Retry Budget
> 
> System should limit:
> 
> ```text
> total retries
> ```
> 
> per Task/service/time window.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3448. Retry budget exhausted
> 
> Then:
> 
> ```text
> DEGRADED
> WAIT
> SWITCH_PROVIDER
> ESCALATE
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3449. Bulkhead Pattern
> 
> Разделить Resources, чтобы один failure domain не утянул всё.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3450. Example
> 
> Separate worker pools:
> 
> ```text
> research
> GitHub
> email
> physical
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3451. If Email API hangs
> 
> Research tasks continue.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3452. Tenant/Project isolation
> 
> Large Project should not consume:
> 
> ```text
> 100% workers
> ```
> 
> and starve all others.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3453. Resource Quotas
> 
> Per:
> 
> ```text
> organization
> project
> agent pool
> capability
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3454. Backpressure
> 
> Если incoming work > capacity:
> 
> ```text
> do not keep accepting infinitely
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3455. Backpressure options
> 
> ```text
> queue
> throttle
> reject low-priority work
> defer
> scale
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3456. Queue depth as signal
> 
> Persistent growth means:
> 
> ```text
> capacity < demand
> ```
> 
> or downstream failure.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3457. Queue ≠ storage archive
> 
> Need bounded operational queues.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3458. Overload Protection
> 
> System can enter:
> 
> ```text
> DEGRADED MODE
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3459. Degraded Mode
> 
> For example:
> 
> ```text
> stop speculative agents
> pause low-priority scans
> preserve critical workflows
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3460. Graceful Degradation
> 
> Не всё или ничего.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3461. Service Criticality
> 
> Classify:
> 
> ```text
> CRITICAL
> IMPORTANT
> OPTIONAL
> BACKGROUND
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3462. During incident
> 
> Pause:
> 
> ```text
> BACKGROUND
> ```
> 
> first.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3463. Capability Degradation
> 
> World State can update:
> 
> ```text
> research_search = DEGRADED
> ```
> 
> instead of claiming unavailable.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3464. Provider Failover
> 
> Capability Resolver searches:
> 
> ```text
> alternative provider
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3465. Failover types
> 
> ```text
> HOT
> WARM
> COLD
> MANUAL
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3466. Hot failover
> 
> Backup already active.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3467. Warm
> 
> Ready but needs quick activation.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3468. Cold
> 
> Requires setup.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3469. Manual
> 
> Needs human intervention.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3470. Fallback Provider
> 
> `project.lock` may define:
> 
> ```text
> primary
> backup
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3471. But backup validity must be tested
> 
> A stale backup is not resilience.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3472. Failover Drill
> 
> Periodically:
> 
> ```text
> simulate primary failure
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3473. N-1 Resilience
> 
> Critical capability survives:
> 
> ```text
> loss of one provider
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3474. N-2
> 
> For extreme criticality,
> 
> test two simultaneous failures.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3475. Failure Domain
> 
> Important concept.
> 
> Two providers may look separate but share:
> 
> ```text
> same cloud
> same datacenter
> same database
> same API vendor
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3476. Hidden correlated failure
> 
> Need dependency graph.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3477. Failure Domain Registry
> 
> Possible:
> 
> ```text
> REGION
> CLOUD_PROVIDER
> DATABASE
> MODEL_PROVIDER
> NETWORK
> POWER
> ORGANIZATION
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3478. Resilience requires diversity across failure domains
> 
> Not merely multiple Resource IDs.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3479. Dependency Health Propagation
> 
> If:
> 
> ```text
> Database X FAILED
> ```
> 
> affected services become:
> 
> ```text
> DEGRADED / FAILED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3480. Dependency graph enables blast-radius calculation
> 
> Question:
> 
> ```text
> what breaks if Resource X fails?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3481. Blast Radius
> 
> List:
> 
> ```text
> services
> agents
> projects
> capabilities
> decisions
> ```
> 
> affected.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3482. Impact Analysis before maintenance
> 
> Before shutting service:
> 
> ```text
> simulate blast radius
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3483. Maintenance Mode
> 
> Resource can be:
> 
> ```text
> DRAINING
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3484. Draining
> 
> Do not assign new work.
> 
> Allow existing safe work to finish.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3485. Then:
> 
> ```text
> MAINTENANCE
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3486. Rolling Upgrade
> 
> For replicated services:
> 
> ```text
> upgrade one instance
> ↓
> verify
> ↓
> upgrade next
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3487. Canary Infrastructure Upgrade
> 
> Small subset first.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3488. Rollback
> 
> If health degrades:
> 
> ```text
> restore previous version
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3489. Schema Migration
> 
> Database evolution is dangerous.
> 
> Need:
> 
> ```text
> versioned migrations
> backward-compatible rollout
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3490. Expand/Contract Pattern
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> add new column
> ↓
> support old + new
> ↓
> migrate data
> ↓
> switch readers
> ↓
> remove old
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3491. Avoid breaking all workers at once
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3492. Event Schema Versioning
> 
> Event payloads also evolve.
> 
> Need:
> 
> ```text
> event_type
> schema_version
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3493. Consumer compatibility
> 
> Older consumer may not understand v2.
> 
> Options:
> 
> ```text
> upcaster
> compatibility layer
> reject safely
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3494. Event Upcasting
> 
> Historical Event v1 can be transformed:
> 
> ```text
> in-memory
> ```
> 
> to current representation during replay.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3495. Never silently rewrite historical Event log
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3496. Command Versioning
> 
> Same principle.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3497. Distributed State categories
> 
> Useful split:
> 
> ```text
> AUTHORITATIVE STATE
> EPHEMERAL STATE
> DERIVED STATE
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3498. Authoritative
> 
> ```text
> Project
> Decision
> Claim
> Resource binding
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3499. Ephemeral
> 
> ```text
> worker heartbeat
> temporary cache
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3500. Derived
> 
> ```text
> dashboard counts
> search index
> embeddings
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3501. Different durability requirements
> 
> Do not over-engineer caches,
> 
> do not under-engineer Decisions.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3502. Storage Architecture
> 
> Practical v0.1:
> 
> ```text
> PostgreSQL
> +
> Object Store
> +
> Queue/Event Broker
> +
> Redis optional
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3503. PostgreSQL
> 
> Stores:
> 
> ```text
> canonical semantic state
> tasks
> leases
> outbox
> decisions
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3504. Object Store
> 
> Stores:
> 
> ```text
> large Artifacts
> datasets
> reports
> CAD
> logs
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3505. Queue/Event Broker
> 
> Could later be:
> 
> ```text
> NATS
> RabbitMQ
> Kafka
> Redpanda
> ```
> 
> Но v0.1 не должен зависеть от конкретного продукта в semantic layer.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3506. Redis
> 
> Optional:
> 
> ```text
> cache
> short-lived coordination
> ```
> 
> not canonical truth.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3507. Start simple
> 
> Для MVP даже:
> 
> ```text
> PostgreSQL queue tables
> ```
> 
> могут быть достаточны.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3508. Why
> 
> Premature distributed infrastructure can consume the whole project.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3509. Modular Monolith First
> 
> Начальная рекомендация остаётся:
> 
> ```text
> FastAPI
> PostgreSQL
> workers
> object store
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3510. Logical distribution first
> 
> Clear module boundaries:
> 
> ```text
> Runtime
> World State
> Verification
> Federation
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3511. Physical microservices later
> 
> Only where:
> 
> ```text
> scale
> failure isolation
> independent deployment
> ```
> 
> justify it.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3512. Microservice tax
> 
> Every service adds:
> 
> ```text
> network
> deployment
> observability
> versioning
> failure modes
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3513. Therefore service boundary should follow:
> 
> ```text
> clear operational reason
> ```
> 
> not fashion.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3514. Eventual Consistency
> 
> Many views can tolerate:
> 
> ```text
> slightly stale data
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3515. Example
> 
> Dashboard:
> 
> ```text
> 3 seconds stale
> ```
> 
> usually fine.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3516. Strong Consistency
> 
> Needed for:
> 
> ```text
> approval
> resource reservation
> financial commitment
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3517. Consistency by domain
> 
> Avoid one global consistency model.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3518. CAP-like reality
> 
> During network partition:
> 
> ```text
> not every distributed operation
> can remain both globally consistent
> and always writable
> ```
> 
> Architecture must define which side each function chooses.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3519. Example
> 
> Public metrics:
> 
> ```text
> availability preferred
> ```
> 
> Resource booking:
> 
> ```text
> consistency preferred
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3520. Network Partition
> 
> Two nodes lose connection.
> 
> Each continues local work where safe.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3521. Partition policy
> 
> Could be:
> 
> ```text
> LOCAL_CONTINUE
> READ_ONLY
> STOP
> ```
> 
> depending Resource/action.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3522. Example
> 
> Research reading:
> 
> ```text
> LOCAL_CONTINUE
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3523. Cross-node shared equipment reservation:
> 
> ```text
> STOP / READ_ONLY
> ```
> 
> unless conflict-safe mechanism exists.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3524. Split-Brain Prevention
> 
> Critical shared resource should not be controlled independently by two disconnected controllers.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3525. Leader / Ownership Lease
> 
> One node holds current authority to mutate resource.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3526. Federation boundary
> 
> Federated nodes remain autonomous.
> 
> Do not try to run one global distributed transaction across organizations.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3527. Instead
> 
> Use:
> 
> ```text
> agreements
> events
> sagas
> reconciliation
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3528. Cross-Organization Saga
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> Org A reserves budget
> ↓
> Org B reserves lab
> ↓
> Org C confirms material
> ```
> 
> If C fails:
> 
> ```text
> release B
> release A
> ```
> 
> where policies allow.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3529. Some remote commitments may not be compensatable
> 
> Then workflow enters:
> 
> ```text
> MANUAL_RESOLUTION
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3530. Dead Letter Queue
> 
> Message that repeatedly cannot process:
> 
> ```text
> DLQ
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3531. DLQ is not trash
> 
> Contains:
> 
> ```text
> message
> error
> attempt history
> context
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3532. DLQ Review
> 
> Possible:
> 
> ```text
> retry after fix
> discard with reason
> manual conversion
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3533. Poison Message
> 
> One malformed Event should not block entire queue.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3534. Consumer Isolation
> 
> Bad event:
> 
> ```text
> quarantine
> ```
> 
> continue processing others.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3535. Schema Validation before queue processing
> 
> Reject malformed inputs early.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3536. Backward compatibility
> 
> External/federated Events need especially strict validation.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3537. Event Deduplication
> 
> By:
> 
> ```text
> event_id
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3538. Event Ordering
> 
> Global ordering usually unnecessary.
> 
> Need:
> 
> ```text
> ordering per aggregate/resource
> ```
> 
> where relevant.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3539. Aggregate Revision
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> Project17 revision 42
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3540. Out-of-order Event
> 
> If revision 44 arrives before 43:
> 
> ```text
> buffer
> request replay
> or reconcile
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3541. Lamport/vector clocks?
> 
> Potentially later for complex federation.
> 
> Not required in MVP.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3542. Monotonic local revision first
> 
> Simpler and easier to reason about.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3543. Time is tricky
> 
> System clocks may differ.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3544. Therefore distinguish
> 
> ```text
> occurred_at
> recorded_at
> sequence/revision
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3545. Do not rely only on timestamps for ordering
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3546. Clock synchronization
> 
> For physical telemetry, good time synchronization can be important.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3547. Telemetry Fabric
> 
> Dense sensor streams should not flood semantic Event Bus.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3548. Separate layers
> 
> ```text
> Raw Telemetry Stream
> ↓
> Aggregation/Detection
> ↓
> Semantic Events
> ↓
> World State
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3549. Example
> 
> Instead of sending:
> 
> ```text
> 10,000 temperature samples
> ```
> 
> to World State,
> 
> send:
> 
> ```text
> MACHINE_OVERHEATING
> ```
> 
> with evidence reference to raw stream.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3550. Time-Series Store
> 
> Later:
> 
> ```text
> TimescaleDB
> InfluxDB
> similar system
> ```
> 
> for dense telemetry.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3551. Semantic Event Threshold
> 
> Derived event:
> 
> ```text
> temperature exceeded limit
> for 30 seconds
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3552. Raw data remains available for verification
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3553. Backpressure from telemetry
> 
> Sensor burst must not starve:
> 
> ```text
> governance
> task execution
> ```
> 
> Use isolated channels/pools.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3554. Priority Queues
> 
> Possible classes:
> 
> ```text
> EMERGENCY
> CRITICAL
> NORMAL
> BACKGROUND
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3555. Emergency
> 
> Physical stop/safety alert.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3556. Critical
> 
> Production failure.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3557. Background
> 
> Periodic scouting/indexing.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3558. Priority Inversion
> 
> Low-priority task may hold Resource needed by critical task.
> 
> Need:
> 
> ```text
> preemption
> priority inheritance
> or safe wait
> ```
> 
> depending Resource.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3559. Preemption
> 
> Only if Action safely interruptible.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3560. Non-preemptible Action
> 
> Physical test may need complete cycle.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3561. Resource Scheduler therefore needs:
> 
> ```text
> preemptibility
> ```
> 
> metadata.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3562. Checkpointable Tasks
> 
> Long computation can periodically save:
> 
> ```text
> progress
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3563. Resume
> 
> After failure from last checkpoint.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3564. AI Agent checkpoint
> 
> Not raw hidden reasoning.
> 
> Store:
> 
> ```text
> Task state
> Artifacts
> Claims
> open questions
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3565. This makes AI work resumable without dependence on private chain-of-thought.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3566. Disaster Recovery
> 
> Need define:
> 
> ```text
> RPO
> RTO
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3567. RPO
> 
> Recovery Point Objective:
> 
> ```text
> сколько данных допустимо потерять
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3568. RTO
> 
> Recovery Time Objective:
> 
> ```text
> сколько времени допустим простой
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3569. Different classes
> 
> Governance/Decisions:
> 
> ```text
> very low RPO
> ```
> 
> Caches:
> 
> ```text
> RPO irrelevant
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3570. Backup Layers
> 
> ```text
> database backup
> object-store backup
> configuration
> secrets metadata
> package locks
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3571. Backup without restore test is not enough
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3572. Restore Drill
> 
> Periodically:
> 
> ```text
> restore isolated environment
> ```
> 
> and verify.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3573. Backup Integrity
> 
> Check:
> 
> ```text
> hashes
> completeness
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3574. Point-in-Time Recovery
> 
> PostgreSQL can support:
> 
> ```text
> restore to time T
> ```
> 
> for catastrophic mistakes.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3575. But logical bad decision should not always be fixed by database rollback
> 
> Historical audit must remain.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3576. Compensating semantic correction preferable
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> wrong Claim approved
> ```
> 
> create:
> 
> ```text
> correction/supersession
> ```
> 
> not rewrite whole database history.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3577. Multi-Region Deployment
> 
> Later possible:
> 
> ```text
> Region A
> Region B
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3578. But not first milestone
> 
> Multi-region significantly complicates:
> 
> ```text
> consistency
> latency
> failover
> cost
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3579. Regional Resilience
> 
> Needed only when operational requirements justify it.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3580. Data Residency
> 
> Some objects may have:
> 
> ```text
> allowed regions
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3581. Scheduler must respect residency
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3582. Compute locality
> 
> Move:
> 
> ```text
> computation to data
> ```
> 
> where required.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3583. Federation is useful here
> 
> Remote node executes locally,
> 
> returns semantic result.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3584. Secrets Infrastructure
> 
> Secrets should live:
> 
> ```text
> outside ordinary World State
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3585. Secret References
> 
> World State stores:
> 
> ```text
> secret_ref
> ```
> 
> not raw credentials.

> ---
> 
> # 3586. Secret Broker
> 
> Issues:
> 
> ```text
> short-lived scoped credentials

>

> 
> # 3587. Credential Rotation
> 
> External credentials change without rewriting Project semantics.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3588. Credential Revocation
> 
> On agent compromise:
> 
> ```text
> revoke immediately
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3589. Secret Audit
> 
> Record:
> 
> ```text
> which identity
> accessed which credential
> for which Action
> ```
> 
> without logging secret value.

> ---
> 
> # 3590. Runtime Identity
> 
> Every worker/agent/service has:
> 
> ```text
> machine identity
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3591. Mutual authentication
> 
> Internal services should not trust network location alone.

> ---
> 
> # 3592. Zero-trust-like principle
> 
> ```text
> authenticate
> authorize
> scope
> audit

> 
> per sensitive request.

> # 3593. Service Mesh?
> 
> Possible later.
> 
> Not required for MVP.

>

>

> 
> ```text

> is policy still valid?

> 
> ```text
> planning
> ```
> 
> and:

> ```text
> execution

> # 3596. Therefore high-risk Action rechecks policy immediately before execution

>

> ```text

> # 3599. Runtime Guard
> 
> Before Action:
> 
> ```text
> check binding
> check approval
> check resource state
> check constraint

> # 3600. Then execute.

> 
> # 3601. Observability
> 
> Нужны три уровня:
> 
> ```text
> logs
> metrics
> traces
> ```

> # 3602. Logs
> 
> Detailed events/messages.

> ---
> 
> # 3603. Metrics
> 
> Aggregated operational measurements.

> ---
> 
> # 3604. Traces
> 
> Cross-service execution path.

>

> ```text

> capability health
> open gaps
> verification queues
> ```

> 
> ```text
> why Project X blocked
> ```

> # 3607. Dual Observability
> 
> ```text
> SYSTEM OBSERVABILITY
> +
> SEMANTIC OBSERVABILITY

> 
> # 3608. System Observability
> 
> ```text
> latency
> errors
> CPU
> queue depth
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3609. Semantic Observability
> 
> ```text
> blocked projects
> failed capabilities
> stale claims

> # 3610. Correlate both
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> GitHub API latency ↑
> ↓
> Repo Scout queue ↑
> ↓
> Technology Observatory stale
> ↓
> Project gaps unresolved
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3611. This creates operational causal graph
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3612. Service Level Objective
> 
> For internal component:
> 
> ```text
> availability
> latency
> durability
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3613. Capability-level SLO
> 
> More meaningful:
> 
> ```text
> Repository Discovery
> 95% of requests < 5 min

> 
> # 3614. Internal component can be healthy
> 
> while capability fails due to dependency.

> ---
> 
> # 3615. Error Budget
> 
> Could define:
> 
> ```text
> allowed failure/unavailability
> ```
> 
> for noncritical capabilities.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3616. When error budget exhausted
> 
> Prioritize:
> 
> ```text
> reliability work
> ```
> 
> over new features.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3617. But not needed for every tiny module initially
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3618. Health States
> 
> At component level:
> 
> ```text
> HEALTHY
> DEGRADED
> FAILED
> UNKNOWN
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3619. Health aggregation
> 
> If one optional dependency failed:
> 
> ```text
> DEGRADED
> ```
> 
> not necessarily:
> 
> ```text
> FAILED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3620. Readiness vs Liveness
> 
> Liveness:
> 
> ```text
> process alive?
> ```
> 
> Readiness:
> 
> ```text
> can it serve work correctly?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3621. Example
> 
> Process alive,
> 
> but database disconnected:
> 
> ```text
> live = YES
> ready = NO
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3622. Startup Recovery
> 
> On service restart:
> 
> ```text
> load state
> reclaim valid leases?
> recover timers
> resume queues
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3623. Do not assume empty memory means empty world
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3624. Crash Recovery Protocol
> 
> ```text
> start
> ↓
> recover durable state
> ↓
> reconcile in-flight work
> ↓
> become READY
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3625. In-flight reconciliation
> 
> Determine:
> 
> ```text
> which Actions may have completed externally
> ```
> 
> before requeue.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3626. Exactly this area is critical for physical/financial actions.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3627. Leader Election
> 
> Some singleton jobs:
> 
> ```text
> consolidation
> periodic scheduler
> ```
> 
> may need one active leader.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3628. But avoid singleton where horizontal workers can safely share queue.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3629. Leader failure
> 
> New instance acquires:
> 
> ```text
> leadership lease
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3630. Scheduler High Availability
> 
> Several scheduler instances can operate if:
> 
> ```text
> claiming tasks atomically
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3631. Horizontal Scaling
> 
> Worker pools scale:
> 
> ```text
> based on queue depth
> ```
> 
> within budget.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3632. Autoscaling limits
> 
> ```text
> min
> max
> cost budget
> rate limits
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3633. Scaling agents without scaling dependencies may worsen outage
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> 100 agents
> → same rate-limited API
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3634. Dependency-aware Autoscaling
> 
> Check downstream capacity first.
> 
> ---
>

> 
> ```text

> ↓
> Repo Worker throttle
> ↓
> Scout Scheduler slows new tasks

> 
> ---
> 
> # 3636. This avoids queue explosion.

> ---
> 
> # 3637. Cost-aware Scaling
> 
> Compute/AI workers have real cost.

> ---
> 
> # 3638. Runtime can have:
> 
> ```text
> max_cost_per_hour
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3639. Cost Circuit Breaker
> 
> If unexpected usage:
> 
> ```text
> exceeds threshold
> ```
> 
> pause noncritical workloads.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3640. Runaway Agent Protection
> 
> Detect:
> 
> ```text
> too many tool calls
> repeated loops
> token explosion
> ```
>

> 
> # 3641. Budget Guard
> 
> Terminate/escalate when:
> 
> ```text
> progress insufficient
> ```

> 
> Agent reports:
> 
> ```text
> new artifact

> state change
> ```
> 
> not just:
> 
> ```text
> still thinking
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3643. Stagnation Detector
> 
> If no meaningful progress:
> 
> ```text
> cancel or replan
> ```

> 
> # 3644. Distributed Deadlock
>

> 
> ```text
> Tasks
> Resources
> Approvals
> Organizations
> ```

> # 3645. Wait-For Graph
> 
> ```text

> Approval C waits Artifact A

> 
> cycle.

> 
> # 3646. Deadlock Detector
> 
> Search cycles in active wait graph.

> 
> # 3647. Resolution options
> 
> ```text
> break dependency
> change provider
> escalate
> cancel branch
> ```

> 
> # 3648. Orphan Detection
> 
> Objects with no active owner:
> 
> ```text
> running task without worker
> reservation without project
> pending approval for cancelled task
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3649. Reaper Service
> 
> Periodically detects stale:
> 
> ```text
> leases
> holds
> orphan temp objects
> ```

> 
> # 3650. Reaper must never delete canonical evidence
> 
> Only operational cleanup.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3651. Event Storm
> 
> One Event may trigger:
> 
> ```text
> thousands of downstream recalculations
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3652. Example
> 
> Popular package vulnerability.
> 
> Affects:
> 
> ```text
> 10,000 projects
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3653. Need batching
> 
> Instead of:
> 
> ```text
> 10,000 immediate deep analyses
> ```
> 
> do:
> 
> ```text
> impact index
> priority queue
> batch review
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3654. Event Coalescing
> 
> Repeated resource status changes:
> 
> ```text
> UP
> DOWN
> UP
> DOWN
> ```
> 
> may be coalesced for some derived systems.
> 
> Canonical events preserved.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3655. Debounce
> 
> Wait short interval before expensive recomputation.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3656. But critical safety Event bypasses debounce
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3657. Event Priority
> 
> Safety:
> 
> ```text
> immediate
> ```
> 
> Analytics:
> 
> ```text
> batchable
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3658. Materialized View Workers
> 
> Update:
> 
> ```text
> matches
> open gaps
> dashboards
> ```
> 
> asynchronously.

> 
> # 3659. Stale view indicator
> 
> UI should know:
> 
> ```text
> last_updated_at
> ```

> 
> # 3660. Never present stale derived view as current without metadata
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3661. Search Index
> 
> Can lag behind DB.
> 
> Canonical query should be available for critical operations.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3662. Vector Index
> 
> Always derived.
> 
> Can rebuild.

> ---
> 
> # 3663. Graph Projection
> 
> Can also be materialized/rebuildable.

> ---
> 
> # 3664. Data Repair
> 
> If derived index corrupt:
> 
> ```text
> rebuild from canonical store
> ```
> 
> ---
>

>

> 
> ```text
> foreign keys
> constraints
> transactions
> checksums
> ```
> 
> where possible.

> 
> Reject:
> 
> ```text

> invalid enum
> missing provenance
> ```
> 
> before canonical commit.

> # 3667. Quarantine Store
> 
> Malformed external data:
> 
> ```text
> stored separately

> 
> for inspection.

> # 3668. Data Repair Procedure
> 
> Human/agent may:
> 
> ```text
> normalize
> fix schema
> reingest

> # 3669. Immutable Raw Ingest
> 
> Keep original external payload where lawful/useful.
>

> 
> # 3670. Then transformations are traceable.

> # 3671. Disaster Scenario
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> main database unavailable
> ```
> 
> What happens?
>

> 
> # 3672. Read-only degraded mode
> 
> If replica available:
> 
> ```text
> read
> no authoritative writes
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3673. Queue incoming Commands?
> 
> Only if safe to replay later.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3674. High-risk actions
> 
> Pause if authoritative state unavailable.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3675. External side-effect prohibition under uncertain state
> 
> Strong default.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3676. Database failover
> 
> Requires:
> 
> ```text
> single authoritative writer
> ```
> 
> to avoid split-brain.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3677. Object Store outage
> 
> Tasks requiring large Artifacts wait.
> 
> Metadata-only operations may continue.

> # 3678. Model Provider outage
> 
> Capability Resolver switches provider if approved.

> ---
> 
> # 3679. Internet outage
> 
> Local tasks continue.
> 
> Federated/external tasks:
> 
> ```text
> WAITING_NETWORK
> ```

> 
> # 3680. Power/physical site outage
> 
> Resources at site become:
> 
> ```text
> UNKNOWN/UNAVAILABLE
> ```

> 
> # 3681. Recovery Event
> 
> When site returns:
> 
> ```text
> RESOURCE_RECOVERED
> ```
> 
> triggers reconciliation, not immediate blind resume.

> 
> # 3682. Why reconciliation
> 
> Physical world may have changed while disconnected.

> ---
> 
> # 3683. Digital Twin Freshness
> 
> After reconnect:
> 
> ```text
> refresh state
> ```
> 
> before issuing Commands.

> # 3684. Safety Interlock
> 
> Physical device controller can reject stale state commands.

> ---

> # 3685. Control Plane vs Data Plane
> 
> Useful distinction.

> 
> Handles:
> 
> ```text
> goals
> policies
> scheduling
> bindings
> ```
>

> # 3687. Data/Execution Plane
>

> 
> ```text
> actual tasks

> # 3689. High-risk execution may require live control plane

> relevant state
> events

> Agent lease expires.

> 
> # 3709. Test 7
> 
> Irreversible Action status unknown.
> 
> Expected:
> 
> ```text
> no blind retry
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 3710. Test 8
> 
> Two workers claim same Task.

> 
> ```text

> ```text
> Every automatic recovery is auditable.

>

> 
> ```text
> High-risk action never depends
> only on volatile process memory.

> 
> ### Invariant 8
> 
> ```text
> External failure must not silently
> become successful domain state.
