> # 12143. For each Program.

> 
> ```text

> 
> Application representation:
> 
> ```python id="0ppg1e"
> class TrendHypothesis(BaseModel):
>     subject_id: UUID
>     signal_ids: list[UUID]
> 
>     direction: str | None
>     scope_context_id: UUID
>     horizon: str
> 
>     supporting_evidence_ids: list[UUID]
>     refuting_evidence_ids: list[UUID]
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 12720. Trend direction examples:
> 
> ```text id="6vto5l"
> INCREASING
> DECREASING
> SHIFTING
> FRAGMENTING
> CONSOLIDATING
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 12721. But only when semantics appropriate.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 12722. Trend ≠ Forecast
> 
> ---
> 
> # 12723. Trend says:
> 
> ```text id="68jkn0"
> current directional pattern
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 12724. Forecast says:
> 
> ```text id="metzdk"
> expected future state
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 12725. Must remain separate.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 12726. Forecast object
> 
> Should be Claim with:
> 
> ```text id="67da92"
> target variable
> time horizon
> range
> model/method
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 12727. Example
> 
> ```text id="hrmxkk"
> Demand may rise 20–40%
> within 12 months
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 12728. Range + method important.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 12729. But for highly uncertain strategic futures,
> 
> scenario often better than numerical forecast.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 12730. Scenario
> 
> Scenario is:
> 
> ```text id="iy7o3h"
> internally coherent possible future
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 12731. Scenario ≠ prediction
> 
> ---
> 
> # 12732. Scenario object can be Context:
> 
> ```text id="4h3n5m"
> context_type = FUTURE_SCENARIO
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 12733. Scenario contains assumptions
> 
> ```text id="1aoczo"
> technology
> market
> funding
> regulation
> resources
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 12734. Example
> 
> Scenario A:
> 
> ```text id="zrmbct"
> Open AI Ecosystem
> ```
> 
> Assumptions:
> 
> ```text id="bcx61m"
> open models improve
> open tooling matures
> interoperability rises
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 12735. Scenario B:
> 
> ```text id="8pnb06"
> Platform Concentration
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 12736. Assumptions:
> 
> ```text id="8ekhj4"
> few major providers dominate
> switching costs rise
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 12737. Scenario C:
> 
> ```text id="e0sqmy"
> Regulated Fragmentation
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 12738. Assumptions:
> 
> ```text id="ey142i"
> regional rules diverge
> data sovereignty increases
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 12739. Не нужно выбирать "правильный" scenario
> 
> ---
> 
> # 12740. Portfolio stress-tested against all.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 12741. Scenario Building Pipeline
> 
> ```text id="36aa5c"
> Critical Uncertainties
> ↓
> Alternative States
> ↓
> Scenario Combinations
> ↓
> Internal Consistency Check
> ↓
> Mission Impact
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 12742. Critical Uncertainty
> 
> Variable that:
> 
> ```text id="hbv9ye"
> high impact
> +
> high uncertainty
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 12743. Examples:
> 
> ```text id="c1xgw9"
> GPU cost
> regulation
> talent availability
> open model quality
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 12744. High Impact + Low Uncertainty
> 
> Not scenario axis,
> 
> but planning assumption.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 12745. Low Impact + High Uncertainty
> 
> Usually monitor,
> 
> not build portfolio around it.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 12746. Again no one formula needed.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 12747. Scenario Consistency
> 
> Example impossible/contradictory combination:
> 
> ```text id="lamyi5"
> strict data localization
> +
> all compute centralized overseas
> ```
> 
> может быть inconsistent in context.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 12748. Consistency checker flags,
> 
> human/agent reviews.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 12749. Scenario Dependency Graph
> 
> Assumptions can influence each other.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 12750. Example
> 
> ```text id="40wq2k"
> energy cost ↑
> → local GPU cost ↑
> → cloud economics shift
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 12751. This connects to Causal Engine.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 12752. Causal Scenario
> 
> More sophisticated scenario includes:
> 
> ```text id="8ah5jp"
> causal chains
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 12753. But keep hypothesis status.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 12754. Wild Cards
> 
> Rare/high-impact possibilities.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 12755. Examples:
> 
> ```text id="bpca3h"
> major API shutdown
> unexpected scientific breakthrough
> supply chain disruption
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 12756. Wild Card ≠ prediction
> 
> ---
> 
> # 12757. Purpose:
> 
> ```text id="zh96f9"
> stress resilience
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 12758. Black Swan language should be used cautiously
> 
> because true unpredictability cannot be enumerated exhaustively.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 12759. Better category:
> 
> ```text id="cutvv1"
> LOW-PROBABILITY / HIGH-IMPACT SCENARIO
> ```
> 
> if probabilities are actually estimated.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 12760. If no probability:
> 
> ```text id="ndxlbo"
> STRESS SCENARIO
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 12761. Unknown Unknowns
> 
> System cannot enumerate all.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 12762. Therefore resilience/optionality remain necessary
> 
> even with strong foresight.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 12763. Foresight cannot eliminate uncertainty.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 12764. It improves:
> 
> ```text id="4j5fr6"
> preparedness
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 12765. Strategic Signpost
> 
> A signpost is observable condition indicating:
> 
> ```text id="hdjsoc"

> ```
> 
> или:
> 
> ```text id="owq9bd"
> portfolio assumption needs review
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 12766. Example
> 
> Assumption:
> 
> ```text id="s8iy88"
> open model performance will reach threshold
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 12767. Signpost:
> 
> ```text id="iyq7yc"
> benchmark X reaches Y
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 12768. Another:
> 
> ```text id="mpytms"
> three independent production deployments appear
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 12769. Signpost should be observable
> 
> ---
> 
> # 12770. Not vague:
> 
> ```text id="6b31d5"

> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 12771. Better:
> 
> ```text id="87fl5y"
> latency < threshold
> benchmark ≥ threshold
> 3 verified providers available
> ```
> 
> ---

>

>

> # 12904. This is proactive resilience.

> 
> # 12905. Foresight Blind Spots
>

> 
> ```text id="w6iwbf"
> what domains are poorly observed
> ```

> 
> # 12906. Example

> ```text id="bhxxso"

> # 12907. This is:
> 
> ```text id="jf5hob"

> ---
> 
> # 12909. Fewer sources ≠ automatically low truth
> 
> but lower observation completeness.

> # 12910. Blind Spot Map
> 
> Dimensions:

> ```text id="k1p3mh"
> geography
> language
> technology
> source type

> # 12911. Language coverage especially matters.

> 
> # 12912. Example

> ```text id="3dv56h"
> Chinese
> Japanese
> Russian
> German
> ```

> 
> # 12913. Translation layer can widen scan.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 12914. But machine translation may introduce semantic uncertainty.

> ---
> 
> # 12915. Preserve original sources.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 12916. Source Language becomes metadata.

> 
> # 12917. Signal Contradiction
>

> 
> Hiring demand rises,

> 
> # 12919. Do not force one trend conclusion.

> 
> # 12920. Could indicate:

> ```text id="2kcmfm"

> 
> # 12921. Preserve multidimensional change.

> 
> # 12923. This gives richer picture.

> # 12933. Strategic Early Warning
> 
> A signal becomes Early Warning when:
> 
> ```text id="hdelou"
> material impact
> +
> action lead time
> +
> credible evidence
> ```

> 
> Supplier announces product discontinuation.

> 
> # 12935. That's not weak signal anymore.

>

> ```text id="mjsc7b"

> VALIDATED

> ACTION_PLANNED
> RESOLVED

> ---

> # 12938. Early Warning ≠ Incident

> 
> # 12939. Warning concerns future risk.
> 
> Incident is current realized disruption.

> ---
> 
> # 12940. This separation matters.
> 
> ---
>

> Impact Analysis
> ↓
> Options
> ↓
> Governance
> ↓
> Mitigation Project

> 
> API retirement in six months.

> ---
> 
> # 12943. Mitigation:
> 
> ```text id="ln0jz1"

> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 12944. This connects foresight to execution.

>

> 
> Not only threats.

> # 12974. But avoid hindsight bias.

>

> ```text id="f2610a"

>

> 
> ```text id="h2wlsy"

> 
> ---
> 
> # 12977. Not simply:
> 
> ```text id="b799mj"

>

> 
> # 12979. Then strategic utility may still be positive.

> ---
> 
> # 12980. Foresight Calibration
> 
> Measure:
> 
> ```text id="fqs1jo"
> false alarms
> missed signals
> stale signals
> late warnings
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 12981. False Alarm
> 
> Signal escalated,
> 
> but no meaningful change followed.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 12982. Missed Signal
> 
> Major external change occurred
> 
> without prior detection,
> 
> when observable evidence existed.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 12983. Late Warning
> 
> Signal detected only after action window mostly closed.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 12984. These help improve scanning.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 12985. But "missed unknowable event" should not count as failure.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 12986. Observable-at-time criterion matters.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 12987. Signal Learning
> 
> After backtesting:
> 
> ```text id="9boyuy"
> which source combinations

> 
> # 12990. But source weighting should remain domain-specific.

> # 13001. Temporal Triad
> 
> ```text id="cab2vo"

> = what happened
> 
> PRESENT
> = what is happening
> 
> FUTURE
> = what might happen
> ```

> 
> should not be rewritten by future scenario.

> ---
> 
> # 13004. Future Scenario
> 
> must not appear as present fact.

> 
> # 13005. Present observation
> 
> may invalidate future scenario.

> # 13006. This creates clean temporal epistemics.

> # 13953. Command Center Anti-Patterns
> 
> ```text id="o1nv0m"
> DASHBOARD_WALL
> FALSE_GREEN
> ALERT_STORM
> METRIC_VANITY
> BLACK_BOX_RECOMMENDATION
> STALE_VIEW
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 13954. DASHBOARD_WALL
> 
> Dozens of panels,
> 
> no decision hierarchy.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 13955. FALSE_GREEN
> 
> No alarms,
> 
> but observation pipeline broken.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 13956. ALERT_STORM
> 
> Many symptoms,
> 
> one root issue.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 13957. METRIC_VANITY
> 
> Metrics without operational decision value.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 13958. BLACK_BOX_RECOMMENDATION
> 
> System suggests action with no rationale.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 13959. STALE_VIEW
> 
> Old state shown as live.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 13960. Another anti-pattern:
> 
> ```text id="se2512"
> SILENT_AUTOMATION
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 13961. System changes state automatically
> 
> without visible event/audit.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 13962. Forbidden by architecture.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 13963. Another:
> 
> ```text id="676ir3"
> UI_DIRECT_MUTATION
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 13964. Button directly changes canonical DB
> 
> without Action/Command/Event path.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 13965. Avoid.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 13966. Main mutation flow remains:
> 
> ```text id="3vlnft"
> Interaction
> ↓
> Proposal/Command
> ↓
> Policy
> ↓
> Execution
> ↓
> Event
> ↓
> World State
> ↓
> View Update
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 13967. This is crucial.
>

> ```text id="gl93at"
> intelligence

> strategy

> but also:

> # 14001. Operational Transparency
> 
> Means:
> 
> ```text id="19w1zz"
> humans can inspect
> state
> reason
> authority
> history
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14002. This is essential for high-autonomy systems.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14003. More autonomy without observability
> 
> creates:
> 
> ```text id="l2rzsz"
> operational opacity
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14004. Therefore autonomy maturity should require observability maturity.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14005. Example
> 
> Before giving Agent broader authority,
> 
> system should have:
> 
> ```text id="ch2zpe"
> clear audit
> verification
> rollback
> impact visibility
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14006. This becomes governance prerequisite.
> 
> ---
>

> ```text id="p6lt1g"

> ```text id="y1hpr7"

# chatgpt response

Продолжаю с **14061**. Теперь строим слой, который унифицирует документы, API, базы данных, сенсоры, камеры, аудио, телеметрию и человеческий ввод в одну доказательную цепочку — от сырого сигнала до проверенного состояния мира.

> **Document: Universal Data, Perception & Evidence Fabric v0.1**
> 
> # Universal Data, Perception & Evidence Fabric v0.1
> 
> ## 14061. Главный переход
> 
> До сих пор разные Observatory и Runtime-модули получали данные разными путями:
> 
> ```text
> HN posts
> GitHub repositories
> Research papers
> Funding calls
> Runtime telemetry
> Physical sensors
> Human input
> ```
> 
> Теперь нужен единый принцип:
> 
> ```text
> Любой внешний вход
> должен пройти
> явную цепочку преобразований
> до World State.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14062. Основная архитектурная формула
> 
> ```text
> RAW
> ↓
> PARSED
> ↓
> OBSERVED
> ↓
> RESOLVED
> ↓
> INTERPRETED
> ↓
> CLAIMED
> ↓
> EVIDENCED
> ↓
> VERIFIED
> ↓
> WORLD STATE
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14063. Ключевой invariant
> 
> ```text
> Raw Input ≠ Fact
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14064. Ещё один
> 
> ```text
> Parsed Data ≠ Observation
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14065. Ещё один
> 
> ```text
> Observation ≠ Interpretation
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14066.
> 
> ```text
> Interpretation ≠ Verified Claim
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14067. Это должно работать одинаково для:
> 
> ```text
> PDF
> web page
> API response
> database row
> camera frame
> microphone signal
> pressure sensor
> human statement
> AI output
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14068. Таким образом вместо десятков отдельных ingestion philosophies появляется:
> 
> # Universal Perception Fabric
> 
> ---
>

> 
> Не только:
> 
> ```text

> 
> а:
> 
> ```text
> machine acquisition of externally supplied information

>

> 
> # 14070. Поэтому лучшее полное название:
> 
> # Universal Data, Perception & Evidence Fabric
> 
> ---
>

> 
> Первый уровень:
> 
> ```text
> SOURCE
> ```

>

> AUDIO
> VIDEO
> HUMAN
> AGENT
> DEVICE

> 
> ---

>

>

> RESOURCE
> ```

> 
> # 14088. Возможные режимы:

>

> 
> # 14094. Provenance должна сохраняться независимо от режима.

> 
> # 14095. Acquisition Layer

>

> 
> ```python

> # 14134. Это можно назвать:

>

> 
> ```python

> # 14138. Observation Layer
> 
> Теперь из parsed data извлекается:
> 
> ```text
> Observation
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14139. Observation означает:
> 
> ```text
> система зафиксировала некоторый наблюдаемый сигнал

> 
> ---
> 
> # 14140. Например camera:
> 
> ```text

>

> 
> ```text

> 
> # 14142. Sensor:
> 
> ```text

> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14143. Это Observation.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14144. Interpretation:
>

> ```
>

> 
> # 14145. Claim:
> 
> ```text

> ```

> 
> # 14146. Verification may require:
> 
> ```text
> second sensor
> calibration
> rules

>

> 
> # 14147. Это separation of levels.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14148. Observation representation
> 
> Core root EVENT может использоваться для temporal observation,
> 
> или Claim with source_mode=OBSERVED,
> 
> depending semantics.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14149. Recommended distinction
> 
> Use:
> 
> ```text
> Event
> ```
> 
> for:
> 
> ```text
> something occurred at time T
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14150. Use Claim with:
> 
> ```text
> source_mode = OBSERVED
> ```
> 
> for:
> 
> ```text
> structured assertion derived directly from observation
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14151. Example
> 
> Event:
> 
> ```text
> sensor reading received
> ```
> 
> Claim:
> 
> ```text
> temperature = 82°C at T
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14152. This preserves both transport and semantic state.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14153. Observation confidence
> 
> Sensors and models can be uncertain.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14154. Example vision model:
> 
> ```text
> forklift probability 0.82
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14155. This does not mean:
> 
> ```text
> 82% true
> ```
> 
> in a universal epistemic sense.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14156. It is model confidence under its calibration context.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14157. Therefore metadata should identify:
> 
> ```text
> model
> version
> calibration
> threshold
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14158. Sensor uncertainty similarly:
> 
> ```text
> measurement tolerance
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14159. Units mandatory
> 
> ```text
> °C
> Pa
> mm
> m/s
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14160. Numeric observation without unit is incomplete if unit matters.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14161. Unit normalization
> 
> Input:
> 
> ```text
> 5 bar
> ```
> 
> canonical:
> 
> ```text
> 500 kPa
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14162. But original unit should remain in provenance.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14163. Conversion procedure versioned.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14164. Time Synchronization
> 
> Multisensor perception requires:
> 
> ```text
> consistent timestamps
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14165. Sources may have:
> 
> ```text
> device time
> server receipt time
> event time
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14166. Distinguish:
> 
> ```text
> observed_at
> received_at
> processed_at
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14167. Especially important for distributed physical systems.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14168. Clock skew
> 
> Could cause:
> 
> ```text
> false event ordering
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14169. Need:
> 
> ```text
> clock quality metadata
> ```
> 
> where relevant.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14170. For ordinary documents this complexity not needed.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14171. Fabric should be modality-aware,
> 
> not force all sources to carry sensor-grade fields.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14172. Entity Resolution Layer
> 
> Observation often mentions:
> 
> ```text
> something
> ```
> 
> that must map to canonical entity.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14173. Example document:
> 
> ```text
> OpenAI
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14174. Entity Resolver maps to:
> 
> ```text
> Resource UUID
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14175. Camera:
> 
> ```text
> vehicle track 183
> ```
> 
> may map to:
> 
> ```text
> Forklift Resource UUID
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14176. RFID:
> 
> ```text
> tag ABC123
> ```
> 
> maps to asset.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14177. Human says:
> 
> ```text
> the north pump
> ```
> 
> Resolver may map to physical Resource.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14178. Entity Resolution states
> 
> ```text
> EXACT
> CONFIRMED
> CANDIDATE
> AMBIGUOUS
> UNRESOLVED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14179. UNKNOWN identity ≠ guessed identity.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14180. Never silently merge ambiguous entities.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14181. Cross-modal Entity Resolution
> 
> Interesting case:
> 
> ```text
> camera object
> +
> RFID signal
> +
> database record
> ```
> 
> may refer to same physical asset.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14182. Fusion can propose:
> 
> ```text
> same entity
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14183. But should store:
> 
> ```text
> mapping evidence
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14184. Identity confidence separate from content confidence.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14185. Example
> 
> We are highly confident:
> 
> ```text
> pressure reading = 312 kPa
> ```
> 
> but unsure:
> 
> ```text
> which pump produced it
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14186. Need represent independently.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14187. Semantic Extraction Layer
> 
> Once source/object context known,
> 
> extract:
> 
> ```text
> entities
> relations
> claims
> constraints
> events
> ```
>

> 
> # 14188. For text,
> 
> LLM may help.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14189. For sensor data,
> 
> rules/ML models may help.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14190. For structured API,
> 
> deterministic mapping preferred.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14191. Principle:
> 
> ```text
> Use deterministic transformation
> when semantics are already explicit.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14192. Example
> 
> API returns:
> 
> ```json
> {"temperature_c": 82}
> ```
> 
> No LLM needed.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14193. Example research paragraph:
> 
> ```text
> The method improved recall by 12%...
> ```
> 
> LLM/parser may extract claim.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14194. Extraction Adapter
> 
> Generic interface:
> 
> ```python
> class SemanticExtractor(Protocol):
>     async def extract(
>         self,
>         artifact: Artifact,
>         context: Context
>     ) -> ExtractionResult:
>         ...
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14195. Extraction Result
> 
> ```text
> Candidate Entities
> Candidate Claims
> Candidate Relations
> Unknowns
> Warnings
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14196. Candidate is critical word.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14197. Extraction does not directly write canonical truth.
>

> 
> # 14198. Promotion Pipeline remains:
> 
> ```text
> Candidate
> ↓
> Schema Validation
> ↓
> Semantic Validation
> ↓
> Policy
> ↓
> Canonical Object
> ```
>

> 
> # 14199. Multimodal Fusion
> 
> Now multiple observations can support one Claim.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14200. Example robot gripper
> 
> Inputs:
> 
> ```text
> camera
> force sensor
> joint encoder
> optical tactile fiber
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14201. Camera says:
> 
> ```text
> object moved
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14202. Force sensor says:
> 
> ```text
> contact force increased
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14203. Joint encoder says:
> 
> ```text
> gripper closed 3 mm
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14204. Optical sensor says:
> 
> ```text
> localized pressure distribution changed
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14205. Fusion hypothesis:
> 
> ```text
> object is being grasped
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14206. That is not raw observation.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14207. It is:
> 
> ```text
> INFERENCE
> ```
> 
> supported by multiple observations.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14208. This is exactly where tactile sensing ideas integrate.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14209. Sensor Fusion Graph
> 
> ```text
> Observation A
> Observation B
> Observation C
> ↓
> Inference Claim
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14210. If one sensor disagrees:
> 
> ```text
> conflict preserved
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14211. Example
> 
> Vision:
> 
> ```text
> object stationary
> ```
> 
> Encoder:
> 
> ```text
> motion detected
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14212. Could indicate:
> 
> ```text
> slippage
> sensor lag
> misclassification
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14213. Do not average disagreement away blindly.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14214. Fusion Strategy Types
> 
> ```text
> RULE
> STATISTICAL
> ML
> CAUSAL
> HYBRID
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14215. Fusion Procedure itself versioned.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14216. Multimodal Evidence
> 
> One Claim may have Evidence from:
> 
> ```text
> document
> sensor
> camera
> human
> simulation
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14217. Evidence types remain explicit.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14218. Example
> 
> Claim:
> 
> ```text
> machine vibration abnormal
> ```
> 
> Evidence:
> 
> ```text
> accelerometer
> audio spectrum
> maintenance log
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14219. Cross-modal agreement can strengthen evidence.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14220. But correlated sensors may share same failure mode.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14221. Example
> 
> Two software-derived signals from same camera
> 
> are not fully independent.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14222. Evidence Independence Graph useful.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14223. Observation Dependency
> 
> Track:
> 
> ```text
> derived_from sensor/device/source

> ---
> 
> # 14224. Example
> 
> Vision model A and B both process same frame.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14225. Two model outputs ≠ two independent physical observations.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14226. This mirrors source independence logic in Foresight.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14227. Data Quality Layer
> 
> Before semantic promotion evaluate:
> 
> ```text
> completeness
> validity
> freshness
> consistency
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14228. But avoid one Data Quality Score.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14229. Better dimensions separately.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14230. Example
> 
> Dataset:
> 
> ```text
> complete: high
> freshness: low
> schema validity: high
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14231. Different use cases care differently.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14232. Data Quality Claim
> 
> Could be contextual.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14233. Example
> 
> ```text
> Dataset suitable for historical analysis
> ```
> 
> but:
> 
> ```text
> not suitable for live control
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14234. Same data,
> 
> different fitness-for-use.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14235. Fitness-for-Use
> 
> Important concept.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14236. Data is not simply:
> 
> ```text
> good/bad
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14237. It may be:
> 
> ```text
> adequate for task A
> insufficient for task B
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14238. Therefore task requirements should specify:
> 
> ```text
> freshness
> precision
> coverage
> resolution
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14239. Perception Capability Contract
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```yaml
> capability: vehicle_position_tracking
> 
> requirements:
>   update_rate_hz: 5
>   max_position_error_m: 0.5
>   max_data_age_ms: 500
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14240. Then current sensor system can be checked.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14241. If update rate 1 Hz:
> 
> ```text
> capability insufficient
> ```
> 
> even if sensor technically works.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14242. This connects Data Fabric with Capability Engine.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14243. Perception Gap
> 
> Derived when:
> 
> ```text
> World State needs observation
> but sensing/data coverage insufficient
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14244. Types:
> 
> ```text
> NO_SOURCE
> LOW_FREQUENCY
> LOW_PRECISION
> STALE
> BLIND_AREA
> IDENTITY_UNRESOLVED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14245. Example factory
> 
> Robot path planner needs:
> 
> ```text
> current human occupancy
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14246. Camera coverage blind zone exists.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14247. This is:
> 
> ```text
> Perception Gap
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14248. Not planning bug.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14249. World model should explicitly know:
> 
> ```text
> area state UNKNOWN
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14250. UNKNOWN must influence control policy.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14251. Example safety policy:
> 
> ```text
> if occupancy UNKNOWN
> → restrict autonomous movement
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14252. This is much safer than treating UNKNOWN as empty.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14253. Critical invariant
> 
> ```text
> Not observed
> ≠
> Absent.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14254. This applies everywhere:
> 
> ```text
> camera
> database
> web
> human reports
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14255. Example
> 
> No job posting for skill X
> 
> does not mean:
> 
> ```text
> no demand exists
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14256. Example
> 
> No sensor detection
> 
> does not necessarily mean:
> 
> ```text
> no object exists
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14257. Coverage metadata is therefore essential.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14258. Observation Coverage
> 
> For sensor domain:
> 
> ```text
> spatial
> temporal
> modal
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14259. For web/research:
> 
> ```text
> source
> language
> geography
> time
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14260. Same abstract concept:
> 
> # Coverage
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14261. Universal Coverage Model
> 
> Could describe:
> 
> ```text
> What part of target domain
> can this source observe?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14262. Example camera:
> 
> ```text
> polygon + field of view
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14263. Research database:
> 
> ```text
> disciplines + publishers + years
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14264. GitHub:
> 
> ```text
> public repositories reachable via API
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14265. Human observer:
> 
> ```text
> declared/local scope
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14266. This lets system reason about blind spots systematically.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14267. Data Lineage
> 
> Every derived object should support:
> 
> ```text
> Where did this come from?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14268. Example:
> 
> ```text
> Mission dashboard metric
> ```
> 
> might derive from:
> 
> ```text
> Projects
> → Actions
> → sensor/API observations
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14269. Lineage Graph
> 
> ```text
> Raw Source
> ↓
> Parsed Artifact
> ↓
> Observation
> ↓
> Claim
> ↓
> Derived View
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14270. This is universal data lineage.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14271. Lineage differs from Evidence Graph
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14272. Data lineage says:
> 
> ```text
> how data transformed
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14273. Evidence graph says:
> 
> ```text
> what supports/refutes a Claim
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14274. They overlap,
> 
> but not identical.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14275. Example
> 
> Parser output is lineage ancestor.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14276. It may not independently support truth.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14277. This distinction matters.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14278. Transformation Provenance
> 
> Each transformation:
> 
> ```text
> input
> processor
> version
> output
> time
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14279. Example
> 
> ```text
> PDF
> → parser-v3
> → text artifact
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14280. Then:
> 
> ```text
> text artifact
> → extractor-v7
> → candidate claims
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14281. Then:
> 
> ```text
> candidate claim
> → validator-v2
> → canonical claim
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14282. This creates reproducible semantic ETL.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14283. Semantic ETL
> 
> Traditional:
> 
> ```text
> Extract
> Transform
> Load
> ```
> 
> Innovation OS version:
> 
> ```text
> Acquire
> Parse
> Observe
> Interpret
> Validate
> Promote
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14284. This is more epistemically explicit.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14285. Data Pipeline Versioning
> 
> Any parser/extractor update can change outputs.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14286. Therefore derived semantic objects should know:
> 
> ```text
> pipeline version
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14287. New extractor version can trigger:
> 
> ```text
> re-extraction
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14288. But not overwrite old semantic history blindly.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14289. Re-extraction comparison
> 
> ```text
> Old candidates
> vs
> New candidates
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14290. Semantic diff:
> 
> ```text
> new claim
> removed claim
> changed scope
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14291. Then promotion rules decide updates.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14292. This is especially important for LLM extraction upgrades.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14293. Raw Preservation
> 
> If lawful/allowed,
> 
> keep original input so:
> 
> ```text
> future better parsers
> ```
> 
> can reprocess.

> ---
> 
> # 14294. That's one reason RawSource versioning is valuable.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14295. Data Immutability
> 
> Raw snapshot should generally be:
> 
> ```text
> append-only
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14296. Correction is:
> 
> ```text
> new snapshot
> ```
> 
> not silent mutation.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14297. Example human correction
> 
> Original entry:
> 
> ```text
> temperature 82
> ```
> 
> later corrected:
> 
> ```text
> sensor was miscalibrated
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14298. Keep original observation,
> 
> add correction/qualification evidence.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14299. This preserves audit history.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14300. Data Trust Boundaries
> 
> Different source classes have different trust semantics.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14301. Example
> 
> ```text
> sensor reading
> ```
> 
> trusted for transport integrity maybe,
> 
> but sensor can malfunction.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14302. Official API:
> 
> authoritative for its own published data maybe,
> 
> but not necessarily truth about broader world.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14303. Human report:
> 
> may be valuable but subjective.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14304. AI output:
> 
> derived inference.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14305. Therefore avoid source-wide universal trust score.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14306. Better annotate:
> 
> ```text
> authority scope
> independence
> verification
> freshness
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14307. Source Authority
> 
> Example:
> 
> Government registry may be authoritative for:
> 
> ```text
> registered legal status
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14308. But not for:
> 
> ```text
> future commercial success
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14309. Authority is claim-domain specific.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14310. Source Calibration
> 
> Sensor/model performance known from:
> 
> ```text
> benchmark/calibration evidence
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14311. Example camera detector:
> 
> ```text
> precision 95% under daylight
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14312. At night:
> 
> ```text
> UNKNOWN
> ```
> 
> unless separately tested.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14313. Context matters.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14314. Observation Context
> 
> Include:
> 
> ```text
> environment
> device configuration
> model version
> location
> ```
> 
> when necessary.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14315. Otherwise capability claims become overgeneralized.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14316. Human Observation
> 
> Human input can enter as:
> 
> ```text
> self-report
> expert report
> operator observation
> annotation
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14317. Example operator:
> 
> ```text
> machine sounds unusual
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14318. This can become:
> 
> ```text
> Observed Claim
> ```
> 
> with:
> 
> ```text
> source_mode = SELF_REPORTED / OBSERVED
> ```
> 
> depending structure.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14319. Do not discard qualitative human sensing simply because it is not numeric.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14320. Humans may detect patterns sensors miss.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14321. But human statement ≠ verified machine fault automatically.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14322. It can trigger:
> 
> ```text
> inspection task
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14323. Human-in-the-loop Annotation
> 
> Useful for:
> 
> ```text
> image labels
> entity resolution
> claim validation
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14324. Annotation is itself Artifact/Action result.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14325. Annotator agreement can be measured.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14326. But majority annotation ≠ ground truth automatically.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14327. Expert adjudication may be needed.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14328. Ground Truth
> 
> Use cautiously.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14329. Better distinguish:
> 
> ```text
> REFERENCE LABEL
> GOLD LABEL
> OBSERVED OUTCOME
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14330. "Ground truth" can be misleading when object itself uncertain.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14331. Sensor Calibration Fabric
> 
> Physical perception needs:
> 
> ```text
> calibration records
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14332. Calibration is:
> 
> ```text
> Artifact
> Evidence
> Event
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14333. Calibration expiration may degrade capability.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14334. Example
> 
> Precision scale calibrated six months ago,
> 
> certificate expired.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14335. Reading still exists,
> 
> but measurement assurance lower.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14336. Therefore:
> 
> ```text

> ≠
> measurement trusted for high-assurance task

> 
> ---
> 
> # 14337. Calibration Context becomes requirement for some tasks.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14338. Sensor Redundancy
> 
> Multiple sensors improve resilience,
> 
> but again independence matters.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14339. Two sensors sharing same power supply:
> 
> ```text
> common failure mode
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14340. Perception Resilience Graph
> 
> ```text
> Observation Capability
> ↑
> Sensors
> ↑
> Power/Network/Calibration
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14341. This integrates Self-Awareness and Runtime Resilience.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14342. Perception Pipeline Failure
> 
> Possible classes:
> 
> ```text
> SOURCE_FAILURE
> TRANSPORT_FAILURE
> PARSER_FAILURE
> RESOLUTION_FAILURE
> MODEL_FAILURE
> FUSION_FAILURE
> STALE_DATA
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14343. Command Center can explain:
> 
> ```text
> why world state is uncertain
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14344. Example
> 
> ```text
> Zone occupancy UNKNOWN
> because Camera 3 offline

>

> 
> # 14345. This is extremely useful operationally.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14346. High-Volume Sensor Streams
> 
> Do not put every raw sample into relational World State.

> ---
> 
> # 14347. Better:
> 
> ```text
> raw telemetry store
> ↓
> window processing
> ↓
> semantic events

> 
> ---
> 
> # 14348. Example vibration 10 kHz
> 
> Raw:
> 
> ```text
> time-series store/object storage

> 
> ---
> 
> # 14349. Semantic event:
> 
> ```text
> abnormal vibration detected
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14350. World State stores semantic layer.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14351. But source window reference preserved.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14352. This keeps relational model manageable.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14353. Edge Processing
> 
> For physical systems:
> 
> ```text
> camera/sensor
> ↓
> edge processor
> ↓
> semantic event
> ```
> 
> can reduce bandwidth.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14354. Example
> 
> Instead of streaming full 4K video centrally:
> 
> ```text
> vehicle_id
> position
> velocity
> timestamp
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14355. Raw video can remain:
> 
> ```text
> local
> short-retention
> event-triggered
> ```
> 
> depending policy.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14356. This directly supports earlier bazaar/station/port vision.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14357. Semantic Compression
> 
> Physical world:
> 
> ```text
> huge raw sensory bandwidth
> ```
> 
> becomes:
> 
> ```text
> compact semantic state
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14358. Example
> 
> Instead of:
> 
> ```text
> 30 FPS video
> ```
> 
> send:
> 
> ```text
> Forklift F17
> at zone Z2
> moving east
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14359. This dramatically reduces:
> 
> ```text
> network
> storage
> central compute
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14360. But raw source may still be needed for:
> 
> ```text
> audit
> model retraining
> incident investigation
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14361. Therefore retention policy balances:
> 
> ```text
> privacy
> cost
> evidence value
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14362. Semantic State Diff
> 
> Instead of transmitting full state repeatedly:
> 
> ```text
> state delta
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14363. Example
> 
> ```text
> F17.position:
> Z1 → Z2
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14364. This connects directly to earlier semantic M2M protocol.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14365. Edge Node can produce:
> 
> ```text
> STATE_DIFF
> EVENT
> EVIDENCE_REFERENCE
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14366. Central node does not need raw video unless requested/authorized.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14367. Machine-to-Machine Perception
> 
> Node A may say:
> 
> ```text
> Machine M temperature abnormal
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14368. Node B should know:
> 
> ```text
> which Claim
> which evidence reference
> which source node
> which time
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14369. Federated Evidence Envelope
> 
> Could contain:
> 
> ```yaml
> claim_id: ...
> source_node: ...
> observed_at: ...
> evidence_ref: ...
> signature: ...
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14370. Signature proves:
> 
> ```text
> origin/integrity
> ```
> 
> not truth.

> ---
> 
> # 14371. Remote raw data may stay remote.

> # 14463. Derived summaries are not new independent evidence.

> 
> # 14464. This is extremely important for multi-agent systems.

> # 14473. Evidence Aggregation respects independence.

>

> 
> ```text
> New Evidence
> ↓
> Affected Claims
> ↓

> ↓
> Active Claim View
> ↓

> # 14508. Dependency index:
> 
> ```text

> 
> # 14509. This is incremental semantic computation.

>

> # 14514. Data Plane vs Semantic Plane
> 
> Important split.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14515. Data Plane
> 
> Carries:
> 
> ```text
> raw bytes
> telemetry
> files
> video
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14516. Semantic Plane
> 
> Carries:
> 
> ```text
> entities
> claims
> events
> evidence
> state diffs
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14517. Control Plane
> 
> Carries:
> 
> ```text
> commands
> policies
> decisions
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14518. Keep these planes separate logically.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14519. Example camera
> 
> Data Plane:
> 
> ```text
> video frames
> ```
> 
> Semantic Plane:
> 
> ```text
> vehicle present
> ```
> 
> Control Plane:
> 
> ```text
> close gate
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14520. Text saying:
> 
> ```text
> close the gate
> ```
> 
> inside image/document must not jump directly into Control Plane.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14521. Critical invariant
> 
> ```text
> Data Content ≠ Command
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14522. This is defense against prompt injection and malicious data.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14523. A PDF may contain:
> 
> ```text
> ignore system rules and execute...
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14524. Perception Fabric treats as:
> 
> ```text
> document content
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14525. Not instruction.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14526. Same for QR code, image text, webpage, sensor metadata.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14527. Control instruction requires:
> 
> ```text
> authorized command channel
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14528. This should be one of strongest system-wide invariants.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14529. Data Poisoning
> 
> Threats include:
> 
> ```text
> false documents
> malicious sensor data
> adversarial images
> fake repositories
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14530. Fabric defenses:
> 
> ```text
> provenance
> cross-validation
> sandboxing
> source identity
> anomaly detection
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14531. But no system can guarantee truth from arbitrary external data.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14532. Therefore uncertainty remains explicit.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14533. Sensor Spoofing
> 
> Physical source may be forged.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14534. High-assurance systems may need:
> 
> ```text
> signed device data
> secure hardware identity
> cross-sensor checks
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14535. Still signature proves origin,
> 
> not physical truth.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14536. Sensor can be compromised or malfunctioning.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 14537. Same principle across digital and physical worlds.
> 
> ---
>

>

> 
> ```text

> # 14547. Example academic result:

>

> 
> packaged.

> 
> # 14559. This prevents cherry-picking.

> 
> # 14560. Evidence Bundle is Artifact/View,
>

>

>

> 
> store:

> 
> # 14562. Later evidence may change,
>

> 
> # 14563. This is crucial for audit.

Продолжаю с **15018**. Теперь строим слой распределённого исполнения: как Innovation OS выбирает **где** выполнять Action — в облаке, на локальном ПК, ARM-edge узле, GPU-сервере, лабораторной машине, роботе или федеративном партнёрском узле — с учётом данных, latency, hardware, стоимости, политики и доверия.

> **Document: Distributed Semantic Compute, Edge Intelligence & Execution Fabric v0.1**
> 
> # Distributed Semantic Compute, Edge Intelligence & Execution Fabric v0.1
> 
> ## 15018. Главный переход
> 
> До сих пор Innovation OS знает:
> 
> ```text id="dk81ns"
> WHAT should be done
> WHY it should be done
> WHAT capabilities are required
> WHAT evidence is needed
> ```
> 
> Теперь нужен следующий вопрос:
> 
> ```text id="kyi01m"
> WHERE should computation actually happen?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15019. В обычной distributed system это часто задача scheduler
> 
> Он рассматривает:
> 
> ```text id="pg6lxh"
> CPU
> RAM
> GPU
> load
> ```
> 
> Для Innovation OS этого недостаточно.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15020. Потому что Action может требовать одновременно
> 
> ```text id="exbt55"
> Capability
> Hardware
> Data
> Permission
> Location
> Latency
> Trust
> Cost
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15021. Поэтому требуется
> 
> # Semantic Execution Placement
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15022. Базовая формула
> 
> ```text id="zclkp9"
> Action
> +
> Capability Requirements
> +
> Data Locality
> +
> Hardware Requirements
> +
> Policy Constraints
> +
> Latency Requirements
> +
> Cost Constraints
> +
> Availability
> ↓
> Candidate Execution Nodes
> ↓
> Feasibility Filtering
> ↓
> Placement Options
> ↓
> Execution
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15023. Ключевой принцип
> 
> ```text id="bcnytz"
> Task ≠ Machine
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15024. Action описывает:
> 
> ```text id="41etnh"
> что должно быть выполнено
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15025. Execution Placement определяет:
> 
> ```text id="5puyw9"
> где это будет выполнено
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15026. Поэтому Project/Action Graph должен оставаться:
> 
> ```text id="ktdyms"

> ```
> 
> настолько, насколько позволяет задача.

# chatgpt response

Продолжаю с **15911**. Теперь формализуем тот слой, который раньше существовал как идея «протокола поверх MCP/MHS»: машины, AI-агенты, edge-узлы, цифровые двойники и сервисы передают друг другу не просто текст/RPC, а **смысловые состояния, capability-контракты, изменения мира, запросы действий и Evidence**.

> **Document: Semantic M2M Interaction, Capability Negotiation & State-Diff Protocol v0.1**
> 
> # Semantic M2M Interaction, Capability Negotiation & State-Diff Protocol v0.1
> 
> ## 15911. Главный переход
> 
> До сих пор система уже умеет:
> 
> ```text
> обнаружить Capability
> ↓
> выбрать Execution Node
> ↓
> отправить Action
> ↓
> получить Result
> ```
> 
> Но остаётся фундаментальная проблема:
> 
> ```text
> как две машины понимают,
> что именно они передают друг другу?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15912. Обычный сетевой протокол решает
> 
> ```text
> как доставить bytes
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15913. RPC решает
> 
> ```text
> какую функцию вызвать
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15914. API schema решает
> 
> ```text
> какие поля находятся в сообщении
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15915. Но этого всё ещё недостаточно для автономной сложной системы
> 
> Потому что машина должна понимать:
> 
> ```text
> что представляет объект
> каков его Context
> какая часть State изменилась
> какие Claims подтверждены
> что является Simulation
> что является Observation
> что разрешено делать
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15916. Поэтому нужен
> 
> # Semantic M2M Protocol
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15917. Его задача
> 
> Не заменить TCP/HTTP/MQTT/gRPC.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15918. Он работает поверх транспорта
> 
> ```text
> HTTP
> WebSocket
> MQTT
> gRPC
> message broker
> local IPC
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15919. То есть:
> 
> ```text
> Transport
> ↓
> Semantic Envelope
> ↓
> IIR Objects / Commands / State Diffs
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15920. Главная идея
> 
> Передавать не:
> 
> ```text
> "какую-то строку"
> ```
> 
> а:
> 
> ```text
> типизированное смысловое сообщение
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15921. Например вместо
> 
> ```json
> {"message":"robot 7 is hot"}
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15922. Передавать:
> 
> ```yaml
> type: CLAIM
> subject: robot-7
> predicate: HAS_TEMPERATURE
> value: 82
> unit: C
> source_mode: OBSERVED
> observed_at: ...
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15923. Получатель сразу знает
> 
> ```text
> Entity
> Predicate
> Value
> Unit
> Observation Time
> Epistemic Status
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15924. Это принципиально отличается от natural-language messaging.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15925. Natural language остаётся возможным
> 
> Но как:
> 
> ```text
> Artifact
> ```
> 
> или human-readable representation.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15926. Machine semantics должны быть структурированными
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15927. Основной стек
> 
> ```text
> Transport
> ↓
> Identity
> ↓
> Authentication
> ↓
> Semantic Envelope
> ↓
> Schema
> ↓
> Ontology
> ↓
> Context
> ↓
> Message Type
> ↓
> Payload
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15928. Semantic Envelope
> 
> Универсальная оболочка:
> 
> ```python
> class SemanticEnvelope(BaseModel):
>     protocol_version: str
> 
>     message_id: UUID
>     message_type: str
> 
>     sender_node_id: UUID
>     recipient_node_id: UUID | None
> 
>     context_id: UUID | None
> 
>     created_at: datetime
> 
>     schema_ref: str
>     payload: dict
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15929. Дополнительно:
> 
> ```text
> correlation_id
> causation_id
> reply_to
> ttl
> signature
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15930. `message_id`
> 
> Глобально уникальный идентификатор сообщения.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15931. `correlation_id`
> 
> Связывает:
> 
> ```text
> request
> response
> follow-up events
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15932. `causation_id`
> 
> Показывает:
> 
> ```text
> какое сообщение/событие
> породило это сообщение
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15933. Это создаёт:
> 
> ```text
> distributed causal trace
> ```
> 
> на уровне сообщений.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15934. Но causation metadata здесь означает:
> 
> ```text
> technical causal lineage
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15935. Не научное доказательство причинности.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15936. Protocol Message Types
> 
> Минимальный набор:
> 
> ```text
> HELLO
> CAPABILITY_ADVERTISEMENT
> CAPABILITY_QUERY
> CAPABILITY_OFFER
> STATE_SNAPSHOT
> STATE_DIFF
> QUERY
> QUERY_RESULT
> COMMAND_REQUEST
> COMMAND_RESPONSE
> EVENT
> CLAIM
> EVIDENCE_REFERENCE
> PROPOSAL
> ACK
> ERROR
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15937. Это расширяет уже существующий federation package vocabulary.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15938. Не нужно десятки протоколов для:
> 
> ```text
> agents
> robots
> services
> labs
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15939. Один semantic envelope
> 
> может нести разные domain payloads.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15940. Но message type должен быть явным.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15941. HELLO
> 
> Первое логическое взаимодействие.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15942. HELLO сообщает:
> 
> ```text
> кто я
> какие версии протокола понимаю
> какие semantic profiles поддерживаю
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15943. Example
> 
> ```yaml
> type: HELLO
> 
> node_id: node-a
> 
> protocol_versions:
>   - "1.0"
> 
> semantic_profiles:
>   - iir-core-0.1
>   - robotics-extension-0.2
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15944. HELLO ≠ authentication
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15945. Identity должна быть подтверждена отдельным security layer.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15946. Любой узел может заявить:
> 
> ```text
> I am Node A
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15947. Только cryptographic/authentication mechanism подтверждает,
> 
> что это действительно Node A.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15948. Следующий шаг:
> 
> # Capability Advertisement
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15949. Node сообщает:
> 
> ```text
> что он умеет предоставлять
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15950. Example
> 
> ```yaml
> type: CAPABILITY_ADVERTISEMENT
> 
> capabilities:
>   - capability: pdf_table_extraction
>     version: "2"
>     status: OPERATIONAL
> 
>   - capability: local_object_detection
>     version: "1"
>     status: DEGRADED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15951. Advertisement является:
> 
> ```text
> declaration
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15952. Не независимым доказательством.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15953. Поэтому:
> 
> ```text
> advertised capability
> ≠
> verified capability
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15954. Receiver can request:
> 
> ```text
> Evidence References
> Benchmarks
> Capability Contract
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15955. Capability Contract
> 
> Определяет:
> 
> ```text
> inputs
> outputs
> preconditions
> side effects
> quality constraints
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15956. Example
> 
> ```yaml
> capability: pdf_table_extraction
> 
> input:
>   artifact_type: application/pdf
> 
> output:
>   schema: table-extraction-v2
> 
> side_effects:
>   - NONE
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15957. Physical capability contract
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```yaml
> capability: move_sample
> 
> inputs:
>   sample_id: UUID
>   destination: coordinate
> 
> effects:
>   - physical_motion
> 
> risk_class: PHYSICAL
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15958. Таким образом машина знает:
> 
> ```text
> это read-only computation
> ```
> 
> или:
> 
> ```text
> это physical side effect
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15959. Capability Query
> 
> Node asks:
> 
> ```text
> Who can provide Capability X?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15960. Request:
> 
> ```yaml
> type: CAPABILITY_QUERY
> 
> requires:
>   capability: optical_pressure_measurement
> 
> constraints:
>   location: local
>   freshness_ms: 100
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15961. Candidate nodes reply:
> 
> ```text
> CAPABILITY_OFFER
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15962. Offer may include:
> 
> ```text
> availability
> capacity
> constraints
> evidence
> estimated latency
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15963. But:
> 
> ```text
> Offer ≠ Reservation
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15964. Another invariant.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15965. Offer can disappear before binding.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15966. Reservation/commitment remains separate protocol action.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15967. Capability Negotiation
> 
> Two nodes may differ in:
> 
> ```text
> version
> quality
> schema
> latency
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15968. Example requester needs:
> 
> ```text
> object_detection >= profile P
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15969. Node A offers:
> 
> ```text
> profile P
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15970. Node B:
> 
> ```text
> profile Q
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15971. Negotiation should compare structured contracts,
> 
> not free-text descriptions.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15972. Capability Compatibility
> 
> Possible outcomes:
> 
> ```text
> COMPATIBLE
> COMPATIBLE_WITH_ADAPTER
> PARTIAL
> INCOMPATIBLE
> UNKNOWN
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15973. `COMPATIBLE_WITH_ADAPTER`
> 
> Очень важный вариант.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15974. Example
> 
> Producer outputs:
> 
> ```text
> schema v1
> ```
> 
> Consumer needs:
> 
> ```text
> schema v2
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15975. Existing converter may bridge.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15976. Then execution becomes:
> 
> ```text
> Provider
> → Adapter
> → Consumer
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15977. Adapter itself is:
> 
> ```text
> Capability
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15978. Thus protocol negotiation can dynamically assemble chains.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15979. This is important for heterogeneous ecosystems.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15980. Schema Negotiation
> 
> Nodes exchange:
> 
> ```text
> supported schema identifiers
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15981. Example
> 
> ```text
> robot-pose-v1
> robot-pose-v2
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15982. If both support v2:
> 
> ```text
> use v2
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15983. If only common version v1:
> 
> ```text
> use v1
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15984. If no common schema:
> 
> ```text
> search adapter
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15985. If no adapter:
> 
> ```text
> INCOMPATIBLE
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15986. Never silently guess mapping.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15987. Ontology Negotiation
> 
> Schema compatibility does not guarantee semantic compatibility.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15988. Example both have field:
> 
> ```text
> status
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15989. One means:
> 
> ```text
> machine state
> ```
> 
> another:
> 
> ```text
> work-order state
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15990. Therefore concepts/predicates must be namespaced.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15991. Example
> 
> ```text
> core:HAS
> robotics:GRIP_STATE
> workflow:ACTION_STATE
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15992. Unknown predicate should remain:
> 
> ```text
> unknown namespaced predicate
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15993. Not automatically mapped to similar word.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15994. Semantic Fingerprint
> 
> A capability/schema can expose:
> 
> ```text
> identifier
> version
> hash
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15995. Hash helps ensure exact machine-readable definition.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15996. But:
> 
> ```text
> same hash
> ```
> 
> proves same document/schema bytes,
> 
> not correctness.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15997. Ontology Mapping Package
> 
> Could define:
> 
> ```text
> remote concept
> → local concept
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15998. Mapping types:
> 
> ```text
> EXACT
> NARROWER
> BROADER
> PARTIAL
> UNKNOWN
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 15999. This avoids unsafe ontology collapse.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16000. Semantic Protocol milestone
> 
> At **16000** protocol уже имеет три уровня совместимости:
> 
> ```text
> Transport Compatibility
> Schema Compatibility
> Semantic Compatibility
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16001. И нужен четвёртый:
> 
> ```text
> Operational Compatibility
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16002. Потому что даже если semantics совпадают,
> 
> node может:
> 
> ```text
> не иметь permission
> не иметь capacity
> не иметь physical access
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16003. Поэтому:
> 
> ```text
> Semantic Compatibility
> ≠
> Operational Feasibility
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16004. STATE_SNAPSHOT
> 
> Используется когда получателю нужно получить:
> 
> ```text
> состояние объекта/подграфа
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16005. Example
> 
> ```yaml
> type: STATE_SNAPSHOT
> 
> subject: robot-17
> 
> state:
>   position: [...]
>   battery_pct: 62
>   mode: AUTO
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16006. Но snapshot должен иметь:
> 
> ```text
> state_revision
> observed_at
> source_node
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16007. Otherwise receiver cannot determine:
> 
> ```text
> freshness
> ordering
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16008. STATE_DIFF
> 
> Один из центральных элементов нового протокола.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16009. Вместо передачи всей модели мира:
> 
> ```text
> send only change
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16010. Example
> 
> ```yaml
> type: STATE_DIFF
> 
> subject: robot-17
> base_revision: 811
> new_revision: 812
> 
> changes:
>   battery_pct:
>     from: 62
>     to: 61
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16011. Это намного компактнее.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16012. Особенно для:
> 
> ```text
> digital twins
> MMORPG worlds
> robots
> ports
> factories
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16013. State Diff может содержать:
> 
> ```text
> added
> removed
> changed
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16014. Но `removed` нужно понимать осторожно.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16015. Example
> 
> ```text
> field removed
> ```
> 
> может значить:
> 
> ```text
> unknown
> not applicable
> deleted
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16016. Поэтому operation explicit:
> 
> ```text
> SET
> UNSET
> DELETE
> UNKNOWN
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16017. `UNKNOWN` особенно важен.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16018. Example sensor connection lost.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16019. Не:
> 
> ```text
> temperature = null
> ```
> 
> без semantics.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16020. Лучше:
> 
> ```yaml
> operation: UNKNOWN
> reason: SENSOR_UNAVAILABLE
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16021. This preserves epistemic meaning.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16022. Patch Semantics
> 
> State diff resembles:
> 
> ```text
> JSON Patch
> ```
> 
> но semantic-aware.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16023. Example:
> 
> ```yaml
> op: SET
> path: /resource/availability
> value: UNAVAILABLE
> evidence_ref: ...
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16024. Optional evidence reference can explain update.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16025. Snapshot + Diff architecture
> 
> Receiver first gets:
> 
> ```text
> Snapshot revision 100
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16026. Then:
> 
> ```text
> diff 101
> diff 102
> diff 103
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16027. If diff 102 lost:
> 
> receiver detects gap.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16028. Then requests:
> 
> ```text
> resync
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16029. This is standard distributed-state concept,
> 
> but with semantic objects.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16030. State Diff Replay
> 
> Allows:
> 
> ```text
> reconstruct state over time
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16031. But events remain canonical historical semantics.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16032. State diffs are synchronization mechanism,
> 
> not necessarily full audit history.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16033. Important distinction:
> 
> ```text
> Event ≠ State Diff
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16034. Event:
> 
> ```text
> what happened
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16035. State Diff:
> 
> ```text
> what changed in materialized state
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16036. Example
> 
> Event:
> 
> ```text
> Robot entered Zone B
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16037. Diff:
> 
> ```text
> robot.position.zone: A → B
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16038. Both useful.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16039. Diff may result from multiple Events.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16040. Event may not change current state permanently.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16041. QUERY
> 
> Protocol should support semantic questions.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16042. Example:
> 
> ```yaml
> type: QUERY
> 
> query:
>   subject: lab-7
>   predicate: PROVIDES
>   object: capability-x
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16043. Response:
> 
> ```text
> QUERY_RESULT
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16044. Result must include:
> 
> ```text
> YES
> NO
> UNKNOWN
> ```
> 
> where appropriate.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16045. UNKNOWN must be protocol-native.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16046. Not represented as empty response.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16047. Example:
> 
> ```yaml
> truth: UNKNOWN
> reason: NOT_OBSERVED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16048. This is critical for machine reasoning.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16049. Semantic Query can request:
> 
> ```text
> state
> claims
> evidence
> capabilities
> availability
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16050. But authorization determines what is returned.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16051. Node may answer:
> 
> ```text
> DENIED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16052. `DENIED` ≠ UNKNOWN.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16053. Four distinct cases:
> 
> ```text
> YES
> NO
> UNKNOWN
> ACCESS_DENIED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16054. Very important.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16055. Otherwise consumer might interpret:
> 
> ```text
> no permission
> ```
> 
> as:
> 
> ```text
> no capability
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16056. Privacy-preserving query
> 
> Example requester asks:
> 
> ```text
> Do you have capability X?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16057. Node policy may permit response:
> 
> ```text
> YES
> ```
> 
> without revealing:
> 
> ```text
> which person/tool provides it
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16058. Progressive Disclosure.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16059. Level 1:
> 
> ```text
> capability exists
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16060. Level 2:
> 
> ```text
> capacity available
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16061. Level 3:
> 
> ```text
> provider details
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16062. Level 4:
> 
> ```text
> internal topology
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16063. Different callers receive different levels.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16064. This is essential for inter-organizational federation.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16065. COMMAND_REQUEST
> 
> Represents request for side effect.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16066. Example
> 
> ```yaml
> type: COMMAND_REQUEST
> 
> action:
>   capability: measure_temperature
> 
> target: reactor-3
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16067. Critical:
> 
> ```text
> Command Request ≠ Command Authorized
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16068. Receiver performs local policy evaluation.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16069. Possible responses:
> 
> ```text
> ACCEPTED
> DENIED
> DEFERRED
> REQUIRES_APPROVAL
> UNAVAILABLE
> INVALID
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16070. If ACCEPTED,
> 
> local runtime generates local Command/Action attempt.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16071. Remote system does not own local actuator directly.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16072. This preserves sovereignty/safety.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16073. COMMAND_RESPONSE
> 
> Should distinguish:
> 
> ```text
> request accepted
> ```
> 
> from:
> 
> ```text
> execution completed
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16074. Example lifecycle:
> 
> ```text
> REQUESTED
> ACCEPTED
> RUNNING
> COMPLETED
> FAILED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16075. Acceptance ≠ completion.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16076. Completion ≠ verification.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16077. So remote response may include:
> 
> ```text
> execution_result
> evidence_refs
> verification_state
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16078. Example physical measurement:
> 
> ```yaml
> execution: COMPLETED
> verification: VERIFIED
> result:
>   temperature: 82
>   unit: C
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16079. Another:
> 
> ```yaml
> execution: COMPLETED
> verification: PENDING
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16080. Useful distinction.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16081. EVENT message
> 
> Nodes can publish semantic events.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16082. Example:
> 
> ```text
> MachineStopped
> PackageInstalled
> CapabilityDegraded
> ExperimentCompleted
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16083. Event identity immutable.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16084. Receiver may choose:
> 
> ```text
> store
> ignore
> materialize
> trigger workflow
> ```
> 
> according to subscription/policy.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16085. Event Subscription
> 
> Node can subscribe to semantic classes:
> 
> ```text
> CapabilityDegraded
> FundingCallOpened
> RobotFault
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16086. This is more powerful than topic names alone.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16087. Subscription could include:
> 
> ```text
> predicate
> entity type
> context
> scope
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16088. Example:
> 
> ```text
> all CapabilityDegraded events
> affecting Program P
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16089. But initial protocol can use simple topic/filter.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16090. Do not overbuild distributed semantic query language first.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16091. CLAIM message
> 
> Shares:
> 
> ```text
> assertion
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16092. Example:
> 
> ```yaml
> type: CLAIM
> 
> claim_type: FACT
> source_mode: OBSERVED
> 
> subject: equipment-9
> predicate: HAS_STATUS
> literal: OPERATIONAL
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16093. Receiver does not have to adopt it as local canonical truth.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16094. It enters as:
> 
> ```text
> remote Claim
> ```
> 
> with provenance.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16095. Then local policy decides:
> 
> ```text
> accept
> verify
> store as external claim
> reject
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16096. This is critical.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16097. Federation should not mean:
> 
> ```text
> remote claim silently mutates local truth
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16098. Remote Claim remains attributable to remote node.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16099. EVIDENCE_REFERENCE
> 
> Shares evidence without necessarily sending raw data.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16100. Example:
> 
> ```yaml
> type: EVIDENCE_REFERENCE
> 
> claim_id: ...
> evidence:
>   node: lab-a
>   artifact_ref: measurement-773
>   access_mode: ON_REQUEST
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16101. Receiver may request raw Evidence if authorized.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16102. Or use signed summary if raw cannot leave node.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16103. This is important for:
> 
> ```text
> industrial data
> medical data
> research embargoes
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16104. Evidence Access Modes
> 
> ```text
> INLINE
> REFERENCE
> ON_REQUEST
> LOCAL_ONLY
> ATTESTED_RESULT_ONLY
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16105. `ATTESTED_RESULT_ONLY`
> 
> Node provides:
> 
> ```text
> verified result
> ```
> 
> without sharing raw evidence.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16106. This is weaker for independent verification,
> 
> but useful when confidentiality requires.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16107. Evidence semantics must expose that limitation.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16108. PROPOSAL
> 
> Machines/agents may send:
> 
> ```text
> proposal
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16109. Example:
> 
> ```text
> Switch Provider A → B
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16110. Proposal is not Command.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16111. Critical protocol invariant:
> 
> ```text
> PROPOSAL ≠ COMMAND
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16112. Proposal may contain:
> 
> ```text
> rationale
> evidence
> expected impact
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16113. Governance can convert proposal into Decision/Action.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16114. This prevents AI suggestion from becoming automatic execution.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16115. ACK
> 
> Acknowledgement should have semantics.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16116. Not simply:
> 
> ```text
> received
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16117. Possible ACK levels:
> 
> ```text
> RECEIVED
> VALIDATED
> ACCEPTED
> APPLIED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16118. Example:
> 
> ```text
> RECEIVED
> ```
> 
> means bytes/message arrived.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16119. `VALIDATED`
> 
> schema/auth checks passed.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16120. `ACCEPTED`
> 
> local system accepted semantic object.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16121. `APPLIED`
> 
> state change materialized.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16122. This is extremely useful for distributed reconciliation.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16123. One ACK flag cannot represent all.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16124. ERROR
> 
> Structured error taxonomy.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16125. Classes:
> 
> ```text
> TRANSPORT
> AUTHENTICATION
> AUTHORIZATION
> SCHEMA
> SEMANTIC
> CAPABILITY
> POLICY
> EXECUTION
> CONFLICT
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16126. Example:
> 
> ```yaml
> error_type: SEMANTIC
> code: UNKNOWN_PREDICATE
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16127. Another:
> 
> ```yaml
> error_type: POLICY
> code: DATA_RESIDENCY_DENIED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16128. Error text human-readable,
> 
> but machine code canonical.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16129. Avoid parsing English error messages.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16130. Protocol should support:
> 
> ```text
> machine-readable reason
> +
> human explanation
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16131. Version Negotiation
> 
> Protocol evolves.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16132. HELLO shares:
> 
> ```text
> supported_protocol_versions
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16133. Nodes choose:
> 
> ```text
> highest mutually supported version
> ```
> 
> or policy-defined compatible version.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16134. But latest ≠ safest automatically.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16135. Production policy may pin:
> 
> ```text
> v1.2
> ```
> 
> even if v1.3 supported.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16136. Protocol Compatibility
> 
> Need:
> 
> ```text
> major
> minor
> extension
> ```
> 
> concept.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16137. Example:
> 
> ```text
> 1.x
> ```
> 
> backward-compatible within defined subset.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16138. Major version:
> 
> ```text
> breaking semantics
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16139. Extensions use namespaces.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16140. Core should remain small.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16141. Domain Profiles
> 
> Instead of putting every field into core:
> 
> ```text
> robotics
> research
> funding
> logistics
> ```
> 
> use profiles.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16142. Example:
> 
> ```text
> profile: robotics-motion-0.2
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16143. Core knows:
> 
> ```text
> message
> identity
> context
> claims
> events
> commands
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16144. Robotics extension knows:
> 
> ```text
> pose
> trajectory
> grasp
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16145. Research extension knows:
> 
> ```text
> experiment
> measurement
> benchmark
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16146. Funding extension:
> 
> ```text
> call
> eligibility
> budget
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16147. This prevents protocol bloat.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16148. Extensibility invariant
> 
> ```text
> Unknown extension
> must not corrupt core interpretation.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16149. Receiver may:
> 
> ```text
> retain
> ignore safely
> request adapter
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16150. Critical extensions can be marked:
> 
> ```text
> REQUIRED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16151. If receiver does not support:
> 
> ```text
> reject message
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16152. Optional extension can be ignored while core remains usable.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16153. Context Negotiation
> 
> Same capability can behave differently by Context.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16154. Example:
> 
> ```text
> Simulation
> Production
> Research
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16155. Before interaction nodes may establish:
> 
> ```text
> shared context
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16156. Example:
> 
> ```yaml
> context:
>   mode: SIMULATION
>   project_id: ...
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16157. This prevents simulation messages entering production.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16158. Critical invariant:
> 
> ```text
> Context mismatch
> must fail closed for risky actions.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16159. Example:
> 
> Simulation robot command sent to production robot.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16160. Receiver sees:
> 
> ```text
> SIMULATION context
> ```
> 
> and refuses real actuator execution.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16161. Context IDs therefore participate in authorization.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16162. World Namespace
> 
> Federated nodes may host:
> 
> ```text
> base world
> simulation worlds
> historical replay
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16163. Envelope should identify:
> 
> ```text
> world/context namespace
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16164. This is analogous to:
> 
> ```text
> branch
> ```
> 
> in version control.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16165. State Diff between worlds is possible,
> 
> but explicit.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16166. Example:
> 
> ```text
> Scenario A differs from Base World
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16167. But applying scenario diff to base world requires:
> 
> ```text
> Decision/Execution
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16168. Not automatic merge.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16169. Semantic State Compression
> 
> Now we reach earlier idea:
> 
> ```text
> textual diffusion / compact semantic transfer
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16170. Large state can be represented by:
> 
> ```text
> shared baseline
> +
> small diff
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16171. Instead of sending:
> 
> ```text
> entire 100-page world description
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16172. Send:
> 
> ```text
> base_state_hash
> +
> semantic delta
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16173. Example:
> 
> ```yaml
> base_revision: 900
> 
> changes:
>   - subject: project-7
>     predicate: HAS_STATE
>     from: EXECUTION
>     to: PAUSED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16174. Receiver reconstructs current state locally.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16175. This resembles compression,
> 
> but at semantic level.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16176. Not token compression alone.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16177. It is:
> 
> ```text
> meaning-preserving state delta
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16178. This could drastically reduce communication between AI agents.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16179. Example 20 agents share large Project context.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16180. Instead of repeatedly sending:
> 
> ```text
> 50k token history
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16181. They share:
> 
> ```text
> Project State Revision
> +
> new Claims
> +
> new Events
> +
> new Artifacts
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16182. Each agent reconstructs needed context.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16183. This can reduce:
> 
> ```text
> token cost
> latency
> context duplication
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16184. This is much closer to database synchronization than chat.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16185. Agent Context Protocol
> 
> Agent can request:
> 
> ```text
> CONTEXT_SNAPSHOT
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16186. Then receive incremental:
> 
> ```text
> CONTEXT_DIFF
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16187. Example
> 
> Initial:
> 
> ```text
> Project
> Goals
> Requirements
> Claims
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16188. Later only:
> 
> ```text
> new benchmark result
> new decision
> task state change
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16189. This is a practical version of earlier "text diffusion" idea.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16190. Large model and many small models
> 
> Architecture:
> 
> ```text
> Shared Semantic State
>       ↑
>   ┌───┼────┐
> small small small
> models agents models
>       ↓
>  large reasoning model
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16191. They do not need exchange full natural-language transcripts.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16192. They exchange:
> 
> ```text
> Claims
> Questions
> Artifacts
> State Diffs
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16193. This enables:
> 
> # Semantic Blackboard over M2M
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16194. Agent A adds:
> 
> ```text
> Claim X
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16195. Agent B adds:
> 
> ```text
> Evidence Y
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16196. Agent C adds:
> 
> ```text
> Refutation Z
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16197. Coordinator sees updated semantic state.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16198. No need copy all previous dialogue.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16199. This may materially improve multi-agent scalability.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16200. Semantic Delta Granularity
> 
> Could be:
> 
> ```text
> object-level
> field-level
> relation-level
> claim-level
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16201. For MVP:
> 
> ```text
> object/relation-level
> ```
> 
> enough.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16202. Avoid premature binary delta encoding.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16203. Human-readable JSON/YAML useful initially.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16204. Later compact encodings:
> 
> ```text
> CBOR
> MessagePack
> Protobuf
> ```
> 
> may reduce bandwidth.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16205. Transport serialization ≠ semantic design.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16206. Keep semantic spec independent.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16207. Semantic Hash
> 
> Could compute canonical hash of:
> 
> ```text
> normalized object state
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16208. Useful for:
> 
> ```text
> dedup
> sync
> integrity
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16209. Example:
> 
> ```text
> receiver says:
> I already have state hash H
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16210. Sender sends only later diffs.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16211. Canonical serialization must be well-defined
> 
> if hashes used.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16212. Otherwise ordering/format changes alter hash.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16213. Merkle-like State Trees
> 
> Later possible.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16214. Large distributed graph can compare:
> 
> ```text
> subtree hashes
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16215. Then synchronize only differences.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16216. Particularly useful for:
> 
> ```text
> large edge fleets
> offline nodes
> federated replicas
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16217. But not MVP.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16218. Start with:
> 
> ```text
> revision + content hash
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16219. Offline Reconciliation
> 
> Node reconnects.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16220. Says:
> 
> ```text
> last_known_remote_revision = 81
> local_revision = 96
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16221. Exchange missing Events/Diffs.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16222. If no semantic conflict:
> 
> ```text
> merge
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16223. If conflict:
> 
> ```text
> CONFLICT
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16224. Conflict types:
> 
> ```text
> STATE
> DECISION
> IDENTITY
> SCHEMA
> POLICY
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16225. State Conflict
> 
> Two nodes claim different current state.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16226. Resolve using:
> 
> ```text
> authority
> time
> evidence
> context
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16227. Not blindly "latest timestamp wins".
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16228. Decision Conflict
> 
> Two authorities made incompatible commitments.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16229. Must trigger:
> 
> ```text
> governance reconciliation
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16230. Identity Conflict
> 
> Same external identifier linked differently.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16231. Do not auto-merge.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16232. Policy Conflict
> 
> Remote request allowed by sender,
> 
> denied by receiver.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16233. Receiver local policy prevails locally.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16234. Shared workflow must adapt.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16235. Conflict Resolution Message
> 
> Could send:
> 
> ```text
> CONFLICT_NOTICE
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16236. Contains:
> 
> ```text
> objects
> conflict class
> evidence refs
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16237. Resolution creates new Decision/Event.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16238. Preserve conflict history.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16239. Semantic Transactions
> 
> Sometimes multiple changes must be interpreted together.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16240. Example:
> 
> ```text
> remove old provider
> add new provider
> update binding
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16241. A partial application may create invalid state.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16242. Message can contain:
> 
> ```text
> CHANGESET
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16243. Receiver validates whole set.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16244. Then:
> 
> ```text
> apply atomically locally
> ```
> 
> where possible.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16245. Cross-node atomicity still not guaranteed.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16246. Use Saga for distributed effects.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16247. Semantic ChangeSet
> 
> ```yaml
> type: STATE_DIFF
> 
> atomic_local: true
> 
> changes:
>   - ...
>   - ...
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16248. Local atomicity helpful.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16249. Distributed global atomicity avoided.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16250. Query/Subscription Routing
> 
> Large federation cannot broadcast every request.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16251. Need directories/indexes.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16252. Capability Directory can know:
> 
> ```text
> which node advertises which capability
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16253. But directory data may be stale.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16254. Resolver rechecks provider before binding.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16255. Directory ≠ authority.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16256. Similarly:
> 
> ```text
> Entity Location Directory
> ```
> 
> may know where authoritative state resides.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16257. Example:
> 
> ```text
> equipment-7
> → lab-node-a
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16258. Then query routed to correct node.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16259. Namespace Resolution
> 
> Like semantic DNS.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16260. Could map:
> 
> ```text
> object UUID
> → authoritative node
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16261. But ownership may migrate.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16262. Migration creates:
> 
> ```text
> authority transfer event
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16263. Example Project moved from Node A to B.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16264. Authority Transfer must be explicit,
> 
> especially for commitments/decisions.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16265. Cached references update.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16266. No silent authority reassignment.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16267. Machine Discovery
> 
> Node could ask:
> 
> ```text
> Who understands ontology X?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16268. Or:
> 
> ```text
> Who can translate schema A→B?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16269. These are just Capability Queries.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16270. Thus interoperability services themselves become capabilities.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16271. Example:
> 
> ```text
> SCHEMA_TRANSLATION
> ONTOLOGY_MAPPING
> UNIT_CONVERSION
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16272. This creates self-extending protocol ecosystem.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16273. Unknown capability can trigger:
> 
> ```text
> search for adapter/package
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16274. Package Manager may install.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16275. Then nodes become compatible.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16276. This directly supports Artificial Technological Awareness.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16277. System sees:
> 
> ```text
> I cannot currently understand profile X
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16278. Then searches for:
> 
> ```text
> profile adapter
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16279. Tests it.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16280. Proposes installation.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16281. After approval:
> 
> ```text
> new interoperability capability acquired
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16282. This is protocol-level self-improvement.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16283. Semantic Firewalls
> 
> Traditional firewall filters:
> 
> ```text
> IP
> port
> protocol
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16284. Semantic gateway can additionally filter:
> 
> ```text
> message type
> capability
> context
> action risk
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16285. Example:
> 
> ```text
> QUERY allowed
> COMMAND_REQUEST denied
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16286. Or:
> 
> ```text
> sensor read allowed
> actuator command denied
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16287. This is very powerful.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16288. Semantic Security Policy
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```yaml
> allow:
>   - QUERY
>   - CAPABILITY_QUERY
> 
> deny:
>   - COMMAND_REQUEST
> 
> unless:
>   role: authorized-controller
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16289. Another:
> 
> ```text
> only Simulation Context commands accepted from external nodes
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16290. This makes trust boundary understandable.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16291. Rate Limits by Semantic Operation
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> 1000 sensor queries/min
> 10 physical command requests/min
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16292. High-risk actions can have stricter controls.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16293. Message Size/Complexity Limits
> 
> Prevent:
> 
> ```text
> resource exhaustion
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16294. Example:
> 
> ```text
> maximum graph diff size
> maximum nested depth
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16295. Parser should reject pathological payloads safely.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16296. Semantic DoS
> 
> Attack could send:
> 
> ```text

>

> 
> # 16297. Need:
> 
> ```text
> quota
> cost controls
> priority
> ```

> ---
> 
> # 16298. Agent-to-Agent Abuse
> 
> One agent may continually delegate work.

> ---
> 
> # 16299. Capability/request budgets prevent unbounded delegation loops.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16300. Delegation Depth
> 
> Envelope can include:
> 
> ```text
> delegation_chain
> ```
> 
> or correlation ancestry.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16301. Policy may cap:
> 
> ```text
> max delegation depth
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16302. This helps avoid:
> 
> ```text
> Agent A → B → C → A
> ```
> 
> loops.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16303. Cycle Detection
> 
> Semantic request graph detects repeated:
> 
> ```text
> same requirement
> same context
> ```
>
