> 
> # 16304. Then:
> 
> ```text
> DELEGATION_LOOP
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16305. Multi-Agent semantic blackboard reduces need for recursive conversations.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16306. Subscription Loop
> 
> Similarly node A forwards event to B,
> 
> B to C,
> 
> C back to A.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16307. Message IDs + lineage prevent reprocessing.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16308. Hop Count
> 
> Could include:
> 
> ```text
> ttl/hop_limit
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16309. Particularly for broadcast/federated routing.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16310. Data Minimization in M2M
> 
> Send:
> 
> ```text
> minimum semantic state necessary
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16311. Example robot asks:
> 
> ```text
> Is corridor clear?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16312. It doesn't need:
> 
> ```text
> full camera stream
> person identities
> facility database
> ```
>

> 
> # 16313. Response:
> 
> ```yaml
> truth: YES
> valid_until: ...
> evidence_quality: VERIFIED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16314. This is both efficient and privacy-preserving.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16315. Semantic Cache
> 
> Node can cache query result.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16316. But response must include:
> 
> ```text
> validity
> freshness
> revision
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16317. Example:
> 
> ```text

> 
> may only be valid for:
>

>

> 
> # 16318. While:

> ---
> 
> # 16319. Cache lifetime is predicate/context-specific.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16320. Semantic TTL
> 
> Could be attached to State/Claim responses.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16321. But TTL expiration means:
> 
> ```text
> stale/unknown
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16322. Not necessarily:
>

> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16323. Important invariant.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16324. Subscription vs Polling
> 
> For fast-changing state:
> 
> ```text
> subscribe
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16325. For slow-changing:
> 
> ```text
> query periodically
> ```
>

> 
> # 16326. Example:
> 
> ```text
> robot pose
> ```
> 
> subscription.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16327. Example:
> 
> ```text
> equipment certification expiry
> ```
> 
> periodic query/event.

> 
> # 16328. Protocol does not mandate one communication style.

> ---
> 
> # 16329. Eventual Consistency
> 
> Many semantic states can be eventually consistent.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16330. Example Technopedia replication.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16331. Some state requires stronger local consistency.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16332. Example:
> 
> ```text
> physical equipment reservation
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16333. The authoritative node enforces local serialization.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16334. Protocol exposes result.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16335. This keeps distributed design tractable.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16336. Machine Negotiation
> 
> Nodes can negotiate more than schema.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16337. Example:
> 
> ```text
> quality
> latency
> price
> evidence level

> 
> # 16338. Requester:
> 
> ```yaml
> need:
>   latency_ms: <= 500
>   verification: VERIFIED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16339. Provider:
> 
> ```yaml
> offer:

> # 16601. Protocol Semantics for Uncertainty
>

> truth
> confidence
> verification

>

> 
> # 16602. Example:

> confidence: 0.72
> verification: UNVERIFIED

> 
> ---
> 
> # 16603. But numeric confidence optional.

> ---
> 
> # 16604. Do not invent pseudo-probabilities.

> ---
> 
> # 16605. UNKNOWN can exist without confidence.

> ---
> 
> # 16606. Example:
> 
> ```yaml

> reason: SENSOR_BLIND_ZONE
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 16607. Much better.

> # 16617. Conversion between coordinate frames is a capability.

> 
> # 16618. Wrong frame mapping can be dangerous.

> # 16619. Do not silently transform without validated mapping.

> ## 17041. Главный переход
> 
> До сих пор Innovation OS уже умеет:

> обмениваться State

>

>

> ```

> 
> # 17042. Потому что одинаковое слово не гарантирует одинаковый смысл
>

>

> ```
> 
> в одной системе может означать:
>

> 
> может означать:
>

> ```
> 
> или:
>

> 
> или:
> 
> ```text

> ```
>

> # 17044. Поэтому interoperability требует не только одинаковой структуры JSON
>

> shared semantic contract
> ```

> ---
> 
> # 17078. Потому что многие ontology bugs возникают из:
> 
> ```text
> category confusion
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17079. Semantic Role
> 
> Concept может иметь роль:
> 
> ```text
> capability
> metric
> unit
> state
> method
> material
> location_type
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17080. Role — application metadata,
> 
> не новый root.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17081. Concept может иметь несколько labels
> 
> ```text
> canonical label
> synonyms
> abbreviations
> translations
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17082. Example
> 
> ```text
> Artificial Intelligence
> AI
> ИИ
> Künstliche Intelligenz
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17083. Они указывают на:
> 
> ```text
> same Concept
> ```
> 
> если meaning действительно совпадает.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17084. Translation ≠ guaranteed equivalence
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17085. Некоторые термины имеют культурно/правово специфический смысл.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17086. Поэтому translation mapping может быть:
> 
> ```text
> EXACT
> APPROXIMATE
> CONTEXTUAL
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17087. Мультиязычный Registry важен для:
> 
> ```text
> EU projects
> research
> law
> international federation
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17088. Но canonical machine identity должна быть language-independent.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17089. Namespace
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> core:
> robotics:
> funding:
> research:
> legal:
> manufacturing:
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17090. Namespaces предотвращают глобальное collision.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17091. Example
> 
> ```text
> research:TRIAL
> ```
> 
> и:
> 
> ```text
> business:TRIAL
> ```
> 
> могут иметь разный смысл.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17092. Не нужно насильно объединять омонимы.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17093. Namespace Ownership
> 
> Кто имеет право изменять namespace?
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17094. Example:
> 
> ```text
> core:
> ```
> 
> может требовать architecture governance.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17095. Experimental namespace:
> 
> ```text
> org.example.experimental:
> ```
> 
> может управляться локальной командой.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17096. Это позволяет:
> 
> ```text
> central semantic stability
> +
> local experimentation
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17097. Core Vocabulary
> 
> Должен быть маленьким.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17098. Уже замороженные roots:
> 
> ```text
> ENTITY
> CONCEPT
> RESOURCE
> PROJECT
> ACTION
> ARTIFACT
> CLAIM
> EVIDENCE
> EVENT
> CONSTRAINT
> DECISION
> CONTEXT
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17099. Core Predicates:
> 
> ```text
> IS_A
> PART_OF
> HAS
> REQUIRES
> PROVIDES
> USES
> PRODUCES
> DEPENDS_ON
> ENABLES
> BLOCKS
> SUPPORTS
> REFUTES
> DERIVED_FROM
> PERFORMS
> ASSIGNED_TO
> CONSTRAINS
> SATISFIES
> TRANSFORMS
> OBSERVES
> AFFECTS
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17100. Всё остальное по возможности:
> 
> ```text
> namespaced extension
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17101. Почему это важно
> 
> Если каждый новый domain добавляет root types,
> 
> через год получится:
> 
> ```text
> hundreds of incompatible semantic primitives
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17102. Тогда универсальный resolver разрушится.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17103. Поэтому правило:
> 
> ```text
> Prefer specialization
> over new root creation.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17104. Example
> 
> Robot:
> 
> ```text
> RESOURCE subtype
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17105. Grant:
> 
> ```text
> RESOURCE subtype
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17106. Experiment:
> 
> ```text
> ACTION / PROJECT
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17107. Digital Twin:
> 
> ```text
> Context/View/materialized state
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17108. Semantic Governance должен защищать эту дисциплину.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17109. Predicate Registry
> 
> Отдельно от Concept Registry.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17110. Predicate definition:
> 
> ```python
> class PredicateDefinition(BaseModel):
>     predicate_id: UUID
>     namespace: str
>     name: str
>     version: str
> 
>     subject_constraints: list[str]
>     object_constraints: list[str]
> 
>     inverse_predicate_id: UUID | None
>     status: str
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17111. Example
> 
> ```text
> PROVIDES
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17112. Expected semantics:
> 
> ```text
> Resource PROVIDES Capability
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17113. Не:
> 
> ```text
> Capability PROVIDES Resource
> ```
> 
> unless explicitly allowed.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17114. Domain/range constraints catch semantic errors.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17115. Example
> 
> ```text
> Project REQUIRES Capability
> ```
> 
> valid.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17116.
> 
> ```text
> Temperature REQUIRES Person
> ```
> 
> likely invalid under normal profile.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17117. But validation should support extension/context exceptions.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17118. Predicate Direction
> 
> Important.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17119. Example:
> 
> ```text
> A DEPENDS_ON B
> ```
> 
> means:
> 
> ```text
> A's operation/success requires B
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17120. Reverse is not same predicate.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17121. Could define inverse:
> 
> ```text
> B ENABLES A
> ```
> 
> sometimes.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17122. But DEPENDS_ON and ENABLES are not exact logical inverses in every context.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17123. Therefore inverse relation should be declared only if semantics exact enough.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17124. Predicate properties
> 
> Could include:
> 
> ```text
> transitive
> symmetric
> antisymmetric
> functional
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17125. Example:
> 
> ```text
> PART_OF
> ```
> 
> may be transitive in many hierarchies.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17126. But beware contextual exceptions.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17127. Example physical assembly:
> 
> ```text
> screw PART_OF motor
> motor PART_OF robot
> ```
> 
> then screw PART_OF robot is reasonable.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17128. Example administrative relation may be less straightforward.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17129. Therefore logical properties can be profile-specific.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17130. Do not overformalize every predicate globally.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17131. Predicate Semantics must also define temporal behavior
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17132. Example:
> 
> ```text
> ASSIGNED_TO
> ```
> 
> is generally temporal.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17133. Person can be assigned to project from:
> 
> ```text
> T1 → T2
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17134. `IS_A` usually less temporal,
> 
> though classifications can evolve.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17135. This matters for bitemporal storage.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17136. Cardinality Constraints
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> Action ASSIGNED_TO zero or many Resources
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17137. Another domain profile may require:
> 
> ```text
> exactly one accountable owner
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17138. That requirement belongs to workflow/governance profile,
> 
> not universal predicate semantics.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17139. Thus distinguish:
> 
> ```text
> ontology constraint
> ```
> 
> from:
> 
> ```text
> application policy
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17140. Ontology says:
> 
> ```text
> what statement means
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17141. Policy says:
> 
> ```text
> what statements/configurations are permitted
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17142. Critical invariant:
> 
> ```text
> Ontology ≠ Policy.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17143. Example ontology:
> 
> ```text
> Person CAN_BE_ASSIGNED_TO Project
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17144. Policy:
> 
> ```text
> only certified reviewer may review safety result
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17145. Do not encode governance rules into fundamental taxonomy if unnecessary.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17146. Schema Registry
> 
> Stores machine-readable representations.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17147. Example schemas:
> 
> ```text
> robot-pose-v1
> claim-v1
> funding-opportunity-v2
> measurement-result-v3
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17148. Schema has:
> 
> ```text
> identifier
> version
> format
> definition
> compatibility
> status
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17149. Supported formats may include:
> 
> ```text
> JSON Schema
> Protobuf
> Avro
> Pydantic-generated schema
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17150. But semantic meaning must be external to serialization syntax.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17151. Example
> 
> JSON Schema can say:
> 
> ```text
> amount: number
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17152. Semantic profile says:
> 
> ```text
> amount represents eligible requested funding
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17153. And:
> 
> ```text
> currency mandatory
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17154. Schema Registry therefore links to Concept Registry.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17155. Field → Concept Mapping
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> temperature_c
> → concept:temperature
> → unit:celsius
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17156. This lets systems understand schema at semantic level.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17157. Semantic Schema
> 
> Can be viewed as:
> 
> ```text
> structure
> +
> concept bindings
> +
> constraints
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17158. Example:
> 
> ```yaml
> schema: measurement-v1
> 
> fields:
>   value:
>     type: number
> 
>   unit:
>     concept: core:UNIT
> 
> semantic_binding:
>   subject: measurement.subject
>   predicate: measurement.property
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17159. This enables generic tools.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17160. Example generic renderer can display measurement without domain-specific handwritten UI.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17161. Generic validator can check unit compatibility.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17162. Generic M2M gateway can reason about message.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17163. This is a major benefit of semantic schemas.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17164. Executable Concept
> 
> Теперь ключевой слой.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17165. Обычный Concept отвечает:
> 
> ```text
> What does this mean?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17166. Executable Concept additionally answers:
> 
> ```text
> How can this meaning participate in computation?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17167. Это не значит, что слово само «исполняется».
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17168. Оно связывается с:
> 
> ```text
> capability contract
> validators
> transformations
> procedures
> views
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17169. Example
> 
> Concept:
> 
> ```text
> TEMPERATURE_MEASUREMENT
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17170. Could link to:
> 
> ```text
> expected unit dimensions
> measurement schema
> verification profile
> compatible sensors
> rendering hint
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17171. Then system can automatically know:
> 
> ```text
> how to request
> validate
> display
> compare
> convert
> ```
> 
> temperature measurements.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17172. Executable Concept Manifest
> 
> ```python
> class ExecutableConceptManifest(BaseModel):
>     concept_id: UUID
> 
>     input_schema_refs: list[str]
>     output_schema_refs: list[str]
> 
>     capability_refs: list[UUID]
>     validator_refs: list[str]
>     procedure_refs: list[UUID]
> 
>     verification_profile_ref: str | None
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17173. Это application artifact/package.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17174. Не менять ontology root.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17175. Concept can remain purely descriptive
> 
> if no executable bindings exist.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17176. Therefore:
> 
> ```text
> Concept
> ⊃
> possibly executable semantic bindings
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17177. Example
> 
> Concept:
> 
> ```text
> CONTRACT_TERMINATION
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17178. It may have:
> 
> ```text
> definition
> legal context
> document templates
> workflow references
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17179. But execution should not imply:
> 
> ```text
> automatically terminate contract
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17180. Action still requires authority/governance.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17181. Critical invariant:
> 
> ```text
> Executable Concept
> ≠
> Authorized Action.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17182. Executability means:
> 
> ```text
> machine-operable semantics
> ```
> 
> not autonomous permission.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17183. Smart Concept
> 
> Можно использовать как user-facing термин для:
> 
> ```text
> Concept
> +
> schema
> +
> capability
> +
> procedures
> +
> verification
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17184. Но canonical internal name лучше оставить:
> 
> ```text
> Executable Concept Manifest
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17185. Это избегает маркетинговой неоднозначности.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17186. Example
> 
> Concept:
> 
> ```text
> GRANT_ELIGIBILITY_CHECK
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17187. Definition:
> 
> ```text
> determine whether applicant/project
> satisfies explicit eligibility constraints
> for a funding opportunity
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17188. Inputs:
> 
> ```text
> Project
> Applicant Organization
> Funding Opportunity
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17189. Output:
> 
> ```text
> YES
> NO
> UNKNOWN
> +
> constraint results
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17190. Procedure:
> 
> ```text
> extract constraints
> normalize project/applicant facts
> evaluate deterministic conditions
> identify unknowns
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17191. Verification:
> 
> ```text
> official call source required
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17192. Thus one semantic concept becomes reusable across:
> 
> ```text
> UI
> agents
> workflow
> M2M
> API
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17193. Another example
> 
> ```text
> ROBOT_OBJECT_GRASP
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17194. Inputs:
> 
> ```text
> robot
> target object
> grasp target
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17195. Preconditions:
> 
> ```text
> robot available
> target localized
> safety state valid
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17196. Side effect:
> 
> ```text
> PHYSICAL
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17197. Verification:
> 
> ```text
> force/tactile/vision evidence
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17198. Different robot implementations can satisfy same semantic contract.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17199. This creates interoperability at action level.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17200. Executable Concept = Interface
> 
> Very important analogy:
> 
> ```text
> Concept definition
> ≈ semantic interface
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17201. Provider can implement interface.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17202. Example:
> 
> ```text
> 3 different OCR systems
> ```
> 
> all implement:
> 
> ```text
> DOCUMENT_TEXT_EXTRACTION
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17203. Workflow targets Concept contract,
> 
> not vendor.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17204. This is similar to:
> 
> ```text
> interface / trait / protocol
> ```
> 
> in programming languages.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17205. But broader because includes:
> 
> ```text
> meaning
> evidence
> context
> units
> policy-relevant metadata
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17206. Semantic Interface
> 
> Could become formal term:
> 
> # Semantic Capability Interface
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17207. Example:
> 
> ```yaml
> interface:
>   concept: document_text_extraction
> 
> inputs:
>   document:
>     type: Artifact
> 
> outputs:
>   text:
>     type: Artifact
> 
> guarantees:
>   provenance_preserved: true
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17208. Implementations:
> 
> ```text
> Tesseract adapter
> Vision model
> Cloud OCR API
> Human transcription
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17209. Notice:
> 
> ```text
> human
> software
> AI
> ```
> 
> can implement same high-level capability.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17210. But execution semantics differ.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17211. This reinforces universal Resource Resolver.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17212. Semantic Interface Conformance
> 
> Provider says:
> 
> ```text
> I implement Interface X
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17213. Need verification:
> 
> ```text
> contract tests
> benchmarks
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17214. Therefore:
> 
> ```text
> implements
> ≠
> conforms
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17215. States:
> 
> ```text
> DECLARED
> TESTED
> CONFORMANT
> NONCONFORMANT
> UNKNOWN
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17216. Conformance can be version-specific.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17217. Example:
> 
> ```text
> provider conforms to v1
> ```
> 
> not necessarily v2.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17218. Interface Versioning
> 
> Semantic change types:
> 
> ```text
> PATCH
> MINOR
> MAJOR
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17219. PATCH
> 
> Clarification that does not alter valid interpretation/behavior.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17220. MINOR
> 
> Backward-compatible additions.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17221. MAJOR
> 
> Meaning/contract change incompatible with previous implementation.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17222. But semantic versioning rules must be stricter than ordinary code versioning.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17223. Example adding optional field:
> 
> ```text
> minor
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17224. Renaming label without changing identity:
> 
> ```text
> patch
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17225. Changing:
> 
> ```text
> UNKNOWN allowed
> ```
> 
> to:
> 
> ```text
> UNKNOWN treated as NO
> ```
> 
> would be:
> 
> ```text
> breaking semantic change
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17226. That must be major.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17227. Changing unit from:
> 
> ```text
> Celsius
> ```
> 
> to:
> 
> ```text
> Kelvin
> ```
> 
> without explicit conversion contract:
> 
> breaking.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17228. This illustrates why semantic compatibility requires more than schema compatibility.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17229. Semantic Diff
> 
> Need tool to compare two versions.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17230. It should detect:
> 
> ```text
> definition change
> domain/range change
> cardinality change
> unit change
> truth semantics change
> state transition change
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17231. Example report:
> 
> ```text
> v1 → v2
> 
> BREAKING:
> predicate object changed
> from Capability
> to Capability | Resource
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17232. This helps architecture review.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17233. Semantic Compatibility Matrix
> 
> For versions:
> 
> ```text
> producer v1
> consumer v1
> consumer v2
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17234. Results:
> 
> ```text
> DIRECT
> ADAPTER_REQUIRED
> INCOMPATIBLE
> UNKNOWN
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17235. This feeds M2M negotiation.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17236. Ontology Mapping
> 
> Between two external ontologies:
> 
> ```text
> Concept A ↔ Concept B
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17237. Mapping relations:
> 
> ```text
> EXACT
> EQUIVALENT_IN_CONTEXT
> BROADER
> NARROWER
> OVERLAPS
> UNRELATED
> UNKNOWN
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17238. `EXACT` should be rare.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17239. Because different standards often have subtle differences.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17240. Example
> 
> One ontology:
> 
> ```text
> Employee
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17241. Another:
> 
> ```text
> Worker
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17242. They may overlap,
> 
> but independent contractors complicate equivalence.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17243. Therefore:
> 
> ```text
> OVERLAPS
> ```
> 
> may be more accurate.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17244. Automatic mapping should create:
> 
> ```text
> Mapping Proposal
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17245. Not canonical equivalence automatically.
> 
> ---

> ```

> 
> ```text

>

>

> 
> # 17414. Example:
> 
> ```text

> IS_A

>

> 
> # 17415. Provider of laser cutting reasonably provides:
> 
> ```text

>

> 
> # 17416. Yet constraints may differ.

> 
> # 17417. So capability inheritance should preserve:

>

>

> 
> ```text

>

> ```text

> ```
>

> # 17423. Instead of creating thousands of arbitrary concept names,

> 
> # 17424. Parameterized Semantics
> 
> Interesting design.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17425. Base Concept:
> 
> ```text
> OBJECT_DETECTION
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17426. Parameters:
> 
> ```text
> target_class
> environment
> minimum_precision
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17427. Requirement:
> 
> ```yaml
> capability: object_detection
> 
> parameters:
>   target_class: forklift
>   environment: indoor
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17428. Provider contract describes supported parameter space.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17429. This avoids ontology explosion.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17430. Same for:
> 
> ```text
> TRANSLATION
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17431. Parameters:
> 
> ```text
> source_language
> target_language
> domain
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17432. Same for:
> 
> ```text
> MEASUREMENT
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17433. Parameters:
> 
> ```text
> property
> range
> precision
> unit
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17434. This is a major design principle:
> 
> ```text
> Don't encode every parameter combination
> as a new Concept.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17435. Use:
> 
> ```text
> Concept + Contract Parameters
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17436. Otherwise registry becomes combinatorial explosion.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17437. Semantic Type vs Instance Parameters
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> TEMPERATURE_MEASUREMENT
> ```
> 
> type.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 17438. Requirement:
> 
> ```text
> range = -20..150°C
> accuracy <= 0.5°C
> ```
> 
> parameters.
> 
> ---
>

> ```text

> ```
> 
> Теперь вопрос становится сложнее:
> 
> ```text

> не существует как готовый Provider.

> ```

> обычно имеет:
> 
> ```text
> tests
> failure history
> integration knowledge
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18590. Novel composition используется если:
> 
> ```text
> existing patterns insufficient
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18591. Architecture Candidate
> 
> Application object/view.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18592. Содержит:
> 
> ```text
> components
> interfaces
> capabilities
> constraints
> unknowns
> verification plan
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18593. Example:
> 
> ```yaml
> architecture_candidate:
>   target: autonomous_inspection
> 
>   components:
>     - camera-a
>     - model-b
>     - edge-node-c
> 
>   provides:
>     - defect_detection
> 
>   unknowns:
>     - line_speed_compatibility
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18594. Candidate architecture ≠ Decision.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18595. Candidate architecture ≠ working system.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18596. Это:
> 
> ```text
> design hypothesis
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18597. Эпистемически:
> 
> ```text
> HYPOTHESIS
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18598. После simulation:
> 
> ```text
> supported hypothesis
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18599. После prototype:
> 
> ```text
> evidenced architecture
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18600. После operational verification:
> 
> ```text
> verified capability package
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18601. Architecture Search Space
> 
> Если есть:
> 
> ```text
> 10 cameras
> 8 models
> 5 compute nodes
> 4 controllers
> ```
> 
> число комбинаций быстро растёт.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18602. Поэтому нельзя:
> 
> ```text
> brute-force every combination
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18603. Нужно раннее pruning.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18604. Порядок:
> 
> ```text
> hard constraints first
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18605. Например сразу исключить:
> 
> ```text
> wrong physical dimensions
> wrong protocol
> wrong jurisdiction
> insufficient latency
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18606. Только потом рассматривать:
> 
> ```text
> cost
> performance
> maintainability
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18607. Search Pipeline
> 
> ```text
> Goal
> ↓
> Requirement Graph
> ↓
> Pattern Candidates
> ↓
> Component Candidates
> ↓
> Hard Constraint Pruning
> ↓
> Interface Compatibility
> ↓
> Architecture Assembly
> ↓
> Operational Analysis
> ↓
> Verification Planning
> ↓
> Pareto Set
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18608. Очень важно
> 
> ```text
> Search ≠ Ranking.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18609. Engine может вернуть:
> 
> ```text
> multiple feasible architectures
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18610. Не обязательно объявлять одну «лучшую».
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18611. Trade-offs могут быть:
> 
> ```text
> cost
> latency
> complexity
> control
> reversibility
> vendor dependence
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18612. Architecture A:
> 
> ```text
> low cost
> cloud-dependent
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18613. Architecture B:
> 
> ```text
> higher upfront cost
> local control
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18614. Architecture C:
> 
> ```text
> hybrid
> more integration complexity
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18615. Decision belongs governance/user.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18616. Architecture Dimensions
> 
> Минимум:
> 
> ```text
> FUNCTIONAL
> TECHNICAL
> PHYSICAL
> ECONOMIC
> OPERATIONAL
> SECURITY
> VERIFICATION
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18617. FUNCTIONAL
> 
> Закрывает ли Capability requirements?
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18618. TECHNICAL
> 
> Совместимы ли:
> 
> ```text
> schemas
> protocols
> runtime
> versions
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18619. PHYSICAL
> 
> Совместимы ли:
> 
> ```text
> dimensions
> power
> location
> mechanics
> environment
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18620. ECONOMIC
> 
> ```text
> purchase
> integration
> operation
> maintenance
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18621. OPERATIONAL
> 
> ```text
> availability
> operators
> maintenance
> support
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18622. SECURITY
> 
> ```text
> trust boundary
> data locality
> privileges
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18623. VERIFICATION
> 
> Можно ли подтвердить desired capability?
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18624. Interface Graph
> 
> Компоненты соединяются через interfaces.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18625. Example:
> 
> ```text
> Camera
> → image stream
> → Vision Model
> → detection objects
> → Robot Planner
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18626. Каждый edge должен быть:
> 
> ```text
> compatible
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18627. Interface mismatch types:
> 
> ```text
> SCHEMA
> PROTOCOL
> UNIT
> TIMING
> SEMANTIC
> PHYSICAL
> AUTHORITY
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18628. Example schema mismatch
> 
> ```text
> Provider outputs BoundingBox-v1
> Consumer expects BoundingBox-v2
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18629. Resolver ищет:
> 
> ```text
> adapter
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18630. Example protocol mismatch
> 
> ```text
> Camera outputs RTSP
> Processor accepts USB camera only
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18631. Нужен:
> 
> ```text
> capture bridge
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18632. Example unit mismatch
> 
> ```text
> mm
> vs
> meters
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18633. Unit converter.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18634. Example timing mismatch
> 
> Camera:
> 
> ```text
> 5 FPS
> ```
> 
> Requirement:
> 
> ```text
> 30 FPS
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18635. Adapter не решит нехватку информации.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18636. Поэтому:
> 
> ```text
> interface bridge
> ≠
> capability upgrade
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18637. Example physical mismatch
> 
> Robot gripper payload:
> 
> ```text
> 2 kg
> ```
> 
> object:
> 
> ```text
> 5 kg
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18638. No software adapter fixes.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18639. Search must distinguish:
> 
> ```text
> bridgeable mismatch
> ```
> 
> от:
> 
> ```text
> fundamental infeasibility
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18640. Adapter Synthesis
> 
> Если direct adapter отсутствует,
> 
> можно составить chain:
> 
> ```text
> A
> → Adapter 1
> → Adapter 2
> → B
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18641. Это похоже на:
> 
> ```text
> type conversion graph
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18642. Но каждое преобразование добавляет:
> 
> ```text
> latency
> failure risk
> loss
> cost
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18643. Поэтому shortest adapter chain не всегда лучший.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18644. Особенно если один adapter:
> 
> ```text
> LOSSY
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18645. Adapter Search Constraints
> 
> ```text
> loss tolerance
> latency
> security
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18646. Example safety-control data:
> 
> ```text
> LOSSLESS_ONLY
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18647. Research exploratory data may tolerate:
> 
> ```text
> CONSERVATIVE conversion
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18648. Adapter itself must have verified capability.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18649. Unknown adapter behavior:
> 
> ```text
> integration risk
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18650. Architecture Candidate should expose adapter count.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18651. Потому что:
> 
> ```text
> many adapters
> ```
> 
> often means:
> 
> ```text
> integration fragility
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18652. Но не всегда.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18653. Standardized adapters can be reliable.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18654. Therefore count alone not score.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18655. Architectural Complexity
> 
> Useful dimensions:
> 
> ```text
> component count
> interface count
> custom code count
> external dependencies
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18656. Again not one opaque score.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18657. Custom Component Gap
> 
> If no provider/adapter exists:
> 
> ```text
> Build Gap
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18658. Example:
> 
> ```text
> need ROS→Semantic M2M translator
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18659. System can create:
> 
> ```text
> Software Development Project
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18660. Thus architecture synthesis can produce new development tasks.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18661. Search space becomes mixed:
> 
> ```text
> existing components
> +
> components that can be built
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18662. Important distinction:
> 
> ```text
> Available Architecture
> ```
> 
> vs:
> 
> ```text
> Buildable Architecture
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18663. Available:
> 
> all components currently exist.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18664. Buildable:
> 
> requires new components.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18665. Another:
> 
> ```text
> Research-dependent Architecture
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18666. Some missing capability may require:
> 
> ```text
> new research
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18667. Example:
> 
> ```text
> required tactile precision
> not demonstrated by known technology
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18668. Then synthesis must say:
> 
> ```text
> Research Gap
> ```
> 
> not pretend engineering solution exists.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18669. Therefore Candidate Readiness classes:
> 
> ```text
> AVAILABLE
> INTEGRATION_REQUIRED
> DEVELOPMENT_REQUIRED
> RESEARCH_REQUIRED
> INFEASIBLE_KNOWN
> UNKNOWN
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18670. This is extremely useful.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18671. Example:
> 
> Architecture A:
> 
> ```text
> AVAILABLE
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18672. Architecture B:
> 
> ```text
> DEVELOPMENT_REQUIRED
> ```
> 
> but lower long-term cost.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18673. Architecture C:
> 
> ```text
> RESEARCH_REQUIRED
> ```
> 
> but potentially transformative.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18674. Strategy Engine can treat these as different options.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18675. Architecture Search should integrate Technology Observatory
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18676. If component missing:
> 
> ```text
> Search GitHub
> Search papers
> Search vendors
> Search labs
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18677. Thus synthesis engine recursively invokes resolvers.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18678. Example:
> 
> ```text
> Need tactile sensing
> ↓
> Capability Resolver
> ↓
> fiber-optic sensing candidates
> commercial tactile skins
> force sensors
> research prototypes
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18679. Each candidate has different maturity.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18680. Technology maturity should be descriptive dimensions.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18681. Possible:
> 
> ```text
> prototype
> production
> research-only
> unknown
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18682. Avoid single TRL if evidence insufficient.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18683. If TRL known from authoritative context:
> 
> store Claim.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18684. Architecture Search can use minimum maturity Constraint.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18685. Example production system:
> 
> ```text
> research-only component
> ```
> 
> may be excluded.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18686. Research demonstrator:
> 
> allowed.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18687. Component Substitution
> 
> Architecture pattern can specify:
> 
> ```text
> interface
> ```
> 
> not specific vendor.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18688. Therefore multiple substitutions possible.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18689. Example:
> 
> ```text
> Vision Model Interface
> ```
> 
> providers:
> 
> ```text
> Local Model A
> Cloud API B
> Edge Model C
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18690. Architecture variant generated for each meaningful binding.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18691. But avoid combinatorial explosion.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18692. Dominance pruning
> 
> If Candidate X is:
> 
> ```text
> worse or equal on all relevant dimensions
> ```
> 
> than Y,
> 
> X can be removed from Pareto set.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18693. But only for comparable quantified/ordered dimensions.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18694. Do not apply subjective hidden preference.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18695. Pareto frontier preserves trade-offs.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18696. Architecture A may dominate B if:
> 
> ```text
> lower cost
> lower latency
> same capability
> same risk constraints
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18697. Then B has no obvious advantage.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18698. Remove B from default view,
> 
> but retain search trace if useful.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18699. Architecture Search Algorithm
> 
> MVP can be:
> 
> ```text
> pattern matching
> +
> constraint filtering
> +
> bounded combinatorial search
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18700. No need for advanced generative architecture search initially.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18701. Later methods may include:
> 
> ```text
> constraint programming
> SAT/SMT
> mixed integer optimization
> graph search
> evolutionary search
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18702. Different subproblems use different solvers.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18703. Example deterministic physical allocation:
> 
> ```text
> constraint solver
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18704. Novel architecture ideation:
> 
> ```text
> LLM
> ```
> 
> can propose patterns.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18705. But LLM-generated architecture remains:
> 
> ```text
> Candidate Hypothesis
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18706. It must pass deterministic checks.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18707. Important:
> 
> ```text
> LLM proposes.
> Solver validates.
> Evidence verifies.
> Governance decides.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18708. This is a strong general architecture principle.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18709. Architecture Generator Agents
> 
> Possible roles:
> 
> ```text
> Requirement Analyst
> Pattern Scout
> Component Scout
> Integrator
> Safety Reviewer
> Verifier
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18710. Multi-agent blackboard receives:
> 
> ```text
> Requirements
> Candidates
> Conflicts
> Unknowns
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18711. Agents do not chat endlessly.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18712. They publish:
> 
> ```text
> Architecture Proposals
> Compatibility Claims
> Evidence
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18713. Semantic State Diff updates synthesis graph.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18714. Requirement Analyst
> 
> Produces:
> 
> ```text
> Requirement Graph
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18715. Pattern Scout
> 
> Searches:
> 
> ```text
> known architecture patterns
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18716. Component Scout
> 
> Searches:
> 
> ```text
> repos
> products
> services
> labs
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18717. Integrator
> 
> Checks:
> 
> ```text
> interfaces
> adapters
> deployment
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18718. Safety Reviewer
> 
> Checks:
> 
> ```text
> side effects
> failure modes
> constraints
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18719. Verifier
> 
> Builds:
> 
> ```text
> verification plan
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18720. Separation helps reduce confirmation bias.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18721. Architecture Critic Agent
> 
> Could actively search for:
> 
> ```text
> hidden assumptions
> single points of failure
> unsupported claims
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18722. Very useful.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18723. Candidate should not be accepted merely because Generator proposed it.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18724. Critic outputs:
> 
> ```text
> Counterclaims
> Risks
> Questions
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18725. Example:
> 
> ```text
> Architecture assumes network connectivity
> but mobile node may be offline.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18726. Creates:
> 
> ```text
> Constraint/Gap
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18727. Failure Mode Analysis
> 
> Architecture synthesis should explicitly ask:
> 
> ```text
> How can this architecture fail?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18728. For each component/interface:
> 
> ```text
> failure
> effect
> detection
> recovery
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18729. This resembles FMEA.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18730. But system can start simple.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18731. Failure Mode object can be:
> 
> ```text
> Claim/Concept
> ```
> 
> plus relations.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18732. Example:
> 
> ```text
> Camera failure
> AFFECTS
> Object Detection
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18733. Architecture resilience depends on:
> 
> ```text
> redundancy
> fallback
> detectability
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18734. Redundancy Synthesis
> 
> If requirement says:
> 
> ```text
> no single point of failure
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18735. Search must include:
> 
> ```text
> alternative provider paths
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18736. Example:
> 
> ```text
> Primary Camera
> +
> Backup Camera
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18737. But if both depend on:
> 
> ```text
> same power supply
> ```
> 
> not independent.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18738. Failure-domain analysis required.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18739. Architecture Graph should include dependency graph down to:
> 
> ```text
> power
> network
> software
> data
> ```
> 
> where relevant.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18740. Dependency depth is risk-based.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18741. No need model every transistor.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18742. But critical shared dependencies matter.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18743. Common-Cause Failure Detection
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> Model A
> Model B
> ```
> 
> both served by same cloud provider.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18744. Superficially two providers,
> 
> operationally one failure domain.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18745. System should detect.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18746. Another:
> 
> ```text
> two sensors
> ```
> 
> same communication bus.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18747. Same principle.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18748. Resilience Option
> 
> Architecture variant may deliberately trade:
> 
> ```text
> higher cost
> ```
> 
> for:
> 
> ```text
> independent redundancy
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18749. User sees trade-off.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18750. Security Architecture Synthesis
> 
> Target system requires:
> 
> ```text
> data confidentiality
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18751. Candidate components must fit trust boundaries.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18752. Architecture can include:
> 
> ```text
> local processing
> gateway
> encryption
> sandbox
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18753. Security should not be afterthought.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18754. Threat Model
> 
> Could be generated from:
> 
> ```text
> assets
> trust boundaries
> interfaces
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18755. Example threats:
> 
> ```text
> data exfiltration
> spoofed sensor
> unauthorized command
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18756. Mitigation requirements feed back into synthesis.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18757. Example:
> 
> ```text
> unauthorized command
> ```
> 
> requires:
> 
> ```text
> authenticated gateway
> authorization
> command expiry
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18758. Architecture Candidate without those:
> 
> ```text
> infeasible under security constraints
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18759. Safety Architecture Synthesis
> 
> Physical systems need:
> 
> ```text
> hazard analysis
> interlocks
> fail-safe states
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18760. Semantic AI layer cannot replace certified/local safety mechanisms.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18761. Therefore any architecture using actuator should require:
> 
> ```text
> local safety controller
> ```
> 
> when domain profile demands.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18762. Example:
> 
> ```text
> LLM
> → robot motor
> ```
> 
> direct architecture:
> 
> ```text
> REJECTED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18763. Valid pattern:
> 
> ```text
> LLM high-level intent
> ↓
> validated semantic action
> ↓
> safety controller
> ↓
> motion controller
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18764. This can be encoded as architecture invariant.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18765. Architecture Rule Registry
> 
> Rules such as:
> 
> ```text
> physical actuator
> REQUIRES
> local safety controller
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18766. Domain profile supplies.

> → Wi-Fi
> → gateway
> → cloud

>

> recurring

> procurement

> integrator
> domain expert

> ```text

> +
> Processes
> +
> Technology

> # 18813. Architecture Search should support all three.

> +

> # 18816. This can be more feasible.

> # 18817. Human-in-the-loop is not failure of automation.

> # 18818. It is legitimate architecture pattern.

> 
> ```text

> ↓
> Human Review
> ↓
> Verified Artifact

> # 18820. Required for some domains.

> ↓
> uncertain case

> Human Resolver

>

> # 18828. Architecture Search and Reversibility
> 
> Strategy Engine values reversible steps.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18829. Candidate may be staged:
> 
> ```text
> Pilot
> ↓
> Partial Deployment
> ↓
> Scale
> ```
>

> 
> # 18830. Instead of one irreversible rollout.

> ---
> 
> # 18831. System can generate:
> 
> ```text
> Staged Architecture Path

> 
> ---
> 
> # 18832. Example:
> 
> Stage 1:
> 
> ```text
> cloud API

> 
> to validate workflow.

> ---
> 
> # 18833. Stage 2:
> 
> ```text
> local model
> ```
> 
> after usage proven.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18834. Stage 3:
>

> specialized hardware

> 
> after scale.

> 
> # 18835. This reduces upfront commitment.

> 
> # 18836. Architecture is therefore not only static graph

> ```text
> evolution path

> Transition 1

> Transition 2

> Target Architecture

> # 18838. Each transition is Project/Program.

> incremental migration

> # 18841. This is important selection dimension.

>

> 
> Candidate that preserves future options may be strategically useful.

> 
> # 18843. Example standard interface allows swapping providers.

> ---
> 
> # 18844. Proprietary tight coupling may reduce future options.

> 
> # 18845. System can expose:

> # 18846. But avoid subjective vendor lock-in score.

> # 18847. Instead show:

> # 18848. Concrete dimensions.

> ---
>

>

> # 18857. Architecture Synthesis and Standards
> 
> Registry supplies:
> 
> ```text
> interfaces
> profiles
> constraints
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18858. Thus synthesis is effectively:
> 
> ```text
> semantic type-directed assembly
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18859. Similar to dependency injection,

> but over heterogeneous physical/digital resources.

> 
> # 18860. This is a major conceptual result.

> # 18861. Type-Directed Architecture Search
> 
> Target output type:
> 
> ```text
> Verified Defect Decision
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18862. Find capability producing it.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18863. Its input requires:
> 
> ```text
> Image Artifact
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18864. Find capability producing Image Artifact.
>

> 
> # 18865. Continue backwards.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18866. This resembles:
> 
> ```text
> program synthesis
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18867. Backward Chaining
> 
> ```text
> Desired Output
> ↓
> Capability producing output
> ↓
> Required Inputs
> ↓
> Capabilities producing inputs
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18868. Good for goal-directed synthesis.

> ---
> 
> # 18869. Forward Chaining
> 
> From available resources:
> 
> ```text
> What capabilities can we construct?
> ```

> ---
> 
> # 18870. Useful for:
> 
> ```text
> opportunity discovery
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18871. Example inventory:
> 
> ```text
> camera
> GPU
> robot arm
> fiber sensor
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18872. System asks:
> 
> ```text
> What higher-order capabilities
> can be composed from these?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18873. This is particularly interesting.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18874. Capability Emergence Discovery
> 
> Resources currently idle may combine into:
> 
> ```text
> new capability
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18875. Example:
> 
> ```text
> camera
> +
> fiber tactile sensor
> +
> robot arm
> ```
> 
> could enable:
> 
> ```text
> delicate manipulation research platform
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18876. This is proactive technological awareness.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18877. But generated opportunity remains:
> 
> ```text
> Hypothesis
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18878. Need evidence/validation.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18879. Architecture Synthesis therefore supports two modes:
> 
> ```text
> GOAL_DRIVEN
> OPPORTUNITY_DRIVEN
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18880. GOAL_DRIVEN:
> 
> ```text
> Need X.
> How build X?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18881. OPPORTUNITY_DRIVEN:
> 
> ```text
> We have A+B+C.
> What useful new capability can emerge?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18882. This second mode is very important for Technopark.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18883. Technopark often owns:
> 
> ```text
> fragmented capabilities
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18884. Value comes from combining them.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18885. System can discover:
> 
> ```text
> latent technological combinations
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18886. Example:
> 
> Lab A:
> 
> ```text
> microscope
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18887. Team B:
> 
> ```text
> vision model
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18888. Repo C:
> 
> ```text
> automated stage control
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18889. Together:
> 
> ```text
> automated microscopy platform
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18890. No single organization may have recognized combination.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18891. This is a central Virtual Technopark function.
> 
> ---
>

> 
> Even more interesting:
> 
> ```text
> technology from domain A
> solves problem in domain B

> 
> ---
> 
> # 18893. Example:
> 
> ```text
> fiber optic sensing
> ```
> 
> from structural monitoring
> 
> applied to:
> 
> ```text
> robot tactile sensing
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18894. This is exactly type of cross-domain discovery user has been exploring.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18895. Synthesis Engine can support:
> 
> ```text
> analogical capability mapping
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18896. It asks:
> 
> ```text
> What physical/informational property
> does technology provide?

> 
> ---
> 
> # 18897. Example fiber sensor provides:
> 
> ```text
> distributed deformation sensing
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18898. Robot requires:
> 
> ```text
> distributed contact/deformation sensing

> ---
> 
> # 18899. Semantic overlap appears.

> ---
> 
> # 18900. Technology transfer hypothesis:
> 
> ```text
> fiber sensing may satisfy
> robot tactile requirement

> 
> ---
> 
> # 18901. This remains HYPOTHESIS.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18902. Then:
> 
> ```text
> research experiment
> ```
> 
> needed.

> ---
> 
> # 18903. This is an excellent use of Capability abstractions.

> 
> # 18904. Analogical Search
> 
> Instead of keywords:
> 
> ```text
> robot tactile sensor
> ```
> 
> search:
> 
> ```text
> distributed deformation sensing
> flexible pressure detection
> strain localization
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18905. Finds technologies from:
> 
> ```text
> civil engineering
> aerospace
> medical
> textiles
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18906. This greatly expands technology scouting.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18907. Functional Abstraction
> 
> Key rule:
> 
> ```text
> Search by function,
> not only product category.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18908. Example requirement:
> 
> ```text
> detect local pressure over flexible surface
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18909. Candidate technologies:
> 
> ```text
> capacitive skin
> fiber optics
> piezoresistive textile
> fluidic sensor
> vision deformation
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18910. Different industries.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18911. This is technology transfer engine.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18912. Property-Based Search
> 
> Resources can be indexed by:
> 
> ```text
> physical principle
> input
> output
> operational envelope
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18913. Example sensor:
> 
> ```text
> input: deformation
> output: optical signal
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18914. Another:
> 
> ```text
> input: pressure
> output: resistance change
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18915. Target requirement can be matched at abstract property level.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18916. This is deeper than semantic labels.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18917. Function–Behavior–Structure
> 
> Classical engineering framework fits.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18918. Represent:
> 
> ```text
> FUNCTION
> BEHAVIOR
> STRUCTURE
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18919. Function:
> 
> ```text
> what system must achieve
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18920. Behavior:
> 
> ```text
> physical/computational mechanism
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18921. Structure:
> 
> ```text
> components and connections
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18922. Example:
> 
> Function:
> 
> ```text
> sense contact
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18923. Behavior:
> 
> ```text
> strain modifies optical transmission
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18924. Structure:
> 
> ```text
> fiber + interrogator + signal processor
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18925. This provides powerful cross-domain abstraction.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18926. Could add as application-level engineering model
> 
> without changing root ontology.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18927. Function is Concept/Capability.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18928. Behavior is:
> 
> ```text
> Concept + Claims/Procedure
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18929. Structure is:
> 
> ```text
> Resource/Relation graph
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18930. Excellent fit.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18931. Technology Principle Registry
> 
> Could catalog:
> 
> ```text
> optical interference
> capacitive sensing
> ultrasound
> transformers
> diffusion models
> graph search
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18932. These are:
> 
> ```text
> Concepts
> ```
>

> 
> # 18933. Resource implementation links:
> 
> ```text
> USES physical/computational principle
> ```
>

> 
> # 18934. Search can jump between implementations sharing principle.

> ---
> 
> # 18935. Example:
>

>

> 
> ```text
> metrology

> # 18936. This encourages scientific technology transfer.

> 
> # 18937. Contradiction Detection in Architecture
> 
> Candidate may contain requirements that conflict.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18938. Example:
> 
> ```text
> must be fully offline
> ```
> 
> and:
> 
> ```text
> must use cloud-only API
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18939. Correct result:
> 
> ```text
> UNSATISFIABLE REQUIREMENT SET
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18940. Do not search forever.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18941. Constraint Solver identifies:
> 
> ```text
> minimal conflict set
> ```
> 
> if possible.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18942. Example:
> 
> ```text
> Constraint A
> +
> Constraint F
> ```
> 
> cause impossibility.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18943. Then system can propose:
> 
> ```text
> relax A
> or
> replace cloud-only component
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18944. But relaxing requirement requires Decision.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18945. System never silently changes Goal.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18946. Critical invariant:
> 
> ```text
> Infeasible Requirements
> ≠
> Permission to weaken Requirements.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18947. Requirement Negotiation
> 
> System can present:
> 
> ```text
> If latency requirement changes
> from 50 ms to 200 ms,
> three additional architectures become feasible.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18948. Very valuable for engineering.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18949. This is:
> 
> # Constraint Sensitivity Analysis
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18950. It shows:
> 
> ```text
> which requirements drive architecture
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18951. Example:
> 
> ```text
> local-only processing
> ```
> 
> eliminates 80% providers.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18952. Example:
> 
> ```text
> precision <= 1 micron
> ```
> 
> requires specialized lab.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18953. This supports human design decisions.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18954. Requirement Criticality
> 
> Can derive:
> 
> ```text
> how many architecture candidates depend on constraint
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18955. But does not mean constraint is unimportant.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18956. It indicates:
> 
> ```text
> design leverage
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18957. Requirement Sensitivity View
> 
> Shows:
> 
> ```text
> constraint
> current value
> candidate impact
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18958. Excellent for negotiation.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18959. Architecture Unknowns
> 
> Every Candidate should explicitly list:
> 
> ```text
> unknown compatibility
> unknown cost
> unknown performance
> unknown availability
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18960. Unknowns become:
> 
> ```text
> Evidence Acquisition Tasks
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18961. Example:
> 
> ```text
> Does camera driver work on ARM64?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18962. Options:
> 
> ```text
> read docs
> test device
> search issues
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18963. Evidence planner chooses.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18964. Thus architecture synthesis is iterative.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18965. Loop:
> 
> ```text
> Generate Candidate
> ↓
> Find Unknowns
> ↓
> Acquire Evidence
> ↓
> Refine Candidate

> 
> # 18966. This is far more realistic than one-shot generation.

> 
> # 18967. Architecture Confidence
> 
> Do not use one global confidence number.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18968. Better:
> 
> ```text
> Functional completeness
> Interface verification
> Performance evidence
> Cost certainty
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18969. Candidate may be:
> 
> ```text
> functionally strong
> but economically uncertain
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18970. Another:
> 
> ```text
> fully costed
> but performance unverified
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18971. This multidimensional view supports decisions.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18972. Verification-by-Construction
> 
> Some properties can be guaranteed structurally.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18973. Example:
> 
> ```text
> all outputs typed
> ```
> 
> because compiler enforces.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18974. But performance cannot be guaranteed by schema.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18975. Needs benchmark.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18976. Distinguish:
> 
> ```text
> STATICALLY_VERIFIED
> RUNTIME_VERIFIED
> EXPERIMENTALLY_VERIFIED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18977. Example:
> 
> Schema compatibility:
> 
> ```text
> STATIC
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18978. Actual throughput:
> 
> ```text
> RUNTIME/EXPERIMENT
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 18979. Physical safety:
> 
> often requires multiple assurance mechanisms.

> # 19483. Technology Transfer Hypothesis должна включать:
> 
> ```text
> Source Domain
> Source Capability
> Target Domain
> Target Requirement
> Shared Functional Principle
> Unknowns
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19484. Example
> 
> ```yaml
> source_domain: structural_monitoring
> source_capability: distributed_strain_sensing
> 
> target_domain: robotics
> target_requirement: tactile_surface_sensing
> 
> shared_function:
>   detect_local_deformation
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19485. И обязательно:
> 
> ```text
> why transfer might fail
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19486. Example unknowns:
> 
> ```text
> latency
> surface curvature
> sensor fragility
> sampling rate
> cost
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19487. То есть system не говорит:
> 
> ```text
> "Это решение."
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19488. Она говорит:
> 
> ```text
> "Это проверяемая аналогия."
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19489. Innovation Hypothesis как application object
> 
> Новый root не нужен.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19490. Можно представить как:
> 
> ```text
> CLAIM(type=HYPOTHESIS)
> ```
> 
> +
> 
> ```text
> PROJECT candidate
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19491. Example Claim
> 
> ```text
> Combining Capability A and B
> may satisfy Requirement C
> under Context D.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19492. Opportunity Engine materializes view:
> 
> ```text
> Innovation Hypothesis
> ```
> 
> над Claims/Resources/Projects/Contexts.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19493. Hypothesis lifecycle
> 
> ```text
> DETECTED
> FORMULATED
> SCREENED
> INVESTIGATING
> SUPPORTED
> REFUTED
> ARCHIVED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19494. `DETECTED`
> 
> Raw structural signal.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19495. `FORMULATED`
> 
> Machine-readable hypothesis exists.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19496. `SCREENED`
> 
> Obvious contradictions/duplicates checked.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19497. `INVESTIGATING`
> 
> Evidence acquisition started.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19498. `SUPPORTED`
> 
> Some evidence supports further action.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19499. `REFUTED`
> 
> Evidence materially contradicts hypothesis.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19500. `ARCHIVED`
> 
> Not currently pursued.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19501. `SUPPORTED` still does not mean:
> 
> ```text
> proven commercial success
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19502. It means:
> 
> ```text
> enough evidence exists
> to justify next stage
> ```
> 
> according to context.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19503. Opportunity Detection Source Types
> 
> ```text
> GAP_PATTERN
> DEMAND_PATTERN
> SURPLUS_PATTERN
> EMERGING_TECH
> RESEARCH_RESULT
> COST_SHIFT
> STANDARD_CHANGE
> FAILURE_PATTERN
> CROSS_DOMAIN_ANALOGY
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19504. GAP_PATTERN
> 
> Repeated Capability Gap.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19505. Example
> 
> Across 27 projects:
> 
> ```text
> ARM64-compatible OCR
> ```
> 
> repeatedly missing.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19506. Hypothesis:
> 
> ```text
> develop standardized ARM64 OCR capability package
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19507. DEMAND_PATTERN
> 
> Repeated Requirement from external market.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19508. Example
> 
> HN hiring posts repeatedly request:
> 
> ```text
> Rust
> WASM
> AI inference
> ```
> 
> combination.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19509. Potential hypotheses:
> 
> ```text
> training program
> shared toolkit
> specialized consulting capability
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19510. Engine should not automatically decide which business model is correct.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19511. SURPLUS_PATTERN
> 
> Repeated underused capacity.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19512. Example:
> 
> ```text
> GPU cluster 40% idle
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19513. Opportunity:
> 
> ```text
> shared compute service
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19514. But must check:
> 
> ```text
> energy cost
> security
> licensing
> operator burden
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19515. EMERGING_TECH
> 
> New Resource/Capability appears.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19516. Example:
> 
> ```text
> new compact vision model
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19517. Engine asks:
> 
> ```text
> Which existing gaps
> could this new capability reduce?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19518. This is reverse matching.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19519. Existing architecture:
> 
> ```text
> Gap → Provider
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19520. Opportunity engine additionally:
> 
> ```text
> New Provider → Relevant Gaps
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19521. RESEARCH_RESULT
> 
> New scientific result suggests:
> 
> ```text
> new behavior
> new method
> new material
> new algorithm
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19522. Engine searches:
> 
> ```text
> Where could this behavior be useful?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19523. Example
> 
> Research paper reports:
> 
> ```text
> new flexible optical pressure sensor
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19524. Candidate domains:
> 
> ```text
> robotics
> prosthetics
> medical monitoring
> industrial surfaces
> wearables
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19525. But paper Claim must first be extracted with context.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19526. Example limitations:
> 
> ```text
> laboratory prototype
> low durability
> small sample
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19527. Technology opportunity remains:
> 
> ```text
> research transfer hypothesis
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19528. COST_SHIFT
> 
> Capability existed before,
> 
> but economics changed.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19529. Example:
> 
> ```text
> inference cost ↓ 90%
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19530. Previously infeasible workflows may become feasible.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19531. Opportunity Engine should reevaluate:
> 
> ```text
> archived architecture candidates
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19532. Very important.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19533. Innovation sometimes comes from:
> 
> ```text
> old idea
> +
> new economics
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19534. STANDARD_CHANGE
> 
> New interoperability standard appears.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19535. It may reduce integration cost.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19536. Example:
> 
> ```text
> common machine interface
> ```
> 
> makes previously fragmented equipment composable.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19537. Opportunity:
> 
> ```text
> cross-vendor manufacturing platform
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19538. FAILURE_PATTERN
> 
> Repeated failures can reveal opportunity.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19539. Example:
> 
> ```text
> cloud dependency repeatedly causes downtime
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19540. Hypothesis:
> 
> ```text
> local fallback architecture package
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19541. Failure pattern is often stronger signal than marketing demand.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19542. CROSS_DOMAIN_ANALOGY
> 
> Most generative class.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19543. It needs:
> 
> ```text
> function
> behavior
> constraints
> ```
> 
> comparison.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19544. Technology Representation
> 
> Each technology Resource can be represented as:
> 
> ```text
> Functions
> Inputs
> Outputs
> Operating Envelope
> Underlying Principles
> Required Infrastructure
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19545. Example
> 
> ```text
> Fiber Optic Sensor
> ```
> 
> Functions:
> 
> ```text
> measure strain
> detect deformation
> localize disturbance
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19546. Inputs:
> 
> ```text
> mechanical deformation
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19547. Outputs:
> 
> ```text
> optical signal
> processed spatial measurement
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19548. Principle:
> 
> ```text
> optical modulation / scattering / interference
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19549. Operating envelope:
> 
> ```text
> bend radius
> length
> sampling rate
> temperature range
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19550. Target Requirement represented similarly.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19551. Then matching can operate on:
> 
> ```text
> functional signatures
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19552. Functional Signature
> 
> Possible:
> 
> ```yaml
> function:
>   verb: detect
>   object: deformation
>   distribution: spatial
>   modality: physical
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19553. Another target:
> 
> ```yaml
> function:
>   verb: detect
>   object: contact
>   distribution: surface
>   modality: physical
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19554. Mapper detects:
> 
> ```text
> deformation
> may be proxy for contact

> ---
> 
> # 19555. That bridge itself becomes:
> 
> ```text
> Hypothesis
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19556. Very important:
> 
> ```text
> proxy relationship
> ≠
> equivalence

> 
> ---
> 
> # 19557. Example:
> 
> ```text
> strain

> 
> can indicate contact,
> 
> but also temperature or structural load.

> ---
> 
> # 19558. Therefore contextual discrimination required.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19559. Opportunity Engine should reason through:
> 
> ```text
> causal mechanism
> ```
> 
> where possible.

> ---
> 
> # 19560. Example chain:
> 
> ```text
> Contact
> → Surface deformation
> → Fiber strain
> → Optical change
> → Sensor signal
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19561. This creates mechanistic plausibility.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19562. Stronger than simple embedding similarity.
>

>

> 
> ```text
> Target Need
> ↓
> Abstract Function
> ↓
> Relevant Behaviors
> ↓
> Search Principles
> ↓
> Find Implementations
> ↓
> Check Operating Envelope
> ↓
> Generate Transfer Hypothesis
> ```

> 
> # 19576. But scientific Principle alone insufficient.

> # 19580. Opportunity Quality Dimensions
> 
> No global innovation score.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19581. Better expose:
> 
> ```text
> Novelty
> Problem Evidence
> Technical Plausibility
> Resource Availability
> Evidence Gaps
> Implementation Burden
> Strategic Fit

> 
> ---
> 
> # 19582. `Novelty`
> 
> Descriptive:
> 
> ```text
> known internally?
> known externally?
> combination uncommon?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19583. But novelty itself does not create value.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19584. `Problem Evidence`
> 
> How strong is evidence that problem exists?
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19585. Example:
> 
> ```text
> 1 anecdote
> ```
> 
> vs:
> 
> ```text
> same gap across 200 projects
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19586. `Technical Plausibility`
> 
> Based on:
> 
> ```text
> mechanism
> existing evidence
> compatible envelopes
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19587. `Resource Availability`
> 
> Can needed pieces be accessed?
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19588. `Evidence Gaps`
> 
> What is unknown?
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19589. `Implementation Burden`
> 
> How much:
> 
> ```text
> build
> integration
> regulatory
> training
> ```
> 
> required.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19590. `Strategic Fit`
> 
> Does hypothesis align with current mission?

> ---
> 
> # 19591. Keep dimensions separate.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19592. Opportunity without strategic fit can still be archived for another organization.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19593. Example:
> 
> ```text
> excellent medical-device opportunity
> ```
> 
> but current program focuses:
> 
> ```text
> industrial robotics
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19594. System should not discard globally.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19595. It can mark:
> 
> ```text
> outside current portfolio
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19596. Federation may route to partner organization.

> 
> ```text

> investors

>

> 
> # 19598. But:

> ```text

> # 19600. Opportunity Deduplication
>

> customer problem
> GitHub trend

> 
> ```text
> one hypothesis
> +
> multiple supporting signals

> # 19603. But similar ideas may differ in:

> target market

> 
> # 19604. Therefore dedup:

> solution space

> drones

>

> 
> ```text

> ```

> 
> # 19612. Horizontal:
>

> shared capability used across many domains

> # 19613. Example:
>

> # 19661. Human can inspect.

> 
> # 19662. Technology Transfer Search
> 
> Pipeline:
> 
> ```text
> Target Requirement
> ↓
> Abstract Function
> ↓
> Search Function Registry
> ↓
> Candidate Domains
> ↓
> Candidate Technologies
> ↓
> Mechanism Mapping
> ↓
> Constraint Screening
> ↓
> Transfer Hypothesis
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19663. Alternative reverse pipeline:
> 
> ```text
> Emerging Technology
> ↓
> Extract Functions
> ↓
> Search Existing Gaps
> ↓
> Generate Target Domains
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19664. Both needed.
>

> 
> # 19665. Opportunity Graph
> 
> Nodes:
> 
> ```text
> Problems
> Capabilities
> Technologies
> Resources
> Domains
> Hypotheses
> Evidence
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19666. Relations:
> 
> ```text
> ADDRESSES
> MAY_ENABLE
> ANALOGOUS_TO
> SUPPORTED_BY
> BLOCKED_BY
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19667. Use existing canonical predicates where possible.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19668. Namespaced predicates:
> 
> ```text
> innovation:MAY_ENABLE
> innovation:ANALOGOUS_TO
> ```
> 
> could be justified.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19669. But do not promote speculative relation into `ENABLES`.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19670. Important semantic distinction:
> 
> ```text
> MAY_ENABLE
> ```
> 
> is hypothetical.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19671. `ENABLES`
> 
> should require stronger evidence.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19672. Opportunity Graph is inherently epistemic.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19673. Every edge needs:
> 
> ```text
> Claim type
> provenance
> confidence/verification
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19674. Innovation Signal
> 
> Could be application object:
> 
> ```yaml
> signal:
>   type: repeated_gap
>   subject: arm64_ocr
>   observations: 27
>   period: ...
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19675. Signal ≠ hypothesis.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19676. Signal says:
> 
> ```text
> something repeatedly happened
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19677. Hypothesis says:
> 
> ```text
> a response may create value
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19678. Important separation.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19679. Signal Aggregation
> 
> Examples:
> 
> ```text
> count
> trend
> recurrence
> co-occurrence
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19680. But beware:
> 
> ```text
> frequency ≠ importance
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19681. Rare problem can be critical.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19682. Example:
> 
> ```text
> one catastrophic safety failure
> ```
> 
> may deserve more attention than:
> 
> ```text
> 100 minor UI complaints
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19683. Therefore Opportunity Engine uses multiple dimensions.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19684. Signal Severity
> 
> Can be contextual:
> 
> ```text
> safety
> cost
> delay
> strategic
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19685. Again no universal global score.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19686. Opportunity Trigger
> 
> Possible rules:
> 
> ```text
> Repeated Gap
> +
> Available Solution Candidate
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19687. Another:
> 
> ```text
> New Technology
> +
> Matching Unsatisfied Requirement
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19688. Another:
> 
> ```text
> Underused Resource
> +
> External Demand
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19689. Another:
> 
> ```text
> Repeated Custom Adapters
> +
> Common Interface Pattern
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19690. Another:
> 
> ```text
> Recurring Failure
> +
> Known Alternative Architecture
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19691. Another:
> 
> ```text
> New Scientific Principle
> +
> Cross-domain functional match
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19692. These triggers can be implemented as:
> 
> ```text
> rules
> +
> graph queries
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19693. LLM role
> 
> Useful for:
> 
> ```text
> analogies
> functional abstraction
> hypothesis wording
> ```
>

> 
> # 19694. Deterministic graph/rule engine handles:
> 
> ```text
> counts
> constraints
> known relations
> duplication
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19695. Same principle:
> 
> ```text
> LLM proposes
> structured engine checks
> ```
>

> 
> # 19696. Opportunity Generator Agent
> 
> Inputs:
> 
> ```text
> signals
> gaps
> new capabilities
> patterns
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19697. Output:
> 
> ```text
> Hypothesis
> Mechanism
> Required Conditions
> Unknowns
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19698. Opportunity Critic Agent
> 
> Looks for:
> 
> ```text
> obvious prior art
> wrong analogy
> hidden constraints
> lack of demand
> ```
>

>

> 
> Searches:
> 
> ```text
> papers
> GitHub
> products
> labs
> patents if available
> ```
>

> 
> # 19700. Market/Demand Scout
> 
> Searches:
> 
> ```text
> jobs
> project requests
> procurement

> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19701. Research Scout
> 
> Searches:
> 
> ```text
> scientific feasibility
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 19702. Economic Scout
> 
> Checks:
> 
> ```text
> cost drivers
> substitution economics

>

> 
> # 19703. Standards Scout
> 
> Checks:
> 
> ```text
> interoperability barriers
> ```

> 
> # 19704. Human/Domain Expert role remains essential for:
> 
> ```text
> context
> priority

>
