> 
> # 22063. Ecosystem Trust
> 
> Can emerge from:
> 
> ```text
> verified contracts
> evidence
> past interactions
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22064. But trust is contextual.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22065. A provider reliable for:
> 
> ```text
> software hosting

> 
> does not imply:
> 
> ```text
> laboratory calibration.
> ```

> 
> # 22066. Therefore no universal trust score.

> ---
> 
> # 22067. Network Trust Edge
> 
> Could represent:
> 
> ```text
> scope
> evidence
> expiry
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22068. Example:
> 
> ```text
> Organization A accepts B's calibration certificates
> for profile P.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22069. This is specific interoperability trust.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22070. Federation Trust
> 
> Node can accept:
> 
> ```text
> identity
> claims
> evidence
> ```
> 
> at different levels.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22071. Example:
> 
> ```text
> accept B identity assertions
> but independently verify technical claims.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22072. Trust ≠ Truth.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22073. Signed Data ≠ Correct Data.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22074. Existing federation invariant preserved.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22075. Ecosystem Governance Boundaries
> 
> Different clusters can have:
> 
> ```text
> different policies
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22076. Federation should not require:
> 
> ```text
> one central governance system.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22077. Instead:
> 
> ```text
> interoperable governance boundaries.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22078. Example
> 
> Lab network A permits:
> 
> ```text
> automatic booking
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22079. Lab B requires:
> 
> ```text
> manual approval.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22080. Shared protocol can support both.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22081. Ecosystem Evolution therefore occurs under:
> 
> ```text
> heterogeneous policies.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22082. Local autonomy must remain explicit.
>

> 
> # 22083. Network Formation
> 
> New link can form when:
> 
> ```text
> Demand
> matches
> Supply
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22084. But actual collaboration requires:
> 
> ```text
> agreement/commitment.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22085. So distinguish:
> 
> ```text
> POTENTIAL_EDGE
> ```
> 
> from:
> 
> ```text
> ACTIVE_EDGE
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22086. Potential edge:
> 
> ```text
> semantic match exists.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22087. Active edge:
> 
> ```text
> actual relation/event exists.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22088. This prevents:
> 
> ```text
> imaginary network inflation.
> ```
> 
> ---
>

> 
> Set of potential compatible links.

> ---
> 
> # 22090. Actual Network
> 
> Observed/committed relationships.

> 
> # 22091. Difference is useful.

> ---
>

> 
> Two labs are technically complementary.

> ---
> 
> # 22093. But:
> 
> ```text
> no agreement
> no communication

>

> 
> # 22094. Latent collaboration only.

> 
> # 22095. Opportunity:
> 
> ```text
> possible consortium.
> ```
>

> # 22097. This affects feasibility.

> ---
> 
> # 22502. CONSTRAINT simulation
> 
> Используется для:
> 
> ```text
> scheduling
> allocation
> routing
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22503. SYSTEM_DYNAMICS
> 
> Полезна для:
> 
> ```text
> slow feedback loops
> stocks
> flows
> capacity accumulation
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22504. Example:
> 
> ```text
> Training
> ↓
> More Providers
> ↓
> More Capacity
> ↓
> More Projects
> ↓
> More Training Demand
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22505. PHYSICS simulation
> 
> Для:
> 
> ```text
> robot
> mechanics
> thermal
> fluid
> electrical
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22506. Innovation OS не должен сам реализовывать полноценный physics engine.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22507. Он вызывает:
> 
> ```text
> external simulation capability.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22508. MONTE_CARLO
> 
> Используется когда:
> 
> ```text
> input uncertainty
> ```
> 
> представима диапазонами/distributions.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22509. Example:
> 
> ```text
> supplier delay
> 2–8 weeks
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22510. Но distribution должна иметь основание.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22511. Нельзя автоматически делать:
> 
> ```text
> Normal(5, 1.5)
> ```
> 
> без данных.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22512. При отсутствии distribution можно использовать:
> 
> ```text
> scenario ranges.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22513. Например:
> 
> ```text
> optimistic
> baseline
> adverse
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22514. Но labels тоже не должны скрывать assumptions.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22515. Лучше:
> 
> ```text
> supplier_delay = 2 weeks
> supplier_delay = 5 weeks
> supplier_delay = 8 weeks
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22516. Mechanism
> 
> Теперь важное понятие.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22517. Mechanism — это:
> 
> ```text
> rule structure
> through which actions produce outcomes.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22518. Example
> 
> ```text
> Shared Booking Registry
> ```
> 
> mechanism:
> 
> ```text
> providers publish slots
> requesters search
> matching selects feasible slot
> reservation locks capacity
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22519. Это отличается от:
> 
> ```text
> "создать платформу".
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22520. Платформа — implementation.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22521. Mechanism:
> 
> ```text
> information + allocation rule.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22522. Mechanism Design
> 
> Здесь означает:
> 
> > проектирование правил взаимодействия между участниками системы так, чтобы можно было исследовать их последствия.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22523. Это не:
> 
> ```text
> манипуляция людьми.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22524. Rules должны быть:
> 
> ```text
> explicit
> auditable
> governed
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22525. Примеры Mechanism classes
> 
> ```text
> DISCOVERY
> MATCHING
> ALLOCATION
> PRICING
> ACCESS
> PRIORITY
> VERIFICATION
> INCENTIVE
> COORDINATION
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22526. DISCOVERY Mechanism
> 
> Кто что видит?
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22527. Example:
> 
> ```text
> public capability registry
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22528. MATCHING Mechanism
> 
> Как Requirement сопоставляется Provider?
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22529. Example:
> 
> ```text
> hard constraints first
> then feasible options
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22530. ALLOCATION Mechanism
> 
> Кто получает scarce Resource?
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22531. Example:
> 
> ```text
> reservation queue
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22532. PRICING Mechanism
> 
> Если ресурс коммерческий:
> 
> ```text
> fixed price
> auction
> negotiated price
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22533. Но Sandbox должен уметь моделировать и:
> 
> ```text
> zero-price sharing
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22534. ACCESS Mechanism
> 
> ```text
> who is eligible?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22535. Example:
> 
> ```text
> members only
> academic only
> certified operators only
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22536. PRIORITY Mechanism
> 
> ```text
> who goes first?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22537. Example:
> 
> ```text
> safety-critical jobs
> before normal jobs
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22538. VERIFICATION Mechanism
> 
> Как принимается результат?
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22539. Example:
> 
> ```text
> independent benchmark required
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22540. INCENTIVE Mechanism
> 
> Как участники компенсируются за contribution?
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22541. Это может быть:
> 
> ```text
> money
> credits
> reciprocal access
> recognition
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22542. Не каждую ecosystem interaction надо монетизировать.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22543. COORDINATION Mechanism
> 
> Как участники синхронизируют действия?
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22544. Example:
> 
> ```text
> shared calendar
> semantic event bus
> program board
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22545. Mechanism Contract
> 
> Можно представить:
> 
> ```yaml
> mechanism:
>   inputs: ...
>   eligibility: ...
>   allocation_rule: ...
>   outputs: ...
>   exceptions: ...
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22546. Example
> 
> ```yaml
> mechanism:
>   name: shared_lab_booking
> 
>   eligibility:
>     - operator_certified
>     - material_allowed
> 
>   allocation_rule:
>     type: earliest_feasible_slot
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22547. Mechanism Contract — Artifact.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22548. Он может ссылаться на:
> 
> ```text
> Constraints
> Policies
> Procedural Graphs
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22549. Mechanism ≠ policy text only.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22550. Желательно иметь:
> 
> ```text
> machine-readable rule
> +
> human-readable explanation
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22551. Policy Sandbox
> 
> Policy Artifact может быть:
> 
> ```text
> natural-language document
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22552. Sandbox использует:
> 
> ```text
> machine-readable policy projection.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22553. Example:
> 
> ```text
> "priority is given to urgent safety tests"
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22554. Нужно operationalize:
> 
> ```yaml
> priority:
>   if:
>     project_class: safety_validation
>   weight: high
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22555. Но translation from text to executable rule может быть imperfect.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22556. Поэтому:
> 
> ```text
> policy text
> ≠
> compiled rule
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22557. Need:
> 
> ```text
> Policy Compilation Review
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22558. Similar to code compilation.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22559. Policy Compiler
> 
> Pipeline:
> 
> ```text
> Policy Artifact
> ↓
> Rule Extraction
> ↓
> Semantic Validation
> ↓
> Conflict Check
> ↓
> Executable Rule Set
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22560. LLM может извлекать candidate rules.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22561. Но deterministic validator проверяет:
> 
> ```text
> types
> conditions
> authority
> conflicts
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22562. Example conflict
> 
> ```text
> Rule A:
> all external projects prohibited
> 
> Rule B:
> external projects allowed if certified
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22563. Need detect:
> 
> ```text
> policy conflict.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22564. Policy conflict ≠ automatically resolvable.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22565. Governance decides precedence.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22566. Rule Priority
> 
> Может определяться:
> 
> ```text
> jurisdiction
> authority
> scope
> specificity
> time
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22567. Но legal precedence может быть сложнее.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22568. Innovation OS не должен invent legal hierarchy.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22569. It can require explicit rule source/authority.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22570. Scenario Model
> 
> Каждый simulation run должен хранить:
> 
> ```text
> base state
> scenario patch
> mechanism version
> simulation engine
> parameters
> random seed if relevant
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22571. Это обеспечивает:
> 
> ```text
> reproducibility.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22572. Simulation Run = Action.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22573. Output:
> 
> ```text
> Artifacts
> Events
> Claims
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22574. But all outputs marked:
> 
> ```text
> SIMULATED.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22575. Simulated Events must never enter real Event Journal unmarked.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22576. Лучше:
> 
> ```text
> scenario_event_log
> ```
> 
> separate logical stream.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22577. Could share physical storage,
> 
> but Context must prevent confusion.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22578. Strong invariant:
> 
> ```text
> scenario_event.context != base_context
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22579. Simulation Snapshot
> 
> Resulting state:
> 
> ```text
> Scenario World State
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22580. Это materialized view.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22581. Оно может быть queried как обычный World State,
> 
> но с reality layer.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22582. Это мощно,
> 
> потому что existing resolvers могут работать внутри Scenario.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22583. Example:
> 
> ```text
> What capability gaps remain
> after adding shared GPU cluster?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22584. Resolver runs inside scenario.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22585. Или:
> 
> ```text
> Which Projects become feasible?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22586. Это не требует второго resolver engine.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22587. Scenario as Context overlay.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22588. Base:
> 
> ```text
> World State W
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22589. Patch:
> 
> ```text
> ΔS
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22590. Scenario state conceptually:
> 
> ```text
> W' = W ⊕ ΔS
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22591. But actual implementation should preserve lineage,
> 
> not physically duplicate entire DB.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22592. Use:
> 
> ```text
> base snapshot reference
> +
> overrides
> +
> simulated events
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22593. Copy-on-write concept.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22594. Branching Scenario
> 
> Scenario A can have sub-scenarios:
> 
> ```text
> A
> ├── A1
> └── A2
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22595. Example
> 
> ```text
> A = shared lab marketplace
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22596. A1:
> 
> ```text
> free access
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22597. A2:
> 
> ```text
> usage credits
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22598. Compare structurally.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22599. Scenario Tree
> 
> Useful for:
> 
> ```text
> strategy
> policy alternatives
> uncertain futures
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22600. Scenario Tree should not be mistaken for:
> 
> ```text
> probability tree
> ```
> 
> unless probabilities evidenced.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22601. Branch Weight optional,
> 
> not mandatory.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22602. Scenario Comparison
> 
> Compare:
> 
> ```text
> Scenario A
> Scenario B
> Base
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22603. Dimensions:
> 
> ```text
> capacity
> waiting time
> resource utilization
> unserved demand
> integration cost
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22604. Again:
> 
> ```text
> no overall winner.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22605. Example
> 
> Scenario A:
> 
> ```text
> lower waiting time
> higher operating cost
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22606. Scenario B:
> 
> ```text
> lower cost
> higher queue variance
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22607. Human/governance evaluates.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22608. Outcome Metric
> 
> Every metric must specify:
> 
> ```text
> definition
> unit
> population
> time window
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22609. Example poor:
> 
> ```text
> efficiency +15%
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22610. Better:
> 
> ```text
> median waiting time
> for eligible lab bookings
> over simulated 30-day period
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22611. Metric Provenance
> 
> Simulation result should link:
> 
> ```text
> input data
> model
> formula
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22612. This makes claims auditable.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22613. Counterfactual
> 
> A central use case.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22614. Question:
> 
> ```text
> What would have happened
> if Intervention X had existed?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22615. Example:
> 
> ```text
> Would last month's projects
> have waited less
> with shared scheduling?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22616. Historical replay can provide:
> 
> ```text
> counterfactual simulation.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22617. But counterfactual ≠ historical fact.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22618. It is model output.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22619. Counterfactual Baseline
> 
> Need reconstruct actual state at:
> 
> ```text
> t0.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22620. Then replay:
> 
> ```text
> actual historical events
> ```
> 
> where appropriate.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22621. But intervention changes behavior,
> 
> so one cannot blindly reuse all downstream events.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22622. Example new booking policy changes:
> 
> ```text
> which machine gets used.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22623. Then actual later booking events are no longer valid counterfactual inputs.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22624. Need:
> 
> ```text
> branch point.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22625. Post-branch events generated by model.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22626. This is important for causal correctness.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22627. Historical Replay
> 
> Can validate simulator.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22628. Example:
> 
> ```text
> start from Jan 1 state
> simulate without intervention
> compare to actual Jan 31 state
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22629. If model cannot reproduce basic dynamics,
> 
> policy conclusions weak.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22630. Model Validation
> 
> Compare simulation against:
> 
> ```text
> observed historical behavior.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22631. Dimensions:
> 
> ```text
> queue lengths
> utilization
> delays
> throughput
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22632. Again not one global accuracy score necessarily.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22633. Model Calibration
> 
> Estimate parameters from observed data.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22634. Example:
> 
> ```text
> average setup time
> ```
> 
> from historical Events.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22635. But calibration must avoid data leakage when testing predictive fit.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22636. For operational simulation,
> 
> basic holdout periods can help.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22637. Model Version
> 
> Every run stores:
> 
> ```text
> model_version.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22638. Because outputs may differ after model update.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22639. Scenario Comparison across model versions should be cautious.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22640. Model Assumptions Registry
> 
> Examples:
> 
> ```text
> requests arrive at historical rate
> machine service times unchanged
> participants follow allocation rule
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22641. Each assumption explicit.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22642. Assumption can be:
> 
> ```text
> FACT
> INFERENCE
> HYPOTHESIS
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22643. Example:
> 
> ```text
> machine runtime distribution
> ```
> 
> may be empirical.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22644. Example:
> 
> ```text
> organizations will expose 20% capacity
> ```
> 
> may be hypothesis.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22645. Simulation output strength limited by assumptions.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22646. Therefore result should state:
> 
> ```text
> conditional on assumptions.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22647. Sensitivity Analysis
> 
> Question:
> 
> ```text
> Does conclusion change
> when assumptions vary?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22648. Example:
> 
> ```text
> external participation = 10%
> 20%
> 40%
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22649. If result remains similar:
> 
> ```text
> robust to that parameter range.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22650. If result flips:
> 
> ```text
> sensitive.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22651. Sensitivity Map
> 
> ```text
> parameter
> range
> affected outcomes
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22652. Очень полезно.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22653. Example
> 
> Shared lab marketplace reduces waiting time only if:
> 
> ```text
> at least ~N slots
> ```
> 
> are contributed.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22654. Then N becomes:
> 
> ```text
> critical threshold hypothesis.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22655. Threshold should not be treated as exact if model coarse.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22656. Use:
> 
> ```text
> transition region
> ```
> 
> when appropriate.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22657. Robustness Analysis
> 
> Intervention should be tested under:
> 
> ```text
> normal
> high demand
> resource failure
> ```
> 
> scenarios.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22658. Example booking mechanism works in normal load,
> 
> but collapses at 150% demand.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22659. Important design signal.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22660. Mechanism Stress Test
> 
> Similar to capability stress test.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22661. Example:
> 
> ```text
> remove 30% capacity
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22662. Compare mechanisms.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22663. One may degrade gracefully.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22664. Another may create starvation.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22665. Fairness / Distributional Outcomes
> 
> Institutional rules can affect participants differently.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22666. Simulation should show:
> 
> ```text
> who gains access
> who waits longer
> who becomes excluded
> ```
> 
> at relevant aggregate/role level.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22667. Avoid reducing to one average.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22668. Example:
> 
> ```text
> average waiting time improves
> ```
> 
> while:
> 
> ```text
> small projects wait much longer.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22669. Distribution matters.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22670. Useful views:
> 
> ```text
> median
> percentiles
> group-by eligibility class
> ```
> 
> where justified.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22671. Do not infer sensitive demographic categories.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22672. Use operational classes such as:
> 
> ```text
> small_project
> large_project
> internal
> external
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22673. Mechanism Neutrality
> 
> System should not silently encode:
> 
> ```text
> one stakeholder preference
> ```
> 
> as universal objective.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22674. Example allocator could optimize:
> 
> ```text
> throughput
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22675. But another stakeholder values:
> 
> ```text
> equal access
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22676. Another:
> 
> ```text
> deadline adherence.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22677. Therefore objective function must be explicit.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22678. Example:
> 
> ```yaml
> objective:
>   minimize:
>     - total_wait_time
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22679. Alternative:
> 
> ```yaml
> objective:
>   minimize:
>     - maximum_wait_time
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22680. Different outcomes.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22681. Objective itself is policy choice.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22682. Solver does not decide objective.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22683. Multi-objective Mechanism Analysis
> 
> Can return Pareto alternatives.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22684. Example:
> 
> ```text
> Mechanism A:
> higher throughput
> higher variance
> 
> Mechanism B:
> lower throughput
> more even waiting times
> ```
>

>

>

> 
> # 22926. Then failures increase.

> 
> # 22927. If model includes maintenance dependency,
> 
> effect visible.

> 
> # 22928. Another:
>

>

> 
> # 22929. Another:
> 
> ```text

>

> # 22934. Simulation model itself should be criticized.

> 
> # 22935. Model Critic
> 
> Checks:
> 
> ```text
> missing actors
> unrealistic information
> unstated assumptions
> invalid causal edges
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22936. Example:
> 
> Simulator assumes:
> 
> ```text
> every lab immediately joins marketplace.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22937. Critic flags:
> 
> ```text
> participation assumption unsupported.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22938. Then sensitivity analysis over participation level.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22939. This prevents:
> 
> ```text
> simulation laundering speculation into numbers.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22940. Numerical Precision Rule
> 
> Output precision must not exceed:
> 
> ```text
> input/model precision
> ```
> 
> conceptually.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22941. Example inputs rough ranges.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22942. Output should not claim:
> 
> ```text
> 17.382% improvement.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22943. Better:
> 
> ```text
> approximately 15–20%
> under tested assumptions
> ```
> 
> if model supports.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22944. Or just:
> 
> ```text
> median wait decreased
> from 8–10 days to 5–6 days
> in these runs.
> ```
>

> # 22945. Simulation Uncertainty Sources
> 
> ```text
> PARAMETER
> MODEL
> STRUCTURAL
> DATA
> BEHAVIORAL

> 
> # 22946. PARAMETER
> 
> Unknown values.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22947. MODEL
> 
> Approximation limitations.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22948. STRUCTURAL
> 
> Missing mechanisms.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22949. DATA
> 
> Poor/incomplete observations.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22950. BEHAVIORAL
> 
> Actors may behave differently.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22951. Report uncertainty source separately.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22952. Do not collapse all uncertainty to:
> 
> ```text

> 
> # 22953. Model Ensemble
> 
> Could run:
> 
> ```text
> multiple plausible models.

> 
> # 22954. Example:
> 
> ```text
> strictly rational allocation model
> queue-based model
> bounded-information model

> ---
> 
> # 22955. If all produce similar direction:
> 
> ```text
> mechanism result more robust

> 
> # 22956. Still not certainty.

> ---
> 
> # 22957. Disagreement between models:
> 
> ```text
> model uncertainty high.

> 
> # 22958. Then next task:

> ```text
> collect discriminating evidence.
> ```

> # 22990. Simulation Hierarchy
> 
> Use different fidelity levels:
> 
> ```text
> L0 analytical estimate
> L1 discrete-event
> L2 agent-based
> L3 domain simulator
> L4 hardware/physical twin
> ```

> 
> # 22991. L0
> 
> Fast rough calculation.

> ---
> 
> # 22992. Example:
> 
> ```text

> ```

> ---
> 
> # 22993. L1
> 
> Queues/workflows.

> ---
> 
> # 22994. L2
> 
> Independent institutional actors.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22995. L3
> 
> Detailed specialized model.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 22996. L4
> 
> Hardware-in-the-loop / physical integration.

> 
> # 22997. Higher fidelity ≠ automatically better.

> 
> # 22998. It costs more.

> ---
> 
> # 22999. Choose fidelity based on decision.

> ```text
> participants
> rules
> flows
> capabilities
> decisions

> ```text

> E4 Policy/Mechanism Experimentation

# chatgpt response

Продолжаю с **23352**. Теперь строим вычислительный слой, который превращает heterogeneous hardware — ARM/x86, CPU/GPU/NPU, edge/cloud, браузеры, смартфоны, роботы и серверы — в единый **Capability Fabric**, где workload описывает требования, а система подбирает допустимое место исполнения, не смешивая производительность, стоимость, безопасность и authority.

>

> # 23411. ARM vs x86
> 
> Fabric should treat them as:
> 
> ```text
> different provider capabilities

> 
> not ideological categories.

> 
> # 23412. ARM often offers:
> 
> ```text
> energy efficiency
> integrated accelerators
> mobile/edge availability
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 23413. x86 may offer:
> 
> ```text
> broader legacy compatibility
> high-performance desktop/server ecosystem
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 23414. But actual selection must depend on:
> 
> ```text
> workload contract.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 23415. No global:
> 
> ```text
> ARM better than x86
> ```
> 
> rule.
> 
> ---

> # 23472. Edge Computing
> 
> Edge means:
> 
> ```text
> compute near data/device.

> 
> # 23473. Not necessarily:
> 
> ```text

> ```

>

> privacy

> elasticity

> privacy
> ongoing cost

> 
> ```text

> ↓
> semantic event
> ↓
> central analysis

> privacy exposure

> # 24152. Infrastructure Stress Test
> 
> Scenarios:
> 
> ```text
> cloud outage
> ISP outage
> GPU loss
> power loss
> model provider outage
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24153. Output:
> 
> ```text

> fallback paths
> mission impact.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24154. This closes compute ↔ mission dependency.
>

> 
> # 24155. Compute Dependency Cascade
> 
> ```text
> Node
> ↓
> Execution Capability
> ↓
> Workflow Action
> ↓
> Project
> ↓
> Program
> ↓
> Mission
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24156. Explainable end-to-end.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24157. Example:
> 
> ```text

> → large-model inference unavailable
> → evidence synthesis blocked
> → grant proposal Project delayed
> ```

> # 24158. This is more useful than:

> ```text

> ```

> 
> # 24160. But infrastructure should not infer priority independently.

>

> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24162. This allows:

> 
> ---

> # 24163. Example:

> 
> retained.

> # 24164. Background embedding deferred.

> 
> # 24165. This is not social ranking.

> # 24167. Heterogeneous Agent Execution
> 
> Agent can be decomposed into:
> 
> ```text
> reasoning
> tools
> memory
> perception
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24168. These can run on different nodes.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24169. Example:
> 
> ```text
> vision on phone NPU
> reasoning on local server
> tool execution on workstation
> memory in PostgreSQL
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24170. Agent identity remains one logical Resource.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24171. Execution instances distributed.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24172. Important:
> 
> ```text
> Agent ≠ Process.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24173. One logical agent can have:
> 
> ```text
> multiple execution processes.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24174. Conversely one process can host:
> 
> ```text
> multiple agents.
> ```
> 
> ---

> # 24194. Small Model Swarm
> 
> User earlier considered:
> 
> ```text
> several small models
> +
> one large model.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24195. Compute Fabric can operationalize:
> 
> ```text
> small models on edge nodes
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24196. They produce:
> 
> ```text
> structured semantic partials.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24197. Large model receives:
> 
> ```text
> compressed semantic state
> ```
> 
> instead of all raw context.

> 
> # 24198. This is:
> 
> # Hierarchical AI Compute Pattern

> 
> ```text

> ↓
> semantic summaries / claims
> ↓
> 1 synthesis model

> 
> ```text
> parallelism
> context compression
> local specialization
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24201. Risks:
> 
> ```text
> information loss
> error propagation
> coordination overhead.
> ```

> # 24202. Verification layer required.

> ↓

> # 24204. But quality requires:

> cross-section consistency

# chatgpt response

Продолжаю с **24435**. Теперь строим слой **Distributed Semantic State Fabric**: как один и тот же World State безопасно существует одновременно в центральной системе, локальных узлах, офлайн-копиях, федерациях, кэшах и сценарных ветках — без превращения репликации в «несколько конкурирующих истин».

> **Document: Distributed Semantic State Fabric, Replication, Versioning & Knowledge Synchronization v0.1**
> 
> # Distributed Semantic State Fabric, Replication, Versioning & Knowledge Synchronization v0.1
> 
> ## 24435. Главный переход
> 
> До сих пор World State концептуально можно было представить как:
> 
> ```text
> одна логическая система
> +
> один authoritative semantic graph
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24436. Но реальный Virtual Technopark будет распределён
> 
> ```text
> Cloud
> Lab
> Factory
> Phone
> Laptop
> Robot
> Partner Organization
> Offline Edge Node
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24437. Эти узлы не могут постоянно иметь
> 
> ```text
> полную
> синхронную
> одинаковую
> копию всего World State.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24438. Причины
> 
> ```text
> privacy
> bandwidth
> offline operation
> organizational autonomy
> scale
> latency
> data ownership
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24439. Поэтому нужен слой
> 
> # Distributed Semantic State Fabric
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24440. Его задача не просто
> 
> ```text
> replicate database
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24441. А понять:
> 
> ```text
> WHAT
> can be replicated
> 
> WHERE
> 
> WITH WHICH AUTHORITY
> 
> AT WHICH FRESHNESS
> 
> UNDER WHICH CONTEXT
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24442. Главный invariant
> 
> ```text
> Replication ≠ Authority.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24443. Если Node B получил копию объекта из Node A,
> 
> это не означает:
> 
> ```text
> Node B теперь authoritative owner.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24444. И наоборот
> 
> ```text
> local cache
> ```
> 
> не превращает объект в локальную истину.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24445. Второй invariant
> 
> ```text
> Copy ≠ Independent Truth.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24446. Третий
> 
> ```text
> Stale State ≠ Current State.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24447. Четвёртый
> 
> ```text
> Merge ≠ Blind Overwrite.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24448. Пятый
> 
> ```text
> Synchronization ≠ Global Consensus.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24449. В большой федерации часто не нужен
> 
> ```text
> one globally serialized state.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24450. Нужна:
> 
> ```text
> local authority
> +
> shared semantics
> +
> controlled state exchange.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24451. Основная архитектура
> 
> ```text
> Local World State
> ↓
> Event Journal
> ↓
> Replication Filter
> ↓
> Semantic Diff
> ↓
> Federation Transport
> ↓
> Receiving Node
> ↓
> Validation
> ↓
> Local Materialization
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24452. Source of Truth
> 
> Нужно различать минимум:
> 
> ```text
> AUTHORITATIVE
> REPLICA
> CACHE
> DERIVED
> SIMULATED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24453. AUTHORITATIVE
> 
> Узел имеет право публиковать:
> 
> ```text
> authoritative state
> ```
> 
> для определённого scope.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24454. Example
> 
> Lab A authoritative для:
> 
> ```text
> availability of its own equipment.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24455. Partner B может иметь replica.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24456. Но Partner B не должен публиковать:
> 
> ```text
> machine available
> ```
> 
> как собственный authoritative факт.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24457. REPLICA
> 
> Полученная копия authoritative state.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24458. CACHE
> 
> Временная локальная копия для:
> 
> ```text
> performance
> offline use
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24459. DERIVED
> 
> Вычисленное состояние:
> 
> ```text
> gap
> match
> cluster
> capital snapshot
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24460. SIMULATED
> 
> Сценарная ветка.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24461. Эти типы должны быть видимы системе.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24462. Authority Scope
> 
> Authority не принадлежит узлу «вообще».
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24463. Она относится к:
> 
> ```text
> Entity
> Predicate
> Context
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24464. Example
> 
> Lab A authoritative:
> 
> ```text
> Resource R
> HAS availability
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24465. Но производитель оборудования может быть authoritative для:
> 
> ```text
> model specification
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24466. Независимый тестовый центр может быть authoritative только для:
> 
> ```text
> its own measurement result.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24467. Никто автоматически не authoritative для:
> 
> ```text
> global truth about machine quality.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24468. Поэтому нужен:
> 
> # Authority Contract
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24469. Example
> 
> ```yaml
> authority:
>   subject_scope: lab-a/*
>   predicates:
>     - availability
>     - reservation_state
> 
>   contexts:
>     - operational
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24470. Authority Contract может быть:
> 
> ```text
> Policy Artifact
> +
> machine-readable rules.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24471. Authority ≠ Trust
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24472. Source may be authorized to state:
> 
> ```text
> its own availability
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24473. But recipient may still distrust:
> 
> ```text
> accuracy/freshness.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24474. Поэтому separate:
> 
> ```text
> authority
> provenance
> verification
> trust policy
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24475. Semantic State Unit
> 
> Минимальная синхронизируемая единица не обязательно Entity.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24476. Часто правильнее:
> 
> ```text
> Claim
> Event
> Artifact reference
> Relation
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24477. Example
> 
> Не пересылаем весь Resource object.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24478. Пересылаем:
> 
> ```text
> Resource R
> PROVIDES Capability C
> valid_time ...
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24479. Или:
> 
> ```text
> Resource R
> availability = AVAILABLE
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24480. Это уменьшает:
> 
> ```text
> state coupling.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24481. State Fragment
> 
> Можно определить:
> 
> ```yaml
> fragment:
>   entity_id: ...
>   claims:
>     - ...
>   events:
>     - ...
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24482. Fragment должен иметь:
> 
> ```text
> source
> authority
> version
> context
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24483. State Version
> 
> Не просто:
> 
> ```text
> version = 7
> ```
> 
> глобально.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24484. Потому что разные части World State обновляются независимо.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24485. Нужны:
> 
> ```text
> entity version
> claim version
> artifact version
> event position
> ```
> 
> где уместно.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24486. Global Monotonic Counter
> 
> Не масштабируется хорошо в federation.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24487. Better:
> 
> ```text
> per-authority event sequence
> +
> globally unique event ID
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24488. Example
> 
> ```text
> Lab A:
> event_seq 1051
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24489. Partner B:
> 
> ```text
> event_seq 884
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24490. Global order между независимыми событиями может быть:
> 
> ```text
> unknown.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24491. И это нормально.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24492. Partial Order
> 
> Distributed semantic state должен уметь работать с:
> 
> ```text
> partial ordering.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24493. Example
> 
> Event A:
> 
> ```text
> machine calibrated
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24494. Event B:
> 
> ```text
> project created
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24495. Если они независимы,
> 
> нет необходимости определять:
> 
> ```text
> которое произошло "глобально первым".
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24496. Causal Order важнее global wall-clock order.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24497. Causal Reference
> 
> Event может содержать:
> 
> ```text
> caused_by
> depends_on_event
> supersedes
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24498. Example
> 
> ```text
> RESERVATION_CONFIRMED
> caused_by
> RESERVATION_REQUESTED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24499. Это создаёт:
> 
> ```text
> causal event graph.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24500. Wall Clock
> 
> Timestamp всё равно нужен.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24501. Но он может быть:
> 
> ```text
> source_time
> ingestion_time
> knowledge_time
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24502. Existing bitemporal model расширяется.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24503. Minimum temporal fields
> 
> ```text
> valid_from
> valid_to
> observed_at
> ingested_at
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24504. For events:
> 
> ```text
> occurred_at
> recorded_at
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24505. Clock Skew
> 
> Если edge device ошибается на 5 минут,
> 
> не должно разрушить:
> 
> ```text
> causal ordering.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24506. Поэтому:
> 
> ```text
> timestamp ≠ sole ordering mechanism.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24507. Event Identity
> 
> Каждый event:
> 
> ```text
> UUID
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24508. Дополнительно:
> 
> ```text
> source_node
> source_sequence
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24509. Это позволяет detect:
> 
> ```text
> duplicates
> gaps
> replays
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24510. Event Deduplication
> 
> Если event пришёл дважды:
> 
> ```text
> same event_id
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24511. Apply once.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24512. At-least-once delivery becomes acceptable.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24513. Missing Sequence Detection
> 
> Если received:
> 
> ```text
> 104
> 106
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24514. Node знает:
> 
> ```text
> 105 missing.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24515. It can request:
> 
> ```text
> event 105
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24516. Но sequence only within source stream.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24517. Event Journal Partitioning
> 
> Could partition by:
> 
> ```text
> authority
> organization
> entity
> domain
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24518. MVP:
> 
> ```text
> organization/source node.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24519. Large-scale later:
> 
> ```text
> topic / shard.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24520. Snapshot
> 
> Replaying billions of events is inefficient.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24521. Therefore:
> 
> ```text
> Event Log
> +
> Periodic Snapshot
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24522. Snapshot means:
> 
> ```text
> materialized state at event position.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24523. Example
> 
> ```text
> snapshot:
>   source: lab-a
>   through_seq: 100000
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24524. Then new node gets:
> 
> ```text
> snapshot
> +
> events after 100000.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24525. Snapshot ≠ replacement of event history.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24526. Event history may be archived.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24527. Snapshot is:
> 
> ```text
> reconstruction accelerator.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24528. Snapshot Integrity
> 
> Need:
> 
> ```text
> content hash
> source
> event cursor
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24529. Optionally signature.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24530. Receiving node can verify:
> 
> ```text
> snapshot completeness/integrity
> ```
> 
> within protocol.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24531. Semantic Diff
> 
> Instead of full snapshot every time:
> 
> ```text
> state diff.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24532. Diff example:
> 
> ```yaml
> diff:
>   entity: machine-17
> 
>   changed:
>     availability:
>       from: BUSY
>       to: AVAILABLE
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24533. But transport diff is not necessarily:
> 
> ```text
> canonical event.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24534. Better derive diff from:
> 
> ```text
> Events
> ```
> 
> or version comparison.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24535. Important distinction
> 
> ```text
> Event
> ≠
> State Diff.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24536. Event says:
> 
> ```text
> what happened.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24537. Diff says:
> 
> ```text
> how two states differ.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24538. Example
> 
> Event:
> 
> ```text
> MACHINE_JOB_COMPLETED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24539. Diff:
> 
> ```text
> availability BUSY → AVAILABLE.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24540. One event may create:
> 
> ```text
> many state changes.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24541. One diff may summarize:
> 
> ```text
> many events.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24542. Therefore preserve both.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24543. State Diff Package
> 
> Useful for bandwidth-limited federation.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24544. Could include:
> 
> ```text
> base_version
> target_version
> changes
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24545. Receiver must verify:
> 
> ```text
> has base_version?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24546. If not:
> 
> ```text
> request snapshot or missing chain.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24547. This prevents:
> 
> ```text
> applying diff to wrong base.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24548. Delta Chain
> 
> ```text
> v1
> ↓ diff
> v2
> ↓ diff
> v3
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24549. Chain can be compacted periodically.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24550. Merkle-like Content Addressing
> 
> Useful later for:
> 
> ```text
> large immutable artifacts
> state manifests
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24551. Artifact identified by:
> 
> ```text
> content hash.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24552. Then different nodes can know:
> 
> ```text
> same content
> ```
> 
> even if path/name differs.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24553. But semantic identity remains:
> 
> ```text
> UUID.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24554. Important distinction
> 
> ```text
> Semantic Identity ≠ Content Identity.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24555. Same Artifact entity may have:
> 
> ```text
> multiple versions/hashes.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24556. Two separate Artifacts may contain:
> 
> ```text
> identical bytes.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24557. Therefore hash is not universal entity ID.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24558. Large Artifact Replication
> 
> Examples:
> 
> ```text
> models
> datasets
> video
> CAD
> checkpoints
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24559. Do not put raw bytes in:
> 
> ```text
> semantic event stream.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24560. Instead:
> 
> ```text
> Artifact Metadata
> +
> Content Reference
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24561. Artifact can live in:
> 
> ```text
> Object Store
> Local Storage
> Partner Store
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24562. Semantic layer stores:
> 
> ```text
> URI/reference
> hash
> size
> access policy
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24563. Artifact Location
> 
> Could be multiple:
> 
> ```text
> Node A
> Node B
> Object Store C
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24564. Artifact Location Index derived.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24565. Replication Policy may decide:
> 
> ```text
> where copies should exist.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24566. Example critical model:
> 
> ```text
> 2 independent sites.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24567. Example temporary video:
> 
> ```text
> local-only 24h.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24568. Artifact Retention
> 
> Need:
> 
> ```text
> TTL
> legal retention
> project retention
> permanent archive
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24569. Deletion semantics become complicated.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24570. Especially federation.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24571. Tombstone
> 
> If object logically deleted:
> 
> ```text
> delete event
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24572. Replica that was offline must later learn:
> 
> ```text
> object removed.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24573. Therefore deletion cannot simply mean:
> 
> ```text
> row vanished.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24574. Need:
> 
> ```text
> tombstone / retirement event.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24575. But core already prefers:
> 
> ```text
> soft-delete/history.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24576. Good fit.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24577. Semantic Removal
> 
> Different concepts:
> 
> ```text
> RETRACT
> RETIRE
> DELETE
> HIDE
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24578. RETRACT Claim
> 
> Claim remains historical,
> 
> but no longer asserted.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24579. RETIRE Resource
> 
> No longer active.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24580. DELETE
> 
> May be required for privacy/legal reasons.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24581. HIDE
> 
> Access visibility change.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24582. They must not be conflated.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24583. GDPR/privacy deletion problem
> 
> Distributed replication may require:
> 
> ```text
> deletion propagation.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24584. This differs from historical scientific preservation.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24585. Sensitive/personal data should therefore be:
> 
> ```text
> minimized
> scoped
> rarely replicated.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24586. Selective Replication
> 
> Central concept.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24587. Node should subscribe to:
> 
> ```text
> only relevant semantic slices.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24588. Example robot node needs:
> 
> ```text
> local mission
> device config
> nearby spatial state
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24589. It does not need:
> 
> ```text
> all grants
> all papers
> all global hiring data.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24590. Replication Subscription
> 
> ```yaml
> subscription:
>   contexts:
>     - factory-a
> 
>   entity_types:
>     - RESOURCE
>     - ACTION
>     - EVENT
> 
>   predicates:
>     - REQUIRES
>     - ASSIGNED_TO
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24591. Additional filters:
> 
> ```text
> spatial region
> project
> capability
> organization
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24592. Subscription itself subject to:
> 
> ```text
> authorization.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24593. Query Permission ≠ Replication Permission
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24594. Example user may query:
> 
> ```text
> current aggregated capacity
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24595. But not receive:
> 
> ```text
> continuous raw event stream.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24596. Different privileges.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24597. Replication Modes
> 
> ```text
> NONE
> ON_DEMAND
> SUBSCRIPTION
> SNAPSHOT
> CONTINUOUS
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24598. NONE
> 
> No export.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24599. ON_DEMAND
> 
> Fetch when requested.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24600. SNAPSHOT
> 
> Periodic state.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24601. SUBSCRIPTION
> 
> Relevant changes pushed.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24602. CONTINUOUS
> 
> Near-real-time stream.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24603. Mode depends on:
> 
> ```text
> need
> privacy
> bandwidth
> freshness
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24604. Freshness Contract
> 
> Consumer may require:
> 
> ```text
> max_age = 10 sec
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24605. Or:
> 
> ```text
> 24 hours.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24606. State older than max_age becomes:
> 
> ```text
> STALE.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24607. Not automatically false.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24608. Important invariant
> 
> ```text
> Stale ≠ False.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24609. But stale state may be:
> 
> ```text
> unsafe to use.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24610. Example equipment availability:
> 
> 10-minute-old state may be unacceptable.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24611. Research paper metadata:
> 
> one-day-old fine.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24612. Freshness domain-specific.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24613. Last Known State
> 
> Offline node may hold:
> 
> ```text
> last known state.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24614. UI should show:
> 
> ```text
> last updated 3h ago
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24615. Not:
> 
> ```text
> available now.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24616. Fog of War
> 
> Earlier spatial concept generalizes.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24617. In federation:
> 
> ```text
> unknown current state
> ```
> 
> should be visible.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24618. Useful status:
> 
> ```text
> UNKNOWN
> STALE
> CONFIRMED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24619. Offline-First Node
> 
> Needs:
> 
> ```text
> local replica
> local event journal
> local commands
> sync queue
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24620. Example field laptop.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24621. While offline:
> 
> ```text
> read local cached state
> create local events
> execute preauthorized Actions
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24622. Later:
> 
> ```text
> synchronize.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24623. Offline Writes
> 
> Hard problem.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24624. If two nodes modify:
> 
> ```text
> same logical state
> ```
> 
> offline,
> 
> conflict may arise.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24625. Solution depends on data type.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24626. Therefore:
> 
> # Merge Policy must be semantic.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24627. Not every field should use:
> 
> ```text
> last-write-wins.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24628. Last-Write-Wins
> 
> Can be acceptable for:
> 
> ```text
> low-risk UI preference
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24629. Dangerous for:
> 
> ```text
> financial reservation
> authority
> scientific claim
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24630. Merge classes
> 
> ```text
> APPEND_ONLY
> SET_UNION
> REGISTER
> COUNTER
> ORDERED_LOG
> MANUAL_CONFLICT
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24631. APPEND_ONLY
> 
> Ideal for:
> 
> ```text
> Events
> Evidence
> Comments
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24632. Two nodes add events.
> 
> Merge:
> 
> ```text
> union
> ```
> 
> with deduplication.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24633. SET_UNION
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> tags
> providers discovered
> ```
> 
> where removal semantics carefully handled.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24634. REGISTER
> 
> Single current value:
> 
> ```text
> display name
> preferred UI setting
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24635. Requires conflict strategy.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24636. COUNTER
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> non-critical aggregate statistic
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24637. But accounting counters require stronger semantics.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24638. ORDERED_LOG
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> local sequence of commands.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24639. MANUAL_CONFLICT
> 
> For:
> 
> ```text
> strategic Decision
> legal status
> authority assignment
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24640. Cannot safely auto-merge.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24641. CRDT
> 
> Conflict-free Replicated Data Types may help for:
> 
> ```text
> specific mergeable structures.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24642. But:
> 
> ```text
> CRDT ≠ universal semantic conflict solution.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24643. CRDT can solve:
> 
> ```text
> technical convergence
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24644. It cannot determine:
> 
> ```text
> which scientific claim is correct
> which decision is authorized.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24645. Excellent invariant
> 
> ```text
> Converged Data ≠ Resolved Meaning.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24646. Example
> 
> Two nodes assert:
> 
> ```text
> Machine state = AVAILABLE
> Machine state = MAINTENANCE
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24647. CRDT could preserve both.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24648. But system still needs:
> 
> ```text
> authority/time/context
> ```
> 
> to interpret.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24649. Conflict Types
> 
> ```text
> VALUE_CONFLICT
> AUTHORITY_CONFLICT
> TEMPORAL_CONFLICT
> IDENTITY_CONFLICT
> SCHEMA_CONFLICT
> SEMANTIC_CONFLICT
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24650. VALUE_CONFLICT
> 
> Same scoped property,
> 
> different values.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24651. AUTHORITY_CONFLICT
> 
> Two sources both claim authority.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24652. TEMPORAL_CONFLICT
> 
> States refer to different valid times.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24653. Often not real conflict.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24654. IDENTITY_CONFLICT
> 
> Two records may refer to:
> 
> ```text
> same real entity
> ```
> 
> but different UUIDs.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24655. SCHEMA_CONFLICT
> 
> Field/profile versions incompatible.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24656. SEMANTIC_CONFLICT
> 
> Same words,
> 
> different meaning/context.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24657. Conflict Resolver must classify before resolving.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24658. Example
> 
> ```text
> Machine temperature = 50C
> Machine temperature = 60C
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24659. Could be:
> 
> ```text
> two timestamps
> ```
> 
> not conflict.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24660. Or:
> 
> ```text
> two sensors same time.
> ```
> 
> then measurement disagreement.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24661. Preserve both as Evidence.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24662. Scientific Claims
> 
> Never merge:
> 
> ```text
> Claim A SUPPORTS X
> Claim B REFUTES X
> ```
> 
> into:
> 
> ```text
> X = maybe.
> ```
> 
> automatically.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24663. Keep:
> 
> ```text
> competing Claims
> +
> Evidence.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24664. This is semantic pluralism.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24665. Claim Synchronization
> 
> Claims are good distributed objects because:
> 
> ```text
> appendable
> provenance-rich
> scope-aware.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24666. Retraction creates:
> 
> ```text
> new Claim/Event
> ```
> 
> not destructive overwrite.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24667. This greatly reduces merge complexity.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24668. Event-Sourced Semantics naturally help federation.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24669. State can be reconstructed from:
> 
> ```text
> immutable history
> +
> authority rules
> +
> materialization logic.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24670. Not every state change should overwrite one row.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24671. Materialized State
> 
> Fast operational read model.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24672. If conflict occurs:
> 
> ```text
> materializer may mark state CONFLICTED.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24673. Example
> 
> ```text
> availability:
>   status: CONFLICTED
> 
> sources:
>   - lab_scheduler
>   - maintenance_system
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24674. Better than choosing silently.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24675. Conflict Visibility
> 
> UI should show:
> 
> ```text
> why state uncertain.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24676. Example:
> 
> ```text
> scheduler says available
> maintenance controller says locked
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24677. For safety:
> 
> ```text
> more restrictive state
> ```
> 
> may be operationally selected by policy.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24678. But underlying conflict remains visible.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24679. Safety Policy Example
> 
> ```text
> if machine_state conflict includes MAINTENANCE
> → block execution.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24680. That is:
> 
> ```text
> policy response to uncertainty
> ```
> 
> not semantic resolution.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24681. Merge Authority
> 
> Some conflicts can resolve through:
> 
> ```text
> source precedence.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24682. Example:
> 
> ```text
> device controller
> ```
> 
> authoritative for:
> 
> ```text
> current operational lock.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24683. Scheduling UI not authoritative.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24684. Then materializer can prefer:
> 
> ```text
> controller state.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24685. But preserve outdated scheduler claim historically.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24686. Authority Table
> 
> Could map:
> 
> ```text
> predicate
> context
> authority source
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24687. Example:
> 
> ```yaml
> availability:
>   authority: scheduler
> 
> emergency_lock:
>   authority: device_controller
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24688. Effective availability derives from both.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24689. Derived State Example
> 
> ```text
> effective_available =
> scheduler_available
> AND
> not emergency_locked
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24690. This is better than overwriting fields.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24691. Semantic Materialization Rules
> 
> Need explicit functions:
> 
> ```text
> claims/events
> → operational state.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24692. These rules are:
> 
> ```text
> versioned code/policy.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24693. If materializer logic changes,
> 
> derived state may change without new external events.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24694. Therefore record:
> 
> ```text
> materializer_version.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24695. This is important for reproducibility.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24696. Example old logic:
> 
> ```text
> latest claim wins.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24697. New logic:
> 
> ```text
> authority + valid time.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24698. Rebuild state.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24699. Same event history,
> 
> different derived state.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24700. Need migration/audit.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24701. Projection Version
> 
> Every major materialized view:
> 
> ```text
> view_version.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24702. Examples:
> 
> ```text
> Capability Index v3
> Gap Index v2
> Ecosystem Cluster View v5
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24703. Derived View ≠ Canonical Data.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24704. Therefore safe to rebuild.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24705. Federation Node
> 
> Could expose:
> 
> ```text
> public semantic endpoint
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24706. It may publish:
> 
> ```text
> capability summaries
> offers
> claims
> evidence references
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24707. It may not publish:
> 
> ```text
> private internal events.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24708. Export Profile
> 
> Defines:
> 
> ```text
> what leaves organization.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24709. Example
> 
> ```yaml

>   capabilities: public
>   availability: aggregate
>   people: none
>   internal_projects: none
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24710. Export Transformation
> 
> Sometimes data is:
> 
> ```text
> aggregated
> redacted
> pseudonymized
> ```
> 
> before export.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24711. Example internal:
> 
> ```text
> GPU-01
> GPU-02
> GPU-03
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24712. External:
> 
> ```text
> GPU_POOL_CAPACITY = 3 providers

> ---
> 
> # 24713. This protects infrastructure details.

> ---
> 
> # 24714. But aggregate must be labeled:
> 
> ```text
> derived/exported view.

> 
> ---
> 
> # 24715. Remote node should not infer:
> 
> ```text
> exact topology
> ```
> 
> from aggregate unless provided.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24716. Import Profile
> 
> Receiving organization can define:
> 
> ```text
> which external semantic objects it accepts.

> 
> ---
> 
> # 24717. Example:
> 
> ```text
> official partner claims
> accepted
> 
> unknown public nodes
> discovery-only
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24718. Import Policy can require:
> 
> ```text
> signature
> schema version
> evidence
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24719. Imported Claim state
> 
> Possible:
> 
> ```text
> RECEIVED
> VALIDATED
> ACCEPTED
> REJECTED
> QUARANTINED

> 
> ---
> 
> # 24720. `ACCEPTED`
> 
> does not mean:
> 
> ```text
> true.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24721. It means:
> 
> ```text

> under provenance.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24722. Verification remains separate.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24723. Quarantine
> 
> Malformed/suspicious data can be stored:
> 
> ```text
> outside trusted materialization.

> 
> ---
> 
> # 24724. Useful for:
> 
> ```text
> schema errors
> signature failure
> security concerns
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24725. Quarantined data should not influence:
> 
> ```text
> production resolver

> 
> until cleared.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24726. Federation Protocol Envelope
> 
> Could include:
> 
> ```yaml
> message:
>   type: STATE_DIFF
>   source_org: ...
>   schema_version: ...
>   context: ...
>   payload_hash: ...
>   signature: ...
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24727. Payload types reuse existing:
> 
> ```text
> CAPABILITY_DEMAND
> CAPABILITY_OFFER
> CLAIM
> EVIDENCE_REFERENCE
> EVENT
> STATE_DIFF
> QUERY
> RESULT

>

> # 24728. Need version negotiation.

>

> 
> Node A supports:
> 
> ```text

> 1.0

> 
> # 24730. Node B:
> 
> ```text
> 1.0
> 1.1

> 
> ```text
> 1.0
> ```

> 
> # 24732. Use common compatible profile.

> 
> # 24733. If none:
> 
> ```text
> adapter required.

>

> 
> # 24735. Better:

> 
> # 24736. Example:
>

> v1 producer
> v2 consumer
> adapter

> 
> # 24737. Eventually retire old profile.

> ---
> 
> # 24738. Semantic Versioning
> 
> Could distinguish:
> 
> ```text
> backward-compatible additions
> breaking semantic changes

> 
> # 24739. But semantic compatibility cannot be inferred from:
> 
> ```text
> version number alone.

> # 24740. Need:
> 
> ```text
> compatibility metadata/tests.

>

>

> 
> Stores:
> 
> ```text
> schema
> profile
> version
> compatibility
> migration
> ```

> ---
> 
> # 24742. This is essential for federation.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24743. Predicate Registry remains frozen at core.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24744. Extensions can be:
> 
> ```text
> namespaced.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24745. Example:
> 
> ```text
> robotics:GRASPED
> spatial:INSIDE

> ---
> 
> # 24746. Unknown Predicate
> 
> Receiving node may not understand extension.

> 
> # 24747. It should not:

> ```text

> 
> ---
> 
> # 24748. Options:
> 
> ```text
> preserve opaque
> request ontology
> ignore for materialization
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24749. Opaque Preservation
> 
> Important federation feature.

> ---
> 
> # 24750. Node can retain:
> 
> ```text
> unknown extension payload
> ```
> 
> for forwarding/audit.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24751. But cannot reason over it safely.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24752. Capability Negotiation for Semantics
> 
> Node can advertise:
> 
> ```text
> supports ontology profile X.
> ```

> 
> # 24753. This becomes:
> 
> ```text
> semantic capability.
> ```
>

> 
> # 24754. Resolver can choose:
> 
> ```text
> direct exchange
> adapter
> translation.
> ```

>

> 
> LLM may help map:
> 
> ```text
> Profile A → Profile B
> ```

> ---
> 
> # 24756. But translation creates:
> 
> ```text
> INFERENCE.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24757. It is not identity.

> 
> # 24758. Example:
> 
> ```text
> "operator"
> ```
> 
> may mean different roles.

> 
> # 24759. Mapping must preserve:
> 
> ```text
> scope
> uncertainty
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24760. Semantic Mapping Artifact
> 
> Contains:
> 
> ```text
> source concept
> target concept
> mapping type
> evidence
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24761. Mapping types:
> 
> ```text
> EXACT
> BROADER
> NARROWER
> RELATED
> TRANSFORM
> UNKNOWN
> ```

> 
> # 24762. Avoid pretending:
> 
> ```text
> RELATED = SAME.

>

> 
> # 24763. Translation Pipeline
> 
> ```text
> External Profile
> ↓
> Mapping
> ↓
> Normalized Candidate
> ↓
> Validation
> ↓
> Imported Semantic Object

> 
> # 24764. Original external representation preserved.

> 
> # 24765. This supports future remapping.

> 
> # 24766. Identity Federation
> 
> Another major issue.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24767. Organization A Resource:
> 
> ```text
> UUID_A
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24768. Organization B may already have:
> 
> ```text
> UUID_B
> ```
> 
> for same external lab.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24769. Cannot automatically merge.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24770. Need:
> 
> # Entity Resolution
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24771. Existing external identities:
> 
> ```text
> ORCID
> GitHub ID
> DOI
> company registry IDs
> ```
> 
> can help.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24772. But names alone weak.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24773. Identity Match states:
> 
> ```text
> SAME_CONFIRMED
> SAME_PROBABLE
> POSSIBLE
> DIFFERENT
> UNKNOWN
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24774. `POSSIBLE`
> 
> does not merge UUIDs.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24775. Could create:
> 
> ```text
> identity link claim.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24776. Canonicalization
> 
> Within one local system,
> 
> can choose:
> 
> ```text
> preferred canonical entity.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24777. Across federation:
> 
> ```text
> global canonical UUID
> ```
> 
> may be unrealistic.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24778. Better:
> 
> ```text
> local UUID
> +
> external identities
> +
> federated equivalence claims.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24779. This avoids central identity authority.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24780. Example
> 
> ```text
> Lab A local UUID:
> a-17
> 
> Partner B local UUID:
> b-908
> 
> shared external registry ID:
> 12345
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24781. They can resolve confidently.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24782. But still retain local identities for references.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24783. UUID Namespace
> 
> Could use:
> 
> ```text
> globally unique UUID
> ```
> 
> for newly exchanged entities.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24784. But existing local duplicates still possible.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24785. So UUID alone does not solve entity resolution historically.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24786. Forked Entity
> 
> Sometimes two nodes intentionally diverge.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24787. Example:
> 
> ```text
> Workflow Package v1
> ```
> 
> forked by Lab B.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24788. New semantic identity should be:
> 
> ```text
> new Artifact/Package
> DERIVED_FROM original.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24789. Not conflict.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24790. Fork ≠ Merge Conflict.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24791. Content Fork
> 
> Same starting version,
> 
> independent modifications.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24792. Could later merge like code.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24793. But semantic merge needs:
> 
> ```text
> domain-specific rules.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24794. Workflow merge
> 
> Potentially compare:
> 
> ```text
> nodes
> edges
> contracts
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24795. Ontology merge
> 
> Much harder.

> ---
> 
> # 24796. Decision merge
> 
> Usually inappropriate.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24797. Therefore:
> 
> ```text
> versioning
> ```
> 
> and:
> 
> ```text
> semantic merge

> must stay separate.

> 
> # 24798. Artifact Version Graph
> 
> Not just linear:
> 
> ```text
> v1 → v2 → v3
> ```

> 
> # 24799. Support:
> 
> ```text
> branches
> forks
> merges

>

> 
> # 24800. Example
> 
> ```text
> v1
> ├─ Lab A v2A

> 
> # 24801. Later:
>

>

> ```text

>

> 
> # 24803. This allows Git-like knowledge lineage.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24804. But do not force every semantic object into Git semantics.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24805. Claims are better append-only.

> ---
> 
> # 24806. Documents/code may be versioned artifacts.

> 
> # 24807. Operational state may be event-derived.

> 
> # 24808. Use right versioning model per object.

> 
> # 24809. Knowledge Package
> 
> Could bundle:
> 
> ```text
> Claims
> Evidence references
> Artifacts
> Concept mappings

> 
> # 24810. For transport:
> 
> ```text
> Knowledge Capsule.
> ```

> 
> # 24811. Example
> 
> ```text
> "robot tactile sensing package"
> ```
> 
> contains:
> 
> ```text
> capability definition
> papers
> benchmarks
> procedure
> known limitations

> 
> # 24812. Receiving node imports whole package.

> ---
> 
> # 24813. But each Claim retains:
> 
> ```text
> its own provenance.

> 
> # 24814. Package signature proves:
> 
> ```text
> bundle origin/integrity
> ```

> 
> # 24815. It does not make every Claim true.

> 
> # 24816. Knowledge Synchronization Modes
> 
> ```text
> PUSH
> PULL
> PUBSUB
> GOSSIP
> ON_DEMAND
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24817. PUSH
> 
> Authority sends updates.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24818. PULL
> 
> Consumer fetches periodically.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24819. PUBSUB
> 
> Topic subscription.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24820. GOSSIP
> 
> Useful for:
>

> large decentralized replication

> 
> potentially later.

> 
> # 24821. ON_DEMAND
> 
> Fetch specific object/context.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24822. MVP does not need all.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24823. Start:
> 
> ```text
> PULL
> +
> PUBSUB
> ```
> 
> or simple:
> 
> ```text
> HTTP + event stream.
> ```
> 
> ---
>

> 
> Do not reinvent:
> 
> ```text
> Kafka
> NATS
> PostgreSQL
> object storage

> 
> functionality unless necessary.

> 
> # 24825. Semantic Fabric sits above infrastructure messaging.

>

> 
> Possible:
> 
> ```text
> HTTP
> WebSocket
> SSE
> NATS
> Kafka
> MQTT

> ---
>

>

> 
> ```text
> bundle files

>

> # 24833. Could export:

> ```text

> 
> # 24835. Useful for:

> 
> # 24837. Sync Package
> 
> ```yaml
> sync_bundle:
>   source: ...
>   from_cursor: ...
>   to_cursor: ...
>   payloads: ...
>   manifest_hash: ...

> 
> ---
> 
> # 24838. Could include:
> 
> ```text

> claims
> artifact manifests

> 
> # 24839. Large artifacts optionally separate.

> 
> # 24840. Incremental Sync
> 
> Node remembers:
> 
> ```text
> last accepted cursor
> ```
> 
> per source/subscription.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24841. Then requests:
> 
> ```text
> everything after cursor.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24842. Cursor should be:
> 
> ```text
> opaque
> ```
> 
> to consumer.

> 
> # 24843. Internally may encode:
> 
> ```text
> event sequence / partition offset.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24844. Do not make consumer depend on backend internals.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24845. Cursor Expiry
> 
> If history compacted before consumer catches up:
> 
> ```text
> cursor invalid.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24846. Then:
> 
> ```text
> snapshot resync.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24847. This should be first-class protocol response.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24848. Example:
> 
> ```text
> RESYNC_REQUIRED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24849. Sync State
> 
> Per peer:
> 
> ```text
> last_sent
> last_received
> last_acknowledged
> last_snapshot
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24850. But ACK meaning matters.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24851. ACK_RECEIVED
> 
> Means:
> 
> ```text
> transport received.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24852. ACK_ACCEPTED
> 
> Means:
> 
> ```text
> semantic validation passed.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24853. ACK_MATERIALIZED
> 
> Means:
> 
> ```text
> included in local state.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24854. Different acknowledgements useful.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24855. Avoid:
> 
> ```text
> ACK = everything succeeded
> ```
> 
> ambiguity.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24856. Federation Retry
> 
> If remote unavailable:
> 
> ```text
> outbox retains message.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24857. Retry with:
> 
> ```text
> idempotency key.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24858. Poison Message
> 
> Repeatedly fails validation.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24859. Move to:
> 
> ```text
> dead-letter/quarantine.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24860. Do not block entire stream.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24861. Backpressure
> 
> If receiver slower:
> 
> ```text
> sender must not flood.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24862. Use:
> 
> ```text
> batching
> rate limits
> cursor flow control
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24863. Semantic Prioritization
> 
> Not all updates equal.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24864. Example:
> 
> ```text
> EMERGENCY_LOCK
> ```
> 
> higher urgency than:
> 
> ```text
> description metadata changed.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24865. But transport priority is not:
> 
> ```text
> truth priority.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24866. Need separate:
> 
> ```text
> delivery urgency
> ```
> 
> from:
> 
> ```text
> semantic authority.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24867. Critical Update Profile
> 
> Could include:
> 
> ```text
> must_deliver_fast
> short TTL
> requires ACK.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24868. Example:
> 
> ```text
> equipment unsafe.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24869. But real hard safety control should remain local.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24870. Federation notification is secondary.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24871. Eventual Consistency
> 
> Many shared knowledge domains can use:
> 
> ```text
> eventual consistency.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24872. Example:
> 
> ```text
> paper metadata
> capability catalog
> public project info.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24873. Stronger consistency needed for:
> 
> ```text
> reservation
> financial allocation
> exclusive lock
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24874. Therefore one consistency model is insufficient.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24875. Consistency Profiles
> 
> ```text
> EVENTUAL
> SESSION
> LEASED_EXCLUSIVE
> TRANSACTIONAL_LOCAL
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24876. EVENTUAL
> 
> Replicas converge eventually.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24877. SESSION
> 
> Client sees:
> 
> ```text
> its own writes / monotonic reads
> ```
> 
> where needed.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24878. LEASED_EXCLUSIVE
> 
> Temporary exclusive ownership.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24879. Example:
> 
> ```text
> machine reservation slot.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24880. TRANSACTIONAL_LOCAL
> 
> Strong transaction within one authority domain.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24881. Cross-org global transactions should be minimized.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24882. Better use:
> 
> ```text
> saga / reservation / confirmation.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24883. Example federated booking
> 
> ```text
> REQUEST
> ↓
> REMOTE HOLD
> ↓
> LOCAL ACCEPT
> ↓
> CONFIRM
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24884. If failure:
> 
> ```text
> release hold.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24885. Do not use distributed two-phase commit across organizations initially.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24886. It creates:
> 
> ```text
> tight coupling
> failure complexity.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24887. Saga semantics better.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24888. Ownership Lease
> 
> Temporary authority for:
> 
> ```text
> editing/execution
> ```
> 
> may be useful.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24889. Example:
> 
> ```text
> Agent A claims Action.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24890. Lease expires.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24891. Another agent can claim.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24892. Existing runtime already uses leases.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24893. State Fabric generalizes concept.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24894. Lease ≠ permanent ownership.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24895. Lease Clock
> 
> Expiry depends on time.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24896. Clock skew considerations apply.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24897. Use authoritative lease server/domain.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24898. Conflict-Free Actions
> 
> Some offline Actions can safely merge.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24899. Example:
> 
> ```text
> add note
> attach evidence
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24900. Exclusive Actions cannot.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24901. Example:
> 
> ```text
> approve payment
> reserve unique slot
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24902. Offline execution of exclusive Action may be forbidden.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24903. Therefore:
> 
> # Offline Authority Envelope
> 
> must specify:
> 
> ```text
> which mutation types allowed.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24904. Example field tablet:
> 
> ```text
> can record observation
> cannot approve purchase.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24905. Excellent safety/governance boundary.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24906. Local-First Observation
> 
> Physical edge node may create:
> 
> ```text
> Observation Event
> ```
> 
> offline.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24907. Later upload.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24908. Observation valid time remains:
> 
> ```text
> when observed.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24909. Knowledge time becomes:
> 
> ```text
> when federation learned it.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24910. Bitemporal model handles.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24911. Example
> 
> Sensor measured fault at:
> 
> ```text
> 10:00
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24912. Node reconnects:
> 
> ```text
> 12:00
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24913. Central system records:
> 
> ```text
> valid/occurred time 10:00
> knowledge time 12:00.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24914. This prevents historical distortion.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24915. Late Event
> 
> Event arrives after later events.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24916. Materialized state may need:
> 
> ```text
> recompute.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24917. Example calibration event arrives late.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24918. Historical query for 10:30 changes.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24919. Current state may or may not.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24920. This is why:
> 
> ```text
> event time
> +
> knowledge time
> ```
> 
> matter.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24921. Retrospective Correction
> 
> Source discovers old observation wrong.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24922. Do not edit old event.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24923. Create:
> 
> ```text
> CORRECTION / SUPERSESSION
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24924. Materializer re-evaluates.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24925. Historical audit preserves:
> 
> ```text
> what system believed at each knowledge time.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24926. This is extremely valuable for:
> 
> ```text
> scientific/legal/operational audit.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24927. Query Temporal Modes
> 
> Possible:
> 
> ```text
> VALID_AT
> KNOWN_AT
> CURRENT_BEST
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24928. `VALID_AT`
> 
> What state was valid for real-world time T?
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24929. `KNOWN_AT`
> 
> What did system know at time T?
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24930. `CURRENT_BEST`
> 
> What is current materialized interpretation?
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24931. Example
> 
> Useful for incident reconstruction.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24932. Temporal Query API
> 
> Conceptually:
> 
> ```text
> GET state?valid_at=...
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24933. Or:
> 
> ```text
> known_at=...
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24934. Not all derived views need perfect historical reconstruction in MVP.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24935. But event model should allow future support.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24936. Knowledge Synchronization Priority
> 
> Possible classes:
> 
> ```text
> CRITICAL_OPERATIONAL
> ACTIVE_PROJECT
> REFERENCE
> ARCHIVAL
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24937. CRITICAL_OPERATIONAL
> 
> Near-real-time.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24938. ACTIVE_PROJECT
> 
> Minutes/hours.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24939. REFERENCE
> 
> Daily/on-demand.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24940. ARCHIVAL
> 
> Low priority.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24941. This helps bandwidth-limited nodes.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24942. Mobile Synchronization
> 
> Phone may sync:
> 
> ```text
> current tasks
> required artifacts
> local map
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24943. Not whole repository.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24944. On Wi-Fi/charging:
> 
> ```text
> deeper cache sync.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24945. Good fit with compute fabric.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24946. Offline Knowledge Pack
> 
> Before field trip:
> 
> ```text
> download project subset.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24947. Include:
> 
> ```text
> procedures
> maps
> equipment profiles
> tasks
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24948. Later return:
> 
> ```text
> observations
> results
> photos/artifacts.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24949. This makes Virtual Technopark practical beyond permanent connectivity.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24950. Major milestone
> 
> К **24950** система становится:
> 
> # offline-capable semantic network
> 
> а не:
> 
> ```text
> cloud UI requiring permanent connection.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24951. Selective Knowledge Disclosure
> 
> Federation may answer:
> 
> ```text
> "Can you provide Capability X?"
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24952. Without exposing:
> 
> ```text
> how internally.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24953. This means synchronization can exchange:
> 
> ```text
> capability claims
> ```
> 
> without internal dependency graph.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24954. Great for commercial/federated autonomy.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24955. Remote Query
> 
> Instead of replication:
> 
> ```text
> QUERY → RESULT.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24956. Example:
> 
> ```text
> Find providers of Capability X
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24957. Node returns:
> 
> ```text
> authorized result set.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24958. Query federation reduces:
> 
> ```text
> data duplication.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24959. But increases:
> 
> ```text
> latency
> availability dependence.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24960. Hybrid model best:
> 
> ```text
> cache common/public metadata
> query sensitive/live state.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24961. Replicate vs Query Decision
> 
> Based on:
> 
> ```text
> freshness
> frequency
> sensitivity
> size
> availability needs
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24962. Example:
> 
> Capability taxonomy:
> 
> ```text
> replicate.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24963. Current machine slots:
> 
> ```text
> query/subscribe.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24964. Large proprietary dataset:
> 
> ```text
> do not replicate.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24965. Compute moves to dataset instead.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24966. Knowledge Locality
> 
> Some knowledge is:
> 
> ```text
> public
> organizational
> project-specific
> device-local
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24967. Similar to data locality.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24968. Semantic State itself has:
> 
> ```text
> locality constraints.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24969. Example:
> 
> ```text
> personal notes
> ```
> 
> may never enter shared federation.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24970. Public Claim may.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24971. Local Overlay
> 
> User/org can maintain:
> 
> ```text
> local annotations
> ```
> 
> over shared external object.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24972. Example external paper:
> 
> ```text
> global metadata
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24973. Organization adds:
> 
> ```text
> internal relevance note.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24974. Do not modify external source object.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24975. Use:
> 
> ```text
> local contextual Claim/Artifact.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24976. This is analogous to:
> 
> ```text
> overlay filesystem.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24977. Shared Base + Local Overlay
> 
> Powerful pattern:
> 
> ```text
> Public Knowledge
> +
> Organization Overlay
> +
> Project Overlay
> +
> Personal View
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24978. Same object can have:
> 
> ```text
> different context-specific annotations.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24979. Context layering
> 
> Potential:
> 
> ```text
> GLOBAL
> ORG
> PROGRAM
> PROJECT
> USER
> SCENARIO
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24980. But lower layer should not overwrite upper/base data.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24981. It can:
> 
> ```text
> augment
> override for local view
> ```
> 
> when semantically permitted.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24982. Example:
> 
> Global capability name:
> 
> ```text
> Optical Sensing
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24983. Project local alias:
> 
> ```text
> Skin Sensor Candidate
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24984. Alias ≠ global rename.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24985. Contextual Overrides
> 
> Use carefully for:
> 
> ```text
> display
> planning assumption
> local preference.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24986. Never silently override:
> 
> ```text
> external factual Claim.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24987. Instead create local competing claim.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24988. This keeps provenance.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24989. Knowledge Fork
> 
> Organization may create:
> 
> ```text
> local adapted procedure
> ```
> 
> from public procedure.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24990. It gets:
> 
> ```text
> new Artifact identity
> DERIVED_FROM
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24991. Good for open-source/open-knowledge workflow.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24992. Upstream Sync
> 
> Later public source updates.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24993. Local fork must decide:
> 
> ```text
> merge
> ignore
> review.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24994. Not automatic overwrite.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24995. Upstream Change Detection
> 
> System can alert:
> 
> ```text
> base artifact changed.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24996. Local dependency analysis identifies:
> 
> ```text
> affected forks/projects.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24997. Example:
> 
> Ontology v2 published.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24998. Local extension based on v1.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 24999. Compatibility review needed.
>
