> 
> # 25000. Major milestone
> 
> К **25000** появляется:
> 
> # Semantic Git-like capability
> 
> но не буквальный Git для всего.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25001. Для подходящих объектов система поддерживает:
> 
> ```text
> lineage
> fork
> diff
> merge proposal
> version
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25002. Для operational state:
> 
> ```text
> event sourcing
> ```
> 
> остаётся primary model.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25003. Для claims:
> 
> ```text
> append/supersede
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25004. Для files/code:
> 
> ```text
> artifact version graph.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25005. Для distributed sets:
> 
> ```text
> CRDT-like merge
> ```
> 
> где безопасно.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25006. One Model Does Not Fit All
> 
> Ключевой принцип.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25007. State Classes
> 
> Можно формализовать:
> 
> ```text
> EVENT_STREAM
> ASSERTION_SET
> VERSIONED_ARTIFACT
> MATERIALIZED_STATE
> EPHEMERAL_CACHE
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25008. EVENT_STREAM
> 
> Append-only.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25009. ASSERTION_SET
> 
> Claims/evidence.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25010. VERSIONED_ARTIFACT
> 
> Documents/code/models.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25011. MATERIALIZED_STATE
> 
> Current operational view.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25012. EPHEMERAL_CACHE
> 
> Rebuildable.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25013. Each has:
> 
> ```text
> different sync semantics.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25014. Excellent architecture boundary.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25015. Replication Contract
> 
> For each state class:
> 
> ```yaml
> replication:
>   mode: subscription
>   authority: source_org
>   merge: append_only
>   freshness: 60s
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25016. This allows semantic infrastructure to reason about:
> 
> ```text
> sync behavior.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25017. Storage Tiering
> 
> Data can live in:
> 
> ```text
> Hot
> Warm
> Cold
> Archive
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25018. Hot:
> 
> ```text
> active operational state.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25019. Warm:
> 
> ```text
> recent events/artifacts.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25020. Cold:
> 
> ```text
> older history.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25021. Archive:
> 
> ```text
> long-term retention.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25022. But tier ≠ importance.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25023. An old scientific Artifact may be:
> 
> ```text
> critical
> ```
> 
> yet stored cold because infrequently accessed.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25024. Retrieval layer abstracts.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25025. Storage Placement
> 
> Like compute placement:
> 
> ```text
> Artifact Requirement
> ↔ Storage Provider.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25026. Requirements:
> 
> ```text
> size
> durability
> latency
> privacy
> retention
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25027. This suggests future unified:
> 
> ```text
> Infrastructure Resolver.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25028. But current module focuses state synchronization.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25029. Content Caching
> 
> Popular artifacts replicated near consumers.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25030. Example:
> 
> ```text
> common model
> ```
> 
> cached at 10 edge nodes.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25031. Cache invalidation via:
> 
> ```text
> content hash/version.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25032. Immutable version artifacts simplify caching enormously.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25033. Best practice:
> 
> ```text
> new content
> → new version/hash
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25034. Mutable alias:
> 
> ```text
> latest
> ```
> 
> resolves to version.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25035. Never make:
> 
> ```text
> latest
> ```
> 
> the reproducibility identifier.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25036. Artifact Pinning
> 
> Project lock should pin:
> 
> ```text
> exact versions.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25037. Similar to package managers.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25038. `project.lock` can include:
> 
> ```text
> artifact hashes
> schema versions
> package versions.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25039. This extends reproducible project execution.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25040. Federated Project Lock
> 
> Could reference:
> 
> ```text
> remote capability contract version
> ```
> 
> rather than physical node.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25041. Example:
> 
> ```text
> Lab B:
> microscopy-profile v2
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25042. Actual provider node remains local detail.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25043. Knowledge Dependency Lock
> 
> Research synthesis might pin:
> 
> ```text
> paper versions
> dataset releases
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25044. Later updates trigger:
> 
> ```text
> review available

> 
> not silent synthesis change.

> 
> # 25045. This creates reproducible analytical state.

> 
> # 25046. Search Index Replication

> Full-text/vector indexes are:
> 
> ```text
> derived views.
> ```

> 
> # 25047. Do not replicate indexes as authoritative data necessarily.

> 
> # 25048. Rebuild locally when feasible.

> 
> # 25049. But large vector indexes may be expensive.

> 
> # 25050. Could distribute:

> ```text

> 
> later.

> different embeddings

> 
> for same Artifact.

> 
> # 25053. That's acceptable.

> 
> # 25054. Embedding model/version must be recorded.

> 
> # 25055. Vector search results are:
> 
> ```text
> derived retrieval output.

>

> 
> # 25056. Not canonical relation.

>

> # 25058. Search result completeness then limited.

> # 25059. UI must know:

> 
> # 25061. Very important for federation.

>

> Every search should know:
> 
> ```text
> LOCAL
> ORG

> GLOBAL_PUBLIC

> 
> where meaningful.

> 
> # 25063. Example:

>

>

> ↓

> Local Policy
> ↓

> ↓
> Commit

> Execution

> Event

> can be widely replicated.

> # 25203. Storage Architecture MVP
> 
> Можно начать с:
> 
> ```text
> PostgreSQL
> +
> Object Store
> +
> Transactional Outbox
> +
> Event Journal

> 
> # 25204. PostgreSQL хранит:
> 
> ```text
> canonical entities
> claims
> events
> sync cursors
> metadata

> # 25205. Object Store:
>

> large artifacts

> # 25208. Later, if scale demands:

> 
> adapter.

>

> 
> ```text
> semantic protocol
> must not depend
> on one message broker.

> ```text
> PostgreSQL.

> # 25217. Different storage engines,
>

>

> ```text
> subset.
> ```
>

>

> funding opportunity tables.

> 
> # 25220. But IDs/types remain interoperable.

>

> 
> ```text

> read_state

> # 25223. Event Outbox
> 
> Local transaction:
> 
> ```text

> +
> write outbox

> 
> atomically.

> ---
> 
> # 25224. Publisher later sends.

> 
> # 25225. This prevents:
> 
> ```text

>

> ```text

> ```
> 
> before materialization.

> 
> # 25227. Prevent duplicate processing.
>

> 
> # 25228. Existing runtime pattern reused.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25229. Sync Worker
> 
> Pseudo-flow:
> 
> ```text
> read outbox
> ↓
> build semantic envelope
> ↓
> send
> ↓
> receive ACK
> ↓
> mark delivered

> 
> ---
> 
> # 25230. Incoming:
> 
> ```text
> verify envelope
> ↓
> authorize source
> ↓
> schema validate
> ↓
> deduplicate
> ↓
> append import event
> ↓
> materialize
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25231. Import itself should be observable.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25232. Example Event:

# chatgpt response

Продолжаю с **25512**. Теперь строим технический слой полномочий: кто именно действует, от чьего имени, с каким scope, на какой срок, для какого Action и где проходит граница между **Capability** («умеет») и **Authority** («имеет право»).

> **Document: Zero-Trust Identity, Capability-Based Authorization, Delegation & Agent Security Fabric v0.1**
> 
> # Zero-Trust Identity, Capability-Based Authorization, Delegation & Agent Security Fabric v0.1
> 
> ## 25512. Главный переход
> 
> До сих пор Innovation OS уже знает:
> 
> ```text
> что Resource умеет делать
> ```
> 
> через:
> 
> ```text
> PROVIDES Capability
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25513. Но теперь нужен совершенно отдельный вопрос:
> 
> ```text
> ИМЕЕТ ЛИ Resource ПРАВО
> сделать это сейчас,
> в этом Context,
> над этим объектом?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25514. Это две разные системы
> 
> ```text
> Capability
> ≠
> Authority
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25515. Example
> 
> Agent технически способен:
> 
> ```text
> POST /applications/submit
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25516. Но его Authority может разрешать только:
> 
> ```text
> READ call
> CREATE draft
> VALIDATE proposal
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25517. Тогда:
> 
> ```text
> CAN_EXECUTE_TECHNICALLY = YES
> AUTHORIZED_TO_EXECUTE = NO
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25518. Это один из важнейших invariants всей архитектуры.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25519. Security Fabric должен отвечать минимум на семь вопросов
> 
> ```text
> WHO
> ACTS_FOR_WHOM
> MAY_DO_WHAT
> ON_WHICH_RESOURCE
> UNDER_WHICH_CONTEXT
> UNTIL_WHEN
> WITH_WHICH_CONSTRAINTS
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25520. Базовая схема
> 
> ```text
> Principal
> ↓
> Credential
> ↓
> Delegation
> ↓
> Authorization Policy
> ↓
> Action Request
> ↓
> Policy Decision
> ↓
> Enforcement
> ↓
> Audit Event
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25521. Principal
> 
> Principal — субъект, которому можно приписать действие.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25522. Principal types:
> 
> ```text
> PERSON
> AI_AGENT
> SERVICE
> DEVICE
> ORGANIZATION
> FEDERATION_NODE
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25523. Но не нужно вводить новый IIR root.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25524. Все они могут оставаться:
> 
> ```text
> RESOURCE subtypes
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25525. Principal ≠ Identity Record
> 
> Principal — логический субъект.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25526. Identity Record — способ подтвердить:
> 
> ```text
> кто этот субъект.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25527. Example
> 
> Один Person может иметь:
> 
> ```text
> local account
> GitHub identity
> OIDC identity
> hardware credential
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25528. Они принадлежат одному Principal,
> 
> но являются разными внешними identities.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25529. Existing:
> 
> ```text
> external_identities
> ```
> 
> можно расширить.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25530. Principal ID
> 
> Внутренний:
> 
> ```text
> UUID
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25531. Credential
> 
> Credential доказывает право заявить:
> 
> ```text
> I am Principal P
> ```
> 
> или:
> 
> ```text
> I am acting under delegation D
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25532. Credential types
> 
> ```text
> SESSION_TOKEN
> API_KEY
> OAUTH_TOKEN
> CERTIFICATE
> DEVICE_KEY
> SIGNED_CAPABILITY_TOKEN
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25533. Password не должен распространяться между agents/services.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25534. Лучше:
>

>

>

> 
> ```text
> Identity ≠ Authorization.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25536. Даже идеально подтверждённая личность:
>

> 
> ---
>

> 
> ```text
> Authentication Success

>

>

>

>

> # 25541. Capability-based Authorization
> 
> Термин здесь нужно отличать от:
> 
> ```text

> 
> # 25542. В security context capability token — это:
> 
> > ограниченное, передаваемое или непередаваемое право выполнить определённую операцию над определённым scope.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25543. Чтобы не путать понятия, внутри Innovation OS лучше использовать:
> 
> ```text

> AUTHORIZATION_CAPABILITY
> ```
> 
> на conceptual/API layer.
>

>

>

>   action: grant_application.draft
>   resource_scope: project-123
>   expires_at: 2026-10-01T00:00:00Z

>

>

> CREATE
> UPDATE

> APPROVE

> SUBMIT

> DELEGATE

>

> # 25548. И domain-specific verbs:
>

> START_EXPERIMENT

>

>

> ```
> 
> от:
> 
> ```text

> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25550. И:
>

> ```
>

> 
> ```text

> 
> ---
> 
> # 25551. Это особенно важно для AI agents.

> ---
> 
> # 25552. Agent может:
>

> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25553. Но не обязательно:

> 
> # 25554. Action Scope
> 
> Grant должен ограничивать:
> 
> ```text
> WHAT
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25555. Resource Scope
> 
> И:
> 
> ```text

> 
> ---
> 
> # 25556. Example:
> 
> ```yaml
> actions:
>   - READ
>   - COMMENT
> 
> resources:
>   project_ids:
>     - P1
>     - P2
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25557. Это не разрешает доступ:
> 
> ```text
> к Project P3.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25558. Context Scope
> 
> Authority может зависеть от Context.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25559. Example
> 
> Agent разрешено:
> 
> ```text
> DEPLOY
> ```
>

> 
> ```text

> 
> ---

> # 25560. Но не в:
>

> 
> ---
> 
> # 25561. Reality Scope
> 
> Особенно важно для digital twin:
> 
> ```text
> SIMULATED
> REAL
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25562. Example
> 
> Robot Agent может:
> 
> ```text
> CONTROL_DEVICE
> ```
> 
> в simulation.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25563. Но в real world:
> 
> ```text
> PROPOSE_CONTROL_ONLY.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25564. Это должен enforcement делать технически.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25565. Не prompt.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25566. Time Scope
> 
> Grant имеет:
> 
> ```text
> not_before
> expires_at
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25567. Default для agent delegation желательно:
> 
> ```text
> short-lived.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25568. Потому что long-lived authority увеличивает blast radius.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25569. Temporal Delegation Example
> 
> ```yaml
> delegation:
>   agent: funding-agent
>   actions:
>     - READ
>     - DRAFT
> 
>   expires_in: 8h
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25570. После expiry:
> 
> ```text
> DENY
> ```
> 
> даже если agent всё ещё работает.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25571. Budget Scope
> 
> Authority может иметь:
> 
> ```text
> max_cost
> max_quantity
> max_frequency
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25572. Example:
> 
> ```yaml
> constraints:
>   max_cost_eur: 100
>   max_equipment_hours: 2
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25573. Тогда agent может автоматически:
> 
> ```text
> reserve equipment
> ```
> 
> до лимита.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25574. Но:
> 
> ```text
> €101
> ```
> 
> требует новое approval.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25575. Это:
> 
> # Bounded Machine Agency
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25576. Bounded Agency
> 
> Можно определить как:
> 
> > способность автономно действовать внутри заранее заданного, технически enforceable envelope.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25577. Envelope включает:
> 
> ```text
> actions
> resources
> time
> cost
> risk
> context
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25578. Это намного безопаснее, чем:
> 
> ```text
> "Agent may manage project."
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25579. Generic permission слишком широк.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25580. Permission Envelope
> 
> ```yaml
> authority:
>   principal: agent-7
> 
>   allow:
>     - action: READ
>       scope: project-123
> 
>     - action: CREATE_DRAFT
>       scope: project-123
> 
>   deny:
>     - SUBMIT
>     - SIGN
>     - DELETE
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25581. Explicit deny может быть полезен для clarity.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25582. Но policy evaluator должен иметь:
> 
> ```text
> defined precedence rules.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25583. Default Deny
> 
> Zero-trust принцип:
> 
> ```text
> if permission is not established
> → DENY
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25584. Не:
> 
> ```text
> no rule means allow.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25585. UNKNOWN Authority ≠ Permission
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25586. Another critical invariant
> 
> ```text
> No Policy Match
> ≠
> ALLOW.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25587. Least Privilege
> 
> Agent получает:
> 
> ```text
> minimum permissions required
> for current task.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25588. Не весь набор прав пользователя.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25589. Example
> 
> Person может:
> 
> ```text
> manage entire organization.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25590. Но agent для одной задачи получает:
> 
> ```text
> READ project P
> CREATE proposal draft
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25591. Не:
> 
> ```text
> organization admin.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25592. Delegation Chain
> 
> Authority может идти:
> 
> ```text
> Organization
> ↓
> Person
> ↓
> Agent
> ↓
> Sub-agent
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25593. Но sub-agent не может получить:
> 
> ```text
> больше полномочий,
> чем delegator.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25594. Monotonic Restriction
> 
> Delegation chain должна только:
> 
> ```text
> preserve
> or
> reduce
> ```
> 
> authority.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25595. Не расширять.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25596. Формально:
> 
> ```text
> Authority(child)
> ⊆
> Authority(parent)
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25597. Excellent invariant.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25598. Example
> 
> Person can:
> 
> ```text
> READ
> DRAFT
> SUBMIT
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25599. Delegates Agent:
> 
> ```text
> READ
> DRAFT
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25600. Agent delegates Scout:
> 
> ```text
> READ
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25601. Scout cannot acquire:
> 
> ```text
> SUBMIT.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25602. Delegation Depth
> 
> Можно ограничить:
> 
> ```text
> max_delegation_depth
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25603. Example:
> 
> ```yaml
> delegation:
>   may_redelegate: false
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25604. Это особенно полезно для:
> 
> ```text
> external tools
> temporary agents
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25605. Delegation Purpose
> 
> Grant может быть связан с:
> 
> ```text
> specific Project
> Action
> Goal
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25606. Example:
> 
> ```text
> purpose = prepare funding application P
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25607. Потом agent не должен использовать те же права для:
> 
> ```text
> unrelated Project Q.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25608. Purpose Binding
> 
> Может быть policy condition:
> 
> ```yaml
> context:
>   project_id: P123
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25609. But purpose strings themselves weak.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25610. Лучше ссылаться на:
> 
> ```text
> canonical Project / Action UUID.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25611. Delegation Object
> 
> Application-level schema:
> 
> ```yaml
> delegation:
>   id: D123
>   issuer: principal-A
>   subject: agent-B
> 
>   actions:
>     - READ
>     - CREATE_DRAFT
> 
>   resource_scope:
>     project_id: P123
> 
>   expires_at: ...
> 
>   redelegation: false
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25612. Delegation Lifecycle
> 
> ```text
> PROPOSED
> ACTIVE
> SUSPENDED
> REVOKED
> EXPIRED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25613. REVOKED
> 
> Immediate policy state.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25614. But distributed systems create challenge:
> 
> ```text
> remote node may not know revocation yet.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25615. Therefore short-lived credentials matter.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25616. Revocation Strategies
> 
> ```text
> short TTL
> revocation list
> introspection
> push revocation
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25617. No single mechanism ideal for all environments.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25618. Online services can perform:
> 
> ```text
> live token introspection.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25619. Offline nodes need:
> 
> ```text
> short validity
> +
> local revocation snapshot
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25620. Offline Authority Problem
> 
> If credential is valid for 24h
> 
> but revoked centrally after 1h,
> 
> offline node may not know.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25621. Therefore high-risk offline credentials should have:
> 
> ```text
> very small authority envelope
> ```
> 
> and:
> 
> ```text
> short expiry.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25622. This is risk containment.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25623. Revocation ≠ Undo
> 
> If agent already:
> 
> ```text
> sent message
> purchased item
> started machine
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25624. Revoking authority does not reverse completed action.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25625. Critical invariant
> 
> ```text
> Revocation stops future authority,
> not historical effects.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25626. For reversible actions:
> 
> ```text
> compensating action
> ```
> 
> may exist.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25627. Existing saga semantics reused.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25628. Credential vs Delegation
> 
> Credential proves:
> 
> ```text
> holder / identity
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25629. Delegation defines:
> 
> ```text
> granted authority.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25630. Token may contain both,
> 
> but conceptually keep separate.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25631. Capability Token
> 
> A compact signed representation of:
> 
> ```text
> delegation scope.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25632. Example conceptual token:
> 
> ```text
> subject = agent-7
> action = reserve_equipment
> resource = microscope-class-A
> max_hours = 2
> expiry = 18:00
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25633. Resource server verifies:
> 
> ```text
> signature
> expiry
> scope
> issuer
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25634. It should not need:
> 
> ```text
> full conversation history.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25635. This is essential.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25636. Prompt ≠ Authorization
> 
> Never use:
> 
> ```text
> "You are allowed to..."
> ```
> 
> inside prompt as sole security boundary.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25637. Because model output is:
> 
> ```text
> not enforcement.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25638. Security must live:
> 
> ```text
> outside model
> ```
> 
> in:
> 
> ```text
> policy enforcement layer.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25639. Tool Invocation Gate
> 
> Every side-effecting tool call:
> 
> ```text
> Agent Request
> ↓
> Authorization Check
> ↓
> Policy Decision
> ↓
> Tool Execution
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25640. Model cannot bypass gate by:
> 
> ```text
> generating different text.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25641. Enforcement Point
> 
> Could exist:
> 
> ```text
> API gateway
> tool broker
> device adapter
> resource service
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25642. Best architecture:
> 
> ```text
> distributed enforcement
> +
> central/shared policy semantics.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25643. Because remote node controls its own Resource.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25644. Policy Decision Point
> 
> Evaluates:
> 
> ```text
> principal
> action
> resource
> context
> delegation
> risk
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25645. Policy Enforcement Point
> 
> Actually:
> 
> ```text
> ALLOW
> DENY
> REQUIRE_APPROVAL
> ```
> 
> before Action.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25646. Existing governance effects reused:
> 
> ```text
> ALLOW
> DENY
> REQUIRE_APPROVAL
> REQUIRE_REVIEW
> REQUIRE_EVIDENCE
> REQUIRE_SIMULATION
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25647. Great reuse.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25648. Security Layer should not invent parallel policy vocabulary unnecessarily.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25649. High-Risk Actions
> 
> Examples:
> 
> ```text
> SEND_EXTERNAL_MESSAGE
> SUBMIT_APPLICATION
> PAY
> DELETE
> DEPLOY_PRODUCTION
> CONTROL_PHYSICAL_DEVICE
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25650. They may require:
> 
> ```text
> fresh authority
> strong authentication
> human approval
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25651. Low-Risk Actions
> 
> ```text
> read public artifact
> run local simulation
> create draft
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25652. Could use broader bounded autonomy.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25653. Risk Classification
> 
> Risk belongs to:
> 
> ```text
> Action + Context
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25654. Not agent globally.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25655. Same agent can perform:
> 
> ```text
> low-risk search
> ```
> 
> and:
> 
> ```text
> high-risk purchase.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25656. Therefore:
> 
> ```text
> Agent Risk Level
> ```
> 
> as one global scalar is weak.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25657. Action Risk Profile
> 
> Could include:
> 
> ```text
> financial
> physical
> privacy
> security
> irreversibility
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25658. Example
> 
> ```yaml
> risk:
>   physical: high
>   financial: low
>   reversible: false
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25659. Approval policy can use.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25660. Irreversibility
> 
> Key security dimension.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25661. Actions:
> 
> ```text
> READ
> ```
> 
> usually low irreversibility.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25662.
> 
> ```text
> DELETE_WITHOUT_BACKUP
> ```
> 
> high.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25663.
> 
> ```text
> SEND_EMAIL
> ```
> 
> externally irreversible in practical sense.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25664. Draft email:
> 
> ```text
> reversible.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25665. This naturally supports:
> 
> ```text
> draft-first agent design.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25666. Staged Authority
> 
> Agent can progress:
> 
> ```text
> READ
> ↓
> PROPOSE
> ↓
> DRAFT
> ↓
> REQUEST_APPROVAL
> ↓
> EXECUTE
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25667. Not jump directly:
> 
> ```text
> READ → EXECUTE.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25668. This is especially useful for:
> 
> ```text
> new/unverified agents.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25669. Agent Trust State
> 
> Avoid universal trust score.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25670. Better track:
> 
> ```text
> verified capabilities
> allowed action scopes
> incident history
> current credential state
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25671. Agent may be technically excellent
> 
> but intentionally restricted.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25672. Authority should never be inferred from:
> 
> ```text
> benchmark performance.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25673. Capability Evidence ≠ Authorization Evidence
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25674. Agent Identity
> 
> Logical agent identity should persist across:
> 
> ```text
> process restarts
> node migrations
> model changes
> ```
> 
> where appropriate.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25675. But model version changes may alter:
> 
> ```text
> technical capability profile.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25676. Therefore:
> 
> ```text
> Agent Identity
> ≠
> Agent Runtime Instance
> ≠
> Model Version
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25677. Agent Principal
> 
> Could have:
> 
> ```text
> agent_id
> owner_org
> runtime_instances
> delegations
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25678. Runtime Instance gets:
> 
> ```text
> short-lived credential.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25679. If process compromised:
> 
> ```text
> revoke instance credential.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25680. Logical agent can later restart with new instance.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25681. Device Identity
> 
> Device itself may be Principal.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25682. Example robot controller signs:
> 
> ```text
> measurement event
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25683. Device identity proves:
> 
> ```text
> which registered device emitted event.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25684. Not:
> 
> ```text
> measurement scientifically correct.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25685. Again:
> 
> ```text
> Identity ≠ Correctness.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25686. Service Identity
> 
> Microservice/workers should authenticate as:
> 
> ```text
> services
> ```
> 
> not share human account.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25687. Example:
> 
> ```text
> worker-document-extractor
> ```
> 
> gets:
> 
> ```text
> read input artifact
> write extraction artifact
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25688. Not:
> 
> ```text
> admin database.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25689. This limits blast radius.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25690. Workload Identity
> 
> Interesting extension:
> 
> Each workload execution may have:
> 
> ```text
> ephemeral execution identity.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25691. It inherits only permissions needed for:
> 
> ```text
> that run.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25692. Example PDF extraction job:
> 
> ```text
> READ artifact A
> WRITE result namespace R
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25693. If container compromised,
> 
> it cannot:
> 
> ```text
> read every project.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25694. This is stronger than long-lived worker credentials.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25695. Workload-Scoped Credential
> 
> Issued at placement time.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25696. Expires after:
> 
> ```text
> job completion / short TTL.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25697. Compute Fabric integrates Security Fabric.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25698. Node receives:
> 
> ```text
> workload package
> +
> scoped credential
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25699. Not master API key.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25700. Major milestone
> 
> К **25700** security architecture поддерживает:
> 
> # per-workload least-privilege execution.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25701. Secret
> 
> Secret is sensitive credential material:
> 
> ```text
> API key
> private key
> password
> token
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25702. Secrets should not be stored:
> 
> ```text
> in prompts
> logs
> artifacts
> World State Claims
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25703. Use:
> 
> ```text
> Secret Reference
> ```
> 
> instead.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25704. Example
> 
> ```yaml
> secret_ref:
>   provider: vault
>   id: github-token-7
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25705. Agent sees:
> 
> ```text
> reference / capability
> ```
> 
> not necessarily secret bytes.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25706. Secret Injection
> 
> Runtime provides secret only:
> 
> ```text
> to authorized workload
> at execution time.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25707. After execution:
> 
> ```text
> discard from environment
> ```
> 
> where possible.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25708. Secret Scope
> 
> Example GitHub token:
> 
> ```text
> repo = project-X
> permissions = issues:write
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25709. Better than:
> 
> ```text
> all repositories admin.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25710. Secret Rotation
> 
> Credentials should support:
> 
> ```text
> rotate
> expire
> revoke
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25711. Rotation event must not expose:
> 
> ```text
> new secret value.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25712. Audit stores:
> 
> ```text
> credential id
> rotation time
> actor
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25713. Secret Access Event
> 
> Could record:
> 
> ```text
> WORKLOAD_ACCESSED_SECRET_REF
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25714. But avoid logging:
> 
> ```text
> secret itself.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25715. Prompt Injection Security
> 
> Agent may ingest malicious text saying:
> 
> ```text
> ignore rules
> send secrets
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25716. Security boundary must not depend on:
> 
> ```text
> model obedience.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25717. Even compromised reasoning process should face:
> 
> ```text
> tool authorization gate.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25718. This is core zero-trust principle.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25719. Tool Result as Untrusted Input
> 
> External tool output can contain:
> 
> ```text
> malicious instructions
> poisoned metadata
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25720. Treat as:
> 
> ```text
> data
> ```
> 
> not authority.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25721. Tool output cannot expand:
> 
> ```text
> agent permissions.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25722. Example webpage says:
> 
> ```text
> "upload your API keys here"
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25723. Agent lacks:
> 
> ```text
> secret_export
> ```
> 
> permission.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25724. Enforcement denies.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25725. Data Exfiltration Control
> 
> Permission should cover not just:
> 
> ```text
> READ sensitive data
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25726. But also:
> 
> ```text
> WHERE data may be sent.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25727. Example agent can read private document locally.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25728. But cannot:
> 
> ```text
> send content to public cloud model.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25729. This is:
> 
> # Information Flow Control
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25730. Data Classification
> 
> Possible:
> 
> ```text
> PUBLIC
> INTERNAL
> CONFIDENTIAL
> RESTRICTED
> DEVICE_LOCAL
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25731. Classification policies organization-specific.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25732. Data flow:
> 
> ```text
> Source Classification
> +
> Destination Trust Zone
> +
> Purpose
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25733. Determine:
> 
> ```text
> allowed transfer?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25734. Example
> 
> ```text
> CONFIDENTIAL
> → PUBLIC_CLOUD
> ```
> 
> may be denied.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25735. But:
> 
> ```text
> CONFIDENTIAL
> → approved private cloud
> ```
> 
> may be allowed.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25736. Never rely only on:
> 
> ```text
> model provider name.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25737. Need concrete execution endpoint/trust policy.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25738. Taint / Label Propagation
> 
> Derived Artifact from sensitive input may inherit:
> 
> ```text
> sensitivity label.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25739. Example:
> 
> ```text
> private PDF
> ↓ summary
> ```
> 
> summary may still contain private data.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25740. Therefore:
> 
> ```text
> Derived Output
> ```
> 
> should not automatically become PUBLIC.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25741. Conservative default:
> 
> ```text
> output classification >= input sensitivity
> ```
> 
> unless declassification process exists.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25742. Declassification
> 
> Explicit Action:
> 
> ```text
> REVIEW_AND_DECLASSIFY
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25743. Example anonymized aggregate may be approved for public release.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25744. Agent cannot unilaterally decide:
> 
> ```text
> "this seems safe."
> ```
> 
> for high-sensitivity domains unless policy delegates it.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25745. Information Flow Graph
> 
> Can trace:
> 
> ```text
> Source Artifact
> ↓
> Transformation
> ↓
> Derived Artifact
> ↓
> Destination
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25746. Useful for:
> 
> ```text
> privacy
> audit
> incident response.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25747. Security Provenance
> 
> Every sensitive side effect should know:
> 
> ```text
> principal
> delegator
> credential
> action
> resource
> time
> result
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25748. Audit Event
> 
> Append-only:
> 
> ```yaml
> audit:
>   principal: agent-B
>   action: CREATE_DRAFT
>   resource: proposal-P
>   decision: ALLOW
>   policy_version: ...
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25749. Denied attempts should also be audit-able.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25750. But audit data can itself be sensitive.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25751. Audit Access Policy
> 
> Not every user should see:
> 
> ```text
> all security events.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25752. Auditors may have:
> 
> ```text
> READ_AUDIT
> ```
> 
> separately.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25753. Security Log ≠ General Analytics Log
> 
> Avoid copying:
> 
> ```text
> tokens
> credentials
> sensitive payloads
> ```
> 
> into broad analytics.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25754. Audit Immutability
> 
> High-value events should be:
> 
> ```text
> append-only
> tamper-evident
> ```
> 
> where possible.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25755. But immutability must coexist with:
> 
> ```text
> privacy deletion requirements.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25756. Therefore audit should minimize personal/sensitive payloads.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25757. Store identifiers/reference,
> 
> not unnecessary content.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25758. Human Approval
> 
> Approval is:
> 
> ```text
> Decision
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25759. UI button press alone should create:
> 
> ```text
> authenticated signed/recorded Decision event.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25760. Approval must specify:
> 
> ```text
> what exactly is approved.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25761. Example poor:
> 
> ```text
> Approve
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25762. Better:
> 
> ```text
> Approve submission of Proposal v7
> to Call C
> before deadline D
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25763. Approval Binding
> 
> Bind approval to:
> 
> ```text
> artifact hash/version
> action
> resource
> context
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25764. If proposal changes after approval:
> 
> ```text
> approval may no longer apply.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25765. Critical invariant
> 
> ```text
> Approval of v7
> ≠
> Approval of v8.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25766. This is crucial for agent-generated drafts.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25767. Approval Window
> 
> Could expire:
> 
> ```text
> after N hours
> ```
> 
> or after:
> 
> ```text
> material change.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25768. Material Change Detection
> 
> Examples:
> 
> ```text
> recipient changed
> amount changed
> attachment changed
> terms changed
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25769. Then:
> 
> ```text
> REAPPROVAL_REQUIRED.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25770. Approval Replay Attack
> 
> Old approval reused for new action.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25771. Prevent with:
> 
> ```text
> nonce
> action id
> artifact hash
> expiry
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25772. Two-Person Rule
> 
> Some actions may require:
> 
> ```text
> 2 independent approvers.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25773. Example:
> 
> ```text
> high-value payment
> production safety override.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25774. Policy:
> 
> ```text
> REQUIRE_APPROVAL(count=2)
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25775. Independence matters.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25776. Same person using two accounts should not satisfy.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25777. Approver identities resolved to Principals.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25778. Separation of Duties
> 
> Roles:
> 
> ```text
> REQUESTER
> APPROVER
> EXECUTOR
> REVIEWER
> AUDITOR
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25779. High-risk flow may require:
> 
> ```text
> Requester ≠ Approver
> Builder ≠ Reviewer
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25780. Existing governance principle reused.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25781. Conflict of Roles
> 
> One Principal may hold multiple roles generally.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25782. But specific Action policy can require:
> 
> ```text
> distinct principals.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25783. Example:
> 
> ```text
> Agent builds package
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25784. Independent verifier checks.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25785. Verification Authority
> 
> Verifier needs:
> 
> ```text
> VERIFY
> ```
> 
> permission.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25786. But verifier should not necessarily:
> 
> ```text
> DEPLOY.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25787. This limits self-certification.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25788. Self-Approval
> 
> Default for high-risk actions:
> 
> ```text
> not allowed.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25789. But low-risk fully automated pipeline may allow:
> 
> ```text
> machine verification
> +
> preauthorized execution.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25790. Context dependent.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25791. Delegated Approval
> 
> Person can delegate approval authority?
> 
> Potentially yes,
> 
> but only if policy allows.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25792. Example:
> 
> ```text
> manager → procurement officer
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25793. But:
> 
> ```text
> agent → itself
> ```
> 
> cannot manufacture authority.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25794. Authority Provenance Chain
> 
> Every grant can answer:
> 
> ```text
> where did this authority originate?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25795. Example:
> 
> ```text
> Organization Charter
> ↓
> Role Assignment
> ↓
> Person Delegation
> ↓
> Agent Token
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25796. If chain breaks:
> 
> ```text
> DENY.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25797. This is:
> 
> # Authority Lineage
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25798. Similar to data provenance,
> 
> but for permissions.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25799. Root of Authority
> 
> May be:
> 
> ```text
> organization governance
> resource owner
> legal mandate
> system administrator
> ```
> 
> depending domain.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25800. Security Fabric does not determine legal legitimacy itself.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25801. It records:
> 
> ```text
> declared authority source.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25802. External legal validity may require:
> 
> ```text
> legal verification.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25803. Federation Authorization
> 
> Remote organization requests:
> 
> ```text
> Action X
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25804. Local organization evaluates:
> 
> ```text
> remote identity
> agreement
> local policy
> resource state
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25805. Remote side cannot send:
> 
> ```text
> "I authorize myself."
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25806. Critical invariant
> 
> ```text
> Remote Delegation
> cannot override
> Local Authority.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25807. Federation Pattern
> 
> ```text
> Remote Request
> ↓
> Federated Identity Check
> ↓
> Contract/Agreement Check
> ↓
> Local Policy Decision
> ↓
> Local Execution
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25808. This mirrors earlier federation model.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25809. Federation Identity
> 
> Possible mechanisms:
> 
> ```text
> OIDC federation
> mTLS certificates
> signed organization credentials
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25810. Implementation can vary.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25811. Semantic layer only needs:
> 
> ```text
> verified external Principal
> +
> trust domain
> +
> claims.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25812. Organization Credential
> 
> Could attest:
> 
> ```text
> Principal P belongs to Organization O
> with Role R
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25813. Receiving node may accept:
> 
> ```text
> membership assertion
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25814. But still maps role to:
> 
> ```text
> local permissions.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25815. External Role ≠ Local Permission
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25816. Example remote:
> 
> ```text
> Lab Administrator
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25817. Local policy may allow only:
> 
> ```text
> booking requests.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25818. Role names are not globally authoritative.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25819. Attribute-Based Access Control
> 
> Useful where permission depends on:
> 
> ```text
> role
> organization
> project
> risk
> resource state
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25820. Example:
> 
> ```text
> ALLOW reserve
> IF
> role = researcher
> AND
> training_verified = true
> AND
> machine_state = available
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25821. This is ABAC-like.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25822. Role-Based Access Control
> 
> RBAC remains useful for stable roles.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25823. Capability token useful for:
> 
> ```text
> specific delegated action.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25824. Best system may combine:
> 
> ```text
> RBAC
> +
> ABAC
> +
> capability grants.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25825. Avoid ideological "one authorization model only."
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25826. Role Assignment
> 
> Role itself should be:
> 
> ```text
> time-bounded / scoped
> ```
> 
> where needed.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25827. Example:
> 
> ```text
> Project Reviewer for P123
> ```
> 
> not organization-wide reviewer.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25828. Resource Ownership
> 
> Ownership does not automatically imply:
> 
> ```text
> unlimited operational authority.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25829. Example company owns machine,
> 
> but safety rules still constrain use.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25830. Therefore:
> 
> ```text
> Ownership ≠ Unlimited Authority.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25831. Safety Constraints can override owner preference.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25832. Local safety controller remains final physical gate.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25833. Physical Control Chain
> 
> ```text
> Agent Intent
> ↓
> Authorization
> ↓
> Safety Policy
> ↓
> Device Controller
> ↓
> Physical Action
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25834. Agent never writes directly:
> 
> ```text
> motor PWM
> ```
> 
> through semantic layer.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25835. Device Adapter exposes:
> 
> ```text
> typed safe actions.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25836. Example:
> 
> ```text
> MOVE_TO_POSE
> ```
> 
> not arbitrary memory/register access.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25837. Safety Envelope
> 
> Adapter may enforce:
> 
> ```text
> workspace
> speed
> force
> temperature
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25838. Even authorized agent cannot violate:
> 
> ```text
> hardware safety limits.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25839. Authorization ≠ Safety
> 
> Another invariant:
> 
> ```text
> Allowed Action
> ≠
> Physically Safe Action.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25840. Both checks required.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25841. Security vs Safety
> 
> Security asks:
> 
> ```text
> is actor allowed?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25842. Safety asks:
> 
> ```text
> can action be executed safely?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25843. Verification asks:
> 
> ```text
> did it achieve intended outcome?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25844. Three different layers.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25845. Example:
> 
> Authorized technician starts experiment.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25846. Safety interlock detects door open.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25847. Action denied physically.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25848. Authorization remains valid,
> 
> but execution blocked.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25849. Excellent separation.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25850. Credential Storage
> 
> Human credentials:
> 
> ```text
> password hashes
> MFA records
> hardware keys
> ```
> 
> belong to identity subsystem.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25851. Agents should ideally use:
> 
> ```text
> non-human service credentials.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25852. Do not let agent impersonate human by storing:
> 
> ```text
> human password.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25853. Acting On Behalf Of
> 
> Audit should say:
> 
> ```text
> Agent A
> acting_on_behalf_of
> Person P
> ```
> 
> where delegation exists.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25854. Not:
> 
> ```text
> Person P performed the action.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25855. This distinction is critical.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25856. Example email sent by agent:
> 
> ```text
> actor = agent
> delegator = person
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25857. Provenance should preserve both.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25858. Attribution
> 
> Possible fields:
> 
> ```text
> requested_by
> approved_by
> executed_by
> delegated_by
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25859. They may all differ.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25860. Example:
> 
> ```text
> Person A requests
> Person B approves
> Agent C executes
> Service D sends
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25861. Security model must handle this naturally.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25862. Autonomous Agent Budget
> 
> Agent authority can include:
> 
> ```text
> max_actions
> max_cost
> max_duration
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25863. Example:
> 
> ```yaml
> limits:
>   api_calls: 1000
>   spend_eur: 20
>   runtime_hours: 4
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25864. Exceed:
> 
> ```text
> SUSPEND / REQUEST_EXTENSION
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25865. This prevents runaway loops.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25866. Rate Limit
> 
> Permission may allow:
> 
> ```text
> SEND_MESSAGE
> ```
> 
> but only:
> 
> ```text
> 5/hour.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25867. This reduces:
> 
> ```text
> spam / accidental flood.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25868. Recipient Scope
> 
> Messaging agent may have:
> 
> ```text
> approved recipient list
> ```
> 
> or:
> 
> ```text
> organization domain scope.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25869. Example:
> 
> ```text
> draft to anyone
> send only internal recipients
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25870. Very useful staged autonomy pattern.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25871. External Communication Authority
> 
> Separate capabilities:
> 
> ```text
> DRAFT_MESSAGE
> SEND_INTERNAL
> SEND_EXTERNAL
> PUBLISH_PUBLIC
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25872. Do not collapse into:
> 
> ```text
> WRITE.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25873. Public Publishing
> 
> High visibility.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25874. May require:
> 
> ```text
> approval
> brand/compliance checks
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25875. Again machine-enforced.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25876. Financial Authority
> 
> Separate verbs:
> 
> ```text
> VIEW_BUDGET
> PROPOSE_EXPENSE
> RESERVE_FUNDS
> APPROVE_EXPENSE
> EXECUTE_PAYMENT
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25877. Agent may:
> 
> ```text
> propose
> ```
> 
> without:
> 
> ```text
> pay.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25878. Payment credentials especially should be:
> 
> ```text
> isolated
> short-lived
> transaction-scoped
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25879. Transaction Binding
> 
> Credential can specify:
> 
> ```text
> recipient
> amount limit
> currency
> purpose
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25880. Example:
> 
> ```yaml
> payment_authority:
>   max_amount: 50
>   currency: EUR
>   recipient: supplier-X
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25881. Changing recipient invalidates authority.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25882. Financial transaction data must be audited carefully.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25883. But full financial system is beyond current module.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25884. Package Deployment Authority
> 
> Separate:
> 
> ```text
> INSTALL_SANDBOX
> INSTALL_PRODUCTION
> ACTIVATE
> ROLLBACK
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25885. Agent may be allowed:
> 
> ```text
> sandbox install
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25886. Production activation:
> 
> ```text
> requires approval.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25887. This connects Semantic Package Manager.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25888. Package Signing
> 
> Approved package Artifact can be signed.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25889. Deployment system verifies:
> 
> ```text
> package identity
> hash
> signature
> approval
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25890. But signature alone does not prove package secure.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25891. Security tests remain separate.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25892. Model Deployment
> 
> Model Artifact should also have:
> 
> ```text
> approved version.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25893. Agent cannot silently switch:
> 
> ```text
> model v3 → unknown v4
> ```
> 
> for critical workflow.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25894. Model change may require:
> 
> ```text
> capability revalidation.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25895. This protects against behavioral drift.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25896. Agent Self-Modification
> 
> Very sensitive.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25897. Agent may propose:
> 
> ```text
> new prompt
> new tool
> new model
> new package
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25898. But activation should depend on:
> 
> ```text
> change authority.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25899. Artificial Technological Awareness can suggest self-improvement.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25900. It does not automatically grant itself:
> 
> ```text
> permission to modify itself.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25901. Critical invariant
> 
> ```text
> Self-Awareness
> ≠
> Self-Authorization.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 25902. Another:
> 
> ```text
> Self-Improvement Proposal
> ≠
> Self-Deployment.

> # 26082. Ephemeral Conversation Authority
> 
> Single command may authorize:
> 
> ```text
> one action
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26083. Example:
> 
> ```text
> "Send this email."
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26084. Creates one-shot authority:
> 
> ```text
> SEND message M
> to recipient R
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26085. Not permanent:
> 
> ```text
> SEND_EMAIL_ANYWHERE.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26086. One-Shot Token
> 
> Consumed after successful Action.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26087. Excellent for:
> 
> ```text
> payments
> messages
> deletion
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26088. Replay attempts denied.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26089. Persistent Agent Mandate
> 
> Separate object.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26090. Example:
> 
> ```text
> Monitor project inbox
> and create drafts.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26091. Persistent mandate may allow:
> 
> ```text
> READ incoming
> CREATE draft
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26092. But not send.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26093. Mandate has:
> 
> ```text
> scope
> schedule
> expiry
> revocation.

> # 26094. Automation integration natural.

> must propagate.

>

> 
> # 26110. Confused Deputy Problem
> 
> Service with broad rights may be tricked by less privileged caller.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26111. Example:
> 
> ```text
> file service
> ```
> 
> has access to all files.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26112. Agent asks it to fetch:
> 
> ```text
> unauthorized file.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26113. Service must authorize based on:
> 
> ```text
> caller context
> ```
> 
> not only its own permissions.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26114. Critical security invariant:
> 
> ```text
> Service Authority
> ≠
> Caller Authority.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26115. On-Behalf-Of Token
> 
> Useful:
> 
> ```text
> service acts for caller
> ```
> 
> with attenuated scope.

> 
> # 26116. Prevents confused deputy.
> 
> ---

> # 26117. Delegation Across Services
> 
> ```text
> User
> → Agent
> → Tool Broker
> → External Service

> # 26119. But external services may support different auth models.

>

> 
> # 26121. External Scope Verification
> 
> If connector token has broader external permissions than internal grant:
> 
> ```text
> internal broker must still enforce narrower scope.
> ```

> ---
> 
> # 26122. Because external API key may be:
> 
> ```text
> overprivileged.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26123. Long term better:
> 
> ```text
> external least-privilege credentials.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26124. But adapters provide containment.
> 
> ---
>

> ```
> 
> vs:
> 
> ```text
> Personal GitHub Account.

> # 26127. Same connector ≠ same authority scope.

> 
> # 26131. MHS/device safety layer answers:
> 
> ```text
> whether requested physical operation is allowed/safe.

> 
> # 26132. Semantic M2M handles:
> 
> ```text
> state/context exchange.

> ```text

> 
> для длительного расследования
> 
> или:
> 
> ```text
> Context + Events + Actions + Claims
> ```
> 
> для компактного случая.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26415. MVP лучше использовать:
> 
> ```text
> Incident application object
> ```
> 
> со ссылками на canonical IIR.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26416. Incident Lifecycle
> 
> ```text
> DETECTED
> TRIAGED
> INVESTIGATING
> MITIGATING
> RECOVERING
> VERIFYING
> RESOLVED
> CLOSED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26417. `RESOLVED` ≠ `CLOSED`
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26418. RESOLVED:
> 
> ```text
> service/capability restored.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26419. CLOSED:
> 
> ```text
> investigation/documentation completed.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26420. Также:
> 
> ```text
> MITIGATED ≠ FIXED.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26421. Example
> 
> Primary database broken.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26422. Failover restores service.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26423. Incident:
> 
> ```text
> MITIGATED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26424. Primary defect still exists.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26425. Поэтому remediation может иметь:
> 
> ```text
> temporary mitigation
> permanent correction
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26426. Incident Detection Sources
> 
> ```text
> metric threshold
> log pattern
> trace error
> event rule
> verification failure
> human report
> agent observation
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26427. Detection source itself has:
> 
> ```text
> provenance.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26428. Example
> 
> ```text
> ALERT: queue > 1000
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26429. Это Observation.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26430. Не обязательно Incident.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26431. Critical invariant
> 
> ```text
> Alert ≠ Incident.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26432. Alert может быть:
> 
> ```text
> false positive
> expected spike
> duplicate symptom
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26433. Alert Correlation
> 
> Multiple alerts:
> 
> ```text
> GPU unavailable
> model service timeout
> agent workflow failure
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26434. Могут принадлежать:
> 
> ```text
> one Incident.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26435. Но correlation ≠ causation.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26436. Incident Correlator должен использовать:
> 
> ```text
> time
> dependency graph
> shared resource
> common changes
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26437. Example
> 
> 20 services fail within 30 seconds.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26438. They all depend on:
> 
> ```text
> Identity Provider.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26439. Strong incident grouping candidate.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26440. Semantic Correlation
> 
> Technical identifiers map to semantic objects.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26441. Example trace:
> 
> ```text
> service=embedding-worker
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26442. Semantic registry knows:
> 
> ```text
> Resource R-188
> PROVIDES EMBEDDING_CAPABILITY.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26443. Therefore trace can be connected to:
> 
> ```text
> Capability
> Actions
> Projects.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26444. Resource Instrumentation Contract
> 
> Each runtime component should expose:
> 
> ```text
> resource_id
> service_id
> workload_id
> action_id
> trace_id
> ```
> 
> where applicable.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26445. This is crucial.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26446. Без semantic identifiers observability остаётся:
> 
> ```text
> технической телеметрией.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26447. Trace Context
> 
> Distributed request propagates:
> 
> ```text
> trace_id
> span_id
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26448. Innovation OS добавляет:
> 
> ```text
> project_id
> action_id
> capability_id
> context_id
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26449. Не все поля должны передаваться каждой внешней системе.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26450. Privacy/minimization still applies.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26451. Semantic Trace
> 
> Можно представить:
> 
> ```text
> Mission
> ↓
> Program
> ↓
> Project
> ↓
> Action
> ↓
> Workload
> ↓
> Service
> ↓
> Node
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26452. Это создаёт:
> 
> # Vertical Traceability
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26453. Обычный distributed trace идёт:
> 
> ```text
> service → service → database
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26454. Semantic trace идёт ещё выше:
> 
> ```text
> database call
> → Action
> → Project
> → Mission.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26455. Это принципиально новый уровень.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26456. Example
> 
> ```text
> POST /embedding
> 500
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26457. Semantic interpretation:
> 
> ```text
> Research Synthesis Action A17 failed.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26458. Further:
> 
> ```text
> Project P4 blocked.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26459. Further:
> 
> ```text
> Milestone M2 may slip.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26460. `may slip` — inference.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26461. Нужно маркировать:
> 
> ```text
> FACT
> INFERENCE
> HYPOTHESIS.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26462. Incident Knowledge Model
> 
> Minimum:
> 
> ```text
> observations
> symptoms
> affected resources
> affected capabilities
> candidate causes
> mitigations
> verification
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26463. Symptom
> 
> Observed undesirable state.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26464. Cause Candidate
> 
> Claim:
> 
> ```text
> X may have caused Y.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26465. Root Cause
> 
> Не должен назначаться автоматически без sufficient evidence.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26466. Critical invariant
> 
> ```text
> Most Correlated Event
> ≠
> Root Cause.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26467. Example
> 
> Deployment happened 1 minute before outage.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26468. Это:
> 
> ```text
> candidate causal factor.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26469. Need check:
> 
> ```text
> did affected path use changed component?
> did rollback restore service?
> did reproducer confirm?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26470. Root Cause Confidence
> 
> Лучше не один arbitrary score.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26471. Show evidence dimensions:
> 
> ```text
> temporal alignment
> dependency relevance
> reproduction
> rollback response
> counterevidence
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26472. Example:
> 
> ```text
> Candidate A
> - occurred before failure
> - directly changed dependency
> - rollback restored service
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26473. Stronger than:
> 
> ```text
> confidence = 0.83
> ```
> 
> без объяснения.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26474. Root Cause Candidate States
> 
> ```text
> PROPOSED
> SUPPORTED
> CONTRADICTED
> CONFIRMED
> REJECTED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26475. CONFIRMED should require:
> 
> ```text
> defined verification criteria.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26476. Example
> 
> Bug reproduced under same condition.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26477. Or:
> 
> ```text
> fix removes failure
> while other conditions unchanged.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26478. But distributed systems may have:
> 
> ```text
> multiple contributing causes.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26479. Поэтому:
> 
> ```text
> Root Cause ≠ necessarily single cause.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26480. Incident Causal Graph
> 
> ```text
> Config Change
> ↓
> Memory Leak
> ↓
> Worker Crash
> ↓
> Queue Growth
> ↓
> Action Failure
> ↓
> Project Delay
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26481. Some edges may be:
> 
> ```text
> FACT
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26482. Others:
> 
> ```text
> INFERENCE.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26483. Preserve epistemic type per edge/claim.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26484. Contributing Factor
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> insufficient retry jitter
> ```
> 
> did not initiate outage
> 
> but worsened it.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26485. Distinguish:
> 
> ```text
> TRIGGER
> CONTRIBUTOR
> AMPLIFIER
> ROOT_DEFECT
> ```
> 
> as analytical roles.

> ---
> 
> # 26486. These are not core predicates.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26487. Use namespaced incident semantics.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26488. Blast Radius
> 
> Question:
> 
> ```text
> What is affected?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26489. Start from failing Resource.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26490. Traverse:
> 
> ```text
> PROVIDES
> REQUIRES
> DEPENDS_ON
> ASSIGNED_TO
> PART_OF
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26491. Build impact set.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26492. Example
> 
> ```text
> GPU node
> ↓
> LLM inference capability
> ↓
> Evidence synthesis
> ↓
> Projects P1 P4 P7
> ↓
> Programs G1 G2
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26493. But not every dependency is equally hard.

> 
> # 26494. Need distinguish:
> 
> ```text

> # 26495. Existing Requirement classes help.

> # 26496. If fallback exists:

> ```text
> impact may be degraded,

> # 26497. Impact States
> 
> ```text

> 
> # 26498. UNKNOWN remains important.

> 
> # 26499. Example

> Remote provider state stale.

> # 26500. Cannot conclude:
> 
> ```text
> unaffected.
> ```

> 
> # 26501. Blast Radius Algorithm
> 
> Conceptually:
> 
> ```text
> failed resource
> ↓
> direct capability impact
> ↓
> dependent actions
> ↓
> projects/programs
> ↓
> available substitutes
> ↓
> effective impact
> ```
>

> 
> # 26502. This is not simple graph reachability.

> 
> # 26503. Resolver must consider:

> alternative providers.

> 
> # 26504. Example
> 
> GPU-1 failed.

> ---
> 
> # 26505. GPU-2 exists.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26506. Capability may remain:
> 
> ```text
> AVAILABLE
> ```
> 
> with reduced capacity.

> 
> # 26507. Therefore:
> 
> ```text
> Node Failure ≠ Capability Failure.

> 
> # 26508. Another invariant.

>

> # 26510. This can propagate:

> ```text
> longer queue
> deadline risk

> 
> without complete outage.

> 
> # 26511. Performance Incident
> 
> Not all incidents are availability failures.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26512. Types:
> 
> ```text
> AVAILABILITY
> LATENCY
> CORRECTNESS
> CAPACITY
> SECURITY
> DATA_QUALITY
> PHYSICAL
> ```

> ---
> 
> # 26513. CORRECTNESS incident is especially dangerous.

> 
> # 26514. Example:
> 
> ```text

> 
> ---
> 
> # 26515. Traditional uptime monitor sees:
> 
> ```text
> healthy.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26516. Verification layer sees:
> 
> ```text
> behavioral failure.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26517. Therefore:
> 
> ```text
> Health Check Pass
> ≠
> Capability Correctness.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26518. Need synthetic/semantic verification.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26519. Capability SLO
> 
> Instead of only:
> 
> ```text
> HTTP uptime 99.9%
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26520. Could define:
> 
> ```text
> 98% validated extraction tasks
> meet schema + quality contract
> within 30 s.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26521. This is much closer to:
> 
> ```text
> actual capability.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26522. SLI
> 
> Service Level Indicator.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26523. For semantic capability:
> 
> ```text
> successful verified outcomes / attempts
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26524. Other SLIs:
> 
> ```text
> latency
> queue time
> freshness
> correctness
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26525. SLO belongs to:
> 
> ```text
> Capability + Context.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26526. Not universal.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26527. Example:
> 
> Interactive LLM:
> 
> ```text
> p95 < 5 s
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26528. Batch synthesis:
> 
> ```text
> complete < 2 h
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26529. Different.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26530. Error Budget
> 
> Could track:
> 
> ```text
> allowed SLO violations

> 
> for service operations.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26531. But error budget is an operational policy,
> 
> not moral permission to fail.

> ---
> 
> # 26532. Useful for deciding:
> 
> ```text
> feature work vs reliability work.

> 
> ---
> 
> # 26533. Innovation OS can connect SLO breach to:
> 
> ```text
> Capability Debt.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26534. Example
> 
> Repeated inference failures:
> 
> ```text
> Capability reliability debt.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26535. Creates remediation Project.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26536. Semantic SLO Hierarchy
> 
> ```text
> Infrastructure SLO
> ↓
> Service SLO
> ↓
> Capability SLO
> ↓
> Project Outcome SLO

> 
> ---
> 
> # 26537. Example:
> 
> ```text
> GPU uptime
> ```
> 
> alone insufficient.

> 
> # 26538. More meaningful:
> 
> ```text
> Research extraction capability usable

> # 26540. SLO dependency can explain:

> # 26541. Incident Severity
> 
> Should not be derived only from:

> # 26542. Better dimensions:

> ```text

>

>

> 
> # 26549. But category semantics must be explicit.

> 
> # 26550. Incident Priority ≠ Root Cause Importance

> # 26551. Priority concerns:

> response urgency.
> ```

> # 26552. Root cause importance concerns:

> ```text

> 
> to:

> ```

> # 26554. But true incident start may be uncertain.

> Useful operationally.

> 
> # 26557. Mean Time To Restore

> 
> # 26560. Incident Timeline
> 
> ```text
> change
> ↓
> first symptom
> ↓
> alert
> ↓
> incident opened
> ↓
> mitigation
> ↓
> recovery
> ↓
> verification

>

> # 26566. Both timestamps matter.

> 
> # 26569. Change Event types:
>

> CONFIG_UPDATED

> 
> # 26571. But:

> ```text

> # 26573. Example unrelated documentation update:

> ---
> 
> # 26596. Therefore pre-change metadata:
> 
> ```text
> reversible
> compensatable
> irreversible.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26597. Existing side-effect classes reused.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26598. Runbook
> 
> A runbook is:
> 
> ```text
> reusable recovery procedure.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26599. Represent as:
> 
> ```text
> Artifact
> +
> Procedural Graph
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26600. Example
> 
> ```text
> MODEL_SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE
> ```
> 
> runbook:
> 
> ```text
> check node
> check package
> try verified fallback
> validate output
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26601. Runbook states:
> 
> ```text
> DRAFT
> TESTED
> APPROVED
> ACTIVE
> DEPRECATED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26602. Critical invariant
> 
> ```text
> Runbook Exists
> ≠
> Runbook Works.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26603. Need periodic testing.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26604. Runbook Verification
> 
> Can run in:
> 
> ```text
> sandbox
> simulation
> staging
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26605. Some runbooks can be tested through:
> 
> ```text
> chaos scenarios.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26606. Example:
> 
> ```text
> kill worker
> ```
> 
> in sandbox.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26607. Verify:
> 
> ```text
> failover executes.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26608. Chaos Engineering
> 
> Useful but carefully scoped.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26609. Purpose:
> 
> ```text
> test resilience assumptions.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26610. Not:
> 
> ```text
> randomly break production.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26611. Chaos Experiment = Action/Project.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26612. Must declare:
> 
> ```text
> scope
> blast radius
> rollback
> safety
> authority
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26613. Physical chaos experiments require especially strict governance.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26614. Example:
> 
> simulate sensor loss,
> 
> not necessarily disconnect actual safety sensor.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26615. Prefer simulation when equivalent question can be answered safely.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26616. Incident Response Roles
> 
> ```text
> INCIDENT_COORDINATOR
> INVESTIGATOR
> MITIGATOR
> COMMUNICATOR
> VERIFIER
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26617. Agent roles can fill some.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26618. But high-impact incident command may require:
> 
> ```text
> human authority.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26619. Agent Incident Scout
> 
> Can:
> 
> ```text
> collect telemetry
> build timeline
> identify changes
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26620. Agent Investigator
> 
> Can:
> 
> ```text
> generate causal hypotheses
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26621. Agent Mitigator
> 
> Can execute only:
> 
> ```text
> authorized runbook actions.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26622. Agent Verifier
> 
> Checks:
> 
> ```text
> recovery criteria.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26623. Separation:
> 
> ```text
> Mitigator ≠ Verifier
> ```
> 
> preferably for high-risk incidents.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26624. This reuses Builder ≠ Reviewer principle.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26625. Incident Blackboard
> 
> Shared objects:
> 
> ```text
> Symptoms
> Events
> Hypotheses
> Evidence
> Actions
> Status
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26626. Multiple agents/humans collaborate.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26627. Each hypothesis keeps:
> 
> ```text
> author
> evidence
> state.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26628. No silent consensus merge.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26629. Incident Question Queue
> 
> Examples:
> 
> ```text
> Did deployment v12 affect service X?
> Is fallback provider healthy?
> Did recovery restore correctness?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26630. Each question can become:
> 
> ```text
> Action.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26631. Diagnostic Action
> 
> Examples:
> 
> ```text
> run health check
> query logs
> run benchmark
> compare configuration
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26632. Diagnostic actions should be mostly:
> 
> ```text
> READ_ONLY.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26633. Safer to automate.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26634. Mutating diagnostics should be classified explicitly.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26635. Example:
> 
> ```text
> restart to test
> ```
> 
> is not pure diagnosis.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26636. Recovery Candidate
> 
> System may propose:
> 
> ```text
> restart
> failover
> rollback
> reroute
> scale
> disable feature
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26637. But each candidate has:
> 
> ```text
> expected effect
> risk
> cost
> authority requirement
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26638. Recovery Resolver
> 
> Can reuse:
> 
> ```text
> Requirement ↔ Provider
> ```
> 
> pattern.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26639. Example lost LLM capability.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26640. Candidate providers:
> 
> ```text
> local model
> cloud model
> partner model
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26641. Resolver filters:
> 
> ```text
> privacy
> latency
> compatibility
> authority.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26642. Then propose feasible recovery.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26643. This is:
> 
> # Capability Recovery
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26644. Recovery Objective
> 
> Not necessarily:
> 
> ```text
> restore original component.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26645. Better:
> 
> ```text
> restore required capability.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26646. Example original GPU unavailable.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26647. Temporary CPU fallback may restore:
> 
> ```text
> degraded capability.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26648. This is superior to component-centric ops.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26649. Service Restoration vs Capability Restoration
> 
> ```text
> Service Restored
> ≠
> Capability Restored.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26650. Example service online,
> 
> but result validator still failing.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26651. Therefore recovery verification must test:
> 
> ```text
> capability contract.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26652. Recovery Verification
> 
> Checklist:
> 
> ```text
> service reachable
> output valid
> latency acceptable
> dependencies stable
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26653. For physical system:
> 
> ```text
> machine state healthy
> calibration valid
> test part passes inspection
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26654. Incident cannot be marked RESOLVED merely because:
> 
> ```text
> process restarted.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26655. Critical invariant
> 
> ```text
> Recovery Action Completed
> ≠
> Recovery Verified.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26656. Recovery Evidence
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> benchmark passed
> queue draining
> SLO restored
> verification sample passed
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26657. Evidence linked to Incident.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26658. Recovery Window
> 
> Some systems recover briefly then relapse.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26659. Therefore verification may require:
> 
> ```text
> stability period.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26660. Example:
> 
> ```text
> healthy for 30 minutes
> ```
> 
> before closure.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26661. Duration depends on system.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26662. No universal value.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26663. Recurrence
> 
> Incident repeats after closure.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26664. Link:
> 
> ```text
> RELATED_TO
> ```
> 
> prior incident.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26665. Recurrent incidents can reveal:
> 
> ```text
> structural problem.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26666. Incident Pattern Detector
> 
> Finds:
> 
> ```text
> same symptom
> same component
> same context
> ```
> 
> across history.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26667. Repeated pattern may trigger:
> 
> ```text
> Permanent Remediation Project.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26668. Example:
> 
> ```text
> worker OOM every Monday batch
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26669. Not just restart weekly.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26670. Create:
> 
> ```text
> capacity/model optimization project.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26671. Temporary Mitigation Debt
> 
> Repeated workaround becomes:
> 
> ```text
> Operational Debt.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26672. Example:
> 
> ```text
> manual restart
> ```
> 
> used 30 times.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26673. Opportunity:
> 
> ```text
> fix leak
> automate recovery
> increase capacity.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26674. Operational Debt
> 
> Can be derived from:
> 
> ```text
> repeated incidents
> manual interventions
> known temporary mitigations.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26675. Not a root.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26676. Autonomous Operations
> 
> Now key topic.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26677. Goal is not:
> 
> ```text
> unlimited self-healing.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26678. Goal:
> 
> # Bounded Autonomous Operations
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26679. Automated recovery allowed only if:
> 
> ```text
> runbook approved
> scope bounded
> risk acceptable
> authority valid
> verification available
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26680. Example safe candidate:
> 
> ```text
> restart stateless worker.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26681. Example:
> 
> ```text
> move batch workload
> to another verified node.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26682. Example:
> 
> ```text
> requeue failed idempotent job.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26683. Higher-risk:
> 
> ```text
> database failover
> production rollback
> ```
> 
> may require approval.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26684. Very high-risk:
> 
> ```text
> override safety interlock.
> ```
> 
> should not be autonomous through this layer.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26685. Recovery Autonomy Levels
> 
> ```text
> OBSERVE
> RECOMMEND
> PREAUTHORIZED
> APPROVAL_REQUIRED
> FORBIDDEN
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26686. These can be assigned per runbook Action.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26687. Example
> 
> ```text
> restart worker = PREAUTHORIZED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26688. But:
> 
> ```text
> restore database backup = APPROVAL_REQUIRED.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26689. Recovery Authority has:
> 
> ```text
> time
> scope
> frequency
> budget
> ```
> 
> limits.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26690. Example:
> 
> ```text
> max 3 restarts / hour.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26691. If exceeded:
> 
> ```text
> escalate.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26692. This prevents:
> 
> ```text
> restart loop.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26693. Self-Healing Loop Anti-Pattern
> 
> ```text
> fail
> restart
> fail
> restart
> fail
> restart
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26694. Without diagnosis,
> 
> automation can amplify outage.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26695. Recovery Circuit Breaker
> 
> After N unsuccessful attempts:
> 
> ```text
> stop automation.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26696. Escalate to:
> 
> ```text
> human / deeper investigation.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26697. Automated Recovery Budget
> 
> May limit:
> 
> ```text
> actions
> time
> cost
> risk
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26698. Example:
> 
> ```text
> 2 retries
> 1 failover
> then stop.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26699. Adaptive Runbook
> 
> Could branch:
> 
> ```text
> if node unavailable
> → alternate provider
> 
> if artifact corrupt
> → restore artifact
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26700. Major milestone
> 
> К **26700** system supports:
> 
> # governed self-healing procedures.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26701. But autonomous operations need:
> 
> ```text
> post-action verification.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26702. No verification means:
> 
> ```text
> unknown outcome.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26703. This avoids false recovery loops.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26704. Autonomous Recovery Transaction
> 
> Conceptually:
> 
> ```text
> Detect
> ↓
> Select Approved Runbook
> ↓
> Authorize
> ↓
> Execute
> ↓
> Observe
> ↓
> Verify
> ↓
> Commit Recovery State
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26705. If verification fails:
> 
> ```text
> rollback/next branch/escalate.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26706. Runbook Compiler
> 
> Input:
> 
> ```text
> incident type
> resource
> available recovery capabilities
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26707. Output:
> 
> ```text
> candidate recovery graph.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26708. But compiler should prefer:
> 
> ```text
> approved tested patterns.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26709. LLM-generated emergency runbook:
> 
> ```text
> proposal only.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26710. Not automatically executable.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26711. Critical invariant
> 
> ```text
> Generated Runbook ≠ Approved Runbook.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26712. Existing Package/Governance model handles approval.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26713. Incident Simulation
> 
> Before risky recovery:
> 
> ```text
> simulate if feasible.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26714. Example:
> 
> ```text
> failover database
> ```
> 
> can be tested against:
> 
> ```text
> scenario state.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26715. But simulation may be too slow during acute incident.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26716. Therefore pre-tested runbooks matter.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26717. Preparedness
> 
> System can calculate:
> 
> ```text
> which critical incidents
> have tested recovery paths?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26718. This is:
> 
> # Recovery Coverage
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26719. Example:
> 
> ```text
> Critical Capability C
> has:
> primary provider
> fallback provider
> tested runbook
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26720. Better resilience than:
> 
> ```text
> fallback theoretically exists
> but never tested.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26721. Recovery Readiness dimensions:
> 
> ```text
> fallback available
> runbook exists
> runbook tested
> authority available
> required artifacts available
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26722. No one global resilience score necessary.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26723. Dependency Health
> 
> A service can be healthy,
> 
> but dependency degraded.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26724. Semantic health should consider:
> 
> ```text
> upstream/downstream dependencies.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26725. Example API responds,
> 
> but DB replica lag 30 min.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26726. Capability may be:
> 
> ```text
> DEGRADED.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26727. Health propagation should be:
> 
> ```text
> contract-aware.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26728. Not:
> 
> ```text
> any dependency warning → service red.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26729. Example optional analytics dependency failed.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26730. Main transaction capability still healthy.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26731. Requirement criticality matters.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 26732. Dependency Classes
> 
> ```text
> REQUIRED
> OPTIONAL
> FALLBACK
> ENHANCEMENT
> ```
> 
> ---

> # 26733. Could be encoded through requirement semantics.

>

> # 26735. Based on:

> 
> # 26736. But:

> # 26737. Underlying facts remain visible.

>

> 
> Critical.
