> ```text
> Current Architecture
> Current Capabilities
> Current Incidents
> Current Gaps
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27313. Но технологическая система существует во времени.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27314. Компонент может сегодня быть:
> 
> ```text
> VERIFIED
> STABLE
> SUPPORTED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27315. А через год:
> 
> ```text
> UNMAINTAINED
> INCOMPATIBLE
> EXPENSIVE
> UNSUPPORTED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27316. Поэтому появляется:
> 
> # Technology Lifecycle Engine
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27317. Его задача:
> 
> ```text
> наблюдать изменение
> технологической пригодности
> во времени.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27318. Главный invariant
> 
> ```text
> Working Today
> ≠
> Strategically Sustainable.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27319. И обратный:
> 
> ```text
> Old Technology
> ≠
> Bad Technology.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27320. Новый компонент тоже:
> 
> ```text
> ≠ автоматически лучший компонент.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27321. Поэтому lifecycle-анализ должен быть:
> 
> ```text
> evidence-based
> context-specific
> capability-oriented
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27322. Не:
> 
> ```text
> fashion-oriented.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27323. Lifecycle Subject
> 
> Отслеживаться могут:
> 
> ```text
> Software Package
> Model
> Runtime
> Protocol
> Hardware Platform
> Database
> API
> Standard
> Workflow
> Ontology
> Device
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27324. Все они уже представлены существующими:
> 
> ```text
> RESOURCE
> ARTIFACT
> CONCEPT
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27325. Новый root не нужен.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27326. Lifecycle State — derived/application state.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27327. Возможные состояния:
> 
> ```text
> EXPERIMENTAL
> EMERGING
> SUPPORTED
> MATURE
> LEGACY
> DEPRECATED
> SUNSETTING
> RETIRED
> UNKNOWN
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27328. Эти состояния не должны определяться:
> 
> ```text
> только возрастом.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27329. Например:
> 
> ```text
> 30-летний protocol
> ```
> 
> может быть:
> 
> ```text
> MATURE
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27330. А технология трёхлетней давности:
> 
> ```text
> DEPRECATED.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27331. Следовательно:
> 
> ```text
> Age ≠ Lifecycle State.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27332. EXPERIMENTAL
> 
> Означает:
> 
> ```text
> использование ограничено
> исследовательским/тестовым Context.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27333. EMERGING
> 
> Есть:
> 
> ```text
> growing evidence
> growing ecosystem
> ```
> 
> но production suitability может быть неполной.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27334. SUPPORTED
> 
> Есть:
> 
> ```text
> current support path.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27335. MATURE
> 
> Стабильная технология с:
> 
> ```text
> strong operational evidence.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27336. LEGACY
> 
> Означает:
> 
> ```text
> система всё ещё используется
> и может быть operationally valid,
> но вокруг неё растёт transition pressure.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27337. LEGACY ≠ BROKEN.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27338. DEPRECATED
> 
> Официально или организационно рекомендована замена.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27339. SUNSETTING
> 
> Есть:
> 
> ```text
> active retirement plan.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27340. RETIRED
> 
> Новые production dependencies:
> 
> ```text
> не должны создаваться.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27341. Lifecycle Evidence
> 
> Состояние должно ссылаться на:
> 
> ```text
> vendor notices
> release activity
> security support
> compatibility tests
> internal incidents
> usage
> replacement readiness
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27342. Example
> 
> Repository:
> 
> ```text
> last release 4 years ago
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27343. Это signal.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27344. Но само по себе:
> 
> ```text
> не доказательство непригодности.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27345. Возможно пакет:
> 
> ```text
> feature-complete
> stable
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27346. Поэтому:
> 
> ```text
> No Recent Release
> ≠
> Abandoned.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27347. Нужно смотреть:
> 
> ```text
> open critical issues
> maintainer activity
> dependency compatibility
> security response
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27348. Lifecycle Signal Types
> 
> ```text
> UPSTREAM_SUPPORT
> SECURITY
> COMPATIBILITY
> ECOSYSTEM
> PERFORMANCE
> COST
> OPERABILITY
> INTERNAL_INCIDENT
> SKILL_AVAILABILITY
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27349. UPSTREAM_SUPPORT
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> EOL announced
> maintenance reduced
> maintainer departure
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27350. SECURITY
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> unpatched vulnerabilities
> unsupported crypto
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27351. COMPATIBILITY
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> new OS unsupported
> ARM build absent
> API version removed
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27352. ECOSYSTEM
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> critical plugins disappear
> integration support shrinks
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27353. PERFORMANCE
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> current workload outgrows component.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27354. COST
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> license cost rises
> cloud egress grows
> maintenance labor increases
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27355. OPERABILITY
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> hard to deploy
> hard to observe
> hard to recover
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27356. INTERNAL_INCIDENT
> 
> Repeated incidents provide:
> 
> ```text
> organization-specific lifecycle evidence.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27357. SKILL_AVAILABILITY
> 
> Если технология требует:
> 
> ```text
> rare expertise
> ```
> 
> это может стать operational risk.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27358. Но:
> 
> ```text
> Rare Skill
> ≠
> Bad Technology.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27359. Возможные responses:
> 
> ```text
> training
> documentation
> automation
> replacement
> external support
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27360. Lifecycle Signal ≠ Migration Decision.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27361. Несколько signals могут создать:
> 
> ```text
> Migration Hypothesis.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27362. Example:
> 
> ```text
> x86-only package
> +
> ARM deployment growth
> +
> upstream no ARM roadmap
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27363. Hypothesis:
> 
> ```text
> package may constrain future architecture.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27364. Это ещё не означает:
> 
> ```text
> replace now.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27365. Technology Risk
> 
> Можно представить многомерно:
> 
> ```text
> support risk
> security risk
> compatibility risk
> capacity risk
> skills risk
> vendor risk
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27366. Не сводить в один:
> 
> ```text
> technology score.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27367. Technology Debt
> 
> Technical Debt нужно моделировать аккуратно.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27368. Debt — не просто:
> 
> ```text
> old code.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27369. Он означает:
> 
> > текущее решение создаёт дополнительную будущую стоимость, риск или ограничение по сравнению с доступными альтернативами.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27370. Debt Types
> 
> ```text
> CODE
> ARCHITECTURE
> DEPENDENCY
> DATA
> SECURITY
> OBSERVABILITY
> TEST
> DOCUMENTATION
> KNOWLEDGE
> INFRASTRUCTURE
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27371. CODE Debt
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> temporary workaround
> duplicated implementation
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27372. ARCHITECTURE Debt
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> tight coupling
> single central database dependency
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27373. DEPENDENCY Debt
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> unsupported package.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27374. DATA Debt
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> ambiguous schema
> missing provenance
> unversioned identifiers
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27375. SECURITY Debt
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> long-lived broad credentials.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27376. OBSERVABILITY Debt
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> critical workflow without semantic tracing.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27377. TEST Debt
> 
> Например:
> 
> ```text
> migration cannot be regression-tested.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27378. DOCUMENTATION Debt
> 
> Critical operational knowledge exists only:
> 
> ```text
> in one person's memory.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27379. KNOWLEDGE Debt
> 
> System cannot explain:
> 
> ```text
> why architecture decision was made.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27380. INFRASTRUCTURE Debt
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> single failure domain.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27381. Debt Claim
> 
> Technical debt should be:
> 
> ```text
> Claim
> ```
> 
> with:
> 
> ```text
> Evidence
> Impact
> Context
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27382. Example:
> 
> ```text
> Claim:
> Package P causes recurring manual recovery work.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27383. Evidence:
> 
> ```text
> 12 incidents
> 18 technician-hours
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27384. Debt Interest
> 
> Полезная концепция:
> 
> ```text
> cost of keeping debt unresolved over time.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27385. Example:
> 
> ```text
> manual compatibility patch
> 2h/month
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27386. Debt interest:
> 
> ```text
> recurrent maintenance effort.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27387. Но будущую стоимость нельзя придумывать.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27388. Использовать:
> 
> ```text
> measured history
> or explicit scenario assumptions.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27389. Debt Principal
> 
> Approximation:
> 
> ```text
> cost to remove/refactor/migrate debt.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27390. Again estimate with uncertainty.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27391. Debt Interest > Debt Principal
> 
> Может быть сигналом:
> 
> ```text
> migration economically plausible.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27392. Но это ещё не решение.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27393. Потому что существуют:
> 
> ```text
> migration risk
> opportunity cost
> strategic constraints.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27394. Migration Pressure
> 
> Derived state based on:
> 
> ```text
> lifecycle signals
> debt
> incidents
> future capability requirements
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27395. Possible:
> 
> ```text
> LOW
> RISING
> HIGH
> CRITICAL
> UNKNOWN
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27396. Но не автоматический directive.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27397. Example CRITICAL
> 
> Current component:
> 
> ```text
> vendor EOL tomorrow
> critical security fixes unavailable
> production dependency remains
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27398. Even then:
> 
> ```text
> migration path
> ```
> 
> must be engineered.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27399. Current Architecture Snapshot
> 
> Before migration:
> 
> ```text
> freeze explicit architecture view.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27400. Snapshot includes:
> 
> ```text
> components
> versions
> dependencies
> capabilities
> data stores
> interfaces
> policies
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27401. This becomes:
> 
> ```text
> Baseline Architecture Artifact.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27402. Without baseline:
> 
> ```text
> migration cannot be reliably compared.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27403. Target Architecture
> 
> Separate Artifact.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27404. Contains desired:
> 
> ```text
> components
> interfaces
> capabilities
> constraints
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27405. Critical invariant
> 
> ```text
> Target Architecture
> ≠
> Migration Plan.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27406. Target says:
> 
> ```text
> куда хотим прийти.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27407. Migration Plan says:
> 
> ```text
> как перейти.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27408. Transition Architecture
> 
> Самая часто забываемая часть.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27409. Между:
> 
> ```text
> CURRENT
> ```
> 
> и:
> 
> ```text
> TARGET
> ```
> 
> существует:
> 
> ```text
> TRANSITION.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27410. Transition Architecture может существовать:
> 
> ```text
> weeks
> months
> years.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27411. Example
> 
> ```text
> Legacy DB
> +
> new event system
> +
> sync adapter
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27412. Это временная архитектура.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27413. Но временные решения часто становятся:
> 
> ```text
> permanent by accident.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27414. Поэтому каждый temporary component должен иметь:
> 
> ```text
> owner
> purpose
> exit condition
> review date
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27415. Temporary ≠ Free.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27416. Temporary bridge создаёт:
> 
> ```text
> maintenance burden.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27417. Bridge Debt
> 
> Migration adapter itself can accumulate:
> 
> ```text
> transition debt.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27418. Example:
> 
> ```text
> old schema ↔ new schema transformer.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27419. Если bridge остаётся 5 years:
> 
> ```text
> it becomes architecture.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27420. Поэтому exit criteria обязательны.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27421. Migration Program
> 
> Migration should become:
> 
> ```text
> PROGRAM
> ```
> 
> when sufficiently large.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27422. Structure:
> 
> ```text
> Discovery
> Compatibility
> Prototype
> Pilot
> Dual Run
> Cutover
> Stabilization
> Retirement
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27423. Discovery
> 
> Understand:
> 
> ```text
> actual dependencies
> not assumed dependencies.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27424. Dependency Discovery
> 
> Sources:
> 
> ```text
> code imports
> runtime traces
> DB queries
> network calls
> human workflow
> configuration
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27425. Hidden Dependency
> 
> Critical concept.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27426. Example:
> 
> ```text
> cron script
> ```
> 
> depends on deprecated database column.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27427. Architecture diagrams may omit.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27428. Therefore:
> 
> ```text
> Documented Dependency
> ≠
> Complete Dependency Set.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27429. Runtime observability can reveal:
> 
> ```text
> undocumented coupling.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27430. Migration risk increases with:
> 
> ```text
> unknown dependencies.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27431. Dependency Coverage
> 
> Track:
> 
> ```text
> known
> verified
> suspected
> unknown.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27432. Before critical cutover,
> 
> unknown dependency volume should be:
> 
> ```text
> acceptable under governance criteria.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27433. Compatibility Matrix
> 
> Old/New combinations:
> 
> ```text
> Old Client → Old API
> Old Client → New API
> New Client → Old API
> New Client → New API
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27434. This is essential for staged migration.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27435. Example matrix:
> 
> ```text
> Old Client / New API = adapter required
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27436. Backward Compatibility
> 
> Means:
> 
> ```text
> new provider supports old consumer contract.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27437. Forward Compatibility
> 
> Means:
> 
> ```text
> old provider can tolerate newer representation
> ```
> 
> in some contexts.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27438. But these terms depend on interface direction.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27439. Better always state:
> 
> ```text
> consumer version
> provider version
> contract.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27440. Compatibility ≠ Behavioral Equivalence.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27441. Example API request accepted,
> 
> but:
> 
> ```text
> different rounding semantics.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27442. Functional compatibility requires:
> 
> ```text
> behavioral verification.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27443. Compatibility Contract
> 
> ```yaml
> compatibility:
>   consumer: v1
>   provider: v2
>   status: VERIFIED
>   tests:
>     - ...
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27444. Unknown combination:
> 
> ```text
> UNKNOWN.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27445. Don't assume:
> 
> ```text
> minor version = safe.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27446. Schema Evolution
> 
> Data migrations are particularly risky.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27447. Schema change classes:
> 
> ```text
> ADD_FIELD
> RENAME
> SPLIT
> MERGE
> TYPE_CHANGE
> SEMANTIC_CHANGE
> DELETE
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27448. ADD_FIELD often easier.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27449. DELETE can break:
> 
> ```text
> hidden consumers.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27450. RENAME may actually be:
> 
> ```text
> delete + add
> ```
> 
> for unaware systems.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27451. Semantic Change is most dangerous.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27452. Example field remains:
> 
> ```text
> status
> ```
> 
> but meaning changes.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27453. Schema Diff alone may not detect.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27454. Need:
> 
> ```text
> semantic contract diff.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27455. Data Migration
> 
> Process:
> 
> ```text
> Read Old
> ↓
> Transform
> ↓
> Validate
> ↓
> Write New
> ↓
> Compare
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27456. Never assume transformation correctness from:
> 
> ```text
> successful script completion.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27457. Migration Verification
> 
> Could compare:
> 
> ```text
> row counts
> checksums
> referential integrity
> business invariants
> sample semantics
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27458. Example:
> 
> ```text
> 100,000 rows copied
> ```
> 
> does not prove:
> 
> ```text
> 100,000 meanings preserved.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27459. Data Loss Classification
> 
> Migration must identify:
> 
> ```text
> LOSSLESS
> LOSSY
> UNKNOWN
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27460. LOSSY may be acceptable
> 
> if:
> 
> ```text
> explicitly approved.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27461. Example:
> 
> ```text
> drop obsolete debug field.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27462. But historical audit might need it.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27463. Therefore:
> 
> ```text
> Unused Operationally
> ≠
> Safe To Delete Historically.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27464. Archive Before Destructive Migration
> 
> Useful pattern.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27465. But archive must be:
> 
> ```text
> readable
> documented
> verifiable.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27466. An unreadable backup is not meaningful protection.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27467. Backup Verification
> 
> Before risky migration:
> 
> ```text
> restore test
> ```
> 
> matters more than:
> 
> ```text
> backup job succeeded.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27468. Critical invariant
> 
> ```text
> Backup Exists
> ≠
> Recovery Possible.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27469. Restore Capability must be verified.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27470. Dual Write
> 
> Migration pattern:
> 
> ```text
> old system
> +
> new system
> ```
> 
> both receive writes.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27471. Useful for:
> 
> ```text
> transition.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27472. But dual write introduces:
> 
> ```text
> consistency risk.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27473. Example:
> 
> ```text
> write old succeeds
> write new fails.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27474. Need:
> 
> ```text
> outbox
> reconciliation
> ```
> 
> or event-driven replication.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27475. Direct application dual-write can be fragile.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27476. Better patterns may include:
> 
> ```text
> one authoritative write
> +
> replication.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27477. Authority During Migration
> 
> Critical question:
> 
> ```text
> Which system is authoritative for each field?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27478. Example:
> 
> ```text
> old system authoritative for billing
> new system authoritative for search metadata.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27479. Without explicit authority map:
> 
> ```text
> split-brain semantics.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27480. Migration Authority Matrix
> 
> ```text
> Domain A → Old
> Domain B → New
> Domain C → Shadow only
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27481. Transition changes this matrix over time.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27482. Cutover is partly:
> 
> ```text
> authority transfer.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27483. Not merely traffic routing.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27484. Shadow Read
> 
> New system receives data and answers queries,
> 
> but result not used operationally.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27485. Compare:
> 
> ```text
> old answer
> vs
> new answer.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27486. Useful before cutover.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27487. Shadow Traffic
> 
> Production request copied to:
> 
> ```text
> new implementation
> ```
> 
> without affecting user/result.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27488. Measures:
> 
> ```text
> compatibility
> latency
> correctness.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27489. But shadow traffic may duplicate side effects.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27490. Therefore only for:
> 
> ```text
> read-only
> or side-effect-suppressed execution.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27491. Critical invariant
> 
> ```text
> Shadow Execution
> must not duplicate
> real-world side effects.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27492. Example:
> 
> payment request cannot simply be shadowed into:
> 
> ```text
> second real payment provider.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27493. Need:
> 
> ```text
> simulation/mock boundary.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27494. Shadow Result Comparator
> 
> Compares:
> 
> ```text
> output contract
> semantic equivalence
> performance
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27495. Exact byte equality often unnecessary.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27496. Example LLM migration:
> 
> ```text
> different text
> ```
> 
> may still satisfy same structured result contract.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27497. Therefore comparator is:
> 
> ```text
> domain-specific.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27498. Canary Migration
> 
> Send:
> 
> ```text
> small controlled workload subset
> ```
> 
> to new component.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27499. Observe:
> 
> ```text
> errors
> correctness
> latency
> resource use
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27500. Canary Selection
> 
> Should represent:
> 
> ```text
> relevant workload classes.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27501. Not simply:
> 
> ```text
> 1% random
> ```
> 
> if rare critical cases matter.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27502. Example:
> 
> ```text
> common documents
> edge-case documents
> large documents
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27503. Canary can be:
> 
> ```text
> risk-stratified.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27504. Feature Flag
> 
> Useful for:
> 
> ```text
> route old/new implementation.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27505. Feature Flag itself is:
> 
> ```text
> operational control.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27506. High-impact flags require:
> 
> ```text
> authorization
> audit.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27507. Flag ≠ architecture decision.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27508. It is implementation mechanism.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27509. Strangler Pattern
> 
> Old system gradually replaced:
> 
> ```text
> capability by capability.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27510. Example:
> 
> ```text
> Search
> → new system
> 
> Billing
> → old system
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27511. Useful for complex migration.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27512. This naturally fits Capability Graph.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27513. Instead of replacing:
> 
> ```text
> application monolith
> ```
> 
> as one unit,
> 
> replace:
> 
> ```text
> Capabilities.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27514. This is highly aligned with Innovation OS.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27515. Capability-Level Migration
> 
> ```text
> Capability C
> Current Provider A
> ↓
> Candidate Provider B
> ↓
> Shadow
> ↓
> Canary
> ↓
> Primary B
> ↓
> Retire A
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27516. Much more precise than:
> 
> ```text
> migrate system.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27517. Provider Migration
> 
> A Capability can have:
> 
> ```text
> multiple providers
> ```
> 
> during transition.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27518. Status:
> 
> ```text
> PRIMARY
> SECONDARY
> SHADOW
> FALLBACK
> RETIRED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27519. This fits existing resolver.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27520. Resolver can gradually prefer:
> 
> ```text
> new provider.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27521. But preference change is:
> 
> ```text
> policy/config change
> ```
> 
> with audit.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27522. Migration Wave
> 
> Large architecture may migrate in groups.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27523. Example:
> 
> ```text
> Wave 1:
> internal tools
> 
> Wave 2:
> noncritical production
> 
> Wave 3:
> critical production
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27524. Each wave has:
> 
> ```text
> entry criteria
> exit criteria.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27525. Wave 2 cannot begin merely because:
> 
> ```text
> calendar says so.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27526. Prefer:
> 
> ```text
> evidence gates.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27527. Example Gate
> 
> ```text
> 0 critical defects
> 95% contract coverage
> rollback tested
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27528. Specific values project-defined.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27529. Migration Readiness Matrix
> 
> Dimensions:
> 
> ```text
> compatibility
> data
> operations
> security
> observability
> skills
> rollback
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27530. Better than:
> 
> ```text
> 78% ready.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27531. Example:
> 
> ```text
> Compatibility YES
> Rollback UNKNOWN
> Security YES
> Training NO
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27532. Very actionable.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27533. Migration Blocker
> 
> Any HARD requirement not satisfied.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27534. Example:
> 
> ```text
> no restore test
> ```
> 
> before irreversible DB migration.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27535. Could block cutover.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27536. Migration Constraint
> 
> Examples:
> 
> ```text
> zero downtime
> data residency
> deadline
> hardware availability
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27537. Some constraints conflict.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27538. Example:
> 
> ```text
> zero downtime
> +
> one-time irreversible transform
> +
> no dual-running
> ```
> 
> may be infeasible.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27539. System should report:
> 
> ```text
> constraint conflict.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27540. Not invent impossible plan.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27541. Migration Feasibility
> 
> Separate from:
> 
> ```text
> Target Feasibility.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27542. Example target system works perfectly from empty state.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27543. But converting:
> 
> ```text
> 20 years of legacy data
> ```
> 
> may be prohibitive.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27544. Thus:
> 
> ```text
> Greenfield Success
> ≠
> Brownfield Migration Success.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27545. Brownfield Context
> 
> Requires:
> 
> ```text
> existing users
> data
> integrations
> contracts
> operations.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27546. Greenfield Context
> 
> No legacy dependency.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27547. Same technology can be attractive in greenfield
> 
> but poor migration target for brownfield.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27548. Technology Evaluation should distinguish both.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27549. Migration Option Types
> 
> ```text
> IN_PLACE_UPGRADE
> REPLACE
> REHOST
> REPLATFORM
> REFACTOR
> REIMPLEMENT
> ENCAPSULATE
> RETIRE
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27550. IN_PLACE_UPGRADE
> 
> Same architecture family,
> 
> new version.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27551. REPLACE
> 
> Different implementation/provider.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27552. REHOST
> 
> Move:
> 
> ```text
> same workload
> to new infrastructure.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27553. REPLATFORM
> 
> Some infrastructure/runtime adaptation.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27554. REFACTOR
> 
> Internal restructuring while preserving capability contract.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27555. REIMPLEMENT
> 
> Recreate capability in new technology.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27556. ENCAPSULATE
> 
> Keep legacy behind:
> 
> ```text
> modern interface.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27557. RETIRE
> 
> Capability no longer needed.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27558. Important:
> 
> ```text
> Retirement
> ```
> 
> can be cheapest migration.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27559. Before replacing old component ask:
> 
> ```text
> Do we still need this capability?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27560. Dead Capability
> 
> System may discover:
> 
> ```text
> no active Project requires it.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27561. But absence in current graph may be incomplete.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27562. Need verify:
> 
> ```text
> hidden consumers
> regulatory/archive needs
> future commitments.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27563. Usage Evidence
> 
> Sources:
> 
> ```text
> runtime traces
> API logs
> scheduled jobs
> human confirmation
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27564. No recent traffic:
> 
> ```text
> ≠ unused forever.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27565. Example annual report system.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27566. Usage Window must match:
> 
> ```text
> business cycle.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27567. Retirement Candidate
> 
> State:
> 
> ```text
> CANDIDATE
> VALIDATING
> APPROVED
> SUNSETTING
> RETIRED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27568. Retirement Plan
> 
> Includes:
> 
> ```text
> consumer migration
> data archive
> credential removal
> monitoring removal
> documentation update
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27569. Retirement is:
> 
> ```text
> Program/Action sequence.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27570. Component Off ≠ Retired.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27571. Could still have:
> 
> ```text
> credentials
> DNS
> storage
> billing
> dependencies.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27572. Retirement Verification
> 
> Check:
> 
> ```text
> no active calls
> no active secrets
> no scheduled tasks
> no dependency claims
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27573. Then mark RETIRED.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27574. Zombie Infrastructure
> 
> Resources no longer intentionally used,
> 
> but still:
> 
> ```text
> running
> costing
> exposed.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27575. Detect through:
> 
> ```text
> low/no use
> no owner
> no project mapping
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27576. But:
> 
> ```text
> low use
> ≠ zombie.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27577. Need confirm operational purpose.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27578. Orphaned Resource
> 
> Resource with:
> 
> ```text
> no owner
> no documented purpose
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27579. Creates:
> 
> ```text
> Governance/Knowledge Gap.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27580. Ownership here means:
> 
> ```text
> operational responsibility.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27581. Not necessarily legal ownership.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27582. Architecture Decision Record
> 
> Every significant architecture change should create:
> 
> ```text
> ADR Artifact.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27583. ADR contains:
> 
> ```text
> Context
> Decision
> Alternatives
> Consequences
> Evidence
> Date
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27584. Important:
> 
> ```text
> Decision
> ≠ eternal truth.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27585. ADR remains historical explanation.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27586. Later system can say:
> 
> ```text
> why component A was chosen in 2026.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27587. This prevents future:
> 
> ```text
> architecture archaeology.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27588. ADR Supersession
> 
> New decision:
> 
> ```text
> SUPERSEDES ADR-17
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27589. Old record remains.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27590. Architecture RFC
> 
> Before significant change:
> 
> ```text
> Proposal Artifact.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27591. Could include:
> 
> ```text
> problem
> options
> evidence
> migration
> risks
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27592. RFC ≠ Decision.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27593. Governance approval creates:
> 
> ```text
> Decision.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27594. Architecture Freeze remains:
> 
> ```text
> core ontology changes
> through RFC process.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27595. This module applies same principle to:
> 
> ```text
> implementation architecture.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27596. Architecture Drift
> 
> Actual deployed system may differ from:
> 
> ```text
> declared architecture.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27597. Example:
> 
> documentation says:
> 
> ```text
> Postgres only
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27598. Runtime discovers:
> 
> ```text
> hidden SQLite cache
> ```
> 
> affecting behavior.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27599. That is:
> 
> ```text
> Architecture Drift.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27600. Major milestone
> 
> К **27600** Innovation OS начинает сравнивать:
> 
> ```text
> Declared Architecture
> vs
> Observed Architecture.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27601. Drift Detection Sources
> 
> ```text
> runtime traces
> deployment manifests
> network discovery
> package inventories
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27602. Drift ≠ Automatically Wrong.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27603. Could be:
> 
> ```text
> approved emergency change
> ```
> 
> not yet documented.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27604. Need reconcile:
> 
> ```text
> actual
> desired
> approved.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27605. Architecture State Triad
> 
> ```text
> DESIRED
> DEPLOYED
> OBSERVED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27606. DESIRED
> 
> What governance/config says should exist.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27607. DEPLOYED
> 
> What deployment system believes exists.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27608. OBSERVED
> 
> What telemetry actually sees.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27609. Differences:
> 
> ```text
> drift.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27610. Example:
> 
> Desired:
> 
> ```text
> Model v7
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27611. Deployed manifest:
> 
> ```text
> v7
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27612. Runtime observed:
> 
> ```text
> v6 process still serving 20% traffic.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27613. Important incident/migration signal.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27614. Configuration Drift
> 
> Same pattern.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27615. Device Drift
> 
> Physical node firmware differs from:
> 
> ```text
> approved baseline.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27616. Ontology Drift
> 
> Semantic profile implementations diverge.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27617. Model Drift
> 
> Two meanings:
> 
> ```text
> deployment-version drift
> statistical behavior drift.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27618. Keep separate.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27619. Version Drift
> 
> Wrong model version.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27620. Behavioral Drift
> 
> Same model/system performance changes relative to data environment.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27621. Behavioral drift may trigger:
> 
> ```text
> revalidation.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27622. Architecture Conformance
> 
> Can run checks:
> 
> ```text
> forbidden dependency
> required redundancy
> approved versions
> security boundary
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27623. Example rule:
> 
> ```text
> physical safety controller
> must not depend on cloud LLM.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27624. Deployment graph shows:
> 
> ```text
> dependency exists.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27625. Conformance violation.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27626. This is stronger than:
> 
> ```text
> architecture diagram review.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27627. Architecture Policy-as-Code
> 
> Examples:
> 
> ```text
> no production database direct LLM access
> no single-node critical capability
> private data stays in approved zones
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27628. But architecture policy changes:
> 
> ```text
> governed.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27629. Conformance Engine
> 
> Input:
> 
> ```text
> Observed Architecture Graph
> +
> Architecture Policies
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27630. Output:
> 
> ```text
> Violations
> Unknowns
> Evidence
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27631. UNKNOWN ≠ compliant.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27632. Example:
> 
> ```text
> cannot determine encryption state.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27633. Result:
> 
> ```text
> UNKNOWN
> ```
> 
> not PASS.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27634. Technology Radar
> 
> Useful UI concept.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27635. But avoid:
> 
> ```text
> fashion ranking.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27636. Radar rings might represent:
> 
> ```text
> ADOPT
> TRIAL
> ASSESS
> HOLD
> ```
> 
> only if organization explicitly chooses those semantics.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27637. Better generic:
> 
> ```text
> CURRENT
> EXPERIMENTING
> WATCHING
> RETIRING
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27638. These are portfolio states,
> 
> not intrinsic technology quality.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27639. Example:
> 
> ```text
> RISC-V = WATCHING
> ```
> 
> does not mean:
> 
> ```text
> bad.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27640. It means:
> 
> ```text
> not yet in current production roadmap.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27641. Technology Watch
> 
> Connect:
> 
> ```text
> GitHub Observatory
> Research Observatory
> Vendor Sources
> Standards
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27642. Detect:
> 
> ```text
> new release
> new architecture
> new standard
> new deprecation
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27643. But external novelty does not automatically create migration.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27644. It creates:
> 
> ```text
> Technology Signal.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27645. Relevance Resolver asks:
> 
> ```text
> Does this affect current/future capabilities?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27646. Example new GPU runtime supports:
> 
> ```text
> ARM NPU.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27647. If system has:
> 
> ```text
> ARM inference gap
> ```
> 
> signal highly relevant.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27648. If unrelated:
> 
> ```text
> archive as knowledge
> ```
> 
> without roadmap change.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27649. This prevents:
> 
> ```text
> technology-news-driven architecture churn.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27650. Hype Resistance
> 
> Important.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27651. New technology should not be promoted because:
> 
> ```text
> popular
> viral
> high GitHub stars
> ```
> 
> alone.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27652. Need:
> 
> ```text
> Capability Relevance
> Evidence
> Compatibility
> Operational Fit
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27653. Hype Signal itself can be tracked,
> 
> but separately from:
> 
> ```text
> technical evidence.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27654. Emerging Technology Evaluation
> 
> Stages:
> 
> ```text
> DISCOVER
> UNDERSTAND
> BENCHMARK
> SANDBOX
> PILOT
> ADOPT/REJECT/DEFER
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27655. REJECT here means:
> 
> ```text
> not adopt in this context.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27656. Not:
> 
> ```text
> technology globally bad.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27657. DEFER
> 
> Important state.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27658. Means:
> 
> ```text
> potentially useful
> but timing/conditions not ready.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27659. Trigger condition can be stored.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27660. Example:
> 
> ```text
> reassess when ARM package exists.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27661. This creates:
> 
> # Signpost-Driven Technology Strategy
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27662. Existing Strategy Engine already has:
> 
> ```text
> Signposts.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27663. Technology signpost examples:
> 
> ```text
> vendor releases ARM64 build
> standard reaches stable version
> GPU price falls below threshold
> support contract ends
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27664. Signpost event triggers:
> 
> ```text
> roadmap review.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27665. Not automatic migration.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27666. Experimental Branch
> 
> New architecture can run as:
> 
> ```text
> branch.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27667. Example:
> 
> ```text
> Current:
> Python/FastAPI/Postgres
> 
> Experimental:
> Rust/WASM edge path

> 
> # 27668. Both can coexist.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27669. Experimental branch may test:
> 
> ```text
> specific capability
> ```
> 
> without replacing platform.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27670. This preserves option value.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27671. Architecture Option
> 
> Represents:
> 
> ```text
> possible future architecture
> ```
> 
> with:
> 
> ```text
> entry cost
> reversibility
> dependencies
> evidence.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27672. Option ≠ Commitment.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27673. Example:
> 
> ```text
> Maintain ARM-native branch

> 
> creates future migration option.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27674. Option value comes from:
> 
> ```text
> keeping transition path open.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27675. Example:
> 
> support both:
> 
> ```text
> amd64
> arm64
> ```
> 
> today
> 
> may reduce future migration cost.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27676. But maintaining multi-arch builds also costs.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27677. Thus option has:
> 
> ```text
> carrying cost.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27678. Architecture Option Portfolio
> 
> Could contain:
> 
> ```text
> ARM migration
> graph DB
> WASM edge runtime
> federated storage
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27679. Each remains:
> 
> ```text
> OPEN
> EXPERIMENTING
> COMMITTED
> ABANDONED
> EXPIRED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27680. Portfolio avoids:
> 
> ```text
> all-or-nothing strategy.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27681. Experimental Budget
> 
> Organization may reserve:
> 
> ```text
> compute
> time
> money
> ```
> 
> for architectural experiments.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27682. Again resource accounting.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27683. Experiment does not imply production adoption.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27684. Technology Fitness Function
> 
> Architecture evolution can use:
> 
> ```text
> tests
> constraints
> benchmarks
> ```
> 
> as fitness criteria.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27685. Example candidate architecture must satisfy:
> 
> ```text
> offline support
> ARM64
> local inference
> PostgreSQL compatibility
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27686. These are:
> 
> ```text
> hard constraints.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27687. Other dimensions:
> 
> ```text
> latency
> cost
> maintenance
> ```
> 
> soft/Pareto.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27688. Architecture Candidate Resolver
> 
> ```text
> Target Capability Requirements
> ↓
> Candidate Architectures
> ↓
> Hard Constraint Filtering
> ↓
> Evidence/Benchmarking
> ↓
> Migration Analysis
> ↓
> Pareto Options
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27689. No one magic architecture score.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27690. Architecture candidate itself can be:
> 
> ```text
> Artifact + Context.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27691. Example Candidate A
> 
> ```text
> centralized Postgres
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27692. Candidate B
> 
> ```text
> Postgres + offline replicas
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27693. Candidate C
> 
> ```text
> fully distributed event system.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27694. Compare:
> 
> ```text
> complexity
> offline capability
> operations
> migration cost
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27695. Migration Cost is separate from steady-state cost.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27696. Example Candidate C may be:
> 
> ```text
> best steady-state
> ```
> 
> but:
> 
> ```text
> extremely costly transition.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27697. That can change strategy.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27698. Total Cost of Architecture Transition
> 
> Possible:
> 
> ```text
> engineering
> dual-running
> migration tooling
> testing
> training
> downtime
> support
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27699. Not just:
> 
> ```text
> new software license.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27700. Major milestone
> 
> К **27700** Technology Lifecycle Engine начинает рассматривать:
> 
> # переход как отдельную систему.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27701. Transition Risk Classes
> 
> ```text
> DATA_LOSS
> SERVICE_INTERRUPTION
> BEHAVIOR_CHANGE
> SECURITY_REGRESSION
> PERFORMANCE_REGRESSION
> SKILL_GAP
> OPERATIONS_GAP
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27702. DATA_LOSS
> 
> Obvious but critical.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27703. SERVICE_INTERRUPTION
> 
> Migration may cause outage.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27704. BEHAVIOR_CHANGE
> 
> New implementation subtly changes semantics.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27705. SECURITY_REGRESSION
> 
> New system less constrained.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27706. PERFORMANCE_REGRESSION
> 
> Works correctly,
> 
> but too slow/expensive.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27707. SKILL_GAP
> 
> Team cannot operate new stack.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27708. OPERATIONS_GAP
> 
> No:
> 
> ```text
> monitoring
> backup
> runbook
> recovery
> ```
> 
> for new system.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27709. Production Readiness
> 
> Migration should not finish at:
> 
> ```text
> feature works.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27710. Need:
> 
> ```text
> operability.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27711. Production Readiness Matrix
> 
> ```text
> functionality
> security
> observability
> backup
> recovery
> capacity
> documentation
> skills
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27712. Example:
> 
> ```text
> Functionality YES
> Observability NO
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27713. Then:
> 
> ```text
> not production ready
> ```
> 
> under relevant policy.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27714. Operational Capability Migration
> 
> Need migrate not only application,
> 
> but:
> 
> ```text
> ability to operate it.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27715. Example new database installed,
> 
> but no one knows:
> 
> ```text
> restore procedure.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27716. Technical system exists,
> 
> operational capability incomplete.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27717. This reuses composite capability principle.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27718. New Platform Capability =
> 
> ```text
> software
> +
> operators
> +
> monitoring
> +
> backup
> +
> runbooks
> +
> security
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27719. Excellent.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27720. Skill Migration
> 
> New technology requires:
> 
> ```text
> training
> documentation
> support
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27721. Team skill gap is part of migration plan.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27722. Avoid architecture where:
> 
> ```text
> only migration consultant can operate it.
> ```
> 
> unless acceptable strategy.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27723. Knowledge Transfer
> 
> Before retiring old system experts:
> 
> ```text
> capture procedures
> failure modes
> architecture rationale.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27724. Otherwise:
> 
> ```text
> knowledge loss.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27725. Knowledge Transfer Verification
> 
> Not just:
> 
> ```text
> document written.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27726. Test:
> 
> ```text
> another operator successfully performs recovery.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27727. This verifies transfer.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27728. Bus-Factor Reduction
> 
> Can be viewed as:
> 
> ```text
> Capability Provider Concentration Risk.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27729. One human provider of critical capability:
> 
> ```text
> systemic dependency.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27730. Responses:
> 
> ```text
> train second person
> automate
> document
> external backup
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27731. Again no personal judgment.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27732. Vendor Lock-In
> 
> Need precise definition.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27733. Not:
> 
> ```text
> using vendor = lock-in.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27734. Lock-in means switching cost/dependency significantly constrains options.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27735. Sources:
> 
> ```text
> proprietary APIs
> data format
> contract terms
> specialized skills
> egress cost
> hardware coupling
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27736. Lock-In Evidence
> 
> Could measure:
> 
> ```text
> number of vendor-specific interfaces
> data export feasibility
> migration proof-of-concept
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27737. Avoid simplistic:
> 
> ```text
> vendor lock-in score.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27738. Exit Capability
> 
> Powerful concept.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27739. Every critical vendor dependency can ask:
> 
> ```text
> Can we exit?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27740. Exit Capability includes:
> 
> ```text
> data export
> replacement provider
> migration procedure
> tests
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27741. Vendor use may be completely acceptable if:
> 
> ```text
> exit capability strong.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27742. Conversely nominally open technology may create:
> 
> ```text
> operational lock-in
> ```
> 
> through custom complexity.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27743. Open Source ≠ Easy Exit.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27744. Proprietary ≠ Impossible Exit.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27745. Context matters.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27746. Exit Drill
> 
> Could periodically test:
> 
> ```text
> restore/export into alternate environment.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27747. Similar to disaster recovery drill.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27748. Example cloud database:
> 
> ```text
> export snapshot
> restore locally
> run validation.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27749. This produces actual migration evidence.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27750. Strategic Dependency
> 
> A dependency becomes strategic if loss would affect:
> 
> ```text
> many important capabilities
> ```
> 
> and substitution is difficult.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27751. Dependency centrality alone insufficient.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27752. Need:
> 
> ```text
> importance
> substitutability
> recovery time
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27753. Example tiny authentication library can be strategic.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27754. Strategic Dependency Register
> 
> View:
> 
> ```text
> dependency
> affected capabilities
> alternative providers
> exit readiness
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27755. Useful for architecture strategy.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27756. Technology Concentration Risk
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text
> all AI workloads depend on one model API.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27757. Creates:
> 
> ```text
> provider concentration.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27758. Mitigation:
> 
> ```text
> second model provider
> local model
> abstract interface
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27759. But diversification adds:
> 
> ```text
> complexity
> testing
> cost.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27760. No automatic rule:
> 
> ```text
> more providers always better.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27761. Dependency Abstraction
> 
> Adapter layer may reduce switching cost.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27762. But abstraction itself can:
> 
> ```text
> hide useful provider-specific features.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27763. Therefore:
> 
> ```text
> Abstraction ≠ Free Portability.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27764. Need:
> 
> ```text
> lowest useful common contract
> +
> optional extensions.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27765. This matches Semantic M2M philosophy.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27766. Architecture Bridge
> 
> A bridge should explicitly state:
> 
> ```text
> which semantics preserved
> which degraded
> which unsupported.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27767. Example CUDA→alternative runtime adapter.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27768. Adapter may support:
> 
> ```text
> 90% operators
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27769. Unsupported features remain:
> 
> ```text
> Capability Gap.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27770. Never market adapter as:
> 
> ```text
> full compatibility
> ```
> 
> without evidence.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27771. Hardware Lifecycle
> 
> Compute hardware also evolves.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27772. States may include:
> 
> ```text
> ACTIVE
> CAPACITY_LIMITED
> MAINTENANCE_ONLY
> REPLACEMENT_CANDIDATE
> RETIRED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27773. Hardware replacement signals:
> 
> ```text
> failure rate
> energy
> driver support
> capacity gap
> repair availability
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27774. Age alone not enough.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27775. Example old server may remain excellent for:
> 
> ```text
> archive jobs.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27776. Workload Reassignment Before Retirement
> 
> As hardware ages:
> 
> ```text
> critical workload
> ↓
> new node
> 
> background workload
> ↓
> old node
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27777. This extracts remaining value.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27778. Graceful Hardware Sunset
> 
> ```text
> critical
> → secondary
> → batch-only
> → retired
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27779. But security support may force:
> 
> ```text
> immediate removal.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27780. Device Driver Lifecycle
> 
> Critical for ARM/NPU/GPU.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27781. Hardware may physically work,
> 
> but:
> 
> ```text
> driver stack unsupported.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27782. Then usable capability can decline before hardware failure.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27783. Again:
> 
> ```text
> Physical Health
> ≠
> Software Support.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27784. Model Lifecycle
> 
> AI models need separate lifecycle.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27785. Signals:
> 
> ```text
> quality regression
> provider deprecation
> cost change
> context limits
> new compliance constraints
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27786. Newer model ≠ Better For Every Task.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27787. Model Migration requires:
> 
> ```text
> task-specific benchmark.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27788. Example:
> 
> Model B better overall,
> 
> but worse on:
> 
> ```text
> structured legal extraction.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27789. So current Model A may remain provider for:
> 
> ```text
> specific Capability.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27790. Model Portfolio
> 
> Different models:
> 
> ```text
> routing by task.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27791. Migration may therefore mean:
> 
> ```text
> change routing policy
> ```
> 
> not replace model globally.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27792. Prompt/Agent Lifecycle
> 
> Prompt and agent logic are also versioned Artifacts.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27793. Change can alter:
> 
> ```text
> behavior
> tool use
> output format.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27794. Must be benchmarked for critical agents.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27795. Agent Upgrade
> 
> Flow:
> 
> ```text
> new model/prompt/tools
> ↓
> sandbox
> ↓
> benchmark
> ↓
> shadow
> ↓
> canary
> ↓
> production
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27796. Agent identity can remain same logical Resource
> 
> while:
> 
> ```text
> runtime profile changes.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27797. But significant behavioral change may justify:
> 
> ```text
> new agent version.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27798. Agent Version must preserve:
> 
> ```text
> authority boundaries.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27799. Critical:
> 
> ```text
> Agent Upgrade
> ≠
> Authority Upgrade.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27800. New model does not inherit broader rights.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27801. Authorization remains explicit.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27802. Agent Regression Suite
> 
> Tests:
> 
> ```text
> tool selection
> schema compliance
> refusal boundaries
> evidence behavior
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27803. Especially:
> 
> ```text
> high-impact tool calls.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27804. New model may improve reasoning but:
> 
> ```text
> change action tendencies.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27805. Therefore revalidate:
> 
> ```text
> bounded autonomy.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27806. Protocol Lifecycle
> 
> MCP/M2M/other protocol versions evolve.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27807. Migration needs:
> 
> ```text
> version negotiation
> compatibility adapters
> deprecation windows
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27808. Federation makes abrupt protocol cutover dangerous.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27809. Better:
> 
> ```text
> multi-version window.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27810. Example:
> 
> ```text
> v1 + v2 accepted
> ```
> 
> for transition period.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27811. Then:
> 
> ```text
> v1 sunset.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27812. Sunset Announcement
> 
> Should include:
> 
> ```text
> date
> replacement
> migration guide
> known blockers

> ---
> 
> # 27813. But date may need revision.

> ---
> 
> # 27814. Change should be:
> 
> ```text
> new Event.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27815. Deprecation Notice
>

> 
> ```text
> unsupported.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27816. Need lifecycle dates:
> 
> ```text
> deprecated_at
> support_end
> disable_new_use
> retirement_target
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27817. This prevents ambiguity.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27818. New Dependency Policy
> 
> When component is SUNSETTING:
> 
> ```text
> block new dependencies
> ```
> 
> may be wise.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27819. Existing Projects continue temporarily.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27820. This is:
> 
> ```text
> Containment Before Migration.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27821. Example legacy database.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27822. Policy:
> 
> ```text
> existing consumers allowed
> new projects denied
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27823. That stops debt growth.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27824. Exception requires:
> 
> ```text
> Decision.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27825. Debt Containment
> 
> Often easier than immediate debt removal.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27826. Example:
> 
> ```text
> do not add new endpoints
> to old API.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27827. Meanwhile migration proceeds.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 27828. Migration Queue
>

> # 28348. Главный результат
> 
> Теперь Innovation OS может рассматривать свою архитектуру как:
> 
> ```text
> evolving system
> ```
> 
> а не:
> 
> ```text
> static software installation.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28349. Полный evolution loop
> 
> ```text
> Observe Current Architecture
> ↓
> Detect Lifecycle Signals
> ↓
> Identify Debt / Future Gaps
> ↓
> Discover Alternatives
> ↓
> Build Architecture Options
> ↓
> Analyze Migration Paths
> ↓
> Sandbox / Benchmark
> ↓
> Pilot
> ↓
> Governance Decision
> ↓
> Staged Migration
> ↓
> Verify
> ↓
> Retire Legacy
> ↓
> Learn
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28350. Это добавляет к Artificial Technological Awareness:
> 
> # Evolutionary Self-Awareness
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28351. Теперь система знает:
> 
> ```text
> what it is
> what it depends on
> what is aging
> what alternatives exist
> what transition would require
> ```
> 
> ---
>

> 
> ```text
> destination
> ```
> 
> но и:
> 
> ```text

> ```

> а как:

> # единый производственный цикл инновации.

> Equipment
> Compute
> Organization
> Workflow
> Verification

> 
> в один исполнимый Program.

> 
> ---
> 
> # 28515. Example:
> 
> ```text id="jnlmgi"
> choose cheapest option
> meeting all MUST requirements
> under €500
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28516. Then machine decision can be deterministic/explainable.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28517. Architecture Lock
> 
> Selected project architecture stored as:
> 
> ```text id="hhbyex"
> architecture.lock
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28518. Similar to:
> 
> ```text id="so53j5"
> project.lock.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28519. Contains:
> 
> ```text id="rkt6k6"
> selected providers/contracts
> versions
> assumptions
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28520. But provider not always specific Resource yet.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28521. Example:
> 
> ```text id="h27guu"
> requires CNC capability
> ```
> 
> can remain unresolved until schedule time.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28522. Therefore lock may contain:
> 
> ```text id="kjzwpi"
> capability contract
> ```
> 
> instead of concrete provider.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28523. Late Binding
> 
> Very important.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28524. Bind Resource:
> 
> ```text id="hcg50i"
> as late as practical
> ```
> 
> when availability uncertain.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28525. Example:
> 
> ```text id="atdqfp"
> which exact 3D printer?
> ```
> 
> can be resolved near execution.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28526. Early Binding
> 
> Necessary where:
> 
> ```text id="hmssvv"
> design depends on provider-specific constraints.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28527. Example:
> 
> ```text id="yzgkw8"
> PCB fab minimum trace width.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28528. Then provider characteristics influence design.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28529. Binding Strategy
> 
> Each requirement can specify:
> 
> ```text id="avfx0x"
> EARLY
> LATE
> JUST_IN_TIME
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28530. This reduces unnecessary rigidity.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28531. Cross-Domain Resolver
> 
> Now central engine:
> 
> ```text id="o1vmvg"
> Capability Requirement
> ↓
> Resolver Router
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28532. Router chooses:
> 
> ```text id="8dbv94"
> Talent
> GitHub
> Research
> Funding
> Physical
> Compute
> Federation
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28533. One requirement may need:
> 
> ```text id="t9phfm"
> multiple resolvers.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28534. Example:
> 
> ```text id="x4ey9d"
> optical tactile sensing prototype
> ```
> 
> requires:
> 
> ```text id="fhyz1y"
> knowledge
> person
> lab
> software
> material
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28535. Therefore use:
> 
> # Composite Capability Resolution.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28536. Composite Provider Bundle
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text id="b1a72n"
> Researcher
> +
> Fiber sensor paper
> +
> DAQ software
> +
> Optical interrogator
> +
> Lab time
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28537. Bundle collectively:
> 
> ```text id="5hp7au"
> PROVIDES
> prototype capability.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28538. No single Resource does.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28539. This is one of most important project assembly concepts.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28540. Bundle Constraints
> 
> Need check:
> 
> ```text id="x7011c"
> time compatibility
> location compatibility
> interfaces
> authority
> budget
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28541. Example:
> 
> lab available in Germany,
> 
> expert available remotely,
> 
> equipment requires on-site operator.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28542. Feasible bundle may require:
> 
> ```text id="rbm4lm"
> local technician
> +
> remote expert.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28543. Resource Composition
> 
> Could be:
> 
> ```text id="j8ubnp"
> SEQUENTIAL
> PARALLEL
> JOINT
> ALTERNATIVE
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28544. SEQUENTIAL
> 
> Researcher designs,
> 
> manufacturer builds.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28545. PARALLEL
> 
> Firmware and enclosure developed simultaneously.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28546. JOINT
> 
> Operator + machine needed together.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28547. ALTERNATIVE
> 
> Two possible labs.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28548. This structure later compiles into:
> 
> ```text id="x88swh"
> Program Graph.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28549. Interface Contracts
> 
> Capabilities must connect.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28550. Example:
> 
> Sensor produces:
> 
> ```text id="mgnj2a"
> analog optical signal.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28551. DAQ expects:
> 
> ```text id="xpo6si"
> electrical voltage.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28552. Both individually good,
> 
> but incompatible directly.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28553. Therefore:
> 
> ```text id="a41uhu"
> Capability Match
> ≠
> System Compatibility.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28554. Need:
> 
> # Interface Compatibility.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28555. Interface types:
> 
> ```text id="t9byf5"
> DATA
> PHYSICAL
> ELECTRICAL
> MECHANICAL
> PROTOCOL
> SEMANTIC
> ORGANIZATIONAL
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28556. DATA
> 
> File/schema/model.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28557. PHYSICAL
> 
> Size/shape/material.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28558. ELECTRICAL
> 
> Voltage/current/connectors.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28559. MECHANICAL
> 
> Mounting/tolerance.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28560. PROTOCOL
> 
> API/message format.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28561. SEMANTIC
> 
> Meaning/schema interpretation.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28562. ORGANIZATIONAL
> 
> Contract/access/authority.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28563. Interface Adapter
> 
> If incompatible:
> 
> ```text id="rx0kk2"
> adapter capability
> ```
> 
> may resolve.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28564. Example:
> 
> ```text id="hmbc32"
> optical signal
> → photodiode
> → ADC
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28565. Adapter itself introduces:
> 
> ```text id="ed50g0"
> cost
> latency
> noise
> failure modes.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28566. Therefore adapters belong:
> 
> ```text id="u4ckv2"
> architecture graph.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28567. Interface Gap
> 
> A new gap category/view:
> 
> ```text id="7n6ci4"
> INTERFACE_GAP.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28568. Example:
> 
> ```text id="el079m"
> components exist
> but cannot connect.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28569. This is common in multidisciplinary projects.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28570. Compatibility Chain
> 
> ```text id="sejpki"
> Provider A
> ↓ Interface
> Adapter
> ↓ Interface
> Provider B
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28571. Verification must test:
> 
> ```text id="d1al06"
> whole chain.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28572. Individual component verification insufficient.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28573. End-to-End Capability
> 
> Ultimately:
> 
> ```text id="43rxnd"
> system capability
> ```
> 
> must be verified at system boundary.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28574. Example:
> 
> ```text id="fuh9jq"
> sensor detects pressure
> ```
> 
> not merely:
> 
> ```text id="z3e8tw"
> photodiode works
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28575. This creates:
> 
> # Integration Verification.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28576. Project Architecture Graph
> 
> Contains:
> 
> ```text id="yysjba"
> capabilities
> providers
> interfaces
> adapters
> verification points
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28577. It is distinct from:
> 
> ```text id="f2vfwk"
> Task Graph.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28578. Architecture Graph:
> 
> ```text id="pmeud4"
> what system is composed of.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28579. Task Graph:
> 
> ```text id="l7pw5v"
> what must be done.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28580. Schedule:
> 
> ```text id="2uyqm4"
> when.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28581. Assignment:
> 
> ```text id="hebyyf"
> who/what executes.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28582. Keep separate.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28583. Program Compiler
> 
> Now converts:
> 
> ```text id="743hi3"
> selected Architecture Graph
> ```
> 
> into:
> 
> ```text id="a1s6te"
> Actions.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28584. Example architecture requires custom PCB.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28585. Compiler creates:
> 
> ```text id="m018ti"
> design PCB
> review PCB
> manufacture PCB
> inspect PCB
> test PCB.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28586. Program Compiler should use:
> 
> ```text id="r93td4"
> procedural templates.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28587. Example templates:
> 
> ```text id="kxgfri"
> software development
> hardware prototype
> research experiment
> grant application
> procurement
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28588. Template ≠ fixed workflow.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28589. Compiler adapts based on:
> 
> ```text id="ue9b4i"
> context
> risk
> available capabilities.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28590. Example custom part:
> 
> ```text id="slnwox"
> 3D printed prototype
> ```
> 
> needs less procedure than:
> 
> ```text id="9zalz0"
> medical production component.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28591. Domain policies can add:
> 
> ```text id="ccrr38"
> required reviews.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28592. Compiled Program Graph
> 
> Contains:
> 
> ```text id="2uysoe"
> Actions
> Dependencies
> Decision Gates
> Verification Gates
> Wait States
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28593. Example:
> 
> ```text id="uvt9te"
> Research
> ↓
> Concept Selection
> ↓
> Prototype Design
> ↓
> Fabrication
> ↓
> Integration
> ↓
> Testing
> ↓
> Iteration
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28594. But many branches parallel.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28595. Example:
> 
> ```text id="vwrnyr"
> electronics
> mechanical design
> firmware
> ```
> 
> can run concurrently after interface freeze.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28596. Parallelization Detection
> 
> Compiler can identify:
> 
> ```text id="j1mjsl"
> independent subgraphs.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28597. More parallelism may reduce calendar time.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28598. But may increase:
> 
> ```text id="y2zv2h"
> coordination cost
> integration risk
> resource demand.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28599. Again no assumption:
> 
> ```text id="h6eajo"
> more parallel = better.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28600. Major milestone
> 
> К **28600** система преобразует:
> 
> ```text id="c8pash"
> Mission Architecture
> ```
> 
> в:
> 
> # executable Program Graph.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28601. Program Graph States
> 
> At program level:
> 
> ```text id="u5jmco"
> DRAFT
> RESOLVING
> READY
> EXECUTING
> BLOCKED
> ADAPTING
> VERIFYING
> COMPLETED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28602. `READY`
> 
> means required initial conditions satisfied.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28603. Not necessarily every future Resource already booked.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28604. Can support:
> 
> ```text id="3k45q7"
> late binding.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28605. Resource Resolution Phase
> 
> For each Action:
> 
> ```text id="r8nq8p"
> required capabilities
> → candidate providers.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28606. Example:
> 
> ```text id="l7owyt"
> CAD design
> ```
> 
> may be provided by:
> 
> ```text id="eovg25"
> Person
> AI-assisted workflow
> external engineering firm.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28607. Different provider classes can satisfy same capability.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28608. This is core universal resolver principle.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28609. Human vs AI vs Service
> 
> Do not hard-code:
> 
> ```text id="3oimac"
> Task type → executor type.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28610. Instead:
> 
> ```text id="35kxjo"
> Capability Requirements
> +
> Authority
> +
> Verification.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28611. Example literature scan:
> 
> AI may perform.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28612. Final safety sign-off:
> 
> ```text id="5gnpm8"
> human/authorized specialist
> ```
> 
> may be required.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28613. Hybrid Execution
> 
> Action may decompose:
> 
> ```text id="ne9yw4"
> AI draft
> ↓
> human review
> ↓
> service execution.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28614. This is first-class pattern.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28615. Human-in-the-Loop ≠ Human-does-everything.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28616. AI-in-the-Loop ≠ AI-has-authority.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28617. Role Compiler
> 
> For each Program Graph,
> 
> derive needed roles:
> 
> ```text id="tcd32m"
> Designer
> Researcher
> Fabricator
> Reviewer
> Verifier
> Coordinator
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28618. These roles map to:
> 
> ```text id="zyr74p"
> Capabilities.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28619. Team Builder then resolves:
> 
> ```text id="qunpd7"
> people/agents/services.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28620. Example:
> 
> ```text id="7fa88m"
> Research Agent
> Electronics Engineer
> Lab Technician
> Verification Agent
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28621. Team Hypothesis remains:
> 
> ```text id="03mb4i"
> not consent.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28622. Candidate person ≠ committed participant.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28623. Existing consortium states reused:
> 
> ```text id="esdzfv"
> UNKNOWN
> CONTACTED
> INTERESTED
> NEGOTIATING
> COMMITTED
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28624. Project staffing should distinguish:
> 
> ```text id="l3zcqh"
> candidate
> assigned
> confirmed.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28625. ASSIGNED_TO ≠ ACCEPTED.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28626. For human work,
> 
> assignment may require:
> 
> ```text id="l8z15w"
> consent/contract.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28627. AI/service assignments differ.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28628. Program Resource Plan
> 
> Contains:
> 
> ```text id="rbjw0x"
> human hours
> compute
> equipment
> materials
> money
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28629. This connects:
> 
> ```text id="odx3vj"
> resource accounting.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28630. Program Budget
> 
> Not just money.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28631. Multi-resource budget:
> 
> ```text id="oh9h1j"
> EUR
> person-hours
> GPU-hours
> lab-hours
> material quantities.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28632. Each unit explicit.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28633. Resource Reservation
> 
> Some resources need early booking:
> 
> ```text id="pxcv8f"
> lab
> equipment
> human calendar
> compute quota.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28634. Others can be:
> 
> ```text id="j7a637"
> on-demand.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28635. Reservation Plan
> 
> Compiler can create:
> 
> ```text id="pd0rh2"
> reserve scarce resources first.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28636. Example:
> 
> synchrotron slot in 4 months
> 
> may dictate schedule.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28637. Scarcity-Critical Path
> 
> Traditional critical path uses task duration.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28638. Innovation projects also have:
> 
> ```text id="fzzqfe"
> scarce-resource critical path.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28639. Example:
> 
> ```text id="mn6qgf"
> specialized equipment available once per month.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28640. Task itself 2h,
> 
> but waiting time 30 days.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28641. Need model:
> 
> ```text id="ra4ekt"
> calendar availability.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28642. Program schedule should include:
> 
> ```text id="ibuf1r"
> queue/wait windows.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28643. Time To Capability
> 
> TTC now becomes project-wide.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28644. For missing capability:
> 
> ```text id="6kflbs"
> hire
> buy
> build
> train
> partner
> ```
> 
> have different TTC.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28645. Project option architecture should include:
> 
> ```text id="j4jhgp"
> TTC impact.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28646. Example:
> 
> Buy equipment:
> 
> ```text id="u5k99s"
> 6 months.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28647. External lab:
> 
> ```text id="i4frdv"
> 2 weeks.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28648. But external lab has:
> 
> ```text id="7qx23m"
> less control / recurring cost.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28649. No universal preference.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28650. Funding Resolution
> 
> Program budget creates:
> 
> ```text id="kwe2py"
> Funding Requirements.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28651. Funding Resolver can search:
> 
> ```text id="a39h4z"
> grants
> investors
> internal budget
> sponsors
> procurement.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28652. But funding schedule matters.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28653. Example:
> 
> Grant decision in 9 months
> 
> cannot fund:
> 
> ```text id="j4dh5z"
> prototype due next month.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28654. Thus:
> 
> ```text id="7v4lf5"
> Funding Fit
> ```
> 
> includes:
> 
> ```text id="ekq7kv"
> timing.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28655. Working Capital
> 
> Even awarded grant may pay later.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28656. Program Compiler must distinguish:
> 
> ```text id="opdj5v"
> funding commitment
> cash availability.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28657. Cashflow Graph
> 
> Could model:
> 
> ```text id="m4bakk"
> planned expenses
> expected inflows.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28658. Funding gap may appear:
> 
> ```text id="8sm7t7"
> temporally.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28659. This can alter Program schedule.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28660. Project Compilation therefore includes:
> 
> # resource-time feasibility.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28661. Not simply:
> 
> ```text id="5fxvz2"
> all required resources exist somewhere.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28662. Need them:
> 
> ```text id="gndmc3"
> at compatible times.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28663. Temporal Join
> 
> Example:
> 
> ```text id="7rbd2k"
> Expert available May
> Lab available June.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28664. If expert must attend lab:
> 
> ```text id="q8kyqj"
> bundle infeasible unless schedule changes.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28665. Temporal Constraint Solver
> 
> MVP can use:
> 
> ```text id="2ttbrk"
> simple interval compatibility.

> 
> ---
> 
> # 28666. Later:
> 
> ```text id="hmihmc"
> constraint programming.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28667. Spatial Feasibility
> 
> Resources also have:
> 
> ```text id="nyyl2k"
> locations.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28668. Example:
> 
> material in warehouse A,
> 
> machine in site B,
> 
> deadline tomorrow.

> ---
> 
> # 28669. Logistics Resolver determines:
> 
> ```text id="7wcxm7"
> transfer feasible?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28670. Thus Program Compiler links:
> 
> ```text id="wvagzv"
> time
> space
> resources.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28671. Spatial-Temporal Resource Plan
> 
> For physical programs:
> 
> ```text id="4m6df3"
> Resource
> Location
> Time
> Movement.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28672. Example:
> 
> ```text id="vjnyvj"
> Material Batch
> Warehouse
> ↓ shipment
> Lab
> ↓ processing
> Inspection

> ---
> 
> # 28673. Movement Actions become part of Program Graph.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 28674. Logistics ≠ external afterthought.
> 
> ---
>

> # Innovation Portfolio Intelligence, Shared Capability Planning & Ecosystem-Level Resource Orchestration v0.1

> ## 29318. Главный переход
> 
> До сих пор система умеет собирать:
> 
> ```text
> одну Mission
> ↓
> один Program
> ↓
> набор Projects
> ↓
> Resources
> ↓
> Execution
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29319. Теперь предположим, что одновременно существуют:
> 
> ```text
> 10 Missions
> 100 Missions
> 10 000 Missions
> 100 000 Missions.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29320. Тогда локально разумное решение для одного проекта
> 
> может быть:
> 
> ```text
> глобально неэффективным.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29321. Example
> 
> Каждый из 30 Projects отдельно покупает:
> 
> ```text
> почти одинаковый GPU server.
> ```

> # 29322. Возможно, разумнее создать:
> 
> ```text

> ---
> 
> # 29323. Но обратное тоже возможно.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29324. Один общий GPU cluster может создать:
>

> queue bottleneck
> data locality problems.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29325. Поэтому:
> 
> ```text
> Shared Resource
> ≠
> Automatically Better.

> 
> ---
> 
> # 29326. Portfolio Intelligence должен обнаруживать:
> 
> ```text
> pattern
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29327. Но:
>

> не автоматически принимать решение.

> # 29353. Demand Extraction
> 
> Каждая Mission уже имеет:
> 
> ```text
> Capability Requirements.
> ```

> ---
> 
> # 29354. Их можно агрегировать.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29355. Example
> 
> ```text

> Mission B requires SEMANTIC_SEARCH
> Mission C requires SEMANTIC_SEARCH

> 
> # 29356. Portfolio detects:
> 
> ```text

> 
> ---
> 
> # 29357. Но сначала нужно проверить:
> 
> ```text
> одинаковы ли требования?

> 
> # 29358. Потому что одинаковое имя Capability
> 
> не гарантирует:
> 
> ```text

> 
> # 29359. Example
>

>

> public docs

>

> 
> # 29360. Mission B:
> 
> ```text
> semantic search
> confidential medical docs
> ```

> 
> # 29361. Technical interface may overlap.

> 
> # 29362. Но:
> 
> ```text
> security
> data locality
> evidence requirements

>

> # 29363. Therefore aggregate by:
> 
> ```text
> Capability Contract similarity.

> 
> ---
> 
> # 29364. Demand Cluster
> 
> Can group:
> 
> ```text
> near-equivalent requirements

> 
> ---
> 
> # 29365. But preserve:
> 
> ```text
> constraints
> contexts
> exceptions.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29366. Demand Cluster is derived view.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29367. Example:
> 
> ```text
> CAPABILITY:
> DOCUMENT_EXTRACTION

>

> 
> # 29368. Cluster A:
> 
> ```text
> public documents
> low assurance
> batch
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29369. Cluster B:
> 
> ```text
> confidential
> high assurance
> local execution
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29370. Maybe:
> 
> ```text
> different shared services.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29371. Demand Volume
> 
> Possible dimensions:
> 
> ```text
> number of Missions
> expected hours
> compute load
> equipment hours
> recurrence
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29372. But raw count alone can mislead.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29373. Example:
> 
> 100 Missions each need:
> 
> ```text
> 1 minute/year.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29374. One Mission needs:
> 
> ```text
> 10 000 GPU-hours/month.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29375. Therefore distinguish:
> 
> ```text
> Demand Breadth
> Demand Intensity
> Demand Frequency

> 
> ---
> 
> # 29376. Demand Breadth
> 
> ```text
> how many distinct Missions/Programs need it.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29377. Demand Intensity
> 
> ```text
> how much capacity is consumed.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29378. Demand Frequency
> 
> ```text
> how often it recurs.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29379. Demand Criticality
> 
> Another dimension:
> 
> ```text
> how many critical outcomes depend on it.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29380. Avoid one demand score.

> 
> # 29381. Shared Capability Candidate
> 
> A repeated demand pattern can produce:
> 
> ```text
> Shared Capability Hypothesis.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29382. Example
> 
> ```text
> Many Missions repeatedly need
> PDF → structured semantic extraction.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29383. Candidate:
> 
> ```text
> Shared Document Intelligence Service.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29384. But candidate can have architectures:
> 
> ```text
> central service
> local package
> federated service
> standardized interface
> training/template
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29385. Thus shared capability ≠ central server.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29386. This distinction is critical.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29387. Shared Capability Delivery Modes
> 
> ```text
> CENTRAL_SERVICE
> FEDERATED_SERVICE
> REUSABLE_PACKAGE
> STANDARD
> SHARED_EQUIPMENT
> TRAINING_CAPABILITY
> KNOWLEDGE_COMMONS
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29388. CENTRAL_SERVICE
> 
> One provider serves many Missions.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29389. FEDERATED_SERVICE
> 
> Many providers expose:
> 
> ```text
> same semantic contract.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29390. REUSABLE_PACKAGE
> 
> Projects install locally.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29391. STANDARD
> 
> The shared asset is:
> 
> ```text
> compatibility.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29392. SHARED_EQUIPMENT
> 
> Physical pool.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29393. TRAINING_CAPABILITY
> 
> Increase human provider supply.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29394. KNOWLEDGE_COMMONS
> 
> Common:
> 
> ```text
> data
> documentation
> benchmarks
> patterns.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29395. Portfolio Engine should compare modes.
> 
> ---
>

> 
> Repeated demand:
> 
> ```text
> ARM deployment.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29397. Possible responses:

> central ARM build service

> 
> ---
> 
> # 29398.
> 
> ```text
> multi-arch CI package
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29399.
> 
> ```text
> developer training
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29400.
> 
> ```text
> prebuilt runtime images.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29401. One or several may coexist.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29402. Shared Capability Economics
> 
> Need compare:
> 
> ```text
> repeated local cost
> vs
> shared investment cost.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29403. Example
> 
> 20 teams each spend:
> 
> ```text
> 40h/year
> ```
> 
> maintaining same connector.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29404. Aggregate:
> 
> ```text
> 800h/year.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29405. Shared package may cost:
> 
> ```text
> 250h/year.
> ```
> 
> to maintain.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29406. That creates plausible:
> 
> ```text
> efficiency hypothesis.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29407. But not guaranteed.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29408. Shared service also adds:
> 
> ```text
> governance
> coordination
> support

> 
> cost.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29409. Therefore:
> 
> ```text
> Gross Duplication
> ≠
> Net Savings.

>

> 
> # 29410. Need Total Cost of Shared Capability.
>

> 
> # 29411. Components:
> 
> ```text
> build
> operate
> support
> govern
> migrate
> integrate

> 
> ---
> 
> # 29412. Compare against:
> 
> ```text
> distributed alternatives.
> ```
>

>

>

>

> ```text

>

>

>

> # 29427. Example:

>

> 
> ---
> 
> # 29428. Queue grows.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29429. Possible options:
> 
> ```text

> improve scheduling
> buy second instrument
> outsource
> reduce demand
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29430. Again:
> 
> ```text
> buy more capacity
> ```
> 
> is not automatic.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29431. Portfolio Bottleneck
> 
> Defined as:
> 
> > shared constraint currently limiting progress across multiple Missions.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29432. Could be:
> 
> ```text
> Resource
> Capability
> Policy
> Decision
> Funding
> Knowledge
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29433. Example:
> 
> ```text
> only one legal reviewer
> ```
> 
> blocks 15 consortium agreements.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29434. Possible solutions:
> 
> ```text
> second reviewer
> templates
> automation
> external service
> simpler process.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29435. Bottleneck may be reduced by:
> 
> ```text
> demand reduction
> ```
> 
> rather than supply increase.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29436. Example:
> 
> 20 projects manually review same boilerplate.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29437. Standard template removes 70% demand.
>

> 
> # 29438. This is:
> 
> # Demand-Side Capability Optimization.

> 
> # 29439. Portfolio Engine must look at:
> 
> ```text
> supply
> +
> demand.
> ```
>
