> 
> # 29440. Capability Scarcity
> 
> If:
> 
> ```text
> Demand > Available Capacity
> ```
> 
> repeatedly,
> 
> generate:
> 
> ```text
> Scarcity Signal.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29441. Scarcity Signal alone:
> 
> ```text
> ≠ shortage proof under all periods.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29442. Need time dimension.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29443. Example:
> 
> ```text
> GPU shortage
> ```
> 
> only Friday nights.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29444. Could fix with:
> 
> ```text
> scheduling.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29445. Not new hardware.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29446. Capacity Curve
> 
> For each shared Capability:
> 
> ```text
> available capacity over time.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29447. Demand Curve:
> 
> ```text
> requested capacity over time.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29448. Overlay reveals:
> 
> ```text
> periodic bottlenecks.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29449. Capacity is not always divisible.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29450. Example equipment:
> 
> ```text
> one 4-hour experiment
> ```
> 
> cannot split into 4 one-hour resources.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29451. Need:
> 
> ```text
> booking constraints.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29452. Human specialist:
> 
> ```text
> context switching
> ```
> 
> also makes simple hour aggregation imperfect.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29453. Thus capacity models are domain-specific.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29454. Portfolio Resource Orchestration
> 
> At high level:
> 
> ```text
> Missions
> ↓
> Resource Demands
> ↓
> Shared Capacity
> ↓
> Allocation Decisions
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29455. Scheduler ≠ Authority.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29456. Portfolio Scheduler can propose:
> 
> ```text
> allocations.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29457. Actual allocation follows:
> 
> ```text
> governance / contracts / owner rules.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29458. First-Come-First-Served
> 
> Easy policy.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29459. But can be poor when:
> 
> ```text
> low-impact jobs consume scarce resource
> before critical deadline work.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29460. Alternative policies:
> 
> ```text
> reservation
> priority classes
> fair-share
> quota
> deadline-aware
> auction/market
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29461. No one universal policy.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29462. Policy must be:
> 
> ```text
> explicit
> transparent
> auditable.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29463. Portfolio Engine should not invent hidden priority.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29464. Strategic priority originates in:
> 
> ```text
> governance.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29465. Resource Allocation Request
> 
> Contains:
> 
> ```text
> Mission
> Capability
> Quantity
> Time Window
> Criticality
> Alternatives
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29466. Allocation Decision records:
> 
> ```text
> why
> what policy
> what trade-off.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29467. Rejected allocation does not mean:
> 
> ```text
> Mission rejected.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29468. Resolver can seek:
> 
> ```text
> alternative provider
> schedule
> scope.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29469. Resource Contention
> 
> When two Missions need same unique asset.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29470. System can produce:
> 
> ```text
> Conflict Object/View.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29471. Example:
> 
> ```text
> Mission A needs Lab X Monday
> Mission B needs Lab X Monday.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29472. Options:
> 
> ```text
> A Monday / B Tuesday
> B Monday / A Tuesday
> alternative lab
> parallel capacity
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29473. Portfolio decision may need:
> 
> ```text
> deadline
> impact
> contract
> ```
> 
> context.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29474. Allocation Fairness
> 
> Could be important in shared ecosystems.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29475. But fairness semantics differ by organization.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29476. Therefore Portfolio Engine exposes:
> 
> ```text
> allocation history
> policy
> utilization
> ```
>

> 
> # 29477. It does not invent:

> 
> # 29483. Shared Capability Federation
> 
> Instead of one central laboratory:
> 
> ```text
> Lab A
> Lab B
> Lab C
> ```
> 
> all expose:
> 
> ```text
> MICROSCOPY_CAPABILITY.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29484. Resolver routes demand.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29485. Benefits:
> 
> ```text
> redundancy
> locality
> autonomy.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29486. Costs:
> 
> ```text
> standardization
> verification
> routing complexity.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29487. This is:
> 
> # Federated Capability Pool.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29488. Provider Conformance
> 
> For federation to work,
> 
> providers need:
> 
> ```text
> compatible capability contracts.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29489. Example microscopy profile:
> 
> ```text
> sample size
> resolution
> output format
> operator requirements.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29490. Providers may implement:
> 
> ```text
> different equipment.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29491. Stable contract permits:
> 
> ```text
> substitution.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29492. Portfolio Intelligence can therefore decide to invest in:
> 
> ```text
> standardization
> ```
> 
> instead of:
> 
> ```text
> central infrastructure.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29493. Shared Standard as Infrastructure
> 
> Very important concept.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29494. Sometimes greatest shared asset is:
> 
> ```text
> common interface.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29495. Example:
> 
> 10 independent labs already exist.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29496. Problem:
> 
> ```text
> each has incompatible booking/data interface.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29497. Rather than buy:
> 
> ```text
> 11th laboratory
> ```
> 
> build:
> 
> ```text
> shared capability profile + federation connector.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29498. This converts:
> 
> ```text
> fragmented supply
> ```
> 
> into:
> 
> ```text
> usable network capacity.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29499. Thus standardization can create:
> 
> ```text
> virtual capacity.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29500. Major milestone
> 
> К **29500** Portfolio Intelligence recognizes:
> 
> # physical capacity, organizational capacity and interoperability capacity
> 
> as different things.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29501. Fragmented Capacity
> 
> Resources exist,
> 
> but cannot be easily coordinated.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29502. Symptoms:
> 
> ```text
> different APIs
> unknown availability
> manual onboarding
> incompatible schemas.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29503. Shared interface can unlock:
> 
> ```text
> latent capacity.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29504. This is important for Virtual Technopark.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29505. Virtual Infrastructure
> 
> Does not necessarily own:
> 
> ```text
> physical resources.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29506. It can create infrastructure through:
> 
> ```text
> coordination
> standards
> discovery
> contracts.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29507. This lowers capital requirement.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29508. Example:
> 
> ```text
> 100 independent 3D printers
> ```
> 
> become:
> 
> ```text
> federated manufacturing capacity
> ```
> 
> if standardized enough.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29509. But:
> 
> ```text
> advertised capability
> ≠
> verified production capability.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29510. Verification layer remains mandatory.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29511. Cross-Mission Dependency
> 
> Project A may produce something:
> 
> ```text
> required by Project B.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29512. Example:
> 
> ```text
> Project A builds semantic protocol v2.
> Project B builds port twin requiring v2.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29513. That creates:
> 
> ```text
> inter-project dependency.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29514. Portfolio Graph therefore includes:
> 
> ```text
> Project → Project dependencies.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29515. Existing DEPENDS_ON relation.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29516. But dependence can be on:
> 
> ```text
> Capability
> Artifact
> Decision
> ```
> 
> not only project.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29517. Better model:
> 
> ```text
> Project B
> REQUIRES
> Artifact/Capability produced by A.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29518. Then dependency arises naturally.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29519. Shared Dependency
> 
> Many projects depend on:
> 
> ```text
> same Capability.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29520. Example:
> 
> ```text
> Identity service
> ```
> 
> supports 80 Missions.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29521. This creates:
> 
> ```text
> systemic operational importance.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29522. Portfolio Intelligence can identify:
> 
> ```text
> high downstream impact.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29523. But:
> 
> ```text
> graph centrality
> ≠
> strategic priority.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29524. It is one structural signal.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29525. Portfolio Blast Radius
> 
> For shared capability failure:
> 
> ```text
> which Missions affected?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29526. Observability module already traces upward.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29527. Portfolio layer aggregates:
> 
> ```text
> ecosystem-scale impact.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29528. Example:
> 
> ```text
> Funding API down
> ```
> 
> blocks:
> 
> ```text
> 22 funding workflows.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29529. That may justify:
> 
> ```text
> redundancy investment.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29530. Again as proposal.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29531. Shared Capability Resilience
> 
> Dimensions:
> 
> ```text
> provider count
> failure-domain diversity
> capacity headroom
> fallback readiness
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29532. Provider Count alone insufficient.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29533. Example:
> 
> 3 providers all run on:
> 
> ```text
> same cloud region.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29534. Apparent redundancy,
> 
> common failure domain.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29535. Therefore:
> 
> ```text
> Provider Diversity
> ≠
> Failure-Domain Diversity.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29536. Portfolio planner can identify:
> 
> ```text
> correlated dependencies.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29537. Example:
> 
> ```text
> multiple AI providers
> all dependent on one data source.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29538. Shared latent bottleneck.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29539. Systemic Dependency Graph
> 
> Could include:
> 
> ```text
> Critical Capabilities
> Shared Resources
> Common Suppliers
> Common Standards
> Common Data Sources
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29540. Used for:
> 
> ```text
> resilience analysis.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29541. But do not overstate:
> 
> ```text
> dependency = imminent risk.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29542. It indicates:
> 
> ```text
> exposure.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29543. Exposure + failure likelihood/evidence + impact
> 
> inform planning.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29544. Mission Coupling
> 
> Two Missions can be:
> 
> ```text
> independent
> loosely coupled
> strongly coupled.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29545. Strong coupling example:
> 
> ```text
> same prototype hardware
> same delivery date
> same specialist.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29546. Coupling can produce:
> 
> ```text
> coordination burden.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29547. Portfolio planner can reduce coupling by:
> 
> ```text
> interface freeze
> resource duplication
> schedule separation
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29548. But decoupling can cost:
> 
> ```text
> extra resources.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29549. Shared Project
> 
> If many Missions need same output,
> 
> create:
> 
> ```text
> Shared Project.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29550. Example:
> 
> ```text
> Build Common Authentication Adapter.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29551. Consumers become:
> 
> ```text
> stakeholder Projects.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29552. But shared Project creates new risk:
> 
> ```text
> all consumers wait for it.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29553. Shared Project Scheduling
> 
> Need:
> 
> ```text
> consumer deadlines.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29554. Earliest dependent deadline may constrain.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29555. But consumer can sometimes use:
> 
> ```text
> temporary local workaround.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29556. Portfolio planner may propose:
> 
> ```text
> shared core
> +
> temporary adapters.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29557. Again transition architecture.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29558. Shared Capability Ownership
> 
> Who operates shared infrastructure?
> 
> Possible:
> 
> ```text
> central organization
> consortium
> service provider
> open-source community
> federated maintainers.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29559. Governance model matters.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29560. Technical sharing without:
> 
> ```text
> maintenance responsibility
> ```
> 
> is fragile.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29561. Therefore Shared Capability Proposal requires:
> 
> ```text
> operator model.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29562. Example:
> 
> ```text
> who maintains
> who funds
> who approves changes
> who handles incidents.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29563. This is:
> 
> # Institutional Architecture
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29564. Innovation OS must treat organization design
> 
> as part of capability design.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29565. Shared Service =
> 
> ```text
> technology
> +
> operators
> +
> funding
> +
> governance
> +
> support.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29566. Not merely code.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29567. Existing Dynamic Organization module applies.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29568. Repeated shared capability demand can create:
> 
> ```text
> Organizational Hypothesis.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29569. Example:
> 
> ```text
> Maybe create Robotics Test Center.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29570. But organization creation is:
> 
> ```text
> governance decision.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29571. Organizational Form Options
> 
> ```text
> internal team
> shared service
> consortium
> independent company
> open community
> contract network
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29572. No universal choice.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29573. Portfolio Intelligence should expose:
> 
> ```text
> structural implications.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29574. Example central internal team:
> 
> ```text
> more control
> less federation.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29575. External service:
> 
> ```text
> faster setup
> external dependence.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29576. Open-source community:
> 
> ```text
> wide reuse
> governance/maintainer uncertainty.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29577. These are trade-offs,
> 
> not rankings.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29578. Shared Capability Funding
> 
> Demand from multiple Missions can justify:
> 
> ```text
> pooled funding.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29579. Example:
> 
> ```text
> 10 projects each contribute €1k
> ```
> 
> toward:
> 
> ```text
> shared test rig.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29580. But accounting must track:
> 
> ```text
> commitment
> ownership/access rights
> maintenance.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29581. Shared Asset Cost Allocation
> 
> Possible policies:
> 
> ```text
> equal contribution
> usage-based
> capacity reservation
> grant-funded common pool
> sponsorship.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29582. Again no universal policy.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29583. Cost Allocation ≠ Ownership.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29584. One party may fund:
> 
> ```text
> most asset cost
> ```
> 
> while consortium agreement allows:
> 
> ```text
> shared use.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29585. Need explicit rights.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29586. Shared Resource Access Contract
> 
> Could define:
> 
> ```text
> who
> how much
> when
> under which cost
> with which priority.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29587. This becomes Policy/Artifact.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29588. Portfolio Scheduler reads it.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29589. Shared Service Demand Shaping
> 
> If shared resource overloaded,
> 
> system can:
> 
> ```text
> batch
> cache
> reuse results
> standardize requests
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29590. Example:
> 
> 20 Missions separately compute:
> 
> ```text
> same embedding corpus.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29591. Could build:
> 
> ```text
> shared Artifact.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29592. This eliminates duplicate compute.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29593. But sharing allowed only if:
> 
> ```text
> data rights
> context
> version
> ```
> 
> permit.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29594. Result Reuse
> 
> A Project result can satisfy another Mission requirement.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29595. Before commissioning new work:
> 
> ```text
> search existing Artifacts/Capabilities.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29596. This is:
> 
> # Reuse-First Resolution.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29597. But:
> 
> ```text
> existing artifact
> ≠
> fit-for-purpose.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29598. Verify compatibility.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29599. Example existing dataset:
> 
> ```text
> similar domain
> ```
> 
> but:
> 
> ```text
> wrong license / outdated / low quality.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29600. Major milestone
> 
> К **29600** Portfolio Engine начинает снижать duplication через:
> 
> # verified reuse
> 
> а не через запрет параллельной работы.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29601. Parallel Work Can Be Valuable
> 
> Two teams solving same problem may create:
> 
> ```text
> independent approaches
> competition of hypotheses
> resilience.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29602. Therefore:
> 
> ```text
> Duplication ≠ Waste.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29603. Need classify duplication.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29604. Duplication Types
> 
> ```text
> ACCIDENTAL
> REDUNDANT_FOR_RESILIENCE
> COMPETING_EXPERIMENT
> INDEPENDENT_VERIFICATION
> UNAVOIDABLE_LOCAL
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29605. ACCIDENTAL
> 
> Teams unaware of each other
> 
> build near-identical artifact.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29606. REDUNDANT_FOR_RESILIENCE
> 
> Intentional second provider.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29607. COMPETING_EXPERIMENT
> 
> Different hypotheses.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29608. INDEPENDENT_VERIFICATION
> 
> Replication scientifically useful.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29609. UNAVOIDABLE_LOCAL
> 
> Data/privacy constraints prevent sharing.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29610. Portfolio engine should not merge these blindly.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29611. Duplicate Detection Pipeline
> 
> ```text
> Project Goals
> Capabilities
> Artifacts
> Methods
> ↓
> Similarity Detection
> ↓
> Context Comparison
> ↓
> Duplication Candidate
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29612. Candidate states:
> 
> ```text
> POSSIBLE_OVERLAP
> RELATED
> DUPLICATE_CONFIRMED
> INTENTIONAL_PARALLEL
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29613. AI may detect semantic similarity.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29614. But confirmation may need:
> 
> ```text
> project owner review.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29615. Duplicate Resolution Options
> 
> ```text
> share artifact
> merge effort
> coordinate interfaces
> continue independently
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29616. System recommends structure,
> 
> not forced merger.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29617. Shared Knowledge Discovery
> 
> Two Projects may not duplicate implementation,
> 
> but share:
> 
> ```text
> same research question.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29618. Example:
> 
> ```text
> How durable is optical fiber under repeated bending?
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29619. Could create:
> 
> ```text
> shared experiment.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29620. Both Missions consume result.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29621. This creates:
> 
> # Shared Evidence Production.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29622. Very valuable in research-heavy ecosystem.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29623. Evidence can be:
> 
> ```text
> public
> consortium-shared
> restricted.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29624. Access policy applies.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29625. Shared Experiment
> 
> Could test:
> 
> ```text
> one common unknown
> ```
> 
> for multiple Projects.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29626. Example:
> 
> 5 robotics teams need:
> 
> ```text
> material fatigue curve.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29627. One well-designed experiment may serve all.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29628. But only if:
> 
> ```text
> operating conditions overlap.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29629. Otherwise shared result may not generalize.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29630. Thus:
> 
> ```text
> Same Question Text
> ≠
> Same Experimental Context.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29631. Shared Evidence Contract
> 
> Defines:
> 
> ```text
> population/material
> conditions
> measurement
> quality
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29632. Consumers declare:
> 
> ```text
> whether evidence is applicable.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29633. Portfolio Knowledge Bottleneck
> 
> Repeated unknown appears across many Projects.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29634. Example:
> 
> ```text
> No reliable benchmark for tactile skin durability.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29635. Rather than each project improvise,
> 
> create:
> 
> ```text
> Benchmark Development Program.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29636. This is shared Knowledge Capability.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29637. Benchmark as Infrastructure
> 
> Important.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29638. Shared benchmark can accelerate:
> 
> ```text
> comparison
> verification
> technology transfer.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29639. Similarly:
> 
> ```text
> reference dataset
> reference fixture
> reference procedure
> ```
> 
> can be ecosystem infrastructure.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29640. Infrastructure therefore includes:
> 
> ```text
> physical
> digital
> semantic
> epistemic.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29641. Epistemic Infrastructure
> 
> Examples:
> 
> ```text
> benchmark
> taxonomy
> gold dataset
> standard method
> reference model.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29642. These reduce repeated uncertainty.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29643. Portfolio Engine should discover:
> 
> ```text
> high-reuse epistemic gaps.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29644. Example:
> 
> 50 Missions need:
> 
> ```text
> same entity-resolution benchmark.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29645. Candidate investment:
> 
> ```text
> common Gold Dataset.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29646. Shared Knowledge Capital
> 
> A new reusable asset class/view.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29647. Not new root.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29648. Built from:
> 
> ```text
> Artifacts
> Evidence
> Concepts
> Procedures.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29649. Shared Capability Dependency
> 
> A shared service may itself need:
> 
> ```text
> funding
> operators
> compute
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29650. Therefore portfolio investments create:
> 
> ```text
> new Missions.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29651. Recursive structure:
> 
> ```text
> Missions
> ↓ repeated demand
> Shared Capability Mission
> ↓
> new Capability
> ↓
> supports Missions.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29652. This is:
> 
> # Capability Capital Formation.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29653. Capital Formation Loop
> 
> ```text
> Demand
> ↓
> Investment Hypothesis
> ↓
> Capability Build
> ↓
> Reuse
> ↓
> Lower TTC / Cost
> ↓
> More Missions
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29654. But could also fail:
> 
> ```text
> shared service built
> ↓
> little adoption.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29655. Therefore investments require:
> 
> ```text
> adoption hypothesis.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29656. Demand Evidence ≠ Adoption Guarantee.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29657. Example teams may prefer:
> 
> ```text
> local tools.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29658. Need understand:
> 
> ```text
> switching cost
> integration cost
> governance concerns.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29659. Shared Capability Pilot
> 
> Before large investment:
> 
> ```text
> serve 2–3 Missions.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29660. Measure:
> 
> ```text
> reuse
> integration burden
> quality
> queueing.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 29661. Then scale if supported.
>

> # 30148. Поэтому следующий фундаментальный модуль логично:
> 
> # **Decision Intelligence, Governance Workbench & Human–AI Deliberation Architecture v0.1**
> 
> ---
> 
> # 30149. Его задача не:
> 
> ```text
> AI decides everything.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 30150. А:
> 
> > превращать тысячи распределённых сигналов, альтернатив и предложений в небольшое количество хорошо структурированных, доказательных и своевременных человеческих решений.
> 
> ---
> 
> # 30151. Центральный pipeline:
> 
> ```text
> Signals / Proposals / Conflicts
> ↓
> Decision Identification
> ↓
> Decision Dependency Graph
> ↓
> Evidence Requirements
> ↓
> Option Generation
> ↓
> Trade-off Representation
> ↓
> Deliberation
> ↓
> Decision
> ↓
> Authority Binding
> ↓
> Execution
> ↓
> Outcome Review
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 30152. Он должен различать:
> 
> ```text
> Recommendation
> Proposal
> Option
> Decision
> Commitment
> Execution
> Outcome
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 30153. И предотвращать:
> 
> ```text
> decision overload
> approval fatigue
> hidden machine decisions
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 30154. Также он станет естественным интерфейсом между:
> 
> ```text
> Artificial Technological Awareness
> ```
> 
> и:
> 
> ```text
> Human Governance.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> # 30155. Следующее продолжение логично начать с:
> 
> # **30156 — Decision Intelligence, Governance Workbench & Human–AI Deliberation Architecture v0.1**

Следующий блок можно продолжить с **30156**: Decision Graph, группировка и дедупликация предложений, evidence-ready decision packets, reversible vs irreversible decisions, делегируемые и неделегируемые полномочия, согласование нескольких участников, фиксация разногласий, approval fatigue и архитектура, в которой ИИ усиливает человеческое управление, но не подменяет его.
